19282: Lange Wapper is a water spirit or bogey. Once Dulle Mie wanted to dance during Lent. In the end she dances with Lange Wapper, who is recognised by his goat's legs. At this Lange Wapper swells up and flies out through the roof.
19292: A farmer's cows are sick and Trezeke is suspected of having bewitched them. As a protection an agnus dei medal is buried and Trezeke is invited for coffee. She does not react to the protection at all, but the cows do recover. When things go wrong with the cows again later, the farmer throws a pitchfork at a suspicious cat. The animal is hit in the hind legs. Shortly afterwards it turns out Trezeke has broken both her legs in a fall in the cellar. Once again the cows recover.
46722: A farmer from Viersel who had moved his boundary post had to wander about as a ghost as punishment, with the boundary post on his back. The ghost kept calling out where he should put his post. One evening a drunkard answered: "Put it back where you took it from!" At last the ghost was released.
132007: During an evening walk a couple sees a strange woman wearing a black cloak and a hood. They greet the woman, but she does not greet them back. The man pulls the hood off the mysterious woman, and she bursts apart into a ball of fire and is gone.
132008: A skipper on his way to his ship suddenly notices that someone is walking along with him. After a while that person starts growing bigger and bigger. When the skipper asks him who he is, the mysterious person bursts apart in fire. It may have been the Wandering Jew, or Ahasverus.
132009:
A very rich farmer, out of greed, does not keep his promise to his dead wife: he decides to pray for her at home instead of having holy masses said for her. This happens twice. Both times a black hand appears on the wall with a great deal of noise. The second time the farmer is so frightened that he does not live long afterwards.
The farm and the black hand on the wall are still there.
132010: A boy is not allowed by his aunt to walk at night along a certain road past the mill, because it was said to be haunted there, especially at full moon. The boy, however, never saw a ghost there.
156161: Black cats were dangerous. They were witches who appeared in the shape of an animal and brought misfortune on a house.
156168: In the meadows the horses and cows were always ridden at night, so that they became skin and bone. One night some people kept watch in the meadow and said: "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, be gone". After that the evildoers could no longer leave. They could be released through prayers. They (who?) tied a silk scarf to the gate and said that they (?) should come and get it, but they did not dare.
156185: At the farm 't Rundvoort there was much misfortune caused by the kwade hand (the evil hand, bewitchment). The animals died there and the people fell ill.
156203: A farmer, annoyed by a cat that hindered him at work, put out one of the animal's eyes. The next day one of the neighbour women had lost an eye.
156215: A bell that came from Rome is said to have sunk into the Tutsberg near a tramline between Oevel and Olen.
156222:
An old man often came to stay on a farm in Wijnegem. He had studied for the priesthood. He owned a little book with which he could work magic, but he never showed it to anyone. One morning the man said to the people on the farm: "I'll come with you to Mass. When I come out of church, I'll get five francs from the mayor." What the man had predicted did indeed come true.
When a shoemaker came to the farm to deliver shoes, the sorcerer said to him: "Are you coming back here this evening?" The shoemaker said: "No," but the sorcerer answered: "Before evening falls, you'll be back here." The shoemaker went on his way, but at the bridge in Wijnegem he could go no further and had to turn back. Only after he had been to the farm once more could he get away.
Once, when the sorcerer had gone to church and left his little book on the cupboard, the farmer's wife could not restrain her curiosity. On returning from church the sorcerer said to her: "You are a rascal. What you have copied you may keep." He burned the book and left for Hoogstraten for good. Among other things the book said: "Jesus has three bloody wounds, never sworn and never will swear." The sorcerer could cure all illnesses by saying prayers over people. When the farmer's wife had been given pearls by a woman, the sorcerer hid them behind the manure pit. After that the woman who had given the pearls could no longer enter the farm.
156236: An old woman who lived at the Meirhoeve had a child that suffered from 'de oude man' (the old man, a bewitchment illness). The child was thrown out of the cradle while people stood watching.
156240: Two friends had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what things were like in the hereafter. When one of the friends had died, he came back with the words: "They reckon strictly and they forgive nothing".
156247: In Aartselaar lived a woman named J. who everyone said was a witch. Yet her neighbour never had any trouble with her. One day, when a black cat crept into that man's house through the drain hole for the water, the man's niece said: "Watch out, J. is there!"
156250: Will-o'-the-wisps were small creatures such as cockchafers, which flew above the water and gave off a blue light. Some people claimed that such lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
156256: In a family a son had nearly died. When the little daughter of those people had died, the man who had made the coffin said: "Watch out, for all your children will perish". That was the kwade hand (the evil hand, bewitchment).
156299: A man whose sister was always ill often saw a cat come into his house. One day the man struck the cat and threw the animal far into the cornfield. The next day the man was scolded by his mother-in-law for what he had done. Yet the mother-in-law could not have known that the man had struck that cat.
156310: A woman lived in a house where a butcher had once murdered his wife. The woman always felt as if something was sitting on her back. Whenever she opened the built-in cupboard of the former occupant, it seemed as if something grabbed hold of her. In the end the woman moved away.
156316: A farm on the Beukedreef was haunted. In the morning the cows stood back to front with their tails tied together. Two calves stood with their heads in one halter. People there said it had been haunted that night.
156338: In the woods in Wiekevorst a farmer was visited one evening by a woman. The next day one of that farmer's cows lay dead. One or two weeks later the woman visited again. A day later another cow died. The same thing happened once more after that. The people had masses said and went to the friars of Herentals. There is still a cattle dealer who does not dare to buy animals from that farmer and does not even dare to enter the farm.
156339: A man going to the market in Olen was approached by a gentleman who said: "Sir, do you perhaps have some tobacco for me?" When the man had given the tobacco, the sorcerer squeezed a ball of chalk out of his nose and said: "You have always been a poacher, but now you won't shoot anything any more." When the man went home drunk that evening, he saw a cat sitting by a hedge and said: "Hello, pussycat." The cat replied: "If you hadn't spoken so nicely, you would have been on your deathbed this very day." The man went home. When he saw a fine pheasant flying the next morning, he took his gun and shot, so that the feathers flew in the air. But he could not hit the pheasant. He went home to fetch new bullets and there saw his own hen hanging shot dead on a post. The man went to the abbey of Tongerlo, where he was prayed over. Then the priest said: "Now you may shoot freely, but you will meet something terrible. You will see a big hare. Shoot at it, but leave the animal lying. After that you may take everything with you." On his way home the man did indeed meet a very big hare. But he had no gun and went home. There he got out his gun and shot at the hare, but left the animal lying. After that he was freed from the misfortune.
156361: One Saturday a man had gone to a barber to be shaved. Because it was already twelve o'clock and the man still was not home, his wife grew worried. Only at one o'clock did the man come home. He had been wandering about for a long time, ending up again and again in the same places.
156373: A drunkard had met a woman who had said: "You'll be home late tonight." Disbelieving, the man went on. Along the way a cat kept jumping onto the man's feet, which made him lose his way. In the morning the man was standing in front of the abbey of Tongerlo.
156381: In a house in Lichtaart a sick child cried all the time. When the child died, the pillow was found to be full of thorns from gooseberry bushes. People knew at once who was to blame, for a woman often came to pick gooseberries in the garden. She had bewitched the child.
156396: In Deurne there lived a woman who could make people lose their way, so that they had to wander about for hours.
156422: On seeing a will-o'-the-wisp, a woman called: "Come here, I will baptise you", and then ran inside. A large dog was burnt into the door.
156425: A woman who owned books of magic and kept company with witches came to a farmer's wife to buy a goat. She took the farmer's wife by the arm and went singing and skipping to the stable, saying: "See, now you'll have a bit of trouble later".
156443: When Louis K. from Meerhout had shot at a hare three times, the animal suddenly turned into a woman, who said: "If you dare tell anyone about this, I'll kill you!"
156462: A sick man could not be helped by the doctor. The man was often visited by a suspicious woman. The people sought advice from a man in Antwerp who had studied for the priesthood. When the people wanted to leave, a large black dog blocked their way. They began to pray, after which the dog stepped aside. The next night the man woke up tossing and cried: "There she is again!" A little light came in through the wall. The priest had advised the people to do nine days of penance.
156476: A hunter shot at a hare with a blessed half-franc coin. A short while later a man from the village claimed his wife had fallen off the ladder. In reality the woman had a gunshot wound.
156507: A farmer's wife going to deliver butter carried a pretty butter cloth with white and blue checks. The woman she came to said: "What a pretty blue butter cloth you have!" When the farmer's wife reached her destination, she had no butter left. The witch had taken the butter.
156520: A man cycling to his girlfriend's house saw a growling dog standing in the woods. He had seen the dog there several times. One day the man took a German revolver with him to shoot the dog, but when he wanted to do so, the animal had already disappeared.
156521: A pregnant woman stood next to J. at the market. J. told the woman a story about the neighbour woman, who had been unable to go to her churching because of a witch. When the pregnant woman had given birth and was to go to her churching, she could not get across the road and had to return home with her child without having done it. The next day J. addressed the woman at the market with the words: "You couldn't get across, could you?" A man always saw a cat jump at his horse's head. The man would not give way and had to stand still. That too had been J.
156523: A man who did not believe in witches said at a card evening: "I wish I could meet them all for once." When the man was on his way home that evening, he was surrounded by as many as a hundred cats.
156537: A woman coming back alone from 't Sluis saw a shadowy figure resembling a witte madam (white lady) behind a broom bush. The figure floated on over the broom bushes.
156559: A man who was gathering potatoes met a woman who said: "Mind you don't get lost." "No, I won't get lost," the man replied, but he lost his way all the same. He wandered through water and across the heath and was ill for a long time after the incident.
156586: On a farm a child was seriously ill. The child moaned all the time. When the farmer's wife heard of this, she said the sorceress had to leave the house at once. They lifted the child and found that it had been lying on a pillow with pins. The child died of the witchcraft.
156606: To recognise a witch, one had to cross her footprint. The witch would then look back.
156648: A man coming back from Achter-Olen, where he had been to visit his girlfriend, stopped for another drink in a café. When the man then headed home, his way was blocked by branches. At that spot the man saw a ghost, or so he later claimed.
156654: A man who had been asked to be godfather to a child had to walk a long way. On the way he saw a wagon approaching. He stopped the wagon and asked the driver if he could ride along for a bit. On the way, however, the driver began to curse so badly that the man said: "Be quiet or I will get off your wagon." After that the driver cursed even harder. A little later he suddenly fell silent and did not say another word until they reached their destination. On arrival the driver said: "I will never curse again, because now I have had a fright. The devil, the little black man, was sitting on my whip."
156664: During the war a boy had been given a cap by a woman. After that nothing could be done with the boy. The boy unfastened the harness of a horse and slept at night with a ring to which he had tied threads. The boy was taken to an institution near the German border and eventually died.
156689: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had to haunt, saying: "Where must I carry it? Where must I carry it?" One day a drunkard answered: "Just carry it back to where you took it from".
156694: On a farm the stable was afflicted by the evil hand. The farmer went to the stable door and saw a black cat run away between his feet. That cat was the witch.
156707: A four-year-old child always saw a black cat in the evening. Although the child's father did not believe in witchcraft, he went to Tongerlo for the child. The man had to be there before sunset. In the end, however, the child died anyway. The witch came every day to bring a sack of potatoes for the pigs.
156716: C. put his right foot in the print of a suspected woman's left foot. When the woman looked back, C. knew for certain that she was a witch.
156747: A woman from Lier came to Berlaar hawking waffles. A family bought waffles and gave some to the children. After that those children began screaming at night. They decided not to buy any more waffles from the hawker, and after that they had no more problems with the children.
156800: On a farm the people had much misfortune with their land. The farmer sowed all sorts of things, but nothing came up. In the end the farmer went to the friars. The trouble was caused by a woman from the neighbourhood who had great power.
156824: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend in Zandvliet came to a meadow where he saw a cat sitting on a swing gate. The man knocked the cat off the gate twice, but each time the animal sat back on it. When the man had struck it the second time, the cat said: "Try that once more." The man went on, but not five metres further he was surrounded by ten or twelve cats that bit his leather boots to pieces.
156851: A girl was advised by her mother never to kick a cat or a toad in the evening. For they were all witches who took on the shape of an animal to torment people better.
156853: The Zandhoeve in Stelen was terribly haunted. In the evening the ghosts danced in the kitchen and made a racket with pots and pans. At midnight it was quiet, because then the ghosts went to count their money with a 'luepel' (1).
156860: When there was a fair on a Thursday in Sint-Amands, the owner of café 'Het Varken' was coming home along the Buisstraat. Under a big oak the man saw a woman standing, and he struck up a conversation with her. The woman, however, did not say a word. The man pulled the cap off the woman's head and ran off with it. At home the man threw the cap on the cupboard. When the man woke up the next morning, he saw to his great horror a skull standing on the cupboard. The man had barely sat up when the woman he had seen the evening before came in and said: "You have done something wrong." The man denied it and said: "That's not true, I only took a woman's cap." When the woman had disappeared a little later, the man put the skull away. The next day, however, the skull was standing on the cupboard again. Because this happened every day, the man went to the priest, who said: "Nothing can be done about it. You must take that cap back to the place where you took it, at the same time as when you took it. I will clothe you with the stook (stole?)." The man also took a small child with him to the place of the mischief. Under the oak he saw the woman standing again. When the man put the skull on the woman's head, it turned back into a cap. The woman said: "If you weren't so strongly armed, I would break your neck." It was the devil, appearing in the shape of a woman.
156880: Two children who had been born healthy became disabled at the age of five. The doctors could not explain it. People believed the children had fallen victim to the evil hand. The sister-in-law of the children's mother was said to have been responsible.
156901: If you fell victim to the tormenting of a woman with a bad name, you were not allowed to tell anyone about it. Otherwise you would get twice as much misfortune. One Sunday morning a man drove to early mass at the friars'. On the way he met a farmer's wife who said the evil hand was in her stables. The man replied that he had the same problem and went on: "The worst of it is that we know who is responsible. It is a woman from the neighbourhood, because others don't get the chance". When the man came home, his wife said he should not have spoken about the trouble. The misfortune in the stables continued. One morning the man and his wife went to the friars by back roads without telling anyone. When they went back home, they saw the witch standing in the middle of the road. The next day the man was killed when he fell from his cart. That witch had terribly great power.
156922: Some friends were sitting in a witch's café. Some of the men laughed at the witch, except one. When the men asked how much they had to pay, the witch said: "Just stand up." But none of the men could stand up, except the one who had not mocked her. Then the witch came back and said: "Get out of here." After that everyone could stand up.
156962: In the evening or at night, a man always saw a black dog jumping up against his legs. The man grew frightened and one night took a club with him to beat the dog. The next day a man with bruises was walking around the village.
156969: A woman who was known as a witch in Oelegem moved to Wijnegem. After that a girl in Wijnegem fell ill. Because people believed the girl had fallen victim to the evil hand, they took her to a farmer from Deuren. The girl was cured and lived to an old age.
156999: In a house people tried to chase the cats out of the attic. A neighbour boy kicked a cat and broke its leg. The following week a woman from the neighbourhood had a bandage around her arm.
157013: On a farm there were two cows in calf. When one Sunday morning the two cows could no longer get up, the farmer's wife went to ask the neighbours for help. The neighbour's wife said: "My husband hasn't been to church yet. But I'll vouch for it. Leave the cows lying until after high mass and then they'll jump up". And so it happened.
157017: In Mechelen lived a man who consorted with the devil. He could stick long copper needles into his arms and legs without feeling anything. He spoke a magic formula and was helped by the devil.
157020: At the Driegmaagdekeskapelletje in Booischot three little nuns came haunting at night. Nobody dared to go there any more.
157030: On the road from Wommelgem to Ranst a whole pack of cats was seen. No one knew where those cats came from, but people supposed that a witch had sent the animals.
157099: A man saw a witte madam (white lady) walking across the road. A moment later the apparition had vanished without a trace.
157102: Two sisters who went to gather broom met a witch. One of the sisters was touched by the witch and was ill for two months afterwards.
157124: In Bruggenheide lived a man who claimed his house was haunted. At night banging and rattling could be heard there. When people went to look, they saw peach trees in bloom in the attic. After the people had been to the fathers of Tongerlo, the strange events came to an end.
157156: A boatman sailing in Germany saw a row of black nuns standing on the dike. The boatman's wife began to pray. At her third Hail Mary all the nuns disappeared.
157159: A farmer who had lost three cows in a single day went to the quack in Beers (?). The man also went to church every day to pray against the evil hand.
157169: On a farm there were ten splendid calves that drank well. Because the calves suddenly seemed to stop growing, the farmer went to the friars, who already knew why he had come. The clergymen said the evil hand would have passed on to the people if the farmer had not come to them so quickly. The farmer had to go to mass every Friday for eight weeks. After that the trouble in the stable came to an end.
157187: In Wilrijk lived an ugly old woman who was said to be a witch. Mothers with small children in particular were afraid of her. The witch was sometimes seen sitting at her window with a doll while speaking magic formulas. In this way the witch bewitched a child.
157206: One day a beggar came to a parish priest asking for alms. The priest said he had nothing in the house, but finally allowed the beggar to cut off his silver buckles. When the beggar bent down, the priest laid his hand on the man's shoulder and went inside. The beggar stayed bent over and could move neither forward nor backward. Once inside, the priest called the sexton. The sexton would see a man standing outside and was to go and tell him he could move on. The sexton did so and the beggar could move again.
157216: Three boys had gone to draw lots for military service. Two of them had to join the army. When the three friends had been to the pub on Sunday, two of them went home together. When the two were at the fen, opposite a pub where a witch was said to live, they saw a little kitten walking. One of the boys kicked the animal, sending it flying three or four metres. A little later the boys saw the cat again. The boy kicked the cat again, but it came back once more. When the boy wanted to kick the cat for the third time, suddenly some twenty cats jumped in front of his feet. The ground even shook from it. After the boys had prayed for a while, the cats had disappeared. A little later the two boys were joined by the friend who had been at the pub with them. The two said to him: "I wish that kitten were back here". A little later the kitten was there again. It ran in front of the boys' feet and then crept into a small elm. Then it jumped onto the back of the boy who had just joined his two friends.
157223: A man was coming back late in the evening from visiting his girlfriend, whose mother was a witch. On the way the man heard as many as a thousand cats mewing.
157240: A young man and his girlfriend saw a cat that kept running against their legs. The young man kicked at the cat, but the next moment dozens of cats appeared. When the young man went home, he saw that the street was completely full of cats.
157268: A miller working in the evening was annoyed by a cat that always came scratching under the gate. The miller cut off one of the animal's paws. When the man came home later that evening, he found that his wife had only one hand left.
157279: On a farm a neighbour woman always came to stand at the window or have a drink whenever butter was being churned. When the visitor had left, the cows had foam on their lips or no more butter could be made. There were three knocks on the oven. In the neighbour's house the doors flew open and shut all night. People went to Bornem about the witchcraft, where they were advised to say certain prayers. After that the trouble was over.
157285: At a miller's in Grobbendonk someone shot at a cat at night. The next morning the miller's wife lay in bed with a broken arm.
157293: In Battel lived an old woman who could do magic. When a mother was standing somewhere with her child in her arms, the witch came closer and said: "What a sweet little child!" while stroking the child's head. Shortly afterwards the child began to cry. The doctor did not know what to do, but a herbal healer said: "The child is bewitched. No one but the witch herself can cure it." The witch was forced to lift the spell. The child's head, which had been full of lice, suddenly became clean and the child recovered. The witch quietly left the village because she feared the family's revenge.
157321: A woman who worked for a farmer in Edegem was always picked up by her husband. When the two came onto the main road to Brussels one day, the woman saw something beside the trees and said: "Look at that little child there!" The woman wanted to walk over to it, but her husband held her back and said: "That is a ghost." When the two got home, they broke out in a cold sweat.
157328: Some men were cursing during a card game when a stranger knocked and asked if he could join in. The stranger had struck the door with his hand, causing all the paint to flake off.
157330: A man returning late in the evening from a visit to his family saw a big fire in the middle of the heath. The man walked over and saw lots of cats. Although he was afraid, he said: "Ah, pussycats, are you warming your little paws?" The cats replied: "If you hadn't spoken so nicely, we would have broken your neck."
157381: Witches could change into the shape of small animals, such as rabbits, dogs and cats. A witch could not, for example, take on the shape of a calf.
157411: A man walking home from Heffen one night in the rain with an umbrella saw a black cat sitting by a remote farm. When the man walked past the farm, the cat stood up on its hind legs and walked towards him like that. The cat grew bigger and bigger as it came. The man became so frightened that he struck at the cat with his umbrella. The next moment the animal had vanished.
157435: In Poederlee three children are said to have died through witchcraft.
157442: A sick man could not be helped by the doctor because he was bewitched. After a holy object had been fetched from the friars and placed under the threshold, the witch could no longer come in. When the parish priest came to bless the house, he said: "Just as good exists, so does evil". A friar from Tongerlo firmly maintained that something supernatural existed.
157445: A woman who had a large swelling on her throat claimed that the swelling had appeared when she was ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) at a young age. At that moment someone had come in and grabbed her by the throat.
157462: A man who had not gone to the guldenmis (golden mass) was walking home in the evening and saw, in the Renderstraatje, a mysterious hand writing on the wall in glowing letters: "Strike him dead, strike him dead, for he has not heard the guldenmis". The spot where this happened was later called 'De Hand' (The Hand).
157476: In a family a child had died a few days after birth. People claimed it was the fault of a witch from the neighbourhood who had stroked the child. After the child's death the witch never came there again.
157479: A dead person came back to reveal a murder that had been kept secret.
157494: A man coming back from Mechelen on foot suddenly found himself in a meadow. However fast the man walked and whichever direction he chose, he kept wandering about in the meadow. That man was ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) until morning came.
157519: A sorcerer went to a meeting where all the sorcerers would be present. While the sorcerer was away, people wanted to burn the man's magic skin. They searched the sorcerer's house and found the skin. But the sorcerer sensed what was going on and transported himself back to his house in one second.
157529: In Itegem a man always came by with a cart pulled by calves. One day that man saw a cowherd flying through the air. The boy had simply been thrown into the air by the witches.
157537: Many people did not dare to go on the Franse Weg in the dark, because lights appeared there that vanished into the Binnepad. Sometimes in the morning little white cloths hung on the washing line. The lights were the little souls of two children who had been murdered there long ago.
157546: A woman was visited by a saleswoman who gave her son a sweet. The boy, who was seven at the time, died. The saleswoman was a witch.
157554: A farm in Boechout was always haunted. The occupants were forced by poverty to move from there to Kontich.
157557: In Wilmarsdonk lived a wizard who could open a locked door by throwing his cap against it.
157593: A woman from Kapellen always saw a cat sitting by the well when she went to fetch water. The woman's husband asked the cat: "Little cat, my pussycat, what are you doing here?" When the cat answered "nothing", the farmer struck the animal. The next day a suspected woman lay injured in her bed.
157605: Some people on their way to church saw fruit lying on the ground by a witch's house. If you could not leave that fruit alone, you became bewitched.
157633: A man from Achterlee saw a chicken running between his legs on his way home. The man kicked at the animal but could not hit it. Strangely, the chicken never flew up cackling, but always jumped four or five metres away without making a sound. The man grew afraid and started to run. The chicken followed him to his house and then disappeared.
157637: A man who could overlezen (cure by reciting prayers) had to go and look at a heifer on the farm of a witch. Two days later nearly all of that man's cows lay dead.
157642: In a house in Geel there was a little baby that one day began to cry incessantly. A neighbour woman claimed the child was bewitched and advised the mother to invite all the women of the neighbourhood for coffee. When everyone was there, the neighbour put a cross under the door. After the coffee everyone went home except one woman who could not get up from her chair. That woman confessed she had bewitched the child. Before removing the cross, the people gave the witch a good beating. After that she never came by again and the child was cured.
157652: One night a poacher was in Kalfort. Because he had not caught anything yet, he began to swear like a heretic. A little later he was jumped by a beast that scratched open his chest and held on to him tightly. The man could not get rid of the beast. With great difficulty he got home towards morning.
157661: Black cats were ghosts. They were incarnations either of the devil or of a witch.
157664: One morning a man went with his wheelbarrow to the market of Sint-Niklaas to buy a pig. On the way he met a very old little woman who sat down on his wheelbarrow and after a while went away. When the man came back from Sint-Niklaas he had one pig with him. By the time he got home the animal was already dead.
157687: Some people who were together on a Sunday afternoon decided to hold a cursing contest. The man who had come up with the idea said: "I'll count to three and then everyone as loud as they can. We'll see if we can lure the devil." A little later everyone began to curse. At a certain moment a horse's hoof struck the table, and a blue flame came out of it. The whole room stank of sulphur. The people stopped cursing for good.
157711: In the lane near S. stood a little chapel where a nun returned in the evenings in the form of a light.
157720: A woman lay rigid and sweating in her bed at night. At the foot of her bed she saw the mare (nightmare spirit) moving. After the woman had received a relic from the fathers of Turnhout, she was no longer troubled by the mare.
157731: A miller's son could work magic. He could turn a clod of earth into a mouse.
157785: In Geel there once lived a witch who often went about in the form of a cat. One evening a man said to a cat that came and sat at his feet: "Are you old mother X?" The cat answered: "Yes" and then vanished.
157792: In Zoerle-Parwijs lived a witch who often went out alone at night. When a calf was being sold in the village, the witch was interested in it. But a farmer who had more means bought the calf. About two weeks later, one morning at the farm, they found the witch standing in the stable by the calf, rubbing the animal's head. When the farmer's wife asked what she was doing there, she replied: "I've just come to see how the calf is doing". Three weeks later the calf was dead.
157793:
A man said to a friend: "I can make that woman from Donk dance and walk here for eight hours." The man immediately suited the action to the word.
One day a mother of ten children said: "I am going dancing, even if it is with the devil." The mother danced with a handsome gentleman. Suddenly the bystanders saw that the gentleman had a horse's foot. Then the devil jumped behind a tree and flew away.
157805: A bewitched woman went on pilgrimage to friars in France. When they came to a stream and saw no bridge, the pilgrims asked the farmers whether there was a bridge anywhere. The farmers answered "no" in surprise. The pilgrims waded through the water and got wet up to their waists. When they looked back afterwards, they saw no stream and heard the farmers calling: "Why should there be a bridge if there is no water?"
157809: A farmer was married to a witch who always left for the sabbath in the evening. One day the farmer decided to stay awake to see what exactly his wife did. So he saw the witch say around midnight: "Over hedge and stile to Cologne into the wine cellar" and then fly off on a broom. The farmer decided to follow his wife and said: "Through hedge and stile to Cologne into the wine cellar". However, he arrived at his destination with scratches all over his face.
157834: If you had eaten too much in the evening, you were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night. You then suddenly felt a heavy weight on your stomach. It seemed like a heavy hairy beast with sharp claws.
157854: On the Wimp lived a woman who had had twins 'from the camp'(?). The woman had drowned the children. Ever since, a will-o'-the-wisp was always seen above the water in the evenings.
157867: If one wanted to know whether a suspected woman was a witch, one had to walk behind her and place one's foot crosswise in her footprint. If she was a witch, she would look back the next moment.
157881: A shopkeeper who saw a witch coming with her daughter did not want to sell those two women anything. The witch could do all sorts of things. Once she bewitched a man from the neighbourhood so that he was stuck fast in his chair. That man sometimes saw rats and mice coming in.
157905: A cat walked up to a brewer's hand and asked: "How is the beer doing?" The hand chopped off one of the cat's paws. The next morning the brewer's wife lay in bed with one arm.
157914: In the old days, when something went wrong somewhere, a witch was often blamed. In Herselt lived a woman who always carried a rosary. She fingered the beads of the rosary, but she did not pray. The children were warned about that witch by their mother. One evening a girl had to stay the night with that witch. When the girl got up in the morning, there were scratches all over her face.
157926: A farm near the border of Oevel was haunted. The plates danced in the racks and the lid of the stove flew a good half metre into the air. Strangely enough, nothing was ever broken.
157942: In a family where a child was seriously ill, the parents wanted to take the child to the friars of Dendermonde. But the mother of the sorceress who had made the child ill objected. To prevent the parents from going to the friars, the sorceress cured the child at once.
157975: A man coming back alone from Breendonk suddenly saw a witte madam (white lady) walking along a woodland path. The man got away as fast as he could.
157982: Jefke's mother met a woman from the neighbourhood who said: "My, what a chubby child you have!", to which the mother replied: "How can you know that? You haven't seen the child yet!" The witch went on: "You're being churched tomorrow, aren't you?" When the mother got home, she found her child was ill. The woman went on foot to Tongerlo, where a friar told her: "It will be hard for you and for me. But on the ninth day you will hold the child in your hands, deathly ill. If you keep your courage, the child will live". Everything the friar had foretold came true. A few days later the mother was again visited by the witch, who came to ask for something. The mother refused, for she was convinced the witchcraft would otherwise return.
158016: On a farm in Oelegem a cat came in through the drain hole for the water. In doing so the animal knocked over a bucket of water. Since that incident the people on that farm had much misfortune. All the animals in the stable died. When a friar came to overlezen (exorcise with prayers) the place, the clergyman sweated terribly.
158044: A man who was threshing at a farmer's saw a witch approaching, who said: "It's good that you've come to help the farmers", and she briefly touched the engine of the threshing machine. After his work at the farmer's, the man went elsewhere to thresh. There his engine no longer worked. Some time later the engine began running so fast that the man himself became frightened. Because his engine was bewitched, the man did not manage to thresh the whole stack that day, though he had planned to be done by half past seven. The next day he had exactly the same problems with the engine.
158099: Once the devil tried to make a man from Tielen enter into a pact with him. The devil gave the man a beautiful pin, which made him very happy. A little later the man found that the pin had disappeared from his trouser pocket, whereupon the devil asked: "Wouldn't you like to be able to do that too?" The man said yes, whereupon the devil took out a rosary. Instead of a cross, a round object hung on the rosary with the inscription: "Throw me into the fire for eternity!" When the man had read that, he knew the devil was standing before him. He made the sign of the cross and a moment later the devil had vanished.
158100: On a farm a black cat was sometimes seen walking across the meadow. Every time that happened, a cow died on that farm.
158101: A farmer who was going to see his girlfriend had to pass the heksenkuil (witches' pit). He could not find his girlfriend's house and ended up in the heksenkuil. The witches had seen to that, for they could not bear anyone going to visit their boyfriend or girlfriend.
158108: A man coming back from a music society rehearsal saw lights and bells on the way and heard chains rattling.
158147: A sorcerer let five or six children ride along on his horse cart and said to their parents: "Just let them come along. They can eat pears and apples for free." The sorcerer took the children to an orchard and said: "You needn't be afraid. No farmer will dare to come. Go ahead and eat." When the farmers came running, they could not get to the orchard.
158168: A boy from Sint-Amands was going out with a girl who was suspected of being a witch. The girl's mother was a widow who was also said to be a witch. One evening the boy arrived at his girlfriend's at half past nine. He pretended to be drunk and dead tired. He had hardly arrived when the girl and her mother got ready to leave. The boy pretended to have fallen asleep, but secretly watched what happened. He saw his girlfriend and her mother take something from the mantelpiece and then disappear. The boy got up and found on the mantelpiece a little box with one small ball left in it. He took hold of the ball and a moment later found himself in a clearing in the woods where a witches' meeting was taking place. He saw his girlfriend and her mother there, who were very startled by his presence. He also saw strange beasts with horns and fiery eyes. All the beasts were hung with silver and gold. After the meeting all the witches went home on a pig. At a large brook the girlfriend and her mother told the boy that he must not say the name 'Mary' or 'Jesus', or else the pig would run off. But the boy said "Jesus, Mary" anyway, and the pig vanished from under him. Suddenly he recognised the place where he was.
158174: In a family in Weert, one of the two sons had died. When the people came back from the hour of prayer and the evening benediction, all the doors of their house flew open and a ghost appeared that said: "Ten masses and you will all be happy." It was probably the ghost of the dead son.
158197: A person who had been ridden by the moon had nightmares and sometimes wandered about in the fields.
158223: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children that flew over the marshes.
158235: A nineteen-year-old girl was pregnant and married. During her pregnancy the girl had convulsions. The girl had twelve children in all, of whom only one survived. An old woman was said to have caused that misfortune. When, on the parish priest's advice, a holy object had been put under the door of that house, the woman could no longer come in.
158236: A witch master who always walked very bent lay in his bed as stiff as a board. When the man was walking to the village one evening, a black cat came and sat in front of his feet. The man kicked the cat away several times, but the animal always came back. Suddenly the cat said: "Stamp at me again if you dare!" The witch master replied: "Get under my feet again if you dare!", but the cat no longer dared.
158258: In a house beautiful black doves flew around at night. Before that, mice had been seen there. They were witches.
158271: On a farm a red cat lay in the manger in front of the animals. In the evening the cows pulled themselves loose, and the next day no butter could be made on that farm. A sorceress had been there who had changed herself into a red cat.
158371: A farmhand who worked at 't Looiend was coming back from the village across the heath. Suddenly he saw a fire with witches dancing around it. The farmhand came closer and said: "In God's name." The next moment the witches ran away.
158430: By the side of the road lay a treasure chest that soldiers had lost. A farmer dumped a cart of manure over the chest, causing hundreds of regiments of soldiers to die of hunger. Every hundred years the farm had to be exorcised because the ghosts of the soldiers came to haunt it. The doors flew open, the horses stamped, in the morning the cows stood turned around in the stable, and soldiers rode through the stable on horseback. When the hundred years had passed, the haunting began again.
158442: In Herselt lived a woman who could change herself into a cat.
158455: Some people coming back from the fair in Balen around midnight were accompanied by a witch-master or wizard. At the Hasselt canal the wizard made all the cats of Ginderbuiten gather on the canal dike. Afterwards many people could not get home and had to wander about until sunrise. The wizard had caused this.
158474: People who were ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) had to get up at night and sleepwalked. They felt a strange pressure on their body. Some believed this was due to the blood standing still.
158497: A man who worked at a kiln was always bothered at night by a black dog that ate his sandwiches. The man told his colleague, who said: "I'll do the night stoking in your place." While the colleague was stoking at night, the dog came up and urinated in the kiln. As soon as the dog went for the sandwiches, the workman hit the animal on its hind legs with a stick. The next day a woman suspected of being a witch had two broken legs. Then they knew at once who the black dog had been.
158516: A family from Vorst found it strange that their child Jef had pneumonia every year. A neighbour woman often visited the family and always brought something for the child. Nine women went on pilgrimage to the chapel for the boy for nine days. From the holy little friar in Hasselt, Jef's father received two holy objects: one for under the threshold and one to hang on Jef's scapular. When the witch came by, you were not allowed to say "Come in", because that gave her power. After a while Jef was cured.
158517: Some people coming back from the Osdrecht fair saw a witte madam (white lady).
158522: In Heist-op-den-Berg lived a man who could make the rats from the whole neighbourhood gather in his house, so that people jumped onto their chairs in fright. Once the man had to go and fetch someone to drive the rats away again, for he could not yet do that himself.
158540: One evening a man struck at a cat that was running back and forth across the road. Afterwards the man got an infection in his hand.
158562: On a farm on the Veenzijde the stable was afflicted by the evil hand. A witch doctor was called in to overlezen (cure with prayers) the animals. Shortly afterwards the animals were cured.
158581: A man visiting friends was told: "If you don't go home to sleep, I'll send you wandering for a whole night". When the man went home in the evening, he had to cross a brook. Only after he met someone who asked him: "What are you still doing here?" did he get home.
158633: Some men going from Isschot to de Hoeven one evening saw a white figure standing in the water by the pit. The men called out to the figure, which then disappeared. Not even twenty metres further they saw the figure again. When the men looked back a little later, they saw to their great fright that the ghost was following them.
158664: A man always saw a ghost walking about with a boundary post on its back when he came home from work. One day the man called to the ghost: "Throw that stone back where you got it". The ghost answered: "I have tried that many times". The man threw the stone away and never saw the ghost again.
158673: A man drove his mother to the doctor because she could not die. The doctor said to the man: "She can die if she wants to". A rumour went round that the mother had once bewitched a daughter of the doctor, so that the girl had not grown.
158704: A witch lived in Achter-Olen. A farmer who lived nearby had much misfortune and saw all his cows die until he had nothing left.
158709: The Molenstraat used to be haunted. A white goat was often seen wandering there in the evening. People tried several times to catch the goat, but did not succeed. Every time they came closer, the goat suddenly vanished without a trace.
158721: A woman who felt fine when going to bed at night had fits around midnight. She would start shouting and had to be calmed by her husband. One day the man caught a little dove sitting on his bean poles in the garden. When he brought the dove inside, his wife screamed loudly, flew at the dove and grabbed it by the neck. The following Tuesday the woman's sister saw, at the market in Niel, the sorceress suspected of causing the harm, with two large bruises on her neck. After that the woman had no more fits at night.
158732: On a farm seven cows died within a short time because of the evil hand. A woman who often visited there had the habit of stroking the animals' heads. When that woman was thrown out, everything went well again on the farm.
158737: In Testelt a man said to his girlfriend: "I need to go to the toilet for a moment, but I'll be right back. If anything comes at you, just hit it with your handkerchief". A little later the girl was approached by a dog and struck at it with her handkerchief. When her boyfriend came back, she saw that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
158749: A year after his death a man appeared three times to his family with a purse. At a certain moment the children remembered that they had promised to have masses said for their father in Hanswijk. The children had forgotten that promise. After the priest of Hanswijk had said the masses, the dead man appeared no more.
158755: A farmer who had eight cows one day could no longer make butter. Someone advised him to churn the milk of each cow separately, since one of the cows was probably bewitched. Because that indeed turned out to be the case, the farmer went to the friars. After the farmer had put a holy object under the door, he could make butter again after a while.
158788: In Vremde there lived a midwife who was suspected of being a witch. If you walked behind that woman and crossed her footprints, she would look back.
158803: If you saw a crow sitting on the well, you could expect misfortune.
158808: A boy lay completely stiff and motionless in his bed. He had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
158836: A woman who was kneading bread got a fright when a rat suddenly came in. A witch said to her: "What you're afraid of!" The witch made one rat after another appear.
158844: A six-month-old girl always began screaming and sweating at six in the evening. The screaming lasted until four or five in the morning. The doctor was called, but he could not make a diagnosis. A few weeks later the exhausted mother told her neighbour what her problem was. "Has anyone ever been in here?" asked the neighbour, to which the mother replied: "Yes". An old little woman from Bruggeneinde had visited. That woman had stood looking at the child for a long time. The mother was given two medals and had to lock everything up well in the evening. One medal she had to put under the threshold of the door and the other under the bedroom window. That evening the child did not scream. At a certain moment the baby began to whimper. When a slapping sound was heard behind the bed, the baby spread its little arms as if in pain. It was exactly midnight. The father got up, but there was nothing to see, although he had heard a sound as if something heavy had fallen over. The next day the mother told her neighbour what had happened. "You can take the medals away now", said the neighbour. After that nothing strange happened any more.
158852: When Selm went to a spinning gathering one evening, he filled the house with mice by magic.
158860: Werewolves were people who had been punished and who turned into a beast at night. After an hour they became human again. A man who was coming back from the fair in Baal with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to go and relieve myself. If you meet anything, just throw your apron". A little later the girl saw something coming. She threw her apron, after which the apparition vanished. When her boyfriend came back, the girl told her story, but she was not taken seriously. When the girl was home, her boyfriend had another drink in her parents' inn. There the girl saw that the young man had pieces of the apron between his teeth. The girl fell ill and died.
158863: At the Kievitkasteel on den Aart (Geel), a lord of the castle had a burial vault built for himself, his wife and his son. The work began in 1872 and was finished in 1876. After his death the lord walked around the castle every night at twelve o'clock. After the castle was demolished and rebuilt, the ghost was not seen again.
158880: When the crucifix fell off the wall at farmer X's one day, the farmer's wife said: "Now the king is dead", to which the farmer replied: "You're mad!" Later that day King Albert was found dead.
158883: Two friends had promised each other that whoever died first would come and tell the other what life in the hereafter was like. When one of the friends had died and the other was threshing in the barn, the dead man appeared with the words: "Dancing and jumping you may do there as much as you like."
158933: A maid who had to fetch water had beckoned to a will-o'-the-wisp and then ran home quickly. On the door the maid had hastily slammed shut, a hand was burnt. No one ever managed to remove the handprint. Some people claimed that will-o'-the-wisps arose from marshes. According to others they were the souls of unbaptised children.
158935: At the little bridge a man had to fight a dog. The dog jumped on him and dragged him to a pit. It was the devil.
158944: On the eleventh day of every month animals on a farm were ill. Each time, a little woman with a bad name had passed by beforehand.
158955: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died innocent, wandering about the world. Joris N. made a painting about it.
158986: A mother was churning butter together with her daughter. Once you had butter, you had to turn the spoons over. But the daughter did not do it properly, whereupon the mother said: "Oh, now you've gone off with other people's butter".
158994: A man who was sometimes ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) would toss and turn in his bed, shouting: "Let me go, let me go!" He sweated and felt as if he was being grabbed by the neck.
159012: By a little chapel in Gierle a farmer came across a black cat that would not be chased away. The farmer threw his dung fork at the cat and injured the animal on the head. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had only one eye left. That is how the saying "At the little chapel I lost my only eye!" came about.
159049: In Liezele lived a sorceress whom everyone except the priest feared. The priest could free someone who was bewitched from the spell. One day the sorceress bewitched the priest himself. She put him, fully clothed, in the middle of the moat around the castle. The priest had to stand there a whole night because he could not get out of the moat.
159059: A man walking through the woods saw the trees swaying back and forth because of a witch.
159061: The minister was a poacher. When he saw a hare running in the wood beside his house, he shot at the animal from the window. One night, as the minister stood at his window waiting for prey, he froze to death. Shortly afterwards the minister's wife woke up. On finding her frozen husband she fetched straw and set it alight to warm him. The minister still had bullets in his pocket, which exploded in the fire, so that the intestines flew out of the man's body. Some time later the room of the pregnant widow was full of lights. The woman believed it was her late husband.
159081: Every evening a farmer heard a cat mewing at the three bunders (fields). It was a white cat that always went and stood behind people's backs and then ran off towards a bush, where it kept mewing. One evening, when the farmer's wife went to milk the cow, a little later she ran crying out of the stable. There were rats all over the cow. When the other people came to look, the rats ran up the walls to the loft. One evening, as the farmer was walking home, he saw the white cat lying in a pit by the three bunders. He went home and told his father, who came along with his gun to the spot. When they arrived, they saw that the cat had gone. The farmer's father saw the cat sitting a bit further on and shot at it. After that they had no more trouble from the cat. It was a sorceress from the village. If she could do no harm elsewhere, she had to do harm at home.
159100: On a farm someone was ill. The people decided not to tell anyone, but the next day a witch from the neighbourhood was already at their door asking: "Is someone ill?" When a calf died on that farm, the farmer decided to bury it secretly at night. The next day the witch came and asked: "Why did you bury that calf? It was still good to eat". The farmer went to fetch a holy object somewhere to put under the door of the stable and under the door of the house. After that the witch never came in again. When the witch came to bring pears some time later, she threw the bag from a distance, saying: "Here you are, for you sometimes do something for me too".
159148: A statue of Mary was once found in the Wijngaardbos in Veerle. When people wanted to take the statue to Averbode, they could not, because it kept falling off the cart.
159162: In a village lived a miller whose wife was said to be a witch. One evening a passer-by saw a cat lying on a doorstep and cut off one of its paws with a knife. The next day the miller's wife lay in bed with only one arm.
159211: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field came to haunt by the Steentjesbeek in Houtvenne, saying: "Where shall I leave my post?" One day someone answered: "Leave it where you took it from!"
159226: A man saw a ghost that was on fire and holding a torn handkerchief.
159228: A farmer coming back from the café met fifteen dogs halfway along the Muizendreef, which blocked his way.
159231: On a farm, on the advice of his brother who was a friar, the farmer put a relic under the gate. Because of this a certain woman who always came for milk or buttermilk could no longer come in. Before that the farm had had problems churning butter.
159233: Some men were gathering potatoes one evening in the company of the witch Jo M. When one of the men said: "They can't frighten me anyway!", Jo answered: "We'll see about that." That evening the man lost his way. Only after Jo had said: "Go on home now" did the man find his way again.
159240: A ship lay at anchor on the Vliet. When the skipper walked to his ship in the evening and crawled into bed, he heard knocking on the hatches. He went up but saw nothing. When he was back in bed, the knocking started again. This time too there was nothing to be seen. The man went back to bed and found it hard to breathe. He tried to shout but could not. The mare (nightmare spirit) had come in through the hatches and had jumped on her victim.
159263: One morning some people saw a black cat sitting on their windowsill. The father stabbed at the animal, but he missed. He believed the cat was a wizard from the neighbourhood.
159272: At the chapel in Oevel a man heaped up a little pile of sand so that a moment later he could conjure rats out of it. A friar from the abbey of Tongerlo took that man's magic power away.
159274: A brewer's hand working in the brewery at night saw cats coming in through the drain hole for the water. He poured boiling water on the cats, which were scalded and ran away. The next day the women of the neighbourhood all had burns.
159292: A man who had moved a boundary post came to haunt after his death with the glowing post in his hands, calling: "Where must I leave it, where must I leave it?" A farmer who had heard this went to the parish priest, who told him: "Just say that he must put the post back where he took it from".
159348: At the Vondel there was always a black sheep. Because that sheep followed passers-by, people did not dare to walk past that place in the evening.
159349: A maid who had special powers worked on a farm. One day, when the maid had to run an errand, she let a whole flock of wild oriental doves settle in her apron along the way.
159371: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. When you saw such a light, you had to say: "I baptise you alone and no other. I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit". Nothing about such matters that had to do with God could be written down, because that was dangerous.
159374: A woman did not dare kill a spider because she believed spiders were sorceresses.
159399: In Kasterlee a plaintive voice was always heard in the evening, calling: "Post here, post there, where must I leave you?" When one day someone answered: "Put it where you took it from!", the voice was heard no more.
159430: A boy was visiting his girlfriend, who lived at the Burcht. When the boy wanted to go home, a woman persuaded him to stay a while longer. At midnight the boy left for home. But the boy was bewitched; his father was just able to stop him from jumping into the green pit.
159444: In a house where a woman came to ask for milk, a man said to his daughter: "Be careful, you must not trust that woman. You must not give her any more milk." When she was refused the milk, the woman grew angry and grabbed the girl by the arm. Afterwards the girl's arm swelled up completely. The girl had to stay in bed for a good eight days.
159447: In the Trichstraat someone is said to have seen a hundred cats walking behind him. When he got home the man told what he had experienced. Some other people went to look, but the cats were no longer to be seen.
159511: People who were ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) had their blood standing still. Those people had strange dreams in which they could walk through a closed door.
159512: One autumn evening Louis was passing the Reigersbos with his cart. Above the Kleine Weel the man saw a blue flame floating. At first Louis thought it was a will-o'-the-wisp. As the light came closer, it turned into the devil, who had goat's legs and a tail and wore a top hat. Louis struck at the devil with his dung fork, but it was no use. When the man made the sign of the cross, the devil vanished at once in a cloud of stinking sulphur and smoke.
159527: A man on his way to his girlfriend's house had to pass a churchyard, where he saw cats fighting. The man threw his knife at the animals and went on. When he then reached his girlfriend, she gave him back his knife with the words: "Here is your knife. You must never do that again."
159570: A farmer whose farmhand had died always heard a deep sigh by the well. One day the farmer asked: "Speak, if I can help you." The voice of the farmhand answered: "I cannot get away. You must fast for me for a whole year." When the farmer had done so, he still heard the sighing and asked: "Are you still not gone?" The voice answered: "No, you did it wrong. You ate before twelve o'clock, and you should have waited to eat until after twelve." The farmer resolved to fast for another year. But before the year was over, the farmer died.
159577: A woman had a two-year-old daughter. When the little girl got new shoes, she felt unwell. Later the child developed epilepsy. All of this was the fault of a witch.
159581: A man who had a black cat came home and called: "Where are you, dear pussycat?" The black cat walked to the drain hole and said: "Where are you, dear pussycat?"
159602: There was a café near Boom. When some men came out of it, they saw a Witte Madam (white lady) approaching in the distance. The apparition walked past in silence, but the men were still afraid to go home.
159614: On a farm where the cows were all sick, the vet was called. But the man could do nothing about it and sent the people to the friars. The clergymen blessed the stable and hung up a picture of Saint Anthony, the patron saint of livestock. After that the cows recovered.
159620: A man walking along the road by the stone bridge saw a beast as big as a small donkey approaching in the dark.
159634: Some people who had attacked the parish priest could not go home. The attackers could only move again after the priest had given them permission.
159647: A woman who had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) lay tied down in her bed and could no longer move.
159682: In a house that was completely locked up, a cat suddenly appeared at the window.
159718: A man coming home through the woods at night kept feeling something rubbing against his legs. When the man saw that they were cats, he struck at the animals. A little further on, however, the man saw as many as a hundred cats.
159737: A man from Nijlen was coming back at night from the fair in Kessel. When the man saw a cat crawl out from under a bridge, he said: "Pussycat, where are you going?" The cat replied: "Janneke asks me: Pussycat, where are you going?"
159740: A woman who had promised to go on pilgrimage had died before she could keep that promise. The woman came to haunt her daughter, who sought advice from the parish priest. The priest told the girl: "When you have made the pilgrimage, your mother will come back to thank you. Make sure you have a cloth in your hands, because she will give you her hand". When the daughter was at the chapel, the ghost of her mother appeared and burned her hand into the cloth.
159761: A woman who worked for a farmer always left at exactly the same time in the afternoon. One day she was followed by a farmhand. He saw the woman disappear into a cornfield, where a little wax doll in the shape of a child lay. The woman sat down by the doll and stuck pins into it. At that moment, somewhere nearby, a child was tormented with terrible pain.
159774: When people could not make butter, they went to the abbey to fight the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). The friar would then give the people something and say prayers.
159779: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who had no name because they had not been baptised.
159791: Some people went to the shop on the day before Christmas to buy cakes. Suddenly they heard bells ringing in the marsh and saw a light. The people were terrified.
159833: A woman suffered greatly from the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). Cows died and the pigs and chickens fell ill. That woman usually went to the friars to have the animals blessed.
159884: If you had beckoned to a will-o'-the-wisp, you had to run inside quickly. Otherwise that person's neck was wrung and the next day a skull was found on the door. Will-o'-the-wisps were unbaptised children. Such lights appeared mainly near marshes.
159918: A young fellow lying in his bed always heard the sheets creaking. The parish priest could not help the boy, so he had to go to the monastery. It was haunting.
159930: A seventeen-year-old boy going to the shop saw a black cat jump between his legs in the street, so that he tripped. He got up and wanted to kick the cat, but he could not. Suddenly the cat was gone and he could go on. About fifty metres further on, however, the animal was there again. The cat jumped up at him. At that moment he saw that he was standing in front of a house whose occupant was suspected of being a witch. Frightened, he went home.
159932: A woman had gone to buy a cow near Leuven. The dealer, a woman, had given her a cup of coffee with two sugar lumps. The woman drank the coffee but left the sugar. After the woman had brought the cow home, she always heard noise at night. The noise began at ten o'clock and lasted until after midnight. Although the cow was tied up, it was always untied again. The doors flew open and a grey cat came in. That cat was the witch. Beyond the threshold the cat could no longer be seen. In the end the people sent for a priest from Brussels. The clergyman prayed until the drops of sweat rolled down his face.
159937: A little child tossing about in its cot always saw something on the wall and would then cry: "Look there, look there!" The child was bewitched and eventually died of the witchcraft.
159941: In autumn, a woman was walking in Nijlen near the house of a witch. In the distance the woman saw the witch walking. The witch picked up a green leaf from a Canadian poplar and said: "You are far behind, aren't you?" The woman did not answer.
159943: A man whose two sons were seriously ill went to the friars for advice. "We will give you a relic," said the friars, "for one of your children will die." When the man came home, one of his sons was already dead. Because the other boy's condition kept getting worse, the man went to the friars again. "If the woman who has the reputation of being a witch keeps coming, the other boy will die too. You must put the relic under the door, so that the witch cannot get in." The next morning the witch indeed could not get in. Three days later the sick boy had fully recovered.
159959: In Berlaar lived a man who always closed the drain hole for the water against the cold. Yet every morning the hole was open. One evening the man kept watch by the drain hole. At a certain moment he heard a cat scratching. The man chopped off one of the cat's paws. The next day his wife lay injured in bed. She had lost an arm.
159972: A man was accompanied by a zwarte madam (black lady) along the Hoge Weg as far as the Leeg Eind in Stabroek. The apparition did not say a word. Other people had also seen the black lady there.
160015: A witch went into a house and stroked the head of the child lying in the cradle there. The child did not learn to walk until it was four years old. The child was taken to the friars to be blessed.
160038: A girl who had been in a relationship had died. After her death the girl came to haunt her parents, to whom she said: "Damn it, you ruined me." The girl was damned.
160050: The mother of schoolmaster M. was visiting a farmer who had a heifer. The witch said: "Oh, that is a fine heifer" and touched the animal. Since then the cow has never given milk again.
160077: If you wanted to know whether someone was a witch, you had to walk behind the suspected person, put your left foot in the print of her right foot and your right foot in the print of her left foot. If the person was a witch, she would then stop.
160089: A man worked for a miller who had a white cat. When the man went home, the cat sometimes followed close on his heels the whole way, which frightened him.
160116: On a farm worked a farmhand who had the reputation of being a real womaniser. When the farmhand came back from the café, he saw a young lady. He said: "Ha, sweetheart" and put his arm around the lady. But the farmhand's arm went right through the figure. Afterwards he went to lie on his bed and died.
160120: A man who was ridden by the mare got lost in a place he knew very well, on his way back from playing cards at his uncle's, who lived on the Bosberg. On his way home the man kept stumbling into a turnip field. The man went into a café, where he was told that he had probably been ridden by the mare.
160128: Several farmhands worked at 't Hooghuis. When those men had eaten well in the evening, they went home. However, they had difficulty getting home, because three large black dogs always jumped at their feet, so that they could hardly take a step. Although the men ate well, they became as thin as rakes.
160136: A girl was going out with the son of a witch. The witch wanted her son to keep living at home for a while because he earned money. The boy gave his mother money for a calf, but that was not enough. When one day around All Saints' the boy was walking through the fields with his girlfriend, the girl suddenly heard a noise in the oak wood. The boy went to look. The next moment the girl saw the boy's mother standing beside her with a neckerchief. The girl said: "Oh God, oh God, it's your mother". When the boy came out of the wood, his mother had vanished. The girl threatened to end the relationship because she was afraid of the witch. When the lovers had stood under an elder tree for less than five minutes, three kittens came out of the wood. Later the boy's sister said that her mother was a real witch. When her chest was broken open, a doll full of pins was found, which was used to torment the children. The woman was known in Nijlen as a witch. Once, after she had been at a farm, the calf and the goats fell ill the following night. The farmer's wife went to the Poor Clares, where she was given a relic. Some time later the witch caused a little boy on that farm to die. When a girl was born after that, that child fell ill too. The mother had the witch come to undo the harm. The witch bent over the child and made some strange movements. Then she told the mother to pray part of a rosary. The next day, after noon, the misfortune would be over. The next day the girl was indeed cured. Whenever the witch later gave the children something, they fell ill. The mother also had to block up the drain hole because it was always full of cats. The mother had also once hit the witch with an umbrella when she appeared in the shape of a cat.
160146: Black cats were witches. If you kicked at them in the evening, they took revenge. They went to the keyhole of a house and blew evil inside through it.
160147: A boy was in a relationship with a girl whose friend was the daughter of a woman who practised the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). The boy wanted nothing to do with the witch's daughter. One day the witch's daughter said to her friend: "May I still come and visit you when you are married?" "Of course you may," the girl answered. When the two were married, the witch's daughter often came to visit. She would give the married woman a pat on the shoulder and bring her smoked meat. One day the woman had put that meat in the soup. Shortly afterwards the woman and her mother-in-law, who had both eaten the soup, were deathly ill. The husband, who had not eaten the soup, was not ill.
160153: A mother went to fetch the doctor for her sick child. On the way the woman tripped over a werewolf lying on the ground there. Because of this the woman never reached the doctor. By day one could get the better of a werewolf, but at night the victims were jumped on by the werewolf and had to carry the beast.
160173: A woman would suddenly fall down while standing in her house. When the parish priest freed her from the witchcraft, he sweated terribly.
160182: A man who was drinking somewhere was told by someone: "You won't get into your house tonight." "We'll see about that," said the man, but the sorcerer was proved right.
160185: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children who came back to earth.
160226: A family from Bornem was often visited by a woman with a bad name. No sooner had the woman left than the doors flew open and broke apart. The dog broke loose and began to bark. When the people went outside, the doors were whole again and the dog was lying in front of its kennel once more.
160238: A mother had seven daughters, all of whom died but one. The daughter who survived had a disability. A woman always came into that house, stroked the girls and said: "Oh, what a lovely child!"
160263: Some friends coming back from Diest went into an inn whose landlady was said to be a witch. When the men had had a few glasses and wanted to leave, the landlady said: "Come on, stay a little longer, you have plenty of time!" When the men left anyway, she said: "You will get lost." The men did indeed get lost on a road they knew like the back of their hand. They kept wandering about until the next morning.
160279: A witch put a hen on her lap and stroked its back until it lay down. Then the witch said: "Over hedge and over hedgerow and into the wine cellar in Cologne". Then she left.
160404: In Wilmarsdonk a returning dead person appeared every night at twelve o'clock.
160423: A man who was married to a woman with a bad name had a sick horse. When the horse lay dying, a cat sat on a beam in the barn. The cat stayed there until the horse was dead. Then it came out of the barn.
160451: A farmer was visited by a man peddling rat poison. The farmer did not want to buy anything and said he had no rats. The peddler replied: "You'll see rats yet!" Eight days later the farm was swarming with rats. The farmer was convinced that a sorcerer had come peddling at his door.
160467: A woman often came to visit a family. One day, when the mother wanted to feed the child, the child began to cry and would not eat. The child also stopped sleeping and grew very thin. The mother took the child to a friar, who blessed it. As the mother was going home, her child was already asking for a slice of bread.
160475: A man was led to the water by a will-o'-the-wisp. The man said: "I baptise you". Because the man had added "Amen", a little later he was overwhelmed by lights. The next time the man said: "I baptise you alone and no other. Without this and without that the baptism will be of no value." and he made the sign of the cross. Because of this the will-o'-the-wisps left the man alone.
160521: A few men who had played some cards after a meeting finally set off for home. One of those men went off alone and got lost. The man wandered around all night and at five o'clock in the morning he was back at the inn he had left. That man had been ridden by the mare and so kept ending up at the same spot.
160529: In a family in Borgerhout, the youngest child was deathly ill. The child always moaned at night and the doctors could not help it. One day the mother went to the friars, who advised her to burn all the child's clothes. The friar also said: "When you go home, you will see an old woman on the bridge. You must not speak to her, and you must not answer if she asks you anything." The mother followed the advice and remembered that the old woman who had stood on the bridge had given her a little cap for her child. When the cap had been burned, the child was cured.
160543: At the Kroon on the old Bevelse Steenweg it was haunted. Butter could not be churned there. The cows rattled their chains.
160558: Fien did not like it that two men were in love with her daughters. When the men left the café where Fien worked one evening, the woman saw to it that they got no further than the grotto in Deurne, where they fell asleep.
160574: A man lying in hospital saw that the boy in the next bed was visited by a woman who had brought biscuits. After the woman left, the man said: "Don't eat the biscuits, because I know that woman. She is a witch." The boy laughed, but half an hour after eating the biscuits he was dying of stomach pain. The boy needed many injections to recover.
160614: The ghost of a dead person haunted the bridge of the abbey of Tongerlo. The ghost never said a word. People were so afraid of it that they no longer dared to go to confession at the abbey of Tongerlo in the morning.
160624: A boy was coming back at night from visiting his girlfriend, who lived near the station. On the way the boy was followed the whole time by a woman carrying two large bundles. At a house the woman struck the bundles together. Then smoke appeared and the woman vanished. The same thing happened every Thursday.
160635: A farmer whose farm was bewitched found maggots in the hens' eggs. The woman who caused it always walked about in the evening.
160689: A mason who never went to church had promised to have a mass said for his deceased relatives. He still had not kept his promise when one day he drove past the churchyard with his horse and cart. Suddenly something heavy jumped onto the cart, making the horses rear. The tormenting spirit laughed loudly and sat down beside the mason. The mason grew frightened and began to sweat terribly. Another time, when the mason passed that churchyard again, the same thing happened. In the end he had the mass said after all and was no longer troubled by the spirit.
160708: A farmhand who came home drunk and cursing every Sunday evening saw one evening a large black dog coming towards him on its hind legs. The dog put its front paws on the drunkard's shoulders and walked with him as far as the farm. After that the farmhand never cursed again. People said the dog had been the devil.
160720: A miller who saw a farmer go by with a wheelbarrow said to a customer who was with him: "Yes, that little farmer keeps working away bravely. I'll make him dance a polka around his wheelbarrow." The miller whistled and the farmer began to dance. Another time the miller also bewitched a woman so that she was stuck all night on the spot where she had to guard the washing.
160733: A man was riding his horse to the vet. On the way the animal suddenly refused to go on and began to sweat. The man put his horse inside somewhere and went to fetch a medal. Then the horse continued on its way.
