160738: In Heffen lived a child who had been bewitched by an old woman and could not get better. The child was taken to the friars, but it was already too late, for the child died. The friars had given the people a medal to put under the threshold. When the woman came to visit again after that, she could not get in.
160739: A beekeeper whose bees all lost their way and flew off believed that the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) was in his beehive, and went to the friars of Herentals. They advised him to walk around his garden and pray the Gospel of Saint John while the bees were flying about. The beekeeper did so and was freed of his problems.
160747: A woman who peddled fish lived near a witch. When that woman went to the market in the morning, she was often plagued by the witch. The woman could then go no further and had to stand still until the spell wore off. Sometimes the peddler's daughter went to the market with her mother. When the mother called: "Are you riding along?", the daughter had to answer: "Let's go." If she said "yes" or "no", she would be bewitched.
160755: In Genebos (Kwaadmechelen) lived a carpenter whose son consorted with the devil. In the evening the carpenter always heard a hellish noise in the house. After a while the son would get up and say: "Go to sleep, father, it's over now."
160758: A farmer had a lot of bad luck with the animals in his stable. A witch from the neighbourhood was the cause. One day the man managed to shoot at the witch in the stable. The next day the neighbour woman wore a bandage around her arm.
160762: On a farm in Varendonk the cows in the cowshed were all untied.
160772: On a farm in Woensdrecht there were four horses. Whenever there was work to be done, nothing could be done with those horses. Someone came to keep watch over the horses. Between midnight and one o'clock the animals were sometimes dancing in the stable. The parish priest came and established that the trouble was caused by three women from the neighbourhood.
160783: People who were ridden by the mare at night had a standstill of the blood. The mare was a big beast that flew onto them at night. In the morning the mare's victims were tired and sweaty.
160804: In Arendonk lived a child who always cried because it had severe stomach pain. The people went to the friars of Bornem, who gave them a relic to put under the blanket. The people were also advised to look inside the child's pillow. When they did, they found a good hundred pins in it.
160809: A man coming back from B. in heavy rain and storm saw on the way the ghost that his neighbour D. always claimed to have seen.
160875: A house in Geel was badly haunted. Sometimes it was so bad that in the morning the house was empty and all the furniture stood on top of the roof. People had the greatest trouble getting the furniture down again.
160883: A fat man from Bevel who always drove a dog cart went to the calf market in Lier one day. Although the man was sober, he lost his way that night and had to go and knock on a door somewhere. Someone took the man as far as the mill, where he saw a woman pass by who said: "And you're still not on the right road." That woman was a witch who had made the man lose his way.
160889: A woman had a great deal of misfortune. She could not make butter and got no good milk from her cows. The woman went to the friars of Tongerlo, who advised her to put her wedding ring under the butter churn. After that the woman had no more problems, but her ring had disappeared.
160904: On his nightly walks a man was always followed by a black cat that walked with him as far as the door. One day the man gave the cat a sound thrashing with a stick. The next day a man who had been beaten black and blue was walking around the village. He was a wizard.
160909: Near the Moerkes, a large deep pool, many will-o'-the-wisps were seen. Those lights could not enter hell, heaven or purgatory.
160970: Near Hove lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. After that woman had given something to a little child, the child died a short time later.
160975: A statue of Mary is said to have once been dug up in the Wijngaardbos in Veerle. When the people wanted to take the statue to Averbode, at a certain spot they could go no further.
160984: At the Bremkapel in Putte it was haunted. At night a folded sheet always appeared there and spread itself out on the ground. After a while the sheet folded itself up again and disappeared.
161015: On a farm in Niel they could not keep a single farmhand. A farmer who was a friend felt sorry for the unlucky farmer and sent his farmhand to that farm to help out. When the farmhand slept there the first night, he was ridden by the mare just like the other farmhands. The next day the farmhand had the farmer's wife sharpen his knife. When he went to bed that evening, he held the knife on his stomach with the blade pointing up. The farmhand did hear a rustling on the roof, but the mare left him alone. Still, the farmhand kept the knife with him for another two weeks.
161072: At the Braekmanshoeve in Walem all the gates opened at midnight. Then a cart with two horses drove through the stable. The cart was driven by a coachman with goat's legs. The next morning two calves were stuck in one halter.
161080: In Westerlo people sometimes saw a glowing tree stump flying through the air. That was Count de Merode, who came to haunt because he had unlawfully seized property.
161095: A man was accompanied by a black cat on his way home in the evening. The cat knew the way to the man's house, went inside with him and lay down in his bed. The next morning the cat had disappeared.
161137: When Hein T. was going home, he was followed on the heath by a large hare. After the man struck at the animal with his walking stick, suddenly so many hares appeared that he had to run quickly to a hut to get to safety.
161142: A man told in an inn that he had seen a witch who had turned herself into a black cat. The cat kept coming to torment the man. In the evening the man and his father kept watch with a gun. In this way they managed to shoot the cat dead. The dead animal was buried in a pit two metres deep. The next day, however, the cat had vanished from the pit, and that same evening the animal was there again, alive and well. They shot the cat again and buried it again. But this time too it came back. Only when they had shot and buried the cat for the third time did it stay away.
161151: Some men always saw a black cat following them at 't Einde. One of the men wanted to kick the animal, but his friends advised him against it. The day after such an incident the man always met a woman who knew exactly what time he had gone home.
161155: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field flew around with the post after his death in the form of a will-o'-the-wisp. The ghost kept asking: "What should I do with this post?" One day someone answered: "Put it back where you got it".
161200: A strong woman who could work hard was unable to get to church. When the woman was halfway there, she was forced, as it were, to turn back. That woman's two daughters died of an unknown illness. One day a man came to visit who made the sorceress who had caused the harm appear at the gate.
161234: In the old days people often told of those who had been ridden by the moon.
161236: A family who always received strawberries from a neighbour had a sick child. They went to the friars for the child, who advised them not to accept any more strawberries in future.
161263: Some people always saw a cat running in front of their feet in the morning on the road to work. It got so bad that after a while the people no longer dared to walk that road. The cat was a witch.
161268: A man looking for shelter decided to spend the night in a haunted castle. At one o'clock in the night the man heard chains rattling. He lay down on the floor and pretended to be dead. A little later a ghost came in and began counting gold coins on the table. Afterwards the man kept the treasure for himself.
161302: A bewitched boy was ill for a long time. People went to the friars on the boy's behalf. The clergymen told them who had bewitched the boy.
161305: Near the Sint-Janskerk it was always haunted. Once a man saw two cups dancing in a corner there. When the man came closer, the cups flew upwards. The man ran away in fear and was chased by a figure, while he heard the sound of horses' hooves. The man took to his heels. Only at the gate of his house did he see that the figure behind him had vanished.
161330: On a farm struck by the zwarte hand (the black hand, witchcraft), the chains began to rattle at midnight. A storm wind rose, but when people went to look, nothing more could be heard. In the morning the animals lay there dead.
161391: A seven-year-old child suddenly could no longer walk. The family sold a bull, but the animal suddenly fell ill. The father went to a man in Waver, who said: "Just have the bull slaughtered, for nothing more can be done about it. Take a good look, the spleen will surely be black." The farmer also had a heifer that was about to calve and was advised to go to the friars of Bornem immediately after the calving. The farmer did so, but he was too late; the heifer calved before he had reached Bornem. The heifer gave not a drop of milk and was therefore sold. But with its new owner the animal gave no milk either. The farmer bought pigs. Three months later the animals were smaller than they had been when they were bought. After the farmer had been to Bornem, he had to do a penance and the pigs grew fat. The farmer believed that the harm had been done to him by a certain woman.
161411: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who came back.
161420: A man walking in Hove was accompanied by a black dog. The man could not get rid of the dog and finally sat down on the toilet. The man had to stay sitting on the toilet all night. Only the next morning could he leave and he saw that the dog had disappeared.
161443: In Retie there once lived a man who consorted with the devil. When that man knocked under the table with his hand, he could fill the whole table with mice. When he ran out of money, he took off his boot and coins came rolling out. That man was very tall and had eyes like a horse's.
161481: In Burcht stood a large farm that was haunted. The well-to-do occupants had to move out because of the haunting. At midnight the cowsheds, pigsties and henhouse were turned upside down. The animals made a lot of noise and tried to break loose. The stable lanterns were lit and everything flew out of the cupboards without anything breaking. Nobody dared to go near that house. The farm therefore stood empty for a long time.
161488: A farmer driving to the field with horse and cart beckoned to a will-o'-the-wisp against his better judgement. The next moment a hundred thousand lights came flying up. After a long time the farmer nevertheless reached the water to baptise the lights.
161539: A man claimed that you must never kick a cat in an alley at night. According to him, most evildoers changed themselves into cats.
161552: On the Battelse steenweg there once lived a woman who did people harm. If you walked past the woman's door at midnight, you could see her sitting on her doorstep. She never visited her neighbours, but always walked past their houses. One morning a mother was washing her little child when the woman came to visit her. Because the mother had taken off the child's relic, the woman had power over the little one. The sorceress stayed until the child had been washed. After that the child grew steadily worse until it finally died.
161554: A mother went to the friars of Tongerlo because her little daughter would not grow. A friar showed the woman a bottle and said: "Here is the witch who is doing this to you." It was an old woman from the heath who often came to visit those people. A relic had to be put under the door, so that the old woman could no longer get in. After that the child became healthy.
161566: A woman who could not keep any children alive sent for the midwife because she was about to give birth again. The midwife went to the wrong house and entered the neighbour's. There she saw that the neighbour, who was known as a witch, was playing with a doll. The child died.
161570: When an unbaptised child had died, a will-o'-the-wisp was seen floating around. That light only disappeared once it was released.
161593: On a bewitched farm in Ginderbroek the man saw a big black cat with eyes like lamps every night. He struck at the animal and heard the next day that a neighbour woman was in bed because she had lost an ear.
161611: On a farm the farmer had a great deal of misfortune. A calf that had been born healthy died five minutes after its birth. It was the farmer's aunt who caused this misfortune.
161614: A man who lived on the Blauberg had bought a heifer. When the animal was about to calve, his sister knew it, although she lived a long way off. The sister owned a little wax doll into which she stuck pins. The man's children fell ill.
161639: The son of the farmer at 't Rinkven had to join the army. The farmer offered the farmhand money on condition that he become a soldier in his son's place. When the farmhand came back from the army and asked for his money, the farmer and his son beat him to death. The farmhand was buried in the stable under the horse's feeding trough. Whenever a horse was later put there, the animal was dead within a few days. Karel S., who later came to live there, heard wonderfully beautiful music in the stable at night once a year.
161652: A man who was out with some friends said to the group: "Here is my red handkerchief". A little later the others met a beast and threw the handkerchief. When the man came back, he still had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
161654: A farm was often visited by a woman. As soon as the cows heard that woman, they began to low and rattle their chains. When a cow had calved, the animal did not even give half a litre of milk. On the farm butter could no longer be made either. The people were advised to keep the visitor out from then on, but she kept coming. A child was born on the farm, and a few days later it had a large lump on its head. The child was taken to the Poor Clares in Antwerp to be blessed. People also went to the abbey of Postel to fight the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) on the farm. A friar gave the farmer something to put under the front door. After that the visitor never came by again and there was no more misfortune on the farm.
161676: In Rijmenam people saw the ghosts of the dead standing in the churchyard at midnight.
161682: A mother saw how a woman always laid her hand on the head or shoulder of her little daughter. That girl had health problems. The mother took her daughter to the friars of the Kluis, who advised the child to hit the witch on the head whenever she had received a pat on the shoulder from her. One always had to strike higher than the witch. Sometimes the girl was also given an apple with a little spot on it. When she ate that apple, she had to vomit a short time later. The friars forbade the girl to eat anything else she had received from the witch.
161685: One evening two men went to fetch an axe they had left at work. When the two men came back, one of them felt something at his heels the whole time. A little later the man felt a shove in his back. He turned around, but saw nothing. A while later the same thing happened and the man lashed out with his axe, after which a calf began to low, although again nothing could be seen. The men walked home in fear. They had barely got inside when they heard a tremendous blow on the door. Outside stood a calf with a split lip, which disappeared the next moment.
161699: When Sus was cycling to the monastery of Tongerlo, he was nearly frightened to death because a cat had jumped in front of his wheel. Sus could hardly go on because his bicycle was completely surrounded by witches. At the bridge Sus suddenly felt something heavy on his back. As soon as Sus reached 't Hof, everything returned to normal.
161727: A farmer who had forgotten his seed tray in the field sent his maid to fetch it. The maid saw a little man sitting on the seed tray. When the maid had pulled off the little man's shirt, the creature said: "Yes, that will be your penance". All day long the maid heard someone calling: "Give me back my little shirt!" The girl's parents had once promised to do a penance, but they had not fulfilled their promise.
161728: A woman from Hoevenen had been asked to be godmother to a child. On her way to the church, which stood in a remote spot because the village had been rebuilt higher up after a flood, the woman heard owls calling. The woman ended up in bed, gravely ill. She did not become the child's godmother because she was ill and because the owl's call might mean bad luck.
161771: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised stillborn children.
161787: A girl was seriously ill. In the girl's room there was a mantelpiece on which lay a little ball of yarn. One day someone picked up the ball and unwound it completely. The girl was cured on the spot. A neighbour was suspected of having made the girl ill.
161820: In Vorst lived a girl who had become seriously ill after coming into contact with a dog. Because of the girl's illness, a man from the neighbourhood could no longer make butter. The man went with a friend to the abbey of Tongerlo. When the men had explained the problem to a friar, the clergyman said: "Go home now. When you get home, you will see that your wife has managed to make butter." And so it was; the friar had neutralised the power of the witches.
161828: In a family with a bewitched child, the victim of the witchcraft flew up to the ceiling three times every evening at the same hour. Strangely enough, the child was never hurt. The parents went to the friars on the child's behalf.
161862: When Father V. from Vorst had to flee the monastery, he took up lodging in the attic room of an old house, where he said mass. After his death the Father came back to point out the pot he had once buried.
161872: A young man was courting one of a farmer's three daughters. One evening, as he walked to his sweetheart's farm with a friend, he saw a strange object rolling along the ground beside him. The apparition could not be caught; it circled the big barn three times and then vanished. When the young man went inside, he sat by the Dutch fireplace. On the table stood a copper lamp with a flame burning in it. At a certain moment the flame in the lamp went out inexplicably. The young man and the girl crawled outside on hands and knees. Ten minutes later the girl's mother, who was already in bed, called: "Come on in!" When the two came in, the lamp was burning again as if it had never gone out. Around eleven o'clock the young man went home. On the way he saw a white apparition that frightened him. He took his clogs in his hand and ran home as fast as he could, tearing his trousers. His sweetheart's mother was a witch who caused ghostly happenings.
161879: If children accepted something from a witch, they were bewitched. The children then did not grow and fell ill.
161883: Bet H. went to do the washing at a farm. In the little room where Bet slept, knocking could always be heard at night. When Bet moved to another room, she heard the knocking there too. It was her dead husband coming to remind her that she had once promised to have a mass said for him. After Bet had the promised mass said, she heard the knocking no more.
161900: A man took a dark road and lost his way. When, after wandering for a long time, the man saw a cyclist coming, he stopped him and asked whether he was still in Turnhout. The cyclist answered that the man was already almost in Ravels and took the lost man home. The man had fallen victim to a witch.
161905: On a farm in Oppuurs there was a five-franc piece in the house. When that coin was put on the table, it fell through it without there being a hole in the table. The parish priest was sent for, and he chopped the table to pieces. With another table it no longer worked.
161939: A wizard could turn himself into a black cat. He would then sit on a low wall somewhere and frighten people.
161973: An eel seller was driving towards morning past a place where witches were feasting. The man quickly said: "Jesus, Mary", and the next moment the witches and their tent had vanished.
161986: A boy was binding the harvest into sheaves in the field. When he had bound one sheaf and set it against a pine tree, a witch came by and said: "And all of them like that." The next moment there were four sheaves bound.
161987: One night a man and his hand had to load sand for a construction company on the sandbanks in the Scheldt. The man had to wake the foreman and went through the pouring rain to the house. When he stood under the little porch roof, a white woman suddenly appeared before him, although the door of the house was still shut. Still badly shaken, the man then returned to the boat, where his hand said: "Now I'm glad you're here. There's been quite a rumbling and banging here!" The boatman looked around and to his great amazement saw a cap lying there that was completely dry despite the heavy rain.
162001: In a house people saw a black cat coming in through the drain hole for the water. They struck at the cat, but it always came back. One day they beat the cat to death. The next day an old woman lay dead in front of the door.
162007: A parish priest had gone to give someone the last rites. On his way home the priest was accosted by a man demanding money. The priest answered: "Wait here, I'll go and get it." The priest fixed the man to the ground by magic. At home the priest said to the altar boy: "Here are five francs. Take them to the man standing on the road and tell him he may go on." After that the man could leave.
162026: A man sometimes had fits because of a witch who lived a little further on.
162028: A man saw the gloeiende paap (glowing priest) at the edge of a wood in Gompel. The gloeiende paap was a dead man who had to haunt because he had stolen land.
162034: A man visiting a friend had to go in by the back door because a large black dog with striking eyes stood at the front door. The man told his friend about the dog. The friend then took a club and broke it on it. There was no one to be seen anywhere.
162049: A man went gathering wood behind the fort of Kessel, where he saw a frog jump in front of his feet. He struck at the frog but could not hit it. The next day the man met a neighbour woman, who said: "Fons, you stay out of my little wood, eh. Last night you went stealing wood there." The man answered: "Then you are that frog from last night."
162086: A man who often cursed met the devil on his way home; the devil had appeared in the shape of a large black dog and jumped onto the man's neck. The man had to carry the devil until he was home. There the dog jumped onto the roof. When the man was dead, a black gentleman kept walking back and forth in the corridor by the room.
162101: A cat that nobody could catch always came to K.'s place. One day someone had hit the cat. The next day there was a woman walking about who had lost an eye.
162161: In the old days, when someone was ill, the misfortune was often blamed on the evil hand and the parish priest was sent for. The priest read prayers over the victim or gave a blessed object to be laid under the threshold or hung up in the house.
162195: At the Patershoeve one morning the cows all stood with their right leg in the ring. All those rings had to be sawn through to free the animals.
162196: A witch could turn herself into a black cat. One day the witch's husband kicked that cat. Later he found his wife lying in bed with only one hand.
162251: During a violent storm a farmer had died by the Dijle in Mechelen. From then on the farmer's ghost always appeared when there was a storm. He rode over the dikes of the Dijle on a white horse in the form of a knight in a black cloak. If there was a breach in the dike, the ghost blew his horn and held back the water with his horse. The local people were thus always warned in time to fill the gap with sand. One day, during a storm, the farmers were celebrating. When they heard the sound of the horn, they said: "We don't need to go, the ghost will keep the breach closed." The ghost was angry because the farmers did not come. He let the meadows flood and never came back.
162252: At the 'binnenvijver' (inner pond) a headless horse walked around between midnight and one o'clock.
162261: A farmer who met a cat one evening kicked at the animal because it kept getting under his feet. Then he heard the cat say: "I'll get you yet." The cat jumped out of a tree and ran after the man. When the man got home, he saw the cat sitting at his door. For two weeks the animal prowled around that man's house.
162267: In Achter-Olen a brandende scheper (burning shepherd-like fiery ghost) who had moved a boundary post wandered about. "What must I do with it?" asked the fiery apparition, to which someone replied: "Carry it to where you took it from".
162305: A man came into a café on the market square and filled the floor with rats and mice by magic. After he spoke a magic formula, the animals went outside again.
162313: On a farm where the cow always miscarried, the farmer's wife went to the White Fathers in Lier. There she was given a relic for the bewitched cow.
162337: A church of the town of Ouden is said to have sunk in the Diepdal. At Christmas bells could still be heard ringing there, but only a few people dared to go and listen. The Romans are said to have stayed there long ago.
162346: In Herentals a man had loaded a cart full of straw. Suddenly the cart tipped over for no apparent reason. His wife, who was a witch, had caused it.
162360: On a farm in Geel-Bel there was always a black bird in the stable. One day the farmer struck the bird down with a red-hot poker. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had a burnt hand.
162362: A man had seen a ghost in the Zeept while he was lifting potatoes for a farmer. Another man was there too, who was not afraid. But when that other man heard the ghost's chain rattling, he also took to his heels.
162367: In Gammel there was a marsh of about four ares. In that marsh lay a bell that could be heard ringing every night at twelve o'clock.
162392: Witches changed themselves into black cats and held meetings at midnight on Klinkhamersbeek. That was a large grate at the start of the Kerkstraat.
162412: In an old people's home lived a woman from Postel who was said to be a witch. The mother superior always locked the door of her own room and took the key with her. One day, when the mother superior came into her room, she saw the witch lying in her bed.
162434: On a farm the animals, although they were all well tied up, walked out in a row one after another through the barred gate. They passed the house door and went through the kitchen, then returned to the stable. The next day exactly the same thing happened. The people had the animals' fodder blessed by the friars, after which the strange events came to an end.
162454: A ghost in a white shirt always haunted the churchyard. In café 'Rome' near the church, a man claimed he was not afraid of the ghost. The man went to the churchyard and pulled the shirt off the ghost. When the man was back home, the ghost stood by his bed. The ghost told the man that he had to return the shirt at the same place; otherwise he would die. If the man took a child with him, nothing could happen. That night the man went to the churchyard with a child on his back to put the shirt back on the ghost. Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
162459: A witch turned herself into a toad and crept into a house through the drain hole for the water. One day the people cut off one of the toad's legs. The next day the witch wore a bandage around her arm.
162469: The gloeiende scheper (glowing fiery ghost) walked about in Zittert with a boundary post in his arms. One day a man had lit his cigar on the fiery apparition. The next moment the man had run off, saying: "I give myself up!" Meanwhile the sparks flew all around.
162494: There were three houses at the Notelaar in Hingene. One evening the occupant of one of those houses was coming home. When he was nearly home, the man saw a kitten walking around him and said: "Well, kitty, what are you doing here?" A moment later there were already two cats. The man said: "Now, kitties, watch out, I'll step on your tails." Then there were four cats, at which the man swore in fear: "Damn it, kitties, get out of the way." Again two more animals had joined. Eight cats walked in a circle around the man and began to dance. When the man asked why the cats had started dancing, the animals replied: "Peer asks us, kitties, why are you dancing? Peer, you're not at home, Peer, hurry on home."
162522: At the Meirhoeve the cows were extremely restless. The household was always visited by a neighbour who came to fetch something. The farmer's wife decided to go to the friars, who said: "She will not come in any more." After that the neighbour indeed never visited again, for a holy object had been placed under the door.
162525: In catechism class there was a boy who could conjure rats and mice. The boy said to the parish priest B.: "I can make that big iron gate open by throwing my cap at it." The boy managed it three times, but after that it no longer worked.
162547: At the Diepdal a bell of a sunken church could be heard ringing at night. The Diepdal had the shape of a church.
162554: A woman from Herenthout had a twenty-year-old son who lay ill in bed. The witch who had made the boy ill could not cure him before sunrise. In the end the boy died.
162570: On a farm in Lichtaart people always saw a big mouse running through the house. One day the farmer's son threw a clog at the mouse, breaking the animal's leg. The next day the boy's grandmother lay in bed with a broken leg.
162584: In the Hellevonder lay a bell that rang at midnight at Christmas. A bell could then also be heard ringing at 'In de drie gezusters' near the Mark.
162644: On a farm the animals were found untied in the mornings and made a lot of noise. It even happened that the animals' ears were pulled off. A sorceress lived near that farm. The friars of Dendermonde came and put an end to the strange events.
162647: A woman coming back from early Mass saw a light come out of the marsh near the Rijmenam market. The woman released the light by baptising it. Such lights were the lost souls of unbaptised children.
162692: A man who had been to the fair in Berendrecht came home at about half past eleven. Strangely, the man simply walked past his house. At five in the morning he had ended up in a ploughed field. In the distance he saw a little light and walked towards it. On the way the man had seen a little woman to whom he had said: "Good evening," but the little woman had not answered.
162703: In the evenings a few men often visited an unmarried woman and sat telling stories around the peat fire. One evening one of the men said: "Shall we curse until the devil comes?" and the men suited the action to the word. At the stroke of twelve a large black dog was suddenly sitting beside the men, though no one had seen it come in. The men no longer dared to go home and slept on the hayloft in the barn. The black dog followed the men and lay down under the ladder to the loft. Because of this the men no longer dared to come down. The next day the dog was gone. After that those men never dared to call on the devil again.
162711: On Veerle Heide stood a farmstead where there was always noise at midnight and where a striking number of cows died. When de Witte was playing cards one evening, he heard a sound outside. The man went to look and threw something at a cat sitting there meowing. The next day a woman was walking around with a wound on her head.
162729: A woman saw her dead father appear every evening at about the same time. The ghost would put its head through the window, sigh and then disappear again. The parish priest advised the woman to ask the ghost what it wanted the next time. When the ghost appeared that evening, the daughter asked: "Father, what do you want?", to which the ghost replied: "You must go on pilgrimage to Duffel, Scherpenheuvel and Leuven". On the day the woman got into the cart to go on pilgrimage, her father's ghost blocked the road. The daughter then said: "Dad, go away, I am going on pilgrimage". The ghost replied: "Thank God, now I am saved. I once made promises, but I did not fulfil them. Now you will do it in my place". After the woman had been on pilgrimage three times, the ghost appeared no more.
162760: In Stelen the sexton wanted to know how many witches there were. He put a piece of the Easter candle under the church door. After Mass everyone went outside except three women who could not get up from their chairs. That is how people found out who the witches in Stelen were.
162787: In Voortkapel-Westerlo lived a woman who could send lice and fleas in procession to the abbey of Tongerlo. At the stroke of twelve the vermin could be seen passing the seven lanes.
162805: Someone struck at a cat that always came to sit in front of the drain hole for the water. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had a hole in her head.
162811: A farmhand worked at the Patershoeve. When he had to go and feed the horse, the door shut behind him by itself, although there was no wind. Though the door was not locked, the farmhand could not open it again. People heard him banging on the door and came to free him. That farm was haunted.
162855: A drunkard was walking at night along a narrow lane from Sint-Job to Wezel when he was followed by a black cat. The man was annoyed by the cat and shouted: "Clear off, or I'll give you a kick!" The cat replied: "You just try that." The drunkard then took off his clogs and ran home as fast as he could. He never went along that lane in the evening again.
162880: The werewolf was someone who disguised himself as a wolf with a skin to frighten people. The werewolf could only be seen in the evening and at night. A girl who was coming back at night from the fair, where she had been with her boyfriend, met the werewolf. The beast leapt at her and tore a piece out of her clothes. The next day the girl found that her fiancé had the fibres of her clothes between his teeth.
162890: A witch who peddled wool often gave the children sweets. If the children accepted the sweets, they were bewitched.
162905: A parish priest found it strange that a light always burned in the church at night. When the priest went to look one night, he found a ghostly priest in the church saying mass. "What are you doing here?" the priest asked the ghost. The ghost was the spirit of a priest who had promised to say a number of masses and had not fulfilled that promise. The priest offered to say the promised masses in the ghost's place. That released the spirit.
162918: In a house a knocking on the back door was always heard in the evening.
162933: In the devil's barn there was a hole that could not be closed. The next day the masonry always fell out again.
162949: In Retie lived a wizard who could turn himself into a cat. Once, when the wizard was coming home with a friend, he said: "Don't be startled". A moment later the friend saw a cat walking beside him instead of a man. Shortly after, the cat sprang away and the wizard reappeared from behind a bush.
162955: A witch whom people greatly feared was said to have lived in Hulshout. That witch appeared sometimes in the shape of a cat, sometimes in that of a human.
162992: A man went with a friend to steal apples at night. First the two came to a pear tree. They could not find a single pear there, although they had seen during the day that the tree was full of big fruit. A little further on, a woman in a white hood stood under the apple tree. The men reached for the apples but could not get hold of a single fruit. When a little later the cap of one of the men flew off, the two ran away. That night the men had been bewitched by the woman standing under the tree, who had kept an eye on them the whole time. The next day the men went back to that spot. They found that the pear tree and the apple tree were full of fruit. The cap was also still lying under the tree.
163012: A miller who had not been able to work much for a while went to his mill because a strong wind had suddenly risen. When the miller saw a black cat coming towards him, he kicked the animal. But the cat kept coming back until the man hit its leg with a piece of wood. When he got home, the man saw his wife lying in bed with a broken arm.
163042: A man was always chased by a black dog when he came back from visiting his girlfriend in Hulshout.
163050: A man went to Herentals with two horses and a load of porcelain for three days. In Herentals lived a man who had studied for the priesthood for eight years and wanted to open a shop. The former seminarian asked the man all sorts of things, but in the end the man lost his patience and refused to answer any more questions. The next day the man's cart was very lightly loaded. Nevertheless the horses reared up, so the man had to get off the cart. Further on the same thing happened again. Only when he had made the sign of the cross over the horses and himself did everything return to normal. Later the man was visited by someone wearing a bowler hat.
163061: A woman who was never in her bed at night was accused by her husband of being a witch. One day in that house someone chopped a leg off a spider. The next day the woman lay in bed. She had lost an arm.
163076: A mother had a son who had a fever every day, although he was not ill. The father believed the old neighbour woman was a witch. The mother put a medal under the doormat. After that the neighbour, who used to come every day to hang up her washing at their house, no longer set foot inside. She never came back, and the boy never had a fever again.
163086: A man had become bewitched after accepting berries from a witch. He had to pray for seven days. On the seventh day all his windows and doors were open without him having touched anything. On the stairs a noise was heard as if a hundred people were walking.
163094: Wieze saw the ghost of his dead grandfather appear on the anniversary of his death. The grandfather appeared in the field, exactly on the spot where he had dropped dead, and said to Wieze: "You shouldn't keep working. Go on home, there's no point any more today."
163108: A mother was often visited by a woman who had thrown her own newborn child into the Netedijk. Once that woman had held the mother's baby, the child cried every night afterwards. The mother went to the friars of the Kluis, who said there was nothing wrong with the child and gave her a holy object. When the woman came by again, she could not get in and said: "May I hold your baby once more? I won't do anything to it any more."
163178:
So many witches lived in Walem that they could dance hand in hand around the church every night. No villager dared go and look. The brown friars of Mechelen were often visited by farmers from Walem who did not know what to do about the witchcraft. The farmers could not help themselves with anything, not even the prayer of Emperor Charles, the Seven Ells prayer, blessed candles or the Gospel of Saint John. Many unknown witches lived in Walem who secretly made sure the cows gave no milk or that the children were tormented at night. Some women were known to be witches. On one farm the witches came and stood by the children's beds at night and made them cry, or they wrung the necks of the cows in the stable.
A woman who could bear it no longer went to the parish priest of Sint-Katelijne. The priest claimed that witches did not exist, which made the woman angry. For she was regularly visited by a witch who came to ask now for a butter spatula, now for a handful of salt. Giving salt to a witch was the most dangerous thing one could do. Every time the cows in the meadow saw the witch, they bolted. In the end the woman went to the Franciscans in Mechelen, who gave her medals to lay under the threshold.
163200: Will-o'-the-wisps were spirits that floated about. Sometimes it was also said that a will-o'-the-wisp was the soul of someone who had come out of his pit (grave?).
163216: A witch went to the neighbours to see a newborn baby. She stroked the baby along its whole length in one movement. The little boy remained a feeble cripple all his life. His arms and legs had grown completely crooked.
163236: On the heath near the Dutch border many poachers caught rabbits at night. One evening a poacher did not manage to shoot a single rabbit, although many animals were about. The man took a piece of Easter candle from his pocket and rubbed the barrel of his gun with it. After that he was able to shoot a rabbit almost at once. When he went to fetch the rabbit from the hedge, he saw a woman there straightening her cap. The next day the man walked past that woman's house. She asked: "Did you shoot a lot yesterday?", to which the man replied: "No, but since you ask, it must surely be you I saw last night."
163239: A man who had bought a cow met someone on the Navelsberg who asked to have a look at the cow. Shortly afterwards the cow fell ill. Because the man had not thought to push the cow backwards into the stable, the animal was still in the power of evil. When the man had held a novena, he saw the power leave the stable on the ninth day. At that spot a black stain could be seen on the wall.
163255: In the Molenstraat in Lichtaart lived a man who could not sleep a wink at night because he was pricked by pins in his bed. However hard the man searched, no pin was to be found. A friend of his wanted to try sleeping in that bed, but exactly the same happened to him. People began to believe that witchcraft was involved and suspected a neighbour. When that woman was no longer let in for a while, the witchcraft came to an end.
163273: A sorcerer went along with some men to the meadow. He struck a sod of grass and the next moment mice were running everywhere.
163303: After the fair in Wintham, a man was walking home along the Polderdamdreef. In the middle of the lane he saw a horse coming towards him. When the man drew his knife to stab the horse, the animal suddenly became twice as big, and the man dropped his knife in fright. The man started to run, but the horse ran along with him. When he reached the farm where he worked as a farmhand, he saw that the farmer was not yet back from the fair, so he could not get in. So the man crept into the orchard and lay down there. But the horse lay down beside him. A long while later the farmhand did get into the house. But he had suffered so much fear that he died that same night.
163318: A farmer coming back late one evening from a visit to his son or daughter saw on the way a will-o'-the-wisp that came to hover above the cart. Because the farmer had heard that such lights were the little souls of unbaptised children, he baptised the light. The next moment a thousand will-o'-the-wisps came and sat on the cart.
163327: If a child would not grow, it was believed to have been struck by the evil hand. A mother whose child suffered from 'the old man' went to Strombeek. There the child was blessed. When mother and child then went to the church, a horrible scream was heard, although no one saw anything.
163375: Some people going to Scherpenheuvel were followed by a cat all the way to Tongerlo. Someone advised them to leave the cat alone because it might be a witch.
163381: A woman who lived in an inn went to a mother who had just had a baby and said: "Oh! You have a lovely baby!" The woman was not a hundred metres away when the child fainted. The mother took the child to the doctor, who found that the child had become even sicker than it already was.
163403: Will-o'-the-wisps came up to people and burnt their hand into the door. That handprint could never be removed. Will-o'-the-wisps were little souls that were not allowed into heaven.
163412: Some men coming home late in the evening saw a herd of calves walking along the way, making a rattling noise behind them. The calves walked along with the men.
163426: A workman often arrived late at his work in Wezel and was then severely punished. When the workman set off in the morning, a black cat always ran in front of his feet, delaying him. On a colleague's advice the man kicked the cat one morning, and it flew a good two metres. But the cat came back. The man kicked the cat three times, saying in turn: "That's one, that's two, that's one." Had he said "That's three", he would have been lost. The man cut a stick of birch wood and carved a cross into it. With that stick he beat the cat. The next day he went to see a suspicious woman from the neighbourhood and found she had a head wound. "You must have come back from a bad trip yesterday?" asked the workman, to which the woman replied: "But I'll get you yet."
163449: In Geel lived a renegade priest who had become a freemason. One evening in an inn the freemason let himself be persuaded to literally 'tell tales from the confessional'. At that moment the doorbell rang. A man got up and went to look, but saw no one. A little later the same thing happened again, at which the men cursed in annoyance. When the bell rang for the third time, the former priest got up himself and went to look. The men heard an icy scream and just saw a band of strange creatures flying through the air with the renegade priest among them. A strong smell of sulphur hung in the air. The renegade priest was never seen again.
163495: At 't Verbrand Hof in Brecht there were haunted cellars. At night all kinds of beasts came out of those cellars. The woman who had lived there had been very wicked.
163523: A German fortune-teller from Bevel often spent time near a child, who fell ill because of it. The boy had been struck by the evil hand. The parents took the child to the friars of Dendermonde, who said: "You gave him something to drink. He will become seriously ill, but he will not die." They had to do penance and put a holy object between the floorboards. When that had been done, the witch could no longer get in.
163543:
On a farm there were six pigs that were growing well.
After a while, however, the pigs' heads became longer than their bodies. The sixth pig killed the fifth, the fifth the fourth, and so on, until only one pig was left. That pig fell ill and died. All this misfortune had been caused by a neighbour woman who was a witch.
163555: On a farm where the butter was always as green as spinach, the farmer went to the friars of Bornem. The friars asked whether a woman perhaps came to the farm. The farmer answered that someone often came to fetch sourdough for baking. The friar advised the farmer to keep that woman out, for she was the culprit, the friar claimed. The farmer followed the advice and had no more trouble with churning.
163585: At a farmer's place there were witches who pulled the cows up by their tails. Once the floor of the stable had been dug up and a wedding ring buried in the ground, nothing strange happened to the cows any more.
163607: In a little house lived a witch whose daughter always said: "I will be destroyed by it, and it is my own mother." The daughter died young. When the witch had to die, she was already very old. She suffered greatly and did not want to die. Later one of her granddaughters came to live in the witch's house. The granddaughter had three children who were always ill.
163616: A witch lived in Wommelgem. When that witch lay dying, a black cat sat on her windowsill. After the witch's death the cat had disappeared.
163627: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of children who had died without baptism and without God.
163657: A farmer had been playing cards in an inn between Klein-Gent and Meirhoeve. On the way home the farmer saw a glowing pulpit with a glowing priest appear on the heath. Terrified, the farmer knelt down and began to pray the Gospel of Saint John. When the farmer had made the last sign of the cross, the strange apparition had vanished. The farmer resolved never to play cards again. After the farmer had gone to confession with a friar in Herentals, the friar said: "You will never see that again." And so it was. The farmer never played cards again.
163674: Some men went out in Lier. One of them put a handkerchief in his trouser pocket there. At the farm in Vremde where that man was staying, a rumbling was heard in the stable at night. The man had to take the handkerchief back to put an end to the witchcraft.
163708: Count (de Merode) flew around in a glowing tree stump. The mayor and aldermen of Hulshout went to the village boundary and said: "Up to here it is ours." The count came no further.
163716: A man who was digging on the heath heard a bell ringing in the Moerkuil at midnight.
163726: On a farm people struck at a black cat that always appeared in the evening. But they could not hit the animal. A little later the cat had disappeared.
163742: A man walking home one evening felt he was being followed. He looked round and saw a black dog. The dog kept following him and grew bigger and bigger. When the man got home, the dog stayed standing in front of the door. By then the animal had become as big as a foal. The man took a gun and wanted to shoot, but the gun did not work. When the man went to bed, he heard the dog walking across the attic, but nobody dared go and look. The next morning the animal was gone.
163770: To learn sorcery, you had to read Duivels Geseling (Devil's Scourge). A sorcerer could make a person stand still.
163772: In Walem lived a thirty-five-year-old young man who claimed that a black cat always crept into his house through the water drain hole. He believed the cat was a witch and struck at it with his dung fork, but in vain. One day he blocked the drain hole so that the cat could no longer get out. Then he attacked the animal with the dung fork until it lay motionless. He took a shovel and threw the cat outside. When the cat hit the ground with a jolt, it came back to life. It jumped into the house of the neighbours, where a man lived who worked at the fair. The next day that man came outside with a bandage around his head.
163776: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in the marshes. They were witches or the souls of returned dead. You were not to beckon to will-o'-the-wisps, or else the lights came closer.
163809: A farmer had a horse that grew very thin. One day a farmhand came to the farmer wanting to work for him. The farmhand kept watch over the horse at night. He saw a beautiful grey foal appear there and took the animal to the smith. When the farmer called his wife for coffee and food the next morning, the farmer's wife could not get out of bed. She had horseshoes on her hands and feet.
163817: A man went along with a friend who was visiting his sweetheart. It was said that the girl's mother was a witch. While the two men were sitting there, the witch suddenly went outside. A little later a doll appeared at the attic hatch. The doll kept spinning round. The two men left at once, but they were frightened, for if that witch could turn herself into a doll, she could surely do other things too.
163827: Four young men had gone to hear the sermon on the occasion of the perpetual adoration. Afterwards one of the men said: "I'll go and fetch that girl over there and then you must attack us." After that game the man walked home between midnight and one o'clock. On a narrow path he saw something crawling with eyes like a car's headlights. The man kept making the sign of the cross. When he walked past the figure, the beast said: "The days are for you and the nights are for me." The man believed he had seen the devil. He ran to a farm, but did not dare knock for fear of being laughed at. The man stayed there praying until dawn broke and he dared to go home again.
163834: The wife of a cattle dealer from Heindonk had been struck by the evil hand. She went to the friars, who revealed to her who the culprit was. It was a woman who was jealous of the cattle dealer's wife because she herself had wanted to marry the cattle dealer.
163858: On a farm the farmer's wife was visited by a woman who asked: "Can you bake a loaf for me every day?" The farmer's wife did so and always kept a few centimes of the money the woman gave her. But the farmer's wife's little son fell ill. The child was thrown back and forth in his cot, so that his head lay where his feet should be. Finally the farmer's wife went to a friar of the Kluis, who was at her brother's house to collect Peter's Pence. The friar said: "I can already see why you have come. I will pray the strongest prayers and then it will surely be over. On your way home you will meet the culprit, but you must not say anything." The farmer's wife did indeed meet the witch at the bridge, but no word was spoken. The farmer's wife had also been given a holy object to put under the door and one to give to her child. After that the witch never set foot in their house again.
163864: People who had been ridden by the moon had a lot of bad luck.
163905: A man who had loaded a big wheelbarrow with wood had met a woman who had made him lose his way. Because of this the man could no longer find his house. In the morning he was released. He was found next to a wheelbarrow.
163929: In the past many shepherds from the Kempen and from Holland passed through Putte on their way to sell their sheep in Mechelen. One day a shepherd was returning from Mechelen with his purse. At the Kruisbaan he was attacked by two robbers and had to hand over his money. The shepherd took his purse, threw it on the ground and said: "Here's my money." When the robbers tried to pick up the money, they could no longer move. The shepherd took his money back and went to the inn 't Hoefijzer, where he rented a room. He put a candle on the table. The shepherd stayed awake all night, because if he went to sleep the devils would kill him. The next day he called the mayor and the police and sent them to the robbers. The two criminals were hanged at the place that is still called 'het Galgenveld' (the Gallows Field). Many people came to watch the execution. At one point so many onlookers were sitting in a tree that the branch broke. Afterwards the bodies of the hanged men were burned. That is why the people of Putte are still called 'de Verbrande Puttenaars' (the Burnt People of Putte).
163931: In one house people were annoyed by a black cat that always sat by the door. Once, when one of the sons came home late, he threw a stone at the animal's head. The next day a man was walking around the village with a bandage around his head. The man claimed he had walked into the door. After that the black cat was never seen at that house again.
163948: Near the clay barns at 't Neerven three will-o'-the-wisps were often seen. They were the little souls of unbaptised children.
163997: A woman who practised the evil hand caused her daughter to die young and her granddaughter to waste away completely and eventually die as well.
164011: At 't Schrans in Berlaar a girl always saw a black hand floating in her room at the stroke of midnight. Her parents went to the fathers of the Kluis. The next day a father was already at their house to pray over the room and the girl. After that the haunting came to an end.
164030: Every night a white lady roamed about in the Tongsken, luring people along and drowning them in the pool of the Vingerlink.
164052: A family with three children was always visited by a witch. Each time, one of the children received an apple or a pear from the witch. After a while the child became seriously ill. When the parents took the child to the friars, the clergymen said: "Whoever always gives a child an apple or a pear is a witch. If the child keeps eating that fruit, it will never get better." From then on the parents forbade the child to accept anything from the witch. The child recovered and stayed healthy.
164110: People who had eaten buckwheat porridge late in the evening and then went to bed were sometimes ridden by the mare.
164124: A man who refused to go along with the rural policeman cursed the whole time. At a certain moment a big black dog leapt into the crowd, at which everyone ran away. The man was convinced he had seen the devil.
164141: In Muizen a witch made the children cry on Sundays.
164152: A farmer from Wezel came to a monastery farm to ask whether he could buy a calf. The deal was made, but the calf had not yet been born. After the calf was born, the farmer sent his farmhand to the buyer. The farmhand answered: "I'm not going in there. If that woman comes and stands in the doorway, my horse won't go any further." That woman sometimes handed out pears to people. She had quarrelled with her neighbour, who was a blacksmith. She always said: "You can bend iron, but I'll bend you some day too." The smith laughed at those words, but some time later he began to cough and he died of his illness.
164159: A man went out into the countryside every evening, where he saw cats walking around him. Eventually the man took a gun with him and shot at the cats. The next day his own wife lay in bed with a broken leg.
164160: A woman who had gone to fetch water at the pump ran back inside with her buckets a moment later, shouting: "Witte Madame (the white lady) is there!" Her husband went to look but saw nothing.
164161: A man who was courting a girl who was a witch fell ill one night and was dead seven days later.
164169: The maid of Charel P. consorted with the devil. From time to time the maid lay rigid in bed. She would then talk to herself and say: "Are you coming at twelve o'clock?" At midnight the maid was drenched in sweat. For five years she had not gone to mass at Easter.
164172:
In Broechem lived a witch who did harm everywhere. When she came back from the fields, she would go and wash a little bowl at someone's well. The people of that farm would then have bad luck and went to the friars. Without being told anything, the friar asked: "Doesn't a woman come to wash a little bowl in your well?" The people confirmed this and were advised to keep that woman out from then on. One night, when the people got up because their child was crying so badly, they saw the woman standing by their bed. The woman always went to confession in Lier because she could not do so in Broechem; she could not even get as far as the church. The woman could only die after a friar from Lier had taken away her magic power.
At another farm the woman came to ask if she might see the cow. In the stable she sent the farmer's wife away to fetch a bundle of hay. Then she stroked the cow's udder. The next day the cow gave no more milk.
164182: On a farm on the heath the cows were stamping in the cowshed.
164205: A woman who had to do the washing at a farmer's had to start at three o'clock in the morning. To get to work she had to pass the inn of a witch. When she got there, she could not go any further and began to sweat heavily. She walked for a good three hours to cover a distance of ten minutes. When she finally reached the farmer, she told him what had happened to her. The farmer explained that the woman at the inn was a witch.
164215: In Turnhout lived dirty people who had lice. A child of theirs had fallen ill. The people suspected a woman from the neighbourhood of having caused the harm. After the child's death a little crown was found in its pillow. The little crown was burned.
164245: In her employer's house a woman saw a sorcerer make rats run across the table and leave again through the water drain.
164253: A peddler wanted to sell a man a mousetrap, but the man said he had no mice. The peddler said: "Then you might well get some." Half an hour later the man's house was full of mice.
164278: By a tall tree near the church a will-o'-the-wisp always appeared in the evening. It was the soul of an unbaptised child. After the child's body had been dug up and baptised, no light was seen at that spot again.
164287: In a hamlet of Retie lived a family with only one child, who was ill all the time. A neighbour woman often came to visit the child and brought some sweets with her. The child grew sicker and sicker. After a while the animals in the stable fell ill too. The child died, and everyone claimed the neighbour was responsible.
164292: A man who went to the dairy with his wheelbarrow always saw a strange white fellow with a long beard standing in the field there.
164340:
In a little wooden house lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. It was said that this woman owned all kinds of books of magic. 
A boy had been advised by his mother never to go inside that witch's house. One day the boy placed his feet crosswise in the witch's footprints. The witch looked back. 
After that the boy never again dared to walk past the witch's house.
164346: In the old days it often happened that people got lost on a road they knew very well. Those people had been ridden by the mare, it was said.
164378: In one house a woman always came to churn butter when the farmer's wife was ill. One day, however, the butter failed. Then they knew that the woman was a witch.
164398: At a farm on the Hoogstraat, talking cats came in through the drain hole. When those cats were in the house, the people could no longer do anything.
164417: In the evening and at night a dead witheer (Norbertine canon) walked around near the abbey of Tongerlo.
164430: A man who was ridden by the mare in his sleep tried to call out, but no sound came. A minute later the man was freed from the mare.
164442: Witches read bad books. Because they read too far, they had to do harm to themselves or others. Because they could not die, the parish priest had to help them. Witches sometimes appeared in the shape of a white lady, a large dog or a cat.
164458: A woman walking home alone one night saw a dog come up to her on the way. The woman was frightened and after that incident never came home alone again.
164468: In one family two children had died of 'the old man'. Because a woman always came visiting that house, an Easter nail was put under the door, so that the woman could no longer get in. When the woman came back from Mass, she wanted to call on those people. She pulled the door open but shut it again immediately. After that she never visited those people again. There were other people the witch visited as well. There too the children died.
164473: A man who was pulling carrots in his field saw a woman come by, who said: "Shall I make your wheelbarrow full of carrots?" The man laughed, but when he looked, his wheelbarrow was full to the brim. A moment later the woman had vanished.
164600: In a farmhouse, every evening at about the same time, a banging was always heard upstairs. Then a man with a light appeared, dressed all in white and with a long beard. The ghost pointed at Jan, one of the people living in the house. Maria supposed that the ghost had come to point out money hidden somewhere. But when the house was demolished, nothing was found.
164604: A man who had fallen asleep on the litter suddenly woke up and saw a large beast with horns. The man was terrified, but he could not find his gun.
164607: A man from Houtvenne who went outside to the toilet saw a glowing cow floating through the air.
164626: When the baker of Hoevenen was cycling back from Berendrecht one Sunday evening, he was chased by the ghost monks of 't Monnikenhof. Deathly pale, the man came into 't Moorken in Stabroek. The little chapel of Berendrecht was built against the ghost monks.
164639: A man had several sons who lived next to a witch. The boys came home at different hours on Saturday and Sunday, but the witch always knew exactly what time they had come home. The sons only saw a cat.
164663: Louis D. from Zoerle had promised to offer his goat if his sick wife Trieneke S. recovered. But the woman died, so Louis gave his goat to his sister Lien. Shortly afterwards the man met his wife's ghost three times in Oosterloveld. The parish priest advised him to ask the ghost what it wanted. So Louis learned that he still had to offer the goat. Once he had done so, his wife no longer came to haunt.
164666: At Tist B.'s, the witches had brought so much misfortune that the garden had risen because so many animals lay buried in it.
164707: A woman who went to milk the goat always saw a black cat sitting on a plank connecting the goat shed with the aviary. Her father came along once and struck at the cat, but could not hit it.
164713: The werewolf jumped on people's necks and squeezed them to death. In the woods people often met werewolves. These were creatures that were half human and half wolf.
164725: A man coming back from Wechelderzande in the evening saw a cat walking around him. The man kicked at the cat, but the animal jumped on his back.
164743: At the Osselei and on the patershoeve (friars' farm) a large black dog always roamed, which could not be chased away. A carter who worked as a farmhand for a miller said one day: "If he is still sitting there now, I'll hit him with the whip." The dog was there and the man struck at it. Then the dog put its front paws on the man's shoulders and threw him to the ground. Yet the man was a strong fellow. Afterwards he lay in bed for nine weeks, ready to die.
164772: A farmer from Herentals had sold 5 pigs. The next day those pigs all lay dead in their sty with broken legs. The cows in the stables had also been untied and their chains lay on the ground. Yet the stable had been locked. The farmer called the vet, but he could find nothing unusual. All the milk from the cows had to be poured into the sewer and no butter could be made. The farmer's little daughter weighed only three kilos at twelve months old. They took the child to the Poor Clares in Lier. There the farmer and his wife were advised to make a novena. Nine days later the child stood upright in the cradle and began to play. Two months later the child could already walk. Medals and blessed bread had to be put in the porridge. "If you get home safely with the child, she is saved," they had been told. They had also taken the child to Brustem. There a piece of the child's little shirt was laid in the water. If the cloth sank, nothing more could be done. If it floated, there was still hope. The cloth stayed on top. The dean came to bless the farm. He had said: "I will come, but I will suffer more than you." The dean sweated terribly during his intervention, but afterwards the misfortune was over. The clergyman had offered to reveal the culprit, but the farmer did not want that, because it would have been one of the neighbours.
164782: A man who worked as a carpenter for a miller in Oevel was harassed one day by a black cat while walking home. The man threw his lath hatchet (1) at the animal, which then disappeared howling. But the man could not find his hatchet anywhere. Many years later the carpenter went to Limburg to buy an ox. In a cottage he saw a bald old woman sitting. The woman had only one eye and a cat sat on the floor beside her. To his great astonishment the man saw his lath hatchet hanging on the wall. When the carpenter asked the woman whether she had always had only one eye, she answered: "No, a few years ago I lost an eye on the heath." The man quickly made himself scarce.
164810: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children.
164822: A girl wanted to go dancing although her father was seriously ill, and said: "I am going dancing, even if I have to dance with the devil!" A gentleman dressed in black appeared and danced with the girl. Where the devil had danced, scorched patches were seen on the dance floor.
164858: A woman who went to fetch butter from a farmer met a sorceress on the way. When the woman got home, she found that there was no butter in her jug, but a large wooden pin.
164869: A sister and brother went for a walk with their mother. When they were at the Rivierenhof, a violent thunderstorm broke out. They took shelter in a little house that stood there. The woman who lived there offered her guests coffee and sandwiches. When they got home, the mother and her children told the grandmother what had happened. The grandmother clasped her hands and said: "You should not have eaten or drunk there. That will cost you a lot of money yet." Two days later the little daughter fell ill. Because her life was feared for, the girl had to spend several months in the countryside, which cost a lot of money. Her brother also fell ill, but his condition was less serious.
164903: A man who had been called up for military service saw two black nuns on the way, after which he suddenly felt unwell. The next morning the man was dead.
164910: A man who went fishing for eel at Christmas suddenly heard a bell ring twelve times in the water. It was an unconsecrated bell that had flown into the water.
164956: In a house next to which a witch lived, the rattling of chains was always heard in the cowshed at midnight. The doors flew open and shut and the children were often sickly. All this was the result of the evil hand of the woman next door.
164969: A man walking home in the evening suddenly saw a big black cat jump in front of his feet. The cat would not get out of the way, and the man could not hit it when he tried to kick it. A little further on the same thing happened again. The cat went into a house where, people said, a witch lived. The next moment the door opened and a little old woman came out. The woman laughed and said "good evening". The man walked away.
164971: A man who was building dikes in the Netherlands knew that his wife was lying in childbed. A witch from the Netherlands had visited the young mother in the shape of a grey cat. The cat had snatched the rusks from the table. Every year that witch raised two or three hens. She wrung the necks of those hens' chicks, but she did no harm to people.
164996: A farmer from Heist-op-den-Berg had to get up three times one night to go to the stable. All the animals held their heads and tails up as if they had been frightened by something. The stable was full of cats. After the farmer had wounded one of the cats, a neighbour woman lay injured in bed. The farmer went to the fathers of Dendermonde, who said: "Go home without worry, for it will be over." And so it was. The farmer had been given a heart, which he had to hang in the stable, but he was not allowed to open it.
165019: On the feast of Sint-Gummarus people used to go on pilgrimage to Lier. A seventy-year-old pilgrim stayed the night with a workman from Lier. The workman and his wife had already had eleven children, but all had been stillborn. When the pilgrim stayed there, the woman was pregnant again. The pilgrim said: "If you feel anything, you must call me." In the night the child was to be born, the pilgrim laid a white sheet of paper on the woman's belly. Then a spider came down from the ceiling and sat on the paper. The pilgrim pulled off the spider's right leg and then said: "Now go and call the midwife, but she won't come. She'll have fallen off something." The midwife had fallen down the stairs and broken her right arm.
165024: In 't Zindervin in Steeg a frog appeared with a cap on its head.
165043: A man drove his horse and cart to the market. Because the horse was troublesome, the man struck the animal with a whip. When the man was at the market, he saw a woman walking there who had been beaten black and blue. On the way the man had struck the witch with his whip.
165089: A woman from Wijnegem was ridden by the mare. She went to bed black (with black hair?) in the evening and was white in the morning. That woman had been dreaming during the night.
165105: A few days before giving birth, a pregnant woman had had to take a bill to a woman in the neighbourhood for her father, who was a joiner. When the baby was born, the midwife noticed that one of its little hands always dropped down. The young mother immediately remembered her visit to the suspicious woman. The midwife prayed a novena for the child, who was then completely cured.
165112: On a farm there was chaos in the stable at night. The cows crawled all over each other and above every tub stuck out a horse's head. The horse stood with its tail against the manger and no longer had a head. A overlezer (healer who reads prayers over the afflicted) a hundred and four years old claimed that the farmer had the mare in his stable. The mare came at night to ride the animals, so that they grew thin and wasted away. After the farmer threw a blessed object into his stable, he had no more trouble.
165120: A boy from Wijnegem often saw a cat about when he was standing with his girlfriend. The boy did not trust the matter and broke off the relationship.
165137: Some men who had not been given leave for a long time were at work when an old woman came by and said: "Men, this afternoon you will get leave." The men did not believe it, however, and claimed the woman was a witch. The proof came when one of the men put his left foot in the print of the witch's right foot and his right foot in the print of her left foot.
165141: A man had given a witch from his neighbourhood power by answering "yes" to one of her questions. In the evening the witch sat in front of the stable door in the shape of a large grey cat with big eyes. Meanwhile the man's wife, terrified, read from a prayer book.
165168: A man riding to Diest saw at midnight in the woods of Averbode a big wheel of money with devils sitting around it. There was also a witheer (white lord, a Norbertine canon) who said: "Just take one piece out of it, then I will be released." At one o'clock the whole scene had vanished.
165187: A shopkeeper was suspected of being a witch. A man who did not believe the rumours went to buy a shirt in her shop one day. When he got home with the shirt, he found a big fat louse in it. The man immediately threw the shirt into the stove.
165201: When there was a lot of fog, people often saw stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps). These were the souls of lost and unbaptised children. If you dared to come near such a light, it would follow you. These lights did a great deal of harm.
165227: In some places bells could be heard ringing at night. This was the case in the Broek, for example, because bells lay buried there.
165248: A man who went to fetch bands at night crawled into a hollow willow stump. When the man had been sitting there for a quarter of an hour, a second one crawled into the stump and said: "My thing is in here too." The man jumped out of the stump and ran away. When he went to look the next day with some others, he found a skin in the hollow stump. They burned the skin and could hear the werewolf howling.
165275: A man always came to stay with a family in Varendonk at the weekend. The man paced restlessly back and forth the whole time and claimed that he saw the devil, although no one else could see him. The man never went to mass in Veerle and he went to confession with the fathers in Tongerlo.
165279: A woman coming back from Emmelen along a back road was followed the whole time by a black cat. At a crossroads the woman began to pray the Gospel of Saint John, after which the cat disappeared.
165294: A man was walking with two friends over a little bridge across the Edegemse beek to Kontich. On the bridge the man saw a big black dog standing, which did not step aside. The dog moved aside only a little to let the company pass. The men believed that dog was the devil.
165341: The parish priest of Aartselaar had made a collection for Saint Peter. On the way the priest was attacked by someone to whom he had to hand over his purse. The priest threw the purse at his attacker's feet. When people went to church the next morning, they saw the thief standing there with the purse at his feet. The priest had fixed that person to the ground by magic. In the past, priests learned evil first and then good. That is no longer the case now, because it caused too many problems.
165364: A farmer bringing manure to his stable saw a hare sitting by the door. The farmer walked towards it, but the hare ran away. When the hare was sitting there again a little later, the farmer fetched his gun and shot at the animal. Afterwards the man found that his wife had lost a leg.
165399: A thirteen-year-old boy rode on a donkey with a friend to Berlaar-Heikant to fetch reeds. They had to take the reeds to the priest of Begijnendijk. When the two came back from Begijnendijk in the evening, they heard talking near the churchyard. When they reached the gate, however, there was nothing to be seen. A little later the two stood on the right side of the gate and saw behind a heap of sand a group of girls of sixteen, seventeen or eighteen. Suddenly a floating nun appeared behind the girls, who said not a word.
165400: The miller's wife had a child who always woke up at night because of witchcraft.
165419: Six friends were returning from the fair in Lier. From the Mechelpoort onwards the people were followed the whole time by a black cat. When they arrived in Lint, the cat went along with one of the men and tried to get into his house. Although the others still had five minutes to walk, the cat did not go with them.
165421: Near the fens people often saw will-o'-the-wisps. If you challenged such a light, it came closer. Will-o'-the-wisps were spirits, but some people claimed they were glow-worms sitting in the bushes.
165424: A man walking home one evening lost his way. A while later he reached his house, but he could not go inside. He was forced to keep going until he came to a house where, people said, a wizard lived. A moment later the wizard suddenly stood before him, laughing: "Got lost? You'll find your way now." Five minutes later the man was home.
165448: In a house, a woman was ill through witchcraft. A sorceress often came to visit the house. After the woman of the house had laid straw crosses under the door, the sorceress could no longer come in. The husband finally went to the parish priest. After that the witchcraft came to an end.
165452: Whenever a boy came back from visiting his girlfriend, he always saw a strange beast with eyes like the rear lights of a bicycle. One day the boy went to Aarschot to get a revolver. When he met the beast again and wanted to shoot at it, strangely his revolver did not work. When the beast was not around, the revolver did work. For such things one had to use holy water.
165454: A farmer's wife had put a goat she wanted to sell at the back of her stable. One day a woman came to look at the goat. As she walked through the stable, she gave the cows a pat. The next day no more butter could be made on that farm and they had to go to the friars of Mechelen. In another family a little child died after receiving a little dress from the same sorceress.
165457: On a farm they had bought a cow with a big udder, hoping the animal would give as much as twenty-five litres of milk. The animal did indeed give a lot of milk, but the milk was dirty. They called the vet, who gave an ointment to rub on the udder. After that, large sheets of skin came off the udder. The vet said he had come across the same problem in a stable in Pulderbos and could not solve it. The farmer went to the friars of the Ossemarkt.
