A friar came with him to the stable to read away the evil. The friar found that the evil was already far advanced.
165470: On his way home, at the brooms, a man was always set upon by black dogs whenever the friars' little bell rang.
165482: A man lying in his bed heard a knock on the bedroom door. The man lay still, but a little later heard something crawling across the floor. Suddenly something jumped on the man and seized him by the throat. The man began to shout and thought he would die. Yet he was freed. It must have been the mare that had him in her grip. When in the morning the man asked his wife why she had not helped him, she declared that she had heard nothing.
165489: Peer set out one evening with his dog to go fishing. On the way Peer met a woman who wanted to know where he was going. The woman had said: "You won't catch any fish today!" That night Peer lost his way. In the distance he saw a castle with a light burning. As soon as Peer came closer, the light went out. That night Peer indeed could not catch a single fish.
165505: In de Boskant lived people who churned butter by means of a cord and a stone. One day there was no butter under the stone, but a live black cat, which ran off in the direction of a wizard's house.
165519: Cats always came to dance on the Nieuwmoer. When a miller passed by there one day, the cats sang: "Neck and neck, paw and paw, the miller must go in the ditch." The miller really did end up in the ditch.
165531: On a farm people got up at four in the morning to mow. When one of the boys had got up, he saw a cat appear, took the holy water font and struck the animal with it. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was injured.
165532: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field came back to haunt after his death with the words: "Where shall I put it, where shall I put it?" One day someone answered: "Put it where you got it!" That must have been the devil.
165582: On a farm on the Tilburgse weg, the farmer could not keep any calves alive. His own children did not grow either. Because the farmer was often visited by a certain woman, he once put an Easter nail under the door. After that the visitor could no longer come in.
165590: In the church a witch had left a little bag of white sweets shaped like coins on a chair. The children wanted to eat them at once, but their mother did not trust it and buried them. When they were dug up again some time later, they found that they had turned black.
165609: On a farm in Itegem lived a man who had a pretty maid. One day the farm gave lodging to some soldiers. The officer fell in love with the girl and asked her to come with him. When the girl refused, the officer asked whether he might cut off a little of her hair and take it with him in his little chest. The girl agreed. A few days later the girl herself had the chest in her possession. She had made it come back to her.
165611: Witches could change themselves into goats. Sometimes people were chased in the street by goats. At a certain moment those goats would jump into a well and disappear. The next day exactly the same happened in another municipality. Sometimes it was in Boom, sometimes in Terhagen.
165617: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the dead who could no longer get into heaven.
165634: Two girls went together to fetch a cow. On the way one of the girls was given a bag of sweets by a witch. When the girl got home, she fell ill. Her mother went to the convent and was given salt there. The child cried terribly to be freed from the witchcraft.
165638: At midnight a ghost was seen appearing with a post on its back. It was the spirit of someone who had moved a boundary post during his life. One day a drunkard called out: "Don't drag it along! Put it where you got it!" At that the ghost threw the post to the spot where it had stood.
165641: In a family a little child had fallen ill. The illness was blamed on the evil hand, brought into the house during a visit by a supposed witch. The people put a relic under the threshold to drive out the evil hand. After the people had prayed for six weeks, the little girl recovered. The mother went with her daughter from Mol to Westmalle, where the friars read prayers over the child.
165666: A boy had gone with his mother to buy a new cap. When the boy was walking in the park with his new cap, a farmer's wife bumped into him, so that the cap fell into the water. Afterwards people said the witch had been bewitching again. She was made to give the boy a new cap, or else she would no longer receive bread from the municipality.
165667: Two men who went to shoot owls by the church tower one evening decided to turn back because there was not a single owl to be seen. One of the men then said: "Come on, there's a cat in the churchyard. Let's shoot that instead." Although his friend advised against it, the man shot at the cat. The animal that was hit leapt a metre into the air and ran off. On their way home the two men saw the same cat by a statue of Our Lady hanging on a tree. The man said: "Shall I shoot at it again?", but the next moment the cat grew as big as a dog, so the two men ran away. The two men crawled through a hedge and to their great fright saw a calm, motionless woman standing there. Suddenly the man was attacked by the woman and dragged to the door of his house, where he lay dead. The witch had done it.
165695: A man returning on a Sunday evening from the fair in Branst suddenly saw a sorceress standing in front of him. The sorceress knocked the man into the ditch. The man crawled out, but was then struck again. Then the man crawled along the ditch and came out at the end. But there the sorceress was already standing again to hit him.
165703: A man coming back in the dark from visiting his girlfriend walked over the threshold of a house where a witch lived. A man standing with his bicycle near the witch's house heard the parish priest coming with the last sacraments. The sound went on, but the man saw nothing. The witch had caused these apparitions.
165719: Witches could turn themselves into a black cat. If that cat was wounded, the witch was wounded too.
165728: A woman who saw a toad sitting in her house threw the animal into the stove. The next day a sorceress from the village had a burnt face.
165752: A man had been given red cabbages by a woman. Because the cabbages were nearly rotten, the man buried them in his garden. During this job, however, he was annoyed by a cat that kept walking around him. He hit the animal with the spade and said to his household: "Go and see if that woman is lying in her bed!" She was indeed lying in her bed and was ill for two more weeks afterwards.
165817: A bell is said to have once sunk in Bogaerts Wiel. That is why it is haunted there in the evening. According to some, the bell could still be heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night.
165822: Someone had chopped off a cat's front paw. The next day that person found that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost her hand.
165855: One evening on his way home a man saw a witch. About two hundred metres from his house he saw a foal coming towards him. The man hurried home. The next day he kept watch with two friends to shoot the foal dead. But the animal was nowhere to be seen.
165862: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had come back after his death with the words: "Where shall I go with my post? Where shall I go with my post?"
165864: A night watchman was pursued by dogs. He then had to start smoking, because otherwise the dogs would attack him.
165888: On a farm where many animals died and no butter could be made, they went to the friars of Tongerlo. Because those friars were not yet powerful enough at the time, the farmhand was sent to Dendermonde. There the friars said: "Are you the farmhand? Look through the window." The farmhand saw the woman walking by who was suspected of causing the misfortune. The friar gave him a relic. A few days later the farmer's father fell ill. He got a swollen eye. The people went to the friars of Dendermonde again, where they were advised to do penance for nine days. On the third day the eye was already much better. On the ninth day the eye was completely healed. The doctor could not understand it. The witch never showed herself there again.
165892: A fisherman who came past the churchyard drunk at night saw a white man standing there. The fisherman spoke to the apparition, but there was no answer. Then the fisherman pulled the ghost's shirt off. "Friend, why did you do that?" asked the ghost. "I left you alone too!" The fisherman explained that he was drunk, and the ghost replied: "You must sew that button straight on my shirt." After the fisherman had the priest read prayers over him, the clergyman said: "You must do exactly the same as what you did. Otherwise the ghost will break your neck." Accompanied by the priest, the fisherman went to the churchyard and put the shirt back on the ghost. Then the ghost said: "If you had come alone, I would have broken your neck."
165916: The castle of Rielen was so badly haunted that the lord of the castle no longer dared to sleep alone. The lord hired a servant who had to keep watch all night. At night the servant began baking pancakes. While he was baking, bones kept falling down the chimney. When finally a skull had fallen down too, the bones formed a complete skeleton, which said: "I am the old lord of the castle. Follow me." In the cellar the skeleton pointed to a spot on the wall and said: "You must break this open and give the gold you find to the poor. Only then will my spirit find rest!" After the servant had done what the ghost asked, the castle was no longer haunted.
165919: On a farm in Brakel a black cat was often seen. One day a man went to look at a cow that was about to calve. The man got a pat on the shoulder from a woman from the neighbourhood. After that the man could not leave his bed for three weeks. In the monastery he was freed from the evil hand.
165920: A mother breastfeeding her eleven-day-old daughter saw a pedlar woman come in, who laid her neckerchief over the child. After that the baby fell ill. The mother went to the dean of Kontich, but he could not help. When the child's uncle was visiting, the dean said that the girl's heart was full of pins. Ten days later the baby died.
165921: A dying man had to promise a friend that after his death he would come and tell what things were like in the hereafter. When the dead man came back, he said: "Never let a dead man come back again!"
165943: A man driving home with his cart suddenly saw a black cat jump onto the horse, after which the animal stood still. Only when the man had struck the cat away did the horse go on.
165957: On a farm they had one bull. That bull was sold at least ten times, but each time the delivery had to be postponed because the animal was struck by the evil hand. When the parish priest was called in, the bull could finally be delivered.
165961: An old woman who was always out and about in the evenings and at night was skilled in witchcraft. If you walked past her house at midnight, the shutters were glowing because the woman was practising witchcraft. In the village there was a foundling. On the very night the foundling was found, the witch died. Had she lived, people would surely have known where the foundling came from, because the witch always knew everything.
165984: There were three farms in Varendonk. The stable of one of those farms was bewitched. At midnight music could always be heard there. When Fons V. from Eindhout slept above the horse stable one night with his brother, at twelve o'clock the two saw a grey cat fly in through the window. That cat was the witch.
165986: A man returning from Turnhout one evening along the old road saw, at the witches' heath by 't Lensgoor, six cats with glowing eyes sitting there, blocking his way. The man fled to a 'mastenbosje' (?). There he was beaten so hard with 'mastenmutsers' (?) that he fainted and only regained consciousness towards morning.
165988: A woman who had taken over her mother's magic power came into the stable of a farm one day. All the animals the woman had touched were dead the next day.
166001: People said that the will-o'-the-wisps floating about were the little souls of unborn children.
166045: A woman could not sleep at night because she heard roaring in her head and lay sweating and moaning. She had been ridden by the mare. The woman then went to the fathers of Turnhout, who gave her a medal. After that she was never troubled by the mare again.
166053: Some people going to Vremdermolen were followed on the way by a girl. Assuming the girl was a witch, the people made the sign of the cross. At the Oelegem road the girl had vanished.
166057: In the Molenstraat in Lichtaart stood a house that was troubled by witchcraft. A cat sat under the butter churn. The farmer grew angry and kicked the cat, sending the animal flying against the wall. The farmer's wife lashed out at the cat with her knife and hit it on the front paws. The next day the maid lay in bed with severe back pain and an injured toe.
166063: A man who was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend announced that he had to go and relieve himself and gave the girl a handkerchief. When the couple got home, the girl found that her boyfriend still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
166068: A boy of eight or ten was grabbed by the neck every evening when going to bed. The boy would then cry and sweat terribly. He saw a woman standing at the foot of the bed. That woman had once given him fish, and from then on she always came to stand by him on Sundays. The father took the boy to the friars of Kalmthout. Prayers were read over the boy and the friars said: "If he still has it, come back and bring a little shirt and a small bottle of water. There are four of you. I will give each of you a little medal." The next evening the boy was still slightly troubled, but after that the evil was over. The trouble always began at exactly half past ten and the boy could not say anything then.
166073: A diamond cutter who was very strong had problems with his diamonds. Every day some of the stones were broken. It also sometimes happened that he lost his house key or had a headache. The man went to a spiritualist from Charleroi, who could send the spirit of a dead person to the witch. The spiritualist, who had once studied for the priesthood, had to go to great lengths to do so. There, in the mirror, the diamond cutter saw the man and woman appear who were harming him. The diamond cutter then harassed those two people so much that they finally left him alone.
166098: On a farm a knocking on the door was always heard at night. When the farmer's brother came to stay one night, the knocking was not heard. The people went to the friars, who freed them from the torments of the witch. The witch often came to work on that farm. The friars had advised the people not to give her any more milk. The witch had also bewitched the farmer's child. The parents had to do penance and were given a holy object to put above the door. Some time later the witch came through the snow to ask for half a litre of milk, but she could not come in unless someone said: "Come in." The farmer said he no longer sold milk.
166126: People who were bewitched had to go to the abbey of Tongerlo to have prayers read over them and to fetch a relic. Because of that relic, the witches could no longer come in.
166135: People who had been struck by the evil hand and therefore had misfortune with their cows had to go to the monastery.
166138: A white goat always wandered around in the Molenstraat. Some boys wanted to catch the goat, but every time they had almost reached the animal, it suddenly disappeared and they were standing on the other side of the street.
166150: On a farm where a frog always fell into the butter churn, no butter could be made any more. The people were advised to pour boiling water on the frog once, and they did so. The next day a little woman in the neighbourhood was walking around with a bandage around her fingers.
166164: A boy who was walking home with his girlfriend said he had to go and relieve himself on the way. He gave his girlfriend a red handkerchief with white dots, which she was to throw if she met anything. A little later the girl was approached by a big dog and threw the handkerchief at the animal. When the girl then saw her boyfriend coming back, she found that a piece of the handkerchief was sticking out between his teeth. The girl ran away and never wanted to see her boyfriend again.
166167: On a farm where the cows always stayed thin, the misfortune was blamed on the evil hand. One day the farmer bought an exceptionally fat cow from his neighbour, but two days later the animal was as thin as the other cows. No one ever knew who had brought the evil hand over that farm.
166194: When a farmer's wife failed to make butter, the blame was put on some old woman who had visited a few days before. After the parish priest had read prayers over the farm, butter could be made again.
166229: In Schilde there lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. If you walked behind that woman and crossed her footprints, she would look back.
166275: A witch could get in through a door with a small hole in the shape of a cat.
166288: A man who was ridden by the moon was seized by the throat, so that his tie flew through the air. The next day the tie lay on a stack of grain. Victims of the moon could not move or call out.
166328: In Waarloos a man had a lot of trouble with an old woman. One day the little old woman gave him some bracelets. After that the man began to limp. Someone advised the man to throw the bracelets into the fire, and he did. The next day the little old woman was walking around with burnt hands.
166338: In the old days a witte madam (white lady) haunted Hoevenen. One day a baker's boy who was always out early came home deathly pale because he had seen a white lady on the road from Hoevenen to Kapellen. His father advised him to take a walking stick and give the lady a good thrashing. When the boy did so, the white lady swore like a docker.
166361: An old man from Nieuwmoer-Kalmthout was driving a cart to town. On the way a cat came and sat on the cart, so the man struck at the animal with a whip. A little later the cart was full of cats. After the man had made the sign of the cross with his tongue, the cats had disappeared.
166438: A woman pregnant with her first child came into a little sweet shop where soup was on the stove. She craved the soup so much that she asked the shopkeeper if she could have some. She ate the soup with relish. The next day her head was full of lice. That evening she gave birth. The day after the birth all the lice had gone.
166460: A man walking home through the snow one winter evening saw a group of white figures leaping back and forth in the field. The man ran home and told his father what he had seen. The father and his brother went to the spot he had pointed out and could just see the white figures disappear. When they came closer, they found not a single footprint in the snow.
166472: In the past people often told of a ghost that roamed the beguinage and harmed people.
166481: On a farm one evening two calves were standing close together. A large cat was sitting on one of the calves. The next day the calves lay dead. The meat of the animals wobbled in the pan, so that no one dared to eat it. That was witchcraft.
166565: In Oelegem there once lived a farmer called 'Kleudde met zijn hachten' (Kleudde with his chains). This farmer always walked around with chains around his neck because he had been punished by Our Lord. One day a drunkard called out "Take them back to where you got them". After that nothing more was heard of Kleudde with his chain.
166639: A troop of soldiers had lost the war chest at a farm in Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Waver. The farmer had covered the chest under a heap of manure and kept the money for himself. From then on a glowing wagon always drove through the farm's stable. That wagon was driven by something invisible.
166655: Two farmhands worked on a farm, one of whom was always dead tired because he could not sleep at night. One night the other farmhand saw a foal appear. He rode the animal to the smith and had it shod. The next day the farmer's wife lay in her bed with horseshoes on her hands and feet.
166674: In Hoevenen a man saw a little piglet walking in the street. The man took the piglet with him and put it in a pen. The next day there was a stone lying in the pen.
166675: A boy saw a stranger appear in his room, who came to ask for a place to spend the night. The boy hesitated a moment and then agreed. The stranger said: "Shall I bring your girlfriend here now?" A moment later a tremendous thunderclap sounded. The next instant the girl was standing in the room. The boy was startled and made the sign of the cross. A second thunderclap followed and then he was alone again. The next day the boy told the priest what had happened to him. The priest said the boy had met the devil.
166681: A woman had received from her mother on her deathbed the power to throw a cat at people. The woman herself always had a black cat with her. The people at whom she threw the cat always fell ill.
166699: Two men coming back from the pub one Saturday evening saw something strange on the way. Along the road lay a lot of women's hats with little flowers, all together. In the distance the men also heard a strange sound, as if someone were coming.
166738: A boy who did not believe in ghosts wanted to frighten some girls. The boy pulled a white sheet over himself and sat down by the side of the road. Suddenly the boy turned deathly pale with fear. Between the trees he saw two white figures floating towards him two metres above the ground. When the figures reached him, the boy heard a hollow voice cry: "Unbelieving deceiver!" Then the ghosts were gone. The boy died of fright shortly afterwards.
166759: A woman walking home saw a will-o'-the-wisp by the brewery on the canal. Frightened, she hurried home. The faster she walked, the more lights she saw appear in front of her feet. People said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. The woman reasoned that they could not be her own children: two of her children had died, but they had been baptised.
166771: The mother of a girl from Mariekerke had promised to go on pilgrimage to Brucht, but she had died before she could make that pilgrimage. Every night the girl saw the ghost of her dead mother appear, asking her to go to Brucht with her. Before arriving in Brucht the girl was not allowed to give her mother her hand, or they would both be damned. In Brucht the daughter received her mother's hand. After that the ghost appeared no more.
166782: A man standing in a field got lost. When the man began to pray a paternoster to Our Lady of Help, he could immediately find his bearings again. The man had been ridden by the mare, which is why he only got home in the morning.
166798: In an inn in Sint-Job sat a man who had sworn to the devil that he would drink no more beer. The others present tried to persuade the man to drink anyway. At a certain moment the man went outside. He stood there sweating terribly, and two legs like those of a horse were resting on his shoulders. Then the man came back in and drank beer, saying: "Now it doesn't matter, but tonight I will go through something yet."
166801: Will-o'-the-wisps were unbaptised little souls that flew back and forth over the marshes.
166819: The abbot of Postel and the Lords of Retie could not agree on the boundary between their two territories. After a long time it was decided to fetch the shepherd of Postel, since he was thought to know the true boundaries because he spent so much time on the heath of Postel. The shepherd also knew well that the stinginess of the Lord of Retie contrasted sharply with the generosity of the abbot. The shepherd had put a layer of Postel soil in his shoes, and under his woollen cap he had a scoop the grocer used for scooping. The shepherd walked further and further, much to the displeasure of the Lord of Retie, who said: "But that is surely no longer Postel ground!" The shepherd replied: "That is certainly Postel ground." Pointing first to his cap and then to his feet, he said: "I swear by the schepper (both 'creator' and 'scoop') above that I am still standing on Postel ground." After his death, however, the shepherd had to haunt the border area in the form of a burning man.
166828: A pregnant woman with an exceptionally big belly met a witch, who said: "Well, Marie!" and briefly stroked the big belly. The next day the pregnant woman had a miscarriage.
166831: In a house where a woman had long lain sick in bed, a glass cabinet was heard falling over at midnight. It seemed as if everything was broken, but when they went to look, there was nothing to be seen. When the sick woman's brother came to have a look, he saw a large rat run off through the cellar hole. People believed that rat was a witch.
166854: A girl of about twelve on her way to the shop placed her foot crosswise on the footprint of a suspicious woman. Because of this the woman, who was a witch, could go no further. She looked back and said: "Arè begot." The following night the parish priest had to be fetched for the girl, because she was bewitched.
166857: A bewitched woman always saw a thousand fleas and lice in the evening. The priest had said: "It is serious that they come into people's homes like that." Fortunately, the Gospel of Saint John is very powerful against witchcraft.
166871: In the churchyard of Brecht people often saw lights dancing. These lights were the souls of stillborn children.
166893: A miller could hardly find staff any more because all the hands in his service died. An old drunkard claimed not to be afraid and went to work for the miller. The man took a blessed sabre with him to the brewery. When he was bothered by a cat at night, he cut off one of its paws with the sabre. The next morning the miller's wife lay in bed with one arm. It was she who had made the hands die.
166914: Two friends who worked for a farmer stayed overnight at the farm. One day they heard a tremendous racket in the kitchen. Pots and pans rattled and money could be heard jingling too. Someone struck the windowpanes hard three times without breaking them. When the people went downstairs, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen.
166936: The 'tall woman' walked along the churchyard wall every night. She was a soul who could find no rest in the grave.
166958: A mother met an old woman, who said: "You have a lovely little child with you! May I have a look?" When the woman got home, the child began to cry loudly. Shortly afterwards the child died.
166963: In Lippelo the witte madam (white lady) walked back and forth without saying anything.
166993: A mother who had been to Heist with her daughter and had brought back sour cherries fell ill after eating the fruit. At night a witch came into the house in the shape of a cat. The witch always knocked before she came in. The woman's family went to fetch a medal from the friars. After that the situation improved.
167032: A brewer delivered beer to an inn in Polygoon. The innkeeper's wife could never pay, so the brewer's man always came back empty-handed. When once again he was not paid, he said: "I'll strangle you," to which the innkeeper's wife replied: "You won't be able to keep a single barrel on your cart on the way." When the man was on his way, the barrels indeed rolled off the cart on all sides.
167037: A man had heard a friend say that he had seen the devil. The man reacted with disbelief and said: "What? You believe that?! I'd like to see that for myself." When the man was on his way home a long time later, a cat flew into his face. That was the devil.
167045: In Kessel lived a man who had read many books. When this man saw a farmer sowing, he wanted to test his magic power and made the farmer stop sowing and hold his hand up. Then the wizard let the farmer carry on working.
167050: On a farm a sorceress came into the stable where a little piglet lay. As the sorceress came in, the piglet suddenly jumped up and ran up the wall. The animal was having convulsions.
167086: In Turnhout lived a woman who always saw church towers on the window panes. Things often went badly with her children too. The people believed their neighbour was responsible for the misfortune and went to the brown friars to have prayers read over them. A friar prayed until he was drenched in sweat and then said that the woman's mother was responsible for the evil. That mother always walked barefoot and often brought all kinds of things to her daughter.
167093: A farmer's son had a relationship with a girl from a café. Because his parents were against it, they said to their son: "We would rather see you end up in the churchyard than have you marry that girl!" Shortly afterwards the farmer's son took his own life. Because the boy was not allowed to be buried in the churchyard, his parents knocked together a coffin themselves and buried it on a hill. A man who came back from work past that hill in the evenings always saw a light near the boy's burial place that followed him. As soon as the man reached the grave, the light went out.
167100: A man who peddled cups and plates saw a light floating in front of his cart. At that the peddler's dog crept under the wheelbarrow. The man prayed the gospel and saw the ghost come closer.
167101: A man from Postel was ridden by the mare at night. He would then go completely stiff. His family went to the monastery for him, where they were advised to do nine days of penance.
167117: A dying woman asked a relative to close the curtain. "Why, Netje?" they asked. The woman replied: "Over there on the bench five more people are sitting and waiting, who will die together with me." And so it happened.
167122: Three women in Wiekevorst were suspected of being witches. One day all three were at Mass. Some men wanted to put it to the test and stuck a relic under the church door. After Mass the three women stayed sitting in the church because they could not get past the relic.
167143: One evening a man saw a suspicious woman walking in a field. The man crossed the witch's footprints and said: "If you are a witch, look back." The next moment the witch looked back. The next day three of that man's cows and two calves were dead.
167149: In Woensdrecht lived a woman who was said to be able to do witchcraft. When a child in the neighbourhood fell ill, people believed the witch had bewitched it. The child was flung back and forth all the time and drank its own urine. One day the child fell with its head on its clogs. The clogs broke into pieces, but the child felt nothing. When the child was dead, all sorts of beautiful red roses were found in its pillow. The dove that had always appeared while the child was alive had now disappeared.
167155: In Lichtaart lived a young man who went with his mother to visit friends one evening. Suddenly the two saw a black cat standing in the road. The boy wanted to hit the animal with a stick, but his mother stopped him, saying: "Mind you, never strike at a cat in the evening!" Then the cat said: "If you had struck at me, you wouldn't have hit me anyway!" and then vanished.
167177: A man had seen a girl dancing with the devil in the town. The girl had said: "Mother, I am going dancing, even if it is with the devil." Everywhere the devil had walked there was a hole in the wooden floor.
167184: A man said "Through hedge and through hedgerow" instead of "Over hedge and over hedgerow" and arrived at his destination badly injured.
167233: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. If you beckoned to such lights, they came closer. If you baptised the lights, they became good Christians.
167240: A man had a little daughter who was seriously ill during the First World War. Although it was very dangerous to be outside after nine in the evening, the man went to the doctor. The soldiers he met on the way let him through when they knew what it was about. The doctor did not want to go with the man that evening because it was too late and too dangerous. He would come early the next morning. But when the man got home, his daughter was dead. A few days later a second child fell ill. The man decided to go to the friars. The friar asked whether a woman perhaps visited the man regularly. The man explained that every week a woman came to fetch potatoes. That woman had picked up the child and stroked it, saying: "What lovely children you have!" The friar went home with the man and hung a relic around each child's neck. The people also had to make a novena and keep that woman out. They followed the advice. The woman did come back afterwards, but she no longer got in. Some time later the child was cured.
167246: In Nijlen a dead woman came to haunt to tell her family that she had promised to go to Scherpenheuvel on her bare knees. Until that promise was fulfilled, the woman could not be released.
167268: In the Broekstraat lived a witch who had pears. But the schoolchildren were far too scared to accept those pears.
167293: A man who wanted to take a sack of potatoes to Aarschot or to the market by wheelbarrow was often told by his wife: "You won't get there." The man then could not push his wheelbarrow. When he moved the potatoes onto the neighbours' wheelbarrow, he had no more problems.
167302:
A man placed his foot crosswise on the footprints of a woman coming out of church. Every time the man did so, the woman looked back. 
A farmhand who had once worked for that man had a relationship with the witch. In the end he had to dismiss that farmhand.
167318: Shooting stars or 'starlichtjes' (star lights) were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised.
167326: A farm on the Groeningelei was haunted. There was knocking on the door, though nothing could be seen. A fearless farmhand squatting outside felt someone knock on his head, though nothing could be seen. After the farmer had gone to fetch a holy object, no more strange things happened on that farm.
167342: In Zandvliet lived a man who had studied for the priesthood. That man could open a locked door by throwing his cap against it. One day the man said: "Tomorrow morning there will be a train on the ridge of the barn roof." And so it was.
167370: A farmer's wife had fetched flour from a shop to bake cakes, but she had not yet paid for it. When in the evening she left a bowl of dough to rise, a cat came in and said: "Baking cakes, fetching flour, not paying." The farmer's wife poured a pot of hot fat over the cat. The next day a woman in the village lay in bed with burns. That woman died of her injuries.
167373: On the Achterheide stood a farm where one morning the animals stood in the stable with their necks wrung. The horse the farmer had just bought also lay dead the next morning. The farmer went to the dean of Heist-op-den-Berg. On the way, at the Hoge Brug, he met a black cat. A little further on he met a woman he knew well. Although the farmer had not yet told anyone what had happened to him, the woman said: "I didn't wring your animals' necks." The farmer told the dean what he had experienced. The clergyman then said: "Don't tell anyone who it was, because that woman still has her good name among people, but it is her and she won't do it again." Indeed, the farmer had no more problems after that.
167374: On the Brachtse heath lived a farmer whose wife was always away at night. When the farmer told the priest, the priest said: "There must be something unusual in your house. If you find it, ask your wife whether you may go along with her some time." One day the man found an egg in the ashes of the stove. Then the man said to his wife: "Where were you last night? May I come along?", to which the wife replied: "I'll ask over there whether you may come." When he arrived at their destination, the man found himself at a meeting of a kind of guild. When they asked him whether he would join the guild too, he remembered the priest's advice and said: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph, help me." The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the man stood with his wife in the middle of the heath.
167381: On a farm where no butter could be churned, people believed that a woman who came to fetch milk had put the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse) on the farm. They sent for a man from Grobbendonk, who heated a stone until it glowed and poured vinegar on it. He put it in the butter churn. After that they could make butter again. The farmer asked who had done this to them, and the man answered: "I can't say. Walk around the house at about six in the morning, and do that for three days. Then she will make herself known." The farmer did so and saw the woman who came to fetch milk from him.
167402: On a farm, people went to eat at seven in the morning after the work was done. Suddenly a thud was heard in the stable. The farmer went to look and saw that one of the cows was sitting at the back on the 'mesting' (?). The cow behaved strangely, twisted its head and fell dead at the farmer's feet. The farmer got ready to take the dead animal away and stuck the cow in the throat with a knife. The blood that ran out was black. After that a cow died every half hour. The farmer went to the parish priest, who read from his breviary in front of the stable for ten minutes. The clergyman sweated terribly while doing so. Then the farmer had to clean and disinfect the stable. He also had to hide a piece of the Easter candle in an inconspicuous place. After that the farmer had no more misfortune. The next morning a woman who often visited came by. She pulled the door open and then turned right around. She never came back. When the farmer took the dead cow outside, a second animal fell ill. That cow did not die, however, because the clergy had arrived so quickly.
167419: A witch is said to have lived long ago at the border of Zittaart and Zammel. That witch could saw wood without a saw and could make the tables and chairs in the kitchen fall over as she pleased.
167445: A brewer from Vorselaar who believed his wife was a witch always went to visit another brewer in Wechelderzande on winter evenings. When the brewer came home after midnight, he was followed by a black cat. The man gave the cat a hard kick. When he got home, he found his wife lying in bed, and she had lost an eye. Witches only had power after midnight. If one used the name of God, the witches vanished at once. One day the brewer saw a calf leaping about in the field. The brewer said: "Is that a leap for a calf?" The next moment he saw his wife standing before him.
167452: In the old days farmers drove to town with their horses. A farmer from Hoogstraten drove past the house of a woman in Schilde. The driver noticed that the horse always got a bellyache at that spot.
167455: A man who was afraid of nothing went one evening to a little chapel at a crossroads. When the man had walked less than fifty metres, he was followed by five cats. The cats began to meow and to bark like dogs. The man grew afraid and quickened his pace. At the crossroads the animals could go no further. It was as if something was holding them back. Since that incident the man was terrified of witches.
167457: An old woman had visited a house. She had stroked a little boy's head, saying: "Oh, good little man." After that the boy began to cry every night at twelve o'clock. They took the child to the friars, where they were given a relic. After that the boy cried no more.
167474: A doctor was returning from Emblem by coach at night when he suddenly saw a black figure standing in the middle of the road, asking to ride along. When the figure held out his hand, the doctor saw that it was a black hand and drove on.
167491: A man returning from the Roskam had to go through a small wood. There he heard a rustling. He looked and saw a cat turn three somersaults and then disappear. Fifteen metres further on the man saw the same thing again. It happened a third time. That cat was a witch.
167543: In a house in Noorderwijk a witch in the shape of a fly came and sat on the bed.
167582: In 's-Gravenwezel a ghost wandered about at night with the words: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I carry it to?" It was the spirit of a man who had moved a boundary post during his life. One day someone answered: "Carry it, damn it, to the place where you got it!" Since then the ghost has not been seen or heard again.
167586: A man went round the farms to drive away rats. He would recite a spell or a prayer, whistle a tune, and then see all the rats gather around him at a certain time, so that he could lead them to another place. If anyone spoke rudely to him in the café, he said: "Watch out, or tomorrow I'll come with two hundred and fifty rats."
167592: Although all openings in the house were closed, a sick woman always saw an invisible witch come in, who seized her by the throat. After the woman had received a relic from the parish priest, she no longer saw the witch.
167602: A woman who was ridden by the mare tried to call out but could not make a sound. You could see the mare coming and you could see its hands grab your throat.
167611: A farmer who could not make butter had to go to the monastery with a little bottle of water. When the man got there, the bottle was full of 'lodders' (small creatures).
167638: On his way home, a man from Retie saw a woman in a hooded cloak with an umbrella walking near the old mill. When the man reached the woman and said "good evening", there was no answer. The woman had suddenly vanished.
167678: If you suspected a woman of being a witch, you had to walk behind her and draw a sign of the cross on the ground. If the woman was a witch, she would immediately look back.
167684: In Postel a man had moved the boundary post of his field. After his death the man had turned into a glowing post, which called out on the heath at night: "Post here, post there!" One evening a drunkard answered: "Take it to the place where you got it, you beast walking there!" After that the ghost was released.
167703: On a farm in the Molenstraat, people always suffered greatly from the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse). One day, when the farmer's wife went to feed the pigs, she saw the animals sit up on their hind legs and laugh at her. The farmer's wife was ill for a long time afterwards.
167706: At a farm a werewolf always appeared that made passers-by carry it. The hedge there sometimes lay flat against the ground and stood up straight again a moment later.
167714: A woman with her child in her arms was walking unsuspectingly past the house of a witch. At that spot the child suddenly began to cry. The witch came out and invited the mother inside. The witch explained to the mother that other people distrusted her, but that this was unfair because she went to church every day. The mother replied: "That can't be, because the church is too far from here." The witch answered: "If I want, the church will be here in a moment." The mother went outside and told other people what she had experienced. There she was told that the witch had once caused a child to have a fever for thirty-six days. The mother then had a blessing read over her child and was given a blessed little shirt. When she later walked past the witch's house again, the witch did not come out because the child was wearing that shirt.
167738: The Rithaag was always haunted. Ghostly figures came to eat around a table there. Later a pot of money was found in the ground at that spot, and the haunting stopped.
167743: A man on his way to Nijlen felt a cat jump on his back at the railway. The man was flung from one side to the other.
167764: One evening a woman lay almost dead in her bed. The woman had had to fight a large black tomcat all afternoon. That tomcat was in reality a neighbour. The neighbour had caused the death of that man's husband in the same way.
167786: A man struck at a cat he had often seen, but strangely enough could not hit the animal.
167791: One evening a man struck with a club at a black tomcat sitting in his garden. When the man went back inside, he saw that his own mother had lost an eye.
167837: A woman who moved away from Puurs became the victim of a sorceress who always came to visit her. Because of this the woman fell ill and swelled up all over. Only when she visited a relative's house was she briefly relieved of her ailment.
167872: On a farm where many animals died and the animals were often covered in lice, people went to the friars of Bornem. The friars came and laid relics on the beams in the stable. They said the evil was caused by a woman who walked across their yard every Sunday on her way to Mass.
167899: A woman who always saw a dog sitting by her bed in the evening told her story to a priest. The clergyman answered: "The dog will go away and five minutes later the witch will arrive." Five minutes after the dog had run off, the wife of a man from the neighbourhood came to ask forgiveness.
167900: In Okselaar a man was always followed by a little child that jumped onto his back. Nine days later a child died in that man's house. Once, when the man was out on his bicycle, he saw a little child walking there. He asked the child where it came from, but it did not answer. The man could not catch hold of the child and broke out in a cold sweat. The man also saw a light in the sky. As soon as the man was indoors, he saw that the little child had vanished.
167930: A brother and sister were visiting their uncle in Deurne. When a cat came out of the cellar room, the uncle's wife began to stroke it. The woman was jealous of her niece because the cat always went to her. In the evening brother and sister went home by train. When they were about two hundred metres from the station, that same cat was following them. The brother tried several times to hit the cat, but could not. When they got home, the cat was still following them. The boy had had enough and finally managed to stab the cat with a dung fork. Afterwards he did not go to Deurne to see how his aunt was, so as not to cause a scandal, but three days later the aunt died anyway, with three holes in her side.
167949: A woman visited a farm and said: "Look what an udder that animal has." The farmer's wife then said that the cow gave a good bucket and a half of milk. The visitor felt the udder. Two or three days later the cow suddenly gave no more milk. The farmer, who was normally not superstitious, went to the abbey of Tongerlo and had salt and bread blessed there. Nine days later the cow gave milk again.
167958: A farmer who had read too far in the books asked the devil for a barn. The barn would be finished before the cock had crowed three times in the morning. If the devil could manage that, he had a right to the farmer's soul. When the barn was almost finished, the farmer clapped his hands, so that the cocks began to crow too early. At that moment there was still a hole in the barn. Because the barn was not completely finished, the farmer could keep his soul. The devils were so angry that they beat the farmer's head against the wall, so that his brains stuck to it.
167987: Broom was called 'gest', so the broom fields were known as 'geestakkers' (ghost fields). Ghosts wandered on those fields that could not die because they still had to atone for a debt or were waiting for an old promise to be fulfilled. Whoever passed there was pursued by ghosts or ridden by the mare, it was said. The werewolf and Ossaart were there. Elves, black dogs and black cats lived there. When people passed there, they began to sweat and saw the cruellest scenes in their imagination.
168023: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come back to haunt after his death with the words: "Post, where shall I leave you? Post, where shall I leave you?" One day a drunkard answered: "Take it back to the place where you got it!" At that the spirit thanked the drunkard for releasing him.
168025: On a farm the stable was bewitched. The cows broke loose and ran up the walls. When the occupants went to look, they saw that the animals lay in a deep sleep and that their bodies were full of pins. The kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse) had caused this.
168032: A baby was being carried to church by its godparents. On the way they met a witch, who said: "What a beautiful child!" A little later the baby's clothes were full of lice.
168049: A boy who wanted to know whether Genie was a witch put his left foot behind the woman's right foot three or four times. Each time the witch looked back.
168076: A woman from Booischot peddled all sorts of goods, which she carried in a wheelbarrow. Whenever she had sold something somewhere, she gave the children a biscuit. A little boy who had been given such a biscuit one day vomited constantly. After that the people in the neighbourhood advised their children not to accept anything from that woman.
168094: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field came back to haunt after his death in the form of a glowing apparition that called: "Post, where do I leave you, post". One day someone answered: "Leave it where you got it". Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
168095: Behind the station in the Wuitsbergen stood a bewitched house where a constant banging was heard at night. The people fetched the friars, who advised them to pray. The friars also gave them a relic, which freed them from the evil.
168190: In the Prijstraat there used to be a barn where knocking on the roof beams was always heard in the evening. It sounded as if the roof was being struck with heavy hammers. If anyone dared to go into the barn, there was nothing to be heard or seen.
168191: A man always saw a black cat walking over the mantelpiece, making everything fall to the floor. The man went to the priest. The cat always came in through the drain hole for the water. One day the man shot the cat dead. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood lay dead.
168214: A man returning with a friend one night at about eleven o'clock from a visit to his girlfriend saw a great light in the distance and heard a sound like a train. A witch lived in the house the man had come from.
168226: A woman coming back from Blauberg was, to her great fright, followed by a large dog that panted and foamed at the mouth. The next day the woman's brother shot that dog dead in Veerle.
168229: One evening a man saw a large black cat jump on his chest. The man was bewitched by it. He went mad and died.
168234: A man walking along the road always saw a cat jump between his legs. The man took a knife from his pocket and struck at the cat with it. Afterwards a woman in the neighbourhood went about with a red welt on her face.
168245: A man coming home across the heath one night saw a witte madam (white lady) there. When the man was close to the apparition, she disappeared into the roadside verge.
168268: A man coming back from Millegem stopped in at a witch's place for a drink. When the man announced that he was leaving for home, the witch said: "You won't get home." "We'll see about that," said the man, and he jumped on his bicycle. The man had been riding for a long time and no longer recognised his surroundings. In the end he rode back to the café, where the witch said: "I told you that you wouldn't get home." "Yes, but now I will," the man answered. The witch replied: "No, you won't." The man left for the second time and got lost again. When he then came back into the café, the witch said: "Go on home now." After that the man did get home.
168292: A woman with a bad reputation often visited a house. The visitor gave the mother's eldest child a plum. After that the child fell ill and could no longer walk. The doctor could not help, and a penance that was done brought no result either. A while later the mother found a woman who could undo the witchcraft. The people had to do a new penance. Three days later the child was cured. It had had 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness blamed on witchcraft).
168332: A witch had changed herself into a frog. Some people had struck that frog. Later they met a woman who was injured, and so they knew that woman was a witch.
168359: A dead person came to haunt a certain street at night. People were therefore very frightened when they had to pass that spot at night.
168360: A man from Zemst had seen the devil. The devil looked like a gentleman dressed in black and had large horse's legs.
168371: A man went to Lichtaart with his daughter. He went to a house there where he wanted his daughter to work as a maid. "But be careful, because back home they are afraid of my daughter," he said. People believed the daughter was a witch. The girl had been in a house where a baby had just been born. She had touched the baby's little hand, and afterwards the child had begun to cry ceaselessly. People believed the child was bewitched.
168378: Selm decided to tease his uncle Fons because Fons had said: "You can't do anything." Selm made his uncle lose his way, so that Fons did not get home until sunrise.
168419: On a farm on the Bruinbaard along the Kontichse Steenweg there was always misfortune. One time a cow died, another time the animals in the stable had all been untied by morning. People said the place was haunted, and in the end the farmer had to move away.
168442: A man whose cow suddenly stopped giving milk, though it had previously given a good twenty litres, went to the friars of Lier. The clergyman prayed for a while and then gave the man little flowers to put in the cow's drinking water. After that the cow gave two cups of milk. A while later it gave more milk again, until everything was completely normal. The man went and put money in the offering box. He was convinced that a certain woman had brought the misfortune on him. That woman had a bad name and had once touched the cows in the stable. If such a thing is not stopped, the cows become completely emaciated.
168467: One day Sus P. had laughed at a witch, to which the witch had replied: "Just wait, I'll teach you a lesson!" When Sus came back from the fair, he lost his way because he had eaten the sweets he had been given by the witch. Only after wandering in the woods for four hours did Sus get home.
168502: One evening a witch sent her husband off to go for a walk. The man went and was found the next day in Oostmalle. If that witch said: "I want my husband not to speak for three days," then that is what happened.
168526: At an inn all the animals died because of a neighbour woman. After a friar had visited the inn, the misfortune came to an end.
168534: A man coming home in the evening heard rustling in the bushes. A moment later he heard a scream right beside him. So the man ran home as fast as he could.
168562: Some men had shot a hare. When they went to look, they saw that it was a little woman from the village lying there with a gunshot wound. The men themselves had to put the wounded woman on a wheelbarrow to take her home.
168634: When people saw a black cat, they believed it was a witch. Black cats appeared when an accident was going to happen.
168646: A child saw the ghost of his mother sitting in the stairwell. To be able to enter heaven, the ghost still needed to receive half a stuiver.
168671: On the haunted farm 't Rundvoort seven animals died within a year. The animals were sold to a butcher, who could find no disease. The farmer's father-in-law went on pilgrimage to Hakendover, but that did not help. The farmer drove a horse cart to Kessel, because a man lived there who could lift the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse). After that man had been alone in the stable for a while, the problems were solved. Another man also came to that farm, claiming he could make the witch's face appear in a bucket of water. And so the mother-in-law saw her own face in that bucket.
168677: A man who was in a relationship with a jealous girl was always followed by a kitten. One day the man asked: "Well, pussycat, what are you doing here with me?" The cat replied: "Well, Jef, what are you asking me?"
168691: On the ruggeveld there was a low-lying area where bells could sometimes be heard ringing. Those bells were said to have sunk there.
168721: Will-o'-the-wisps moving up and down among the trees were the souls of unbaptised children. Some claimed they were vismoeiers (a kind of glowing insect).
168726: In the past people said that there was a black cat in the woods that was a witch. When passing there, you had to make the sign of the cross so that the cat would run away.
168730: At the Nauweleershoeve a dead person had returned with the words: "They count strictly and they forgive nothing."
168755: A woman died eight days before she was due to give birth to her eighth child. On the day of the funeral the widower heard three knocks on the door. A voice rang out: "Oh husband, oh husband, open your door. Your own wife stands before it." The widower answered: "It cannot be my own wife, for I have none in this world." The man crept quietly outside and went to the neighbours. In the street the woman was seen standing in her shroud, saying: "There are still three pilgrimages to make: one to Duffel, one to Leuven and one to Scherpenheuvel." Then "he saw his wife vanish, brighter than the sun will shine."
168763: One Sunday a friar preached in church that the devil's reign had vanished since the coming of Christ. After mass a man came to the friar and said: "I can't believe all that you preached there. I often go to meetings of freemasons, where the devil is also present, and you should see all that he can still do." The friar wanted to go to such a meeting too. The next day there was a gathering at which everyone had to appear in a tailored suit to be let in. The man would make sure a suit was ready for the friar as well. The next day the man and the friar went to the meeting. They first had to go through a long dark corridor and then came to a large black door where a doorkeeper stood. The two were let in and sat down near the exit. At the stroke of midnight they saw a great fire, out of which the devil leapt. At that moment the friar made the sign of the cross. The next moment the devil cried out in the fire: "Treason, treason." Those present reached for their sabres, but could do nothing because they had lost their power. The devil disappeared without giving instructions.
168778: If you had wounded a cat, you could afterwards meet a person who had a wound in the same place.
168798: In Lille a certain Marie had hidden money in the chimney. After her death Marie came back to haunt to point out the hidden money. But people did not see it.
168809: In a house in Brecht a cat always came in around twelve o'clock. The man grew tired of the game and shot at the cat, which then ran off quickly. The next day it was found that a woman from the neighbourhood had a gunshot wound in her arm.
168819: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps floating over the water were the little souls of unbaptised children. If you struck at such a light, suddenly a great many of them came flying. In reality the will-o'-the-wisps were 'blinkmaden' (glow-worms).
168839: A farmer who was going to mow his field said to his farmhand: "Don't look, eh. When we reach the end of this stretch, all the work will already be done." For the devils were walking behind the farmer, pulling everything up and laying it in heaps.
168846: A man on his way to Merksem struck at a cat with his walking stick at the Hoogmolenbrug. Suddenly the man's walking stick was gone, he began to sweat and could hardly move forward. When the man had finally got past the bridge, he went into the first café he came across for a glass of beer. In that café, to his great dismay, the man saw his walking stick hanging above the mirror. The landlady gave the man his walking stick back on condition that he would never strike at a black cat again. Everyone understood that the landlady was a witch.
168854: A woman lying awake in her bed one evening heard something crawling across the floor. Then the figure crawled onto the bed over the blankets. The woman tried to call out, but could not. She went stiff and felt her throat being squeezed shut. A little later the woman was freed. She had been ridden by the mare.
168865: When the children had just gone to bed in the evening, they saw a white woman coming down the attic stairs.
168869: A man and a woman coming back from the fair around midnight saw a big fire on the street corner. When they went to the same spot the next day, there was nothing to be seen.
168940: In a house where no butter could be made, the woman believed witchcraft was at work. She went to the friars in Bornem. On the way a black cat kept running in front of her feet. At a certain moment the woman felt as if she was being held from behind or dragged through water.
168974: In Neer-Buul near Geel stood a farm that was haunted. The ox sat there on the perch where the chickens slept, and in the evening rotten potatoes were thrown.
168982: Cats you met at night had to be left alone, for they could be witches. If you kicked them, misfortune could befall you.
168990: A woman with a bad name always came into a shop. The shopkeeper made a cross on the road with her wedding ring, hoping the witch would then be unable to come in. The shopkeeper lost the ring. She was pregnant but had a miscarriage. Two years later her ring was found by a farmer who was ploughing.
169024: A woman who lived on the Grijze Berg worked as a maid at the castle of the 'Den Tip' estate. When the woman came home one evening in the dark, she saw a crying child lying on the roadside. A tree had also blown down at that spot. When people went to look at the place the next day, the tree in question was still standing. The crying child will in reality have been a meowing cat. People attributed such events to witchcraft.
169063: A farmer who had bought the Bolkerhoeve had much misfortune in the stable there. All the cows died, and even the farmer and his children did not survive. The farmer's widow remarried and sent for the friars of Dendermonde. The clergyman said: "This is no laughing matter, because it is a serious business." In the end they did manage to drive the evil out.
169087: Three boys went to pick apples at a wizard's place. Afterwards one of the boys could not get out of the orchard; he had to stay standing there. Later they went with the wizard to the town hall, where the wizard had to ask the boy's forgiveness.
169094: Every Sunday during high mass people came to play cards at a bicycle repairer's. When the maid picked up a dropped card one Sunday, she saw that one of the players had a horse's foot. The maid quickly went to fetch the parish priest, who came and drove the devil away with prayers.
169108: On the border between Zandvliet and Berendrecht a white rabbit always crept out of the woods. One night a pot of money was found in those woods. Since then the rabbit has not been seen again.
169136: A man always came to Battel peddling rat poison. People who did not buy poison had to deal with a real plague of rats some time later.
169169: One day a drunkard said: "I wish the devil would take me home." A little later a large black dog appeared, crawled between the man's legs and carried him home. At home, however, the drunkard could not get rid of the dog. So the parish priest had to be sent for.
169173: A man who went to visit his girlfriend in Groot-Vorst was always startled when he heard a chain rattling at the chapel on the way.
169174: A child who was always ill and suffered from an eye ailment had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse). A woman from the neighbourhood had done this to her.
169196: One evening two sweethearts saw a cat walking by the dike of the canal. The boy swore and called to the animal: "You'll come along with us." After that the cat kept accompanying the two.
169223: People who had promised to go on pilgrimage and had died before keeping that promise had to haunt after their death. When people saw a ghost, they usually said: "If you come from God, speak. If you come from the devil, be gone". As soon as the ghost had made its wish known, it disappeared.
169230: A man and a woman went to the friars of Tongerlo because their two-year-old child could no longer walk. "You must give the child salt with bread," the friar had said, "and when you go home you will meet the witch." And so it happened. As long as the child was ill, a swallow always flew around the house. When the child had died, the swallow was seen no more. On that day a slice of white bread lay in the stable.
169239: A woman who woke up at night could hardly move and was completely stiff. She tried to call out, but no sound came. That woman had been ridden by the mare.
169267: A man coming back from 's-Gravenwezel saw two cats sitting on a barrier in the Mathildedreef. He kicked at the cats. When the man went to bed that evening, he saw the cats sitting on a chest by his bed. That must have been witchcraft.
169335: One morning a man saw a young horse walking about and grabbed the animal. At that moment the foal said: "Let me go, for it is me." It was a man who had been turned into a horse by his wife, who was a witch.
169338: On the Innendijck, on the road to the Gelmelslot, there were three roads. There stood an old castle in which Countess Elisabeth van Culemborg lived. Together with the prince of Salm-Salm, this German countess had the church of Salm-Salm built. Where the three roads met there was a turnstile. On either side of the turnstiles sat two white figures that everyone was afraid of. One day five or six people went to that spot, whips in hand. When they had lashed out with their whips, a head with red eyes and a red glowing mouth appeared between the white figures. Then the people ran off to alert the police and the priest. The clergyman said: "Go closer and say: 'If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, vanish.'" Then the glowing head appeared again. The white clothes fell to the ground and the shades vanished in the direction of the churchyard. Then the head also fell to the ground and nothing more was seen.
169340: A girl went to Turnhout with a friend. When the two went back to Weelde later in the day, they met a black cat that would not leave them alone. In the end the girls kicked at the animal. When they arrived in the village, a woman stood in front of them and said: "Go on, kick again!"
169342: A man who lived at the Schellenhoeve on the Achterheide was coming back from 't Goor one evening. He met a cat there and said: "Ah, pussycat, where are you going?", to which the cat replied: "Listen, Suske asks me: Pussycat, where are you going?"
169347: A boy said to his girlfriend: "If you see anything, throw my red handkerchief at it". When the boy came back to his girlfriend a little later, he still had the red pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
169356: A woman returning from Sint-Amands who was having bad thoughts met a sorceress, who told her exactly everything she had thought in the past hour.
169365: In a house where a woman had given birth to her first child, the midwife came by daily to care for the baby. But the child did not grow. At her wits' end, the mother went to the parish priest, who told her the midwife was in league with the devil. The priest gave the mother an Easter nail to put under the threshold, so that the midwife could no longer get in. The mother followed the priest's advice. The midwife never came in again and the child grew up healthy.
169411: People who had been ridden by the moon could no longer find their bearings and got lost. They would then wander about all night.
169415: In Meer there stood a barn that had been built by the devils. In that barn there was a hole that could not be closed. Hens could never be made to brood in that barn. One day fresh straw was fetched to set a brooding hen in the barn. At that moment, however, a voice was heard saying: "Hands off, friend." When the people believed they would have no more chickens, suddenly there were seventeen hens in the barn. The man who lived there quarrelled with his wife one evening. He heard cursing and saw eighty-nine horses' heads appear.
169434: A farmhand owned a special collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. When his master had thrown the collar into the fire, the farmhand was immediately at the oven to save his band.
169438: A man who got into a quarrel with someone at an inn left. He had barely stepped outside when he was surrounded by a hundred cats that meowed menacingly and jumped up at him. The man walked away, but the cats followed him as far as the bridge. There the animals suddenly vanished.
169455: When Nand B. met a cat on his way home one evening, he said: "Puss, you're out and about so late", to which the cat replied: "Yes, Nand, if you hadn't spoken so kindly, I would have broken your neck."
169508: A man walking home one evening around Christmas in 1927 or 1928 met a gentleman dressed in black on the way, who said: "Good day, sir." The man replied, "Good evening." Then the gentleman went on: "Wouldn't you like to sell your soul? Then you'll get everything you want. On a farm near here there is a pond with large white flowers. Pick a handful of those flowers. In the root you will see a man's hand and a woman's hand. Take the flowers with you and at midnight lay them by the big pine tree on the heath next to the poultry farm. A black hen will be walking there. Take that hen, kill the animal and pour the blood into a little pot. With that blood you must write a letter stating what you want to have, and you must also sign that letter." The man thanked the gentleman and went on. He did not, however, do what the gentleman had proposed.
169516: A father whose child was very ill went to the doctor, but the doctor claimed the child was healthy. Then the father went to a man with special powers, who said: "Go to the priest to have bread, salt and water blessed, but don't say who sent you there. I will come this evening". The man had seen at once that the child was full of pins. In the evening he began to pray, and all the pins fell out of the child's body.
169547: In Wiekevorst lived a woman who always had bad luck. One day, when that woman was melting fat, a cat came in through the drain hole for the water. The woman threw boiling fat on the cat. The next day a neighbour's head was completely burned.
169591: At his work in Antwerp, Selm had been given a book of magic by someone. One evening Selm was coming back from the fair with some men. The men decided to have another glass of beer in the Biezenhoed. When a few men announced they wanted to go home, Selm said: "You won't get across that bridge!" And so it was. To get rid of his magic power, Selm had to crawl around the church three times on his knees.
169595: One morning on a farm a horse lay dead in the stable. The farmer's wife lay across the dead horse. Perhaps she had read too far in a magic book, so that in the end she had to do harm to herself.
169596: A man from Osdrecht had become a widower after his wife died in childbed. One day the man heard a knocking at the door. A little later the ghost of his wife came in and said that the man had to dig up money in the stable. The ghost went on: "You must make three pilgrimages for me: one to Diest, one to Leuven and one to Scherpenheuvel. Until those things are done, I will not leave this place." The widower did everything his dead wife had asked of him. He also had a mass said for her.
169618: A man returning from the fair kept seeing a black cat running in front of his feet. He hit and kicked at the cat but could not touch the animal. When the man got home, he found that the cat had vanished.
169631: In Zandvliet a man saw a big werewolf at midnight that jumped on his back. The werewolf was as big as a calf.
169633: One evening a man went to visit a farmer he was friends with. The man spoke to a cat sitting by the roadside: "Pussycat dear, where are you going?", to which the cat replied: "Listen, Suske asks me: Pussycat dear, where are you going?"
169667: A man lying in his bed heard something coming up. It was the mare, which a moment later flew onto him with such force that he almost suffocated.
169673: In 1871 a certain G., who was returning from Wallonia, was murdered by the chapel of Westerlo. After his death the man came to haunt.
169716: When people could not churn butter because of the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse), they went to the monastery.
169764: Two architects were appointed to build Cologne Cathedral. One of the architects sat on the bank of the Rhine, where he was trying to draw a plan for the tower in the sand with a stick. Suddenly a gentleman appeared who took the stick from his hands and made a different drawing, saying: "This is how it must be." The architect had to sell his soul. To get his soul back, he had to solve three questions.
169768: A man who lived near Vremdermolen went to fetch the doctor in Broechem. When he got to the doctor's, someone bumped into him. After that the man could no longer find his bearings. He wandered about until four in the morning and then found himself in a manure pit.
169777: The stable of a pig dealer was full of mice. The man shot at the animals but could not hit a single mouse. What's more, the mice did not run away.
169790: A man sitting in the café saw someone come in who said: "Men, you won't get home tonight." The man replied: "We'll see about that. I'm going home and you keep your hands off me." But the wizard dealt in evil books, and he had touched the man's hand several times. The next morning the man found himself at a place three hours from his home.
169819: A ball was held in Kessel. A girl from the Congregation was not allowed to go to the ball by her mother, but she went anyway. The girl danced with a gentleman until she noticed that he had horse's feet and was therefore the devil himself. The girl died after that incident.
169851: When Pol T. was coming back from 't Kamp at night, he got lost on the Grese heath. Pol went into a house where a light was still burning. In the house beautiful women were dancing to beautiful music. After the man had ordered a glass and said, as was the custom, "Cheers", the women had turned into dancing cats.
169852: A witch went to look at a child lying in a cradle. After that the child began to cry. The parents put a relic under the door. When the witch came by again, she pulled the door open and stuck out her tongue. But she could not come in. One day the witch did visit the people after all. They stoked the fire hot. They put a relic in a shoe and pushed the shoe under the witch's chair. Because of this the witch could not get away and had to confess that every day she stuck a pin into a cushion to bewitch the child. Then the witch pulled the pins out of the child.
169856: On a farm all the animals died in 1914 as a result of the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse). A friar came, but he could do nothing about it.
169873: A hunter saw a hare running in a furrow and shot at it. He hit it and went to the spot where he had seen the hare fall. There lay some wool, and an old woman was getting to her feet.
169887: A scythe stood by a witch's house. Whoever touched that scythe got black spots. The people went to the friars of Tongerlo to see the witch in a mirror. On second thought the friars did not reveal the witch after all, because she was a neighbour of those people.
169905: A man who had been visiting his girlfriend had to go home through the snow along a narrow lane. Because the man thought he had seen a ghost on his way, he quickly went back to his girlfriend's house. His girlfriend's brother came along, but the man would not be reassured. He went back to his girlfriend's house and slept there.
169906: A man with special powers sensed, while in the church of Ekeren, that his farmhand was reading in his book. The man hurried home and read the text again up to where the farmhand had got. When the man met someone on the way who asked for tobacco, the man said: "Money, or else you'll stay standing until I let you go."
169919: A man was cutting clover at three o'clock at night. Suddenly he saw a ghost floating beside the cart, its feet level with the axle. It was the ghost of a man who had once been killed when the cart fell on him.
169934: One evening some young men had lit a fire, around which they jumped, danced and cursed. At a certain moment a large black dog sat growling by the fire. The men grew frightened and made the sign of the cross. Then a loud thunderclap was heard. The dog vanished, leaving behind a strong smell of sulphur.
169983: Witches had to make someone die every year. In Mol lived a witch who had caused many people to die, among them a boy who often walked around near the witch's house and who drowned at a little bridge. The corpses of people who had died because of the witch did not have a pale deathly colour and showed no rigor mortis.
170004: A man dressed as a woman and with horse's legs came into a shop.
170022: A man ploughing a piece of land found a treasure by the side of the road. Since then the calf that jumped onto people's backs between the little chapel and the Bruggenhoeve has not been seen again. With the crowns he had found, the man built a new little house.
170027: A man could free people and animals from the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse). He would transfer the curse to a tree or bush, which then withered.
170034: A man coming back one Sunday evening from visiting his girlfriend got lost, although he knew the way home very well. He had been ridden by the mare.
170047: A man from Breendonk or Oppuurs who had sold his soul to the devil wanted a bigger barn. "Before the cock crows tomorrow, you will have your barn," the devil had said. There was still a small hole in the barn. When a statue of Our Lady was placed in it, she walked away.
170135: Behind the house of a suspected witch, a man shot at a hare. Instead of fur, the man saw feathers whirling about after the shot. Then the animal ran off under the barn door.
170147: On a farm struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse), the cows got swollen udders but gave no milk.
170150: On a farm where the farmer had churned all day, mouse droppings were found in the butter churn in the evening. The farmer believed his neighbour woman was a witch.
170182: On a farm a black cat came begging for milk every morning. The farmer's wife always poured some milk into a saucer. One morning the farmer grew tired of the game and struck at the cat with an axe, and it ran off howling and limping. The next morning the doorbell rang at the time the cat usually appeared. At the door stood an old woman with one leg, begging for a slice of bread.
170194: On a farm where a suspicious woman had been in the stable, animals died. The witch was herself a farmer's wife too, but nobody dared to go and fetch anything from her farm.
170207: A man coming back along the meadows one evening from visiting his girlfriend in Winkelomheide suddenly saw the meadow in front of him moving up and down. He also heard a hellish roar in the air. Chains were rolling down the hill in front of the meadow. Although the man was afraid, he went to have a look anyway. But there was nothing to be seen.
