After the sorceress left, the neighbours came to the midwife and said: "What have you done? She fiddled with your apron strings the whole time. Now you're surely bewitched!" The midwife went inside and cut the strings off her apron. When she threw the strings into the stove, she heard a popping sound and the fire suddenly went out.
179478: A sorcerer had to make a pact with the devil. First he had to pass three tests. The first night he had to wade through water around the church. The second night he had to go through fire, and the third night he had to sign a contract in his own blood.
179532: On a farm near the abbey of Tongerlo the horses were bewitched. It was so bad that fire came out of the roof.
179560: Fourteen cats were dancing around 'de kaak' (the pillory) in Wilmarsdonk. When a man lashed out at the cats with his dung fork, the pack scattered. Some cats called out: "But you haven't got me yet!" Those were witches.
179562: A woman with a small child was visited by a neighbour. The neighbour took the child on her lap and turned its little head all the way round. Then the child's mother said to her: "You had the child on your lap. You did it, and if you don't set that little head right again, you won't leave here."
179586: On a farm in Geel-Zammel the butter churn always tipped over during churning without anyone touching it. One night the farmer saw a cat come into the room and push the churn over. The farmer kicked the cat, and the animal fled howling. The next day the daughter could not get out of bed because her back hurt. That is how people found out that the daughter was a witch.
179605: On a farm there was a cow in the stable that was due to calve in a few weeks. One day a sorceress came into the stable. She rubbed the cow with the palm of her hand. The calf was born far too early and died.
179616: A man walking behind a supposed witch drew a sign of the cross on the ground. When the witch was spoken to by someone a hundred metres further on, she looked back.
179631: A man had shot at a cat at least twenty times without hitting it. He took a cartridge and dipped it in holy water. With the next shot he hit it.
179655: A thirteen-year-old boy who was coming back from the shop with his aunt in the dark saw an umbrella rolling across the road. On another evening the boy saw a stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp) outside. It was the soul of someone who had died unbaptised.
179659: In Putte lived a lord of the castle who had sold his soul to the devil. Because his farmhands did not work hard enough during the harvest, the lord called on the devils for help. The devils were so numerous that they did not even each have one sheaf to bind. Out of boredom the devils then pulled leaves off the bushes. Once, when the farmer set off with his cart, he suddenly saw a marsh in front of him. He sank into it. The horse cart could still be pulled out, but the farmer could not. To drive the devils away, people hung a small chapel at each end of the lanes leading to the castle.
179715: A woman who was ill was visited by a witch who wanted to cure her. That same evening the woman behaved as if she were possessed. The friar came to read prayers over the possessed woman and gave the people a relic to put under the threshold. After that the witch could no longer come in.
179720: Fil had seen a hare in his barn. When the man wounded the hare with an axe, the animal began to bleed and turned into his own wife. A hare only changed shape if one could make it bleed.
179722: A cattle dealer went to a witch and asked whether she had anything to sell. The witch answered: "No, but I'm baking pancakes. If you like, you can have one with me." The dealer accepted the offer. The following night he kept driving around and sweated terribly.
179797: On a farm, peaches were found in front of the door in the middle of winter. A witch had come to put them there. The farmer's wife died after eating the peaches.
179815: A woman who had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel came to haunt after her death because she had not kept the promise. The dead woman appeared to her family to ask them to go on pilgrimage for her; otherwise she could not get where she had to be. A ring of green plants is said to have grown on the spot where the ghost had appeared.
179827: A woman from Retie had married a widower who had several children. Because the woman had not treated the children well, after her death she had to haunt every night to ask for forgiveness.
179833: In a house the milk standing on the third step of the cellar stairs always turned thick. Because the woman of the house believed she was bewitched, she sent for the parish priest. The clergyman blessed the house, after which the problems stopped.
179847: A farmer from Itegem wanted to mow a field of oats, but in his opinion his farmhands were not working fast enough. The farmer stood cursing in the barn doorway, but suddenly could no longer move. One of the farmhands had fixed him to the spot. The priest had to be called to read prayers over the farmer.
179883: A man could no longer sleep. Every time he lay in his bed, he heard noise and rattling. The cows had been untied and made a racket as if they were tearing down the stable. Somewhere there was a rattling kettle. It was put in the loft among the hay, but the next day it was back in the same place. After the priest had visited, things were better for a few days, but afterwards it was the same old story. A woman had come to the farm to buy cows. That woman always spat in her hands when she milked the cows. Since that woman's visit, things had gone wrong on the farm. The farmer's son had hung a holy object under a bridge over a brook behind a farm. When the suspected woman came there, she could not get across the bridge. Only after the witch had removed the holy object could the witch go on. The neighbours saw a white cat crawl out of the farm's loft. They struck at the animal, but missed.
179944: A family in Turnhout had a child that did not grow. When the people looked inside the child's pillow, they found all sorts of things in it. After everything had been removed, the child did grow.
179953: At night Father V. always came haunting with chains that he dragged along the road.
179955: A miller's hand was annoyed by a cat that kept getting in his way. The hand poured a pan of hot fat over the cat. When he came home that evening, he found his wife in bed with burns. The man asked what had happened, and the woman replied: "You should know".
180003: Two men saw a cat sitting on a post somewhere. One of the men picked up the cat and took the animal with him. Because the cat grew heavier and heavier, the man threw the animal away with the words: "You filthy thing!" The cat, however, stayed put and said: "You will put me back where you picked me up". When the man put the cat back in its place, the animal gave him a box on the ear that sent him flying a good five metres.
180008: On a farm where they wanted to take the foal away from the mare, the young animal crawled under the door. That was haunting.
180009: A farmer's wife went with her butter baskets to the market in Antwerp. On the train she sat opposite a strange woman. When the farmer's wife arrived in Antwerp, she could not find her customers and got completely lost. She broke out in a sweat. In the end the farmer's wife came back with her butter. The woman on the train had bewitched her.
180010: In Lichtaart lived a farmhand who went to cut litter by the Snepkensvijver between Herentals and Lichtaart. Suddenly the farmhand saw a little book flying. He picked it up and began to read it. Then his spade suddenly began to jump up and down. The frightened farmhand stopped reading, after which the spade fell back to the ground. When he read on, the spade began to jump again. The farmhand realised he had found a book of magic. When he got home he said to the farmer: "Shall I throw the cupboard open with my cap?" The farmer laughed, but when the farmhand did it, he soon stopped laughing. He wanted to dismiss his farmhand but did not quite dare. The farmhand gave up the magic in time and burned his book.
180076: A man lost his way on his way home. He had a box of matches with him and had to use up all the matches to light his way. Yet he kept ending up at the same spot, because he had been ridden by the mare.
180081: A farmer from Wemmel had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn. The barn had to be standing before the cock had crowed in the morning. At four o'clock at night the barn was almost finished, but when the cock crowed at that moment, all the devils disappeared. There was still a hole in the barn, so the farmer could keep his soul.
180127: People took a sick child to the doctor, but the physician could not help. The child had fallen ill after a woman had come to visit. Ten years later another child of those people was bewitched. That child said: "Mother, that woman grabs me and pinches me."
180131: A man who had gone shooting on the occasion of a wedding was confronted with haunting. As he walked past a house, he saw the hedge there being pulled out.
180134: A girl walking from Heist-op-den-Berg to 't Goor met the same woman three times. The woman said nothing, but the girl was clever enough to walk in the cart track, for there witches were powerless.
180136:
A man coming back from the fair one evening saw six cats jumping around him near the Kapellenberm. The cats held each other by the paws and danced in a circle. The man wanted to get rid of the cats. When the animals asked him what he promised, he answered: "A glass of beer." Then the cats sang: "Had X not spoken so nicely, we would have broken his neck."
Then the cats took the man by the hand to go and drink a glass of beer together.
180162: In Reet there was a child that did not grow and cried all the time. The mother put her wedding ring under the threshold. One day a woman who often visited those people came by. The visitor said: "Oh, may I not come in here anymore?" It was she who had bewitched the child. Now that she could no longer get in, the child became calm again.
180184: In Arendonk lived a woman who bewitched the horses in the fields. There was also a witch who bewitched her own daughter.
180185: A man lay down in his bed in the evening and a little later felt a weight like lead pressing down on him. The man wanted to kick with his legs and wave his arms, but he could not. He tried to call out, but no sound came. He was also sweating terribly. The torment lasted ten minutes and then the man was released. When the man later went through the same thing again, someone advised him to place his clogs crossed in front of the bed. The man did so and was never ridden by the mare again.
180192: On a farm some young pigs had been bought. When the deal was closed, a supposed witch was standing by the sty. The farmer's brother then said: "Now I don't feel easy about it anymore." The next day all the pigs lay dead.
180218: Witches usually turned themselves into black cats. A farmer kicked a cat in the head in his stable. The next day a witch from the neighbourhood appeared with a bandage around her head. The witch was furious and took revenge. Every night at twelve o'clock the farmer fell out of bed and found cat dirt on the carpet.
180226: A farmer who had ten cows and did not believe in witches became poor because all his cows died. The man went to a priest, who freed him from the evil.
180248: Bewitched children cried all the time.
180291: On a farm in Wintham a witch had brought the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) into the stable, so that all the animals there died.
180306: In Oostereind there was a bewitched farm. The people there were often visited by an old woman. On their neighbours' advice, the people locked the door. The witch, however, turned herself into a cat and came in through the water drain hole. In the end they had to close up that hole. After that the people had no more trouble.
180321: A bewitched child cried every evening from eleven o'clock until midnight. A female peddler had entered the house through the water drain hole and had rubbed the child's head. After a small cross was placed under the threshold of that house, the woman never came in again. If the drain hole was closed with a wooden plug, the plug was always gone the next morning.
180327: In the church of Beerzel an Easter nail had been stuck under the door. After Mass a certain woman stayed sitting in the church for a long time, until the sexton finally said: "Go outside, I have to lock the door." The woman replied: "Take that thing from under the door, because I can't get out." The woman was trapped in the church.
180328: In Molenhuizen lived a widow with her daughter. People believed the widow was a witch. A man whose wife had been ill for years went to a clairvoyant in Luik. The clairvoyant made the witch's face appear in a glass of water. The witch had visited the sick woman every day to ask for milk for her cats. When the man passed the witch's house on his way back, his horses suddenly refused to go any further.
180370: On a farm lived a farmhand who could curse like a heathen. The farmer had once said: "If you keep cursing like that, the devil will come some day." When the farmhand was walking home one evening, he was followed by a large shaggy dog. The farmhand grew frightened and remembered his master's words. He quickly made the sign of the cross, whereupon a tremendous thunderclap followed. The dog had vanished.
180390: A man and his wife went to live in a house that had once belonged to a witch. Every night the witch came to churn butter in that house. A black cat always walked on the roof. The forest wardens shot at the animal several times but could not hit it. The friars came to the house, but the people still did not stay living there.
180442: Will-o'-the-wisps followed people. They were the souls of unbaptised children who had been buried somewhere.
180452: A man from Oelegem often visited his parents in Ranst. On the way he had to pass a house where a woman lived who was suspected of being a witch. The man kicked at a cat sitting on the road and a little later saw some twenty or thirty cats. The man fled and tried to go into an inn, but he could not, because the cats were all sitting in front of the door.
180467: A man coming home one evening saw a cat come out of the bushes and said: "Pussycat dear, where are you going?", to which the cat replied: "Jefke asks me: Pussycat dear, where are you going? If you had not spoken so nicely, I would have broken your neck".
180469: If you met a werewolf, you had to throw a red handkerchief at it. The next day the werewolf would still have the threads of the handkerchief between its teeth.
180505: Around All Saints' and All Souls' Day, little lights were often seen above the grass and around the church. They were the souls of the dead.
180513: If someone had been ridden by the mare, a knife was put in a bag and the question was asked: "Where was the mare last night?" The knife would then remain with the person who had been tormented by the mare. A woman who was ridden by the mare one night called out to her husband: "An umbrella over my bed!" Later the woman could remember nothing of what had happened.
180516: A dead parish priest haunted the castle of Begijnendijk.
180523: In the evening a man saw a whole pack of cats appear around his house. Those were the witches of the area. After a while the man went to the priest, who came to read prayers over the house and sweated heavily while doing so. After that the cats no longer appeared.
180563: A pedlar came to a farm where the butter would not churn. The people were advised to put a wedding ring under the butter churn and were freed from their problem. The butter had been bewitched by a woman who lived near them.
180572: In Burcht a strange man had died. The next morning two big black dogs were sitting on the two balls in front of the house. Moreover, the body had disappeared from the coffin, which was filled with stones. People believed this was the work of those two dogs, who were probably helpers of the devil.
180576: On the Wimpelhoeve one animal died after another. At their wits' end, the people went to the monastery for advice. The friars gave them a little lantern called 'the Lamb of God'. The lantern was hung in the stable. The people were also given a small relic to put under the threshold. The next day the witch came up to the door, where she stopped and muttered: "I can do nothing more here." Then she went away. After that the animals on that farm became healthy again.
180608: In Hoevenen a farmer was building a new barn. Because the work was not going well, the farmer said: "It must be finished, even if the devil has to come." Then the devil appeared in the shape of a gentleman. There is said to still be an underground passage connecting that farmer's farmstead with the church.
180611: For a long time there was haunting at the duivelskuil (devil's pit). When people went to look there one day, a black grouse flew up. That was the witch, people said.
180630: A bewitched young man of just over twenty was always gasping for air while saying: "There she is again." That young man died of the witchcraft.
180635: Someone had told a man: "You won't get home today," and he really did not get home. On the way the man was addressed by someone who said: "Now you will get home," and the man did get home.
180651: Near the Dutch border stood a farm whose occupants could curse terribly. At night a horse with chains could always be heard there. The window shutters opened by themselves. People claimed that the devil appeared there at night.
180654: When the Zenne in Heffen had not yet been straightened, there was a castle on the Zenne. After the castle disappeared, a farm stood there. When the Zenne was straightened, everything fell into the water. The lords who lived at the Heffenhof had once promised to give the poor as many meukens (a grain measure) of grain as there were grains in a meuken. Because they could not fulfil that promise, they came to haunt the castle after their death.
180689: In the Molenstraat a man saw as many as a hundred cats jumping in front of his feet. The cats began to bark like dogs. When the man wanted to turn back, the cats left him alone, but when he wanted to go on, the animals raged terribly. The man took the holy object he had in his pocket and held it in front of the cats' snouts. Then the animals scattered.
180729: In Koningshooikt lived a farmer who had sold his soul in exchange for a new barn, to be built by devils between midnight and the first cockcrow the next morning. When the farmer saw at night that the devils came flying with trees and the work was progressing well, he told everything to his wife. The farmer's wife then ran to the henhouse and clapped her hands. The cock immediately began to crow and the devils had lost. The roof of the barn was not yet closed at that moment and no one could close it.
180798: A boy was courting a girl whose mother was suspected of being a witch. Because the girl's mother was against the relationship, the lovers always had to meet somewhere in the street in the evening. One evening a cat came and sat with them. The boy kicked the cat, breaking its leg. The next day the girl's mother lay in bed with a broken leg.
180842: A workman had become bewitched by kicking at a cat. In the evening the man crawled into his bed and no longer moved. The man eventually died in a psychiatric institution.
180844: If you lay down with your ear to the ground on the Oude Steenovenweg, you could hear bells ringing.
180872: Witches could not die if they had promised to go to Scherpenheuvel or to make a donation. People who had made such a promise had to haunt after their death until the promised act had been carried out.
180876: Two men were going somewhere. One said to the other, who was a wizard: "I'll get there much faster than you." The wizard said: "We'll see about that." The man walked and walked and always ended up back in the same place. Only after wandering for hours in the woods did he reach his destination. There stood the wizard, laughing: "I knew I'd get the better of you!"
180900: A man wanted to turn over in his bed at night, but he could not because he was being ridden by the mare.
180918: In 's Gravenhage people were playing cards one evening. At a certain moment a beast came into the house. The beast struck its claw into the door of the room above the cellar, where the farmer's wife was already asleep. That farmer's wife was suspected of being a witch. The claw stayed in the door for years. The card players all ran away.
180929: A woman from Bouwel was suspected of being a witch. A man going to market with a basket met that woman. She briefly touched the basket. When the man arrived at the market, a cat jumped out of his basket. A little later the man found that all the butter had disappeared from his basket.
180971: A boy walking home through a large forest one evening saw a laid table there. There were golden cups on the table. When someone offered the boy a cup, he said: "In God's name", because he did not trust the matter. The next moment the whole scene had vanished. The boy was left holding only a stone cup in his hand.
180976: On a farm in the Moederhoefstraat in Lint all the animals died. A witch from the neighbourhood had brought the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) into the stable there.
180983:
A man often went to visit his girlfriend in the Nieuwmoer. At a corner he always saw a procession of witte wijven (white women). When the man once told the parish priest, the priest said: "Just go back. You won't see anything any more." The man went back, but saw the white women there again. In the end the priest did manage to drive the apparitions away.
Another man coming back from 't Gooreind at night saw that same procession of white women by a little chapel.
180986: A brother and sister were out together when the brother said: "I need to go to the toilet. If you see a dog, throw my handkerchief at it". No sooner said than done. When the man came back to his sister a while later, he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
180987: A man who worked in Berlaar went home on Saturday. On the way he saw a beautiful cat crossing the road, which kept rubbing against the man's legs but would not let itself be caught. The next morning the man was in the Averechten in Itegem and asked: "Pussycat dear, where are you going?", to which the cat replied: "Tistje asks me: Pussycat dear, where are you going? If you had not spoken so nicely, I would have broken your neck".
180990: A man walking along a field path late in the evening kicked at a black cat. The animal stood up on its hind legs and climbed into the air up to the height of the man's face. Then the cat snarled at its attacker: "Little man, little man, if you had not made the sign of the cross this morning, I would have made a little man of you".
181003: A woman always knew everything that happened at her neighbours'. One day on a farm a cow had been slaughtered and hung up. The farm was locked up well and nothing was told to anyone. One morning the sorceress stood there and told everything she knew about the cow.
181017: On a farm where a witch often came by, two children died within eight days. When another child was born, the farmer's wife died. In the stable three cows died. The farmer sold a fourth cow, but had to bring the animal to the slaughterhouse alive. Fearing he would not manage it, he went to the friars, who said: "It is too late, the cow will die." The cow was put on the wagon alive, but the animal died on the way. After that the witch no longer came to visit and the situation improved. The farmer's daughter hanged herself.
181044: A man struck at little lights that came towards him. At that the lights began to scream. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
181101: A rich gentleman had a maid who was a witch. When one of the gentleman's workers lay dying, his wife was desperate. She was pregnant with her ninth child at the time. Someone advised her to go to the friars of Bornem. The woman went there with an uncle and told her story. The friars said to her: "Dear mother, I will help you, but you must be careful, for your husband works with a wicked woman. I will help you, but on the way you must not speak to anyone, and if it is not better on the ninth day, you must write to me." On their way home the mother and her uncle were addressed by a woman who said: "What lovely weather it is, isn't it!" But the two did not answer, which made the woman angry. Not even nine days later the sick man was cured.
181102: When Betje M. lay on her deathbed, nine horses stood on her heart. Betje was a witch. One evening Betje had a visitor. After a while the visitor heard rattling at the door, at which Betje said: "That doesn't matter. It's only the witches." Betje had once sold a dead calf for five francs, while the normal price was only one or two francs. The seller must have been bewitched, because he paid anyway.
181115: The Vrieselhof in Oelegem was a two-family farm whose stable was bewitched. No cows could be kept alive in it.
181140: A girl who always had to cycle to Vorselaar was hindered time after time by a cat, so that she could not make headway. It was an old neighbour woman who turned herself into a cat.
181152: A man with special powers had to do evil, but because he was good-natured, he chose his own chickens as victims. The man also owned an orchard. No thief dared to pick apples in that orchard, because the wizard had once fixed a thief there so that he had to stay sitting in the tree for several hours.
181166: A man saw a rabbit running towards four neighbours. One of the neighbours grabbed the rabbit, whereupon the animal strangely disappeared. A little later the man went to the priest to have two bullets blessed. At first the priest did not want to do it because such things were superstition. When the man kept insisting, the priest put on the vestment in which he said Mass and began to pray until drops of sweat rolled down his face. Then he said: "Can you shoot well? Once you have the rabbit, you must do nothing else with it. You must pick it up and go into your house backwards. Otherwise something could happen to you. You must never sell the bullets. On your deathbed you may pass them on to your children".
181185: A man walking along the stone bridge heard a cart approaching. In the cart sat a small black beast with eyes as big as cups. When the man passed by, the beast jumped away and vanished. Some other men going to Achter-Olen saw the same beast fly over the bridge.
181188: A farmer from Bonheiden was visited by a peddler selling rat poison. "I won't buy it, because I don't need it," said the farmer. The peddler replied: "You'll need it in future." When the man went outside a little later, he saw an army of rats coming. The rats stormed up the cherry tree until it was completely black with rats.
181223: In Noorderwijk lived a man who could make mice. The people told the parish priest. The clergyman then went to the man and said: "Make some mice now," to which the man replied: "That doesn't work in church." The priest asked the man where he had learned to make mice, and the man replied: "From books." The priest then took the man's books away from him.
181226: On the Maloe (?) there was a haunted hut. A man coming back from the market in Balen with some friends decided to have a look in the hut. When he reached the hut he called out: "If anyone's there, come on out." The next moment the man ran off, deathly pale. He never wanted to tell what he had seen.
181230: A child eight days old cried incessantly. The problem lasted until the child was three months old. The evil was caused by a neighbour woman who came to look after the child. One day the mother went to the priest while the father was working in the garden. The father saw the neighbour coming and heard her laughing about his wife having gone to the priest. Yet he had told the neighbour nothing about the visit to the clergyman. After three months the child died.
181250: After his death P. always haunted the same room because he had hidden a basket of apples there.
181270: A man had noticed that his wife was always gone at night, but he did not know where she went. The man heard miaowing in his loft, but when he went to look, there was nothing to be seen. When the next day the man asked his wife: "Did you hear that miaowing too?", the woman pretended to know nothing.
181275: In the old days, when people saw stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps), they did not dare point at them. Stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children, and they came closer if someone pointed at them.
181280: Some hunters thought they saw a hare and shot at the animal. The hare, however, turned out to be a cat. The next day the hunters found that a woman from the neighbourhood had a gunshot wound in her arm.
181296: In Oppem or Brussegem there stood a barn with a hole in it. If anyone tried to brick up that hole, it was open again the next morning. A farmer had such a large harvest that he needed a new barn to store it all. A gentleman came to him and said: "If you sell your soul to me, I will make a barn in one night." The farmer said he first had to ask his wife. The next morning he told the gentleman that he agreed. The devil said: "You must not get up before four o'clock." When the devils were heard working at night, the farmer got up. Because of that the devils ran away, although the barn was not yet finished.
181312: A man lying awake in his bed one evening was seized by the throat and could not move. Although no one could be seen, the man clearly felt that he was being gripped by something or someone. That must have been the mare. Some claimed that the mare was in essence a standstill of the blood.
181313: A pigeon fancier with nine children lost a lot of money because he was dogged by misfortune. Once the man went to a woman who could free him from the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). The woman gave him a white pigeon and said: "Race with this one. She will arrive first and you will win a lot of money." The man bet his entire wages on the pigeon, but the bird never arrived.
181317: In Borgerhout there lived a woman who could take the shape of a dog. One evening a man saying goodbye to his girlfriend kicked at the dog that always wandered about there. The animal limped away. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood lay in bed with a broken leg.
181320: A man coming back from the pub one evening along the Lisperstraat saw armchairs on a corner with people sitting in them drinking. The man was invited to have a drink with them, but he did not trust it and muttered a quick prayer or a piece of the Gospel of St John. A moment later the whole scene had vanished, and the man saw only sods of grass where the figures had been sitting.
181325: Around 1850 there was haunting near the castle of Hollaken. People were afraid to go to that place in the dark. Two strong fellows decided to put an end to the haunting and went there. When the two men were spoken to by a hare, they fled in terror. One of the men came home drenched in sweat and crawled straight into bed. The man claimed that the hare had even come peering in through his attic window.
181380: In Suske's house a strange knocking was always heard. Because his child fell ill, Suske eventually moved. There must have been a witch in the wall.
181407: In a house where a little son was ill, the father went with his two brothers to the friars of Tongerlo. On the way they had many difficulties. Sometimes two women suddenly stood in the road in front of them and would not step aside. At other places they could not get a step further. The friars said to them: "Luckily you did not turn back, for otherwise your son would have died. But now he will certainly recover." And so it happened.
181412: A woman had fallen ill through a witch who lived near her. The woman was given a medal and holy water. She had also been given a prayer she had to say for a certain number of days. During that time she had to put the relic under a stone, so that the witch could not enter her house. The witch came by and stood on the stone, but indeed she could get no further. The woman recovered.
181436: A woman opening the window shutters in the morning saw a cat leap out. She believed that cat was a sorceress.
181439: On a farm they had to send for the priest because the bundles of brushwood were dancing across the floor and the cats were playing with a ball.
181482: A werewolf was a big dog. A werewolf had torn his girlfriend's handkerchief to pieces.
181484: Sorceresses held gatherings at midnight under the tree in the Benedenstraat in Niel. They feasted there and drank from beautiful golden cups. When people went to look at the spot the next morning, the cups had turned into cow horns.
181524: A man who had been travelling in the Netherlands stayed the night in Retie with a woman he did not know was a witch. In the morning the witch said to the man: "A baby was born at your home last night." The witch knew everything.
181554: On a farm, the people suffered from the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) through a neighbour woman. On that farm the animals grew visibly thinner. Other animals did not grow thin but swelled up. The people fetched blessed medals from the friars, which they had to place at the front of every manger. Within a week they would then be freed from the evil. Unfortunately the measure did not help, as the evil was already too deeply rooted.
181584: Poachers and late walkers often saw a shade on the heath carrying a boundary post on its back. The shade called out all the time: "Where shall I take this stone?" One day the forester answered: "Take it back to the place where you got it". Since then the shade has not been seen again.
181587: In the castle on the Muizensteenweg a young nobleman had made a maid of humble birth pregnant. So as not to disgrace his family, the young man refused to marry the girl. The girl knew the castle inside out and decided to take revenge. On Saint Eligius' day the girl cut off the young man's head in a dark corridor. Since then the young man's ghost always wandered the castle corridors on Saint Eligius' day. The ghost held the severed head under its arm and said: "Who will put this head back? Who will put this head back?" But nobody had the courage to approach the ghost. One day a man did walk up to the ghost. But at the sight of the ghost's fixed stare the man was so frightened that he lay in bed with fear for two weeks.
181613: Drunkards who no longer knew how to get home said that they had been ridden by the mare.
181625: Through witchcraft it could happen that the cows in the stable were untied at night.
181632: In a house in Berendrecht a knocking in the cupboard was heard every evening at eight o'clock. The curate was called in, but he did not hear the sound. In the end those people moved away.
181643: The Duke of Salm-Salm often rode to town by coach and then passed the ice cellar, where he said: "Aernout, if you are in there, come out". Then the devil jumped out and sat beside the duke on the cart. In that cellar all sorts of rings, chains and hooks hung on the wall.
181651: In a house knocking was always heard on the cellar door. People went to look, but strangely enough there was nothing to be seen.
181655: A church is said to have sunk in the Diepdal in the Molenhei. On Christmas night bells could still be heard ringing there.
181700: A woman could conjure up mice by throwing sand on the floor. After the parish priest had visited that woman, she had lost her magic power.
181720: A family that had much misfortune was advised to go to the friars of Dendermonde, because they would be able to lift the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) by reading prayers. The mother went to the friars, who said she would be freed, but warned her about an old woman she would meet on a little bridge on the way home. That old woman was responsible for the misfortune. The old woman would speak to the mother, but she had to walk on quickly and make sure the old woman did not touch her. The mother followed the advice and was spared misfortune for good after that.
181725: A statue of Mary is said to have once been found in the Wijngaardbos in Veerle. Because Veerle was a parish of the abbey of Averbode, people wanted to take the statue to the abbey. The statue was put on a cart, but the animals could not pull the cart. In the end it was decided to take the statue to the church of Veerle instead. That went without any problem.
181734: The Uilenhoeve was zwart goed (cursed property). People said that near that farm two little nuns always walked along the road in the evening. They disappeared into the moat around the farm.
181747: One evening a farmer was visiting friends. He saw a cat there and stroked the animal with the words: "Pussycat, are you coming to warm yourself?" When the farmer went home later that evening, he was accompanied by that same cat, which said: "Jan said to me: 'Pussycat, are you coming to warm yourself?'"
181761: A witch sailed across the moat in an eggshell. That witch is said to have done much harm on a farm in Broechem.
181799: At the Puihoeve in Itegem people were playing cards. A farmhand who could not win said: "I'll have to bring in the devil. Then I'll win for sure." Then a black man came in through the back door. The farmhand's luck began to turn. The farmer took a good look at the black man, and when he saw that he had such strange feet, he went to wake the farmer's wife and ask her to send for the priest. The priest came and threw his stole over the farmhand, saying: "This one is mine." The devil replied: "No, he is mine" and struck the farmhand's shoulder with his hand. Afterwards the shoulder was completely burnt. The priest began to pray and said: "You go back where you came from." The devil turned around and left by the back door. A blessed candle had to be lit and people had to keep praying all night until morning came.
181806: Stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. If you saw such a light, you had to make the sign of the cross. The light was then baptised and afterwards it disappeared.
181809: One day a man was visited by a female peddler, who predicted that on a certain day a witch would come by, who would go straight to the stable and do harm there. The man did indeed have misfortune in his stable. Moreover, he had cut his arm with an axe and the wound had become infected. Later the priest was called to bless everything there.
181821: At the Koeketel a ghost dressed all in white walked about every day. Some people claimed it was the ghost of a man who used to live there.
181828: Some men were manuring the field when a witch walked past. Then one of the men began to make strange grimaces. The witch said she had turned that man's bowels upside down.
181843: When people had misfortune with the animals in their stable, they attributed it to witchcraft.
181864: A man who saw an old woman pass by on his way back from the inn was not left in peace in his bed. He was flung from one side to the other, and it went on for hours. When that woman was not nearby, the man had no problems.
181912: A man had heard some witches at one of their gatherings say: "Over hedge and hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar". The man also wanted to fly to that wine cellar, but he made a mistake and said: "Through hedgerow and through hedge!"
181913: As a punishment, a wizard from Charleroi made sure his wife could no longer get out of her armchair.
181938: A farmer coming back from the village at night saw a café standing in the field. Although he had never seen that café before, he went in and asked for a glass of beer. When someone said something, the farmer suddenly found himself standing in the field with a crowbar in his hand; that was his glass.
181969: Some altar boys had heard that witches could not step over a nail from the Easter candle. They pulled the nails out of the candle and put them in the church porch. Because of this a certain woman from the village could not leave the church.
181980: On a farm one morning the chickens all came out with a black comb. A day later they all lay dead in the coop. Someone had been on the farm who had brought the disease in.
182003: In Gierle a witch lay dying. At the foot of the bed sat a black cat. That was the witch's daughter, who was to take over her mother's power. Just as the witch died, someone took an iron and struck the cat dead.
182023: A child that was in great pain suddenly saw a big spider sitting there. The child was being tormented by a witch who stuck pins into a little doll.
182041: People who were ridden by the mare in their beds at night began to talk out loud, but they could not say anything coherent.
182057: A man went through the woods to Noorderwijk to fetch a barrel of beer. At the chapel the man heard beautiful singing and saw two pretty girls jumping into the verge. The man set down his wheelbarrow and a moment later saw two cats leap out of the verge. When he got home, the man crawled into his bed. He died of fright.
182087: A man saw Guldentop coming along a lane with two black dogs. The man looked the strange apparition sternly in the eyes and remained unharmed. When some chickens were stolen from the man, the police did not dare to keep watch in the woods.
182090: A family on the Zwaneven had a child that always fell ill after a female peddler had visited. The people went to the Friars Minor to be freed from the evil. On the way they had many setbacks. In the end they still managed to reach their goal. They took relics home to put under the threshold and pin to the child's clothes. After that the peddler could no longer enter the house and the child recovered.
182097: Near Mechelen a man dressed in black appeared at the fair one day. The man wore a suit and a black silk hat. Suddenly the gentleman began playing all sorts of tunes on an ebony flute. Then hundreds of mice danced and tripped to the rhythm of the music. The longer the gentleman played, the more mice appeared. The owner of one of the fair stalls alerted the police and accused the sorcerer of taking the bread out of his mouth. When the gentleman saw the rural policeman coming, he fled. A moment later the gentleman and the mice had vanished in a cloud of dust. The people just caught sight of two horns and a tail. That gentleman had been the devil.
182112: A twelve-year-old child lay ill in bed. One day the girl was taken on pilgrimage to Brustem. In Brustem the girl was suddenly freed from the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). When she had been home a few days, she suddenly fell ill again. One time she was flung out of bed as far as the cows' manger, another time her bed was found empty and she lay somewhere outside. When people sat inside, the door sometimes flew open three times in one evening without anything to be seen. The girl lay in bed for four, five or six years. A heksenbaas (witch master, a cunning man who fights witchcraft) who lived on the Achterheide said: "When her grandmother dies, she will be cured." And so it happened. The girl talked like everyone else, but she never grew any more.
182132: When people went to make a delivery and came home in the dark, they sometimes saw will-o'-the-wisps at their feet. The people then heard beautiful songs, but could make no headway. They also saw beautiful cats and other animals, but when they kicked at them, they had vanished.
182134: A boy who had pointed at a will-o'-the-wisp was led to the water by the light. Such lights were the souls of unbaptised children. At the water the boy said: "I baptise you in the name of the Father, of the Son". The next moment countless will-o'-the-wisps came flying up and pushed the boy into the water. When the boy said: "I baptise you only in the name of the Father", all the lights had vanished.
182141: Along the Morkhovense baan lay a meadow that was haunted. Some people who had to bring bells to Olen got stuck there with their cart. At a certain moment one of the men said: "Say it in the devil's name and then they'll come out". The next moment the bells and the horses sank.
182165: In the cellar of the Ijzerstein farm the ghost of a dead man came to point out his money. People dug at that spot, but they found nothing.
182168: In a house there was a child that was ill. The child cried all the time and no one knew what was wrong. The people noticed that the child always cried when a certain woman had just visited. They wanted to know whether the woman was a witch and once placed a holy relic under her chair. The woman, who sat close to the stove, wanted to push her chair back, but could not. She knew she had been found out and said: "Go to my house. In the table drawer you will find a little doll with a pin stuck in it. Pull out the pin and the child will stop crying." The people did so and the child suddenly stopped crying.
182177: In a barn built by the devil there was a hole that could not be closed. The next day the masonry always fell out again.
182179: A witch had visited a farmer in Olmen and had touched the cows. When the farmer went to the stable at midnight, the cows flew up against the walls. The 'expert' advised the people to throw away the cows' milk. Three days later the cows behaved normally again.
182189: A woman who wanted to see the ghost of her dead husband once more met someone who said: "I can make him come back". The ghost of the dead butcher came down the stairs dressed in a white waistcoat and with a little stick in his hand.
182207: In the past children were much fatter than now. If a family had a thin child, people said that child would never get fatter if the witch who had it in her power did not want it to. The child could only be cured by having the priest read prayers over it.
182228: A witch caused three children to die by giving them sweets. One of those children died of 'the old man'.
182282: A sorceress always sat in front of the church at midnight. When people drove to the woods to fetch fodder, a hare ran in front of their feet. They struck at the animal with a sickle, but could not get rid of it. The sorceress was behind that.
182315: A man coming home from work one evening with his brother saw a will-o'-the-wisp near the Nete that was quickly coming closer. When the man said, "In God's name," the light flew past. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children, who could beat a person black and blue if that person would not baptise them.
182333: On a bewitched farm the cows crawled in through the water drain hole and went dancing on the table. Witches could bring about such strange events. They could also turn themselves into a cat or a dog.
182348: A woman cutting fodder always saw a cat sitting in front of her. She lashed out at the animal with her sickle, whereupon the cat said: "That way you would cut into my hand". That cat was a witch from Ginderbroek.
182385: A man out hunting polecats at night shot at a cat. The animal disappeared behind a tree and called out: "Suske, you haven't got me."
182397: A boy worked as a farmhand for a man who had special powers. The man owned books of magic, which he had bought for sixty francs at the Oude Markt in Mechelen. The books were fastened together with hooks and eyes and were full of crosses. The man had studied for the priesthood until he was nineteen. Once the man was called in to drive the rats out of a house. He had to send the rats to the nearest house where food could be found. He hesitated, because that was the house of someone who had also studied for the priesthood until nineteen and could therefore send the rats straight back. The man went ahead anyway and told the farmer to build a straw stack in his yard. The wizard made the rats run into the straw stack. The last rat was a very big one. Then the straw stack was set on fire.
182426: At Christmas a farmhand heard the horses talking. One horse asked: "What do you have to do tomorrow?", to which the other replied: "Tomorrow I am going to take my farmer to the churchyard." The next day the farmer ended up under the horse and died.
182429: A girl was riding her bicycle around one Sunday afternoon. At the Voortkapel the girl stopped to rest for a while. She had only just sat down when a black woman came and sat beside her and said: "Oh, what a pretty child you are." It was about four o'clock. The girl became frightened and rode back home. The next day exactly the same thing happened to her. Because the incident repeated itself every day, the girl was taken to the monastery of Tongerlo. She had to be carried, for she felt a terrible tiredness in her legs. The clergyman advised the people to do penance. On the way back the girl was cured.
182443: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were always seen in the evening above the meadows by the Nete. You were not allowed to beckon to such lights, because that was dangerous. People believed that stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children. Some claimed that the lights came from the vapours rising from the marshes.
182448: Some men were sitting around the fire. When one of them cursed terribly, another said: "Watch out, or the devil will come soon." A little later a gentleman dressed in black stood before the men. One of them ran outside and fetched the priest. The priest said some prayers, after which the black man screamed and vanished.
182449: A frog came into a house through the water drain. One day someone touched the frog with a red-hot poker. The next day a neighbour was walking around with a burnt arm.
182490: In Westerlo lived a man who did not go to church. One day the devils were sitting in that man's house. The man took his gun. If he had not been stopped, he would have shot at the devils. The other people could not see those devils.
182498: In a house in Bevel people had put seed potatoes in the loft. Black cats were constantly running around in that loft, ruining the potatoes. Black cats worked together with witches.
182501: From a farm where they could not churn butter, people went to the fathers of Tongerlo. While a father was reading prayers over the butter churn, a black cat suddenly jumped out from under the churn and ran outside. Then the father said: "Did you see the witch now?"
182526: Stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children. If you baptised such a light, it disappeared. A farmer who had a stallicht settle on his horse's harness had struck the light away.
182543: A forty-seven-year-old man gradually fell ill. His hands and feet became paralysed. A cat always came to the farm. People also regularly came to borrow tools. A friar advised the sick man not to lend anything to anyone anymore. The man sat there for four or five years and had to do penance. In the end he died anyway.
182559: If you saw a black cat come in through the drain hole for the water, you were not allowed to touch the animal. If you did, another ten black cats would appear.
182572: A carter coming home at night saw a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp) and said, "Come here, stallicht, I will baptise you." The next moment the cart was completely full of stallichten that wanted to be baptised.
182617: Some people returning from the little chapel of Berendrecht, where they had gone to pray for a sick girl, saw a black cat sitting in the moonlight. The people went to the parish priest. The clergyman only agreed to say prayers over them after they said that otherwise they would go to the higher clergy. After his intervention, however, the priest said: "But it will be too late", and so it was. When the people got home, the girl was dead. The woman who had sat watching over the girl was also someone who dealt in evil, but the people had not known that.
182623: A witch who had learned witchcraft from her mother often came to see a child in the neighbourhood. The child's parents were advised by the priest to keep the witch out or to dress the child in blue. The father went to the friars of the Kluis, where he had to do penance and was given a medal. "Keep that woman out," said the friars, "but the little child will die."
182640: On a farm where no butter could be made, the people went to the friars of the Ossenmarkt, who said: "There is a neighbour woman who will not come in any more." Before that, the people had indeed had a neighbour woman visiting them every day. On the day the people had been to the friars, that neighbour did not come in, not even when she was expressly asked to.
182655: A boy took his girlfriend home after the fair. Because the house was locked, they knocked. The girl's mother answered: "I can't open the door". The two lovers stayed standing at the door and suddenly saw a cow in the street. The boy shouted: "That's your mother!" Later that mother often threatened the boy.
182674: A man who was always reading books saw devils at the table and in other places, with tails as thick as an arm. When the parish priest came to take the books away, the man was freed.
182684: On a farm in Branst the farmer's wife was feeding milk to a calf when an old stable maid with a bad reputation came to stand beside her and patted the calf, saying: "What a fine animal." The next day the calf was dead.
182712: A farmer who was threshing saw a woman pass by, who asked: "Well, is it going well?" After that the farmer could do nothing more. He could no longer lift his flail and said: "You ugly witch, get out of here!" The witch laughed briefly but did go on her way. After that the farmer could thresh again.
182761: A woman had gone to buy eggs in the shop of someone with a bad reputation. When she got home, the woman found a key in her pocket that shone as if it were made of silver. Since she saw the key was not hers, she threw it into the stove. The key burned up like a piece of wood. After that the woman had problems with her son. She took him to the white friars in Dendermonde, where he was given a relic and had prayers said over him. After that the situation improved.
182769: A miller cut off a cat's paw with a knife. When the miller went to bed that night, he found his wife lying in bed and that she had lost a hand.
182776: An old woman with a white cap lived by the church. When that woman stood in the churchyard, the people in the café did not dare to go outside. Three brothers claimed that their little sister had died because of that witch.
182785: On the highway a black cat always prowled around a farm. The people of the neighbourhood were afraid of that cat. Some farmhands took a cudgel and went after the animal. When they caught the cat one evening, they gave it a sound beating, but they did not manage to kill it. The next day the farmer's wife of that farm lay in bed with bruises and lumps on her face.
182853: A weaver always came to Puurs to sell linen. One day the weaver struck at a kitten sitting on a post in front of a farm. Then the kitten said: "Put me back where I was sitting or I will break your neck".
182863: In the old days people planted an elder tree by the well to protect the farm against the evil hand. The evil hand then had no hold on the water supply.
182868: Some people had told a drunkard that somewhere a dead person came back in the shape of a foal. Mockingly the drunkard shouted: "They say it's haunted here, let it come!" When the foal came running up, the drunkard ran away in fear.
182879: A man from Achterlee went hunting in 't Ven. He saw a hare sitting there and hit it. Strangely, the hare was not hurt. It ran to the hunter and sat up on its hind legs.
182895: A mother going to the market with her child met an old woman, who stroked the child's head and said: "What a handsome little fellow you are." After that the child became seriously ill. The child was taken to the friars for advice, who blamed the misfortune on the evil hand. The child remained ill all its life.
182918: A wizard could make mice with copper tails appear. He could also make money, but when he spent the coins, they turned into slices of carrot. One day the wizard had to go to prison. Before he was even under lock and key, he was already back in the inn where he had been fetched from.
182976: A sick girl always began to wail at the same time. The girl had been struck by the evil hand. The people went to the friars of Tongerlo, who gave them a relic to hang around the girl's neck. After that the child recovered.
182990: A farmhand who had gone to look at the pigs with a witch was covered in lice after the witch nudged him with her elbow.
183018: A boy became very ill because he always got sweets from a neighbour woman. The friars of Tongerlo gave the boy's parents a relic to put under the threshold. After that the neighbour could no longer get into the house.
183024: A man wandered about for a long time and kept seeing the Nete in front of him. In the end the man took off his trousers and walked through the water. Then he again wandered about for a long time and ended up in the Smidstraat in Berlaar, where he stood in front of the Burchtgracht. He waded through it, then walked over the garden beds and fell into a furrow. After that the man could find his bearings again. If a lost person had sat on the ground, he was released.
183071: One evening a woman went to sleep at the neighbours'. The neighbour's husband had died and she did not dare stay in the house alone. On the way to the neighbours' house the woman suddenly could not go on. She sweated water and blood and had the greatest difficulty reaching her neighbour's house. When she told the neighbour what had happened, the neighbour said she had been ridden by the mare.
183083: A man conjured a good ten thousand rats onto the roof of a house. The rats all held their tails up. The occupant of the house stood by and said: "They may stay one more night, but tomorrow they must leave." The sorcerer saw to it that the rats were gone the next day.
183091: On a farm struck by the evil hand, all the animals fell ill and died. The people went to the friars of Dendermonde, who advised them not to go outside before sunrise or after sunset. They also had to pour holy water into the well. The people followed this advice, after which the situation improved.
183099: The fish hill was badly haunted. A man ploughing there saw a woman with white mice running about, which a moment later had all vanished. The man could conjure those mice up.
183102: In Mechelen lived a woman who always bewitched her husband. The man became completely emaciated and sometimes had to dance all night long.
183103: On a haunted farm the ox and cart came in through the water drainage hole.
183109: A witch could lift the mill on the corner of the Jos Reusenslei and the Eugène Verelstlaan. When the witch dug up some earth, she could make rats and mice appear.
183114: In Wijnegem two unmarried women had died. In the house, which then stood empty, the dead women came knocking on the walls for three nights in a row.
183159: A mother noticed that a woman was always looking into her house through the window. One day that woman came to bring a jug of milk. As she poured the milk into a bucket, she dropped the jug, which made a loud bang. After the woman left, the mother said to her husband: "You went and bought fish there. Now you see what comes of it." When the man then went outside, he saw that his bicycle tyre was flat. The tyre had burst when the woman dropped the jug.
183189: A girl who had become pregnant by a soldier who had abandoned her fell into a coma and did not know her baby had been born. The girl's mother took care of the child and had it baptised. On the way to the church for the baptism, the people saw a woman approaching. The mother said to the midwife: "Watch out, because X is coming!" X wanted to see the baby, but the midwife would not allow it. Still X managed to stroke the baby's cheek and say: "Oh, my sweet little darling." Then the baby began to cry. The child never stopped crying and died three weeks later. By then it was completely emaciated.
183210: A man was always being thrown back and forth on the road. One day the man took his uncle's gun with him. When the man came home that day, a cat kept jumping against his legs and would not be chased away. The man took his gun and shot at the animal. The next moment the cat turned into a big dog. The man shot again, after which the dog became as big as a lion. The man fired another shot and the lion turned into a little woman. The man was about to shoot once more, but the woman said: "Surely you're not going to shoot me dead, when I'm so fond of you!" The man made the sign of the cross and saw the woman vanish.
183238: In a house where cards were played every evening, a neighbour came to join in one evening. At a certain moment the neighbour said: "It's a quarter to nine, I have to go home." One of the card players said: "Stay ten more minutes and you'll still be home by nine. If you don't stay, you won't be home before twelve." The neighbour left anyway and wandered about until at midnight he heard the bells ringing in a church tower and could find his bearings again.
183252: For two months a woman had been deathly ill every Friday. Only on Saturday did she feel better. The woman called the doctor, who gave her a little bottle and said: "If it is not better in three days, it is serious." After a while the woman realised who had done this to her. She had been visited by a pedlar woman who came to sell something. The previous time the woman had bought something, but this time not, with all the consequences that followed.
183271: A witch is said to have lived between Tielen and Rielen long ago. That witch kept a bull at home. But all the cows the bull covered died after a short time. In the end the farmers took their cows elsewhere.
183291: Miel C. from Olmen often visited his girlfriend in Balen. Every time Miel came home, he could be heard shouting from far away. On the way, Miel was always set upon by dozens of cats.
183306: In the old days people often gathered in the evening in the Laarhut to tell stories by the hearth. The next day everyone knew what had been told there that evening. The people who had been in the hut found this strange, but they had noticed a black cat that had come into the hut through the water drain. They believed the cat was a witch. On the next occasion the owner of the hut sat down beside the drain with a knife. In this way he managed to wound the cat. The next day a woman from the village was walking around with a bandage around her arm.
183319: After her marriage a woman went to live in a house where a witch had lived. That woman's first and second children died. The neighbours said: "You will not keep a single child alive, because the witch said: 'Whoever moves in here after me will have more dead children than living ones.'" The woman did not really believe it, but went to the friars of the Kluis anyway. A friar came to bless the house, after which the woman had no more problems.
183328: A large tarpaulin had been stolen from a farmer. The maid said: "I will make sure the thief brings it back, but you must not look." Otherwise people would find out who the thief was. The farmhand crept into the barn and looked anyway. So he saw that the rag-and-bone man brought the tarpaulin back.
183330: On a farm in Wilmarsdonk the farmer and his wife always went out on Sunday morning. The farmhands would then seize the chance to fry bacon. But a cat always appeared and took the bacon out of the pan. One Sunday the farmhands poured hot fat over the cat. In the village a little old woman lay in bed with burns.
183380: A doctor often heard people in his practice talk about the evil hand. On a farm where the milk was sour every morning, for example, people also believed the evil hand had something to do with it.
183386: A farmer who needed a bigger barn made a deal with the devil. "If you give your soul, your barn will be standing," the devil had said. When the farmer got up one morning, there stood a barn that still had a hole in it. The devil wanted his soul, but the farmer said the barn was not finished and so could keep his soul. People tried several times to close the hole, but did not succeed.
183411: Two girls out for a walk saw a woman walking in the distance. One of the girls said: "Shall I make her look back?" and she placed her foot crosswise on the woman's footprint, after which the woman looked back and began to scold the girl.
183426: A mother whose children came home from school on Saturday afternoon sent them out to play a little longer so she could prepare the meal. As the children walked home, they saw a big black dog. In a hedge they saw a doll hanging. Further on was a shed in which a horse's head was hanging. A mouse was trying to catch the horse's head. The next day the mother told the priest what her children had experienced. The priest came to the spot with his new book and read from it. Afterwards one of the children saw a little headless man walking through the corn.
183427: A family in Retie had to deal with the evil hand. The maid who worked there was a witch. A child is said to have died after the witch had been near it.
183435: Some men were playing cards. One of them mocked the devil. A little later a gentleman came in and joined the card game. When the men wanted to pick up a dropped card, they saw that the gentleman had horse's feet.
183525: A nun saw the ghost of a dead nun with a wooden leg appear. The ghost said: "Go and pray, for I am still in purgatory". Some time later the dead sister appeared again to let it be known that she was in heaven. The ghost left behind a scent that could be smelled throughout the convent.
183531: Around midnight a witheer (Norbertine canon) haunted the Rosdijk, reading his breviary. That priest had once been expelled from his order.
183558: A woman going to the shop in the Vijf Straten was followed the whole time by a cat. "If you are a witch, you will stay standing there", the woman said. When she came back from the shop, the cat was still there and the woman said: "Go on, now you may go". The cat ran off at once.
183564: In a house where a cat always came, people struck at the animal. However, they could not hit the cat.
183568: When a witch had no one in her power, she had to torment herself. Usually she would then prick her skin with pins.
183585: On a farm there was a sick child that screamed all day. One day a sorcerer came by and said: "I will rid you of it. You must make a big fire and I will make the witch come." The witch came, and she had a doll with her that was full of pins. The pins had to be pulled out one by one. Each time the witch pulled a pin from the doll, the child jumped up in its cradle with pain. When that was done, the sorcerer said: "Now you still have another doll somewhere. If you do not go and fetch it, you will be burned alive." The witch did not want to fetch that doll. Then the sorcerer made the witch go right up to the fire. Then the witch gave in and went to fetch the other doll as well, to pull the pins out of it one by one.
183590: A skipper saw a woman walking in a shipyard and said: "Now she is here, and yesterday she was still in the Netherlands!" That woman was a sorceress.
183606: Between Heultje and Meerbeek a witch who 'came back' always appeared. A man playing cards with some friends had to pass that spot to fetch a hood; in winter people wore hoods. When the man saw the witch sitting there, he made a big detour. On his way back the witch was sitting there again. The next morning the man had grey hair where his head had not been covered by his cap. The grey hair was shaved off in the belief that it would grow back normally, but that turned out not to be the case. Some people went to look at the haunted spot and found a broom bush there instead of a witch.
183607:
A werewolf roamed about in Meer. It looked like a big pig with long hair. If you met the werewolf, you had to throw a handkerchief at it. The wolf would then tear the handkerchief to pieces.
The werewolf is said to have once jumped on the back of a passer-by at night. That man could not get home and had to walk around all night.
It was said that a werewolf was a person who had put on a wolf skin.
183610: At the Vrijbroekpark on Stuivenberg there were tales of golden treasures and a golden saddle supposedly hidden there. An eighty-five-year-old woman who lived on Stuivenberg said the field was full of gold. On Stuivenberg there was also a telephone pole where a ghost appeared every night. That haunting woman came every night to guard the treasures from the telephone pole.
183631: On the Duinberg lived a woman who owned books. That woman was always looking for herbs on the heath. On the Duinberg another woman lay tossing in bed because she always felt pain, as if awls were being stuck into her body. People held the witch responsible. Someone had once seen the witch sticking pins without points into a small doll.
183643: At the Berendonkse Hoeve the horses were always foaming at the mouth at night. A woman with loose hair could be seen dancing in the doorway. In the old days, when people had misfortune, they attributed it to the evil hand.
183662: A man on his way to church saw a kitten and said: "Poor kitten, warm yourself, kitten," to which the animal replied: "Wait, I'll get you yet." That same evening the man's bed was full of rats.
183682: A farmer had no money to build a new barn in which to store his harvest. The farmer made a pact with the devil, who would build him a new barn in one night in exchange for the farmer's soul. The farmer's wife learned what had happened and began to pray at night. Then the woman went with a lantern to the henhouse, where the cock began to crow early. Then the devils left the unfinished building. The hole in the barn could never be closed.
183685: Around midnight one was not allowed to go to the churchyard, because then the witches held council there in the shape of owls. They discussed who would have to die the next day.
183723: A man cursed a lot because he consorted with the devil. In the evening the devil often came to visit him. If he then didn't dare go outside, everything in his house began to rattle. The plates fell off the mantelpiece and everything on the table fell to the floor. If the man waited a long time, it seemed as if his whole house was being torn down, and he had to go outside. Out there a very big black tomcat would be walking around. Around that tomcat ran many little kittens. Those little kittens were helpers of the great devil. Once the man had calmed the devil, he left. The devil never came into the man's house when he had visitors.
183786: Once a year a man saw the ghost of his dead mother appear.
183799: A woman who would not believe that the witches always held gatherings in the wine cellars of Cologne once went to look. When one of those present sneezed, the woman said: "God bless you!" The next moment all the witches had vanished.
183834: A farmer had seen four times how a cat had stuck its head through the drain hole for the water. When it happened the next time, the farmer chopped off the cat's head. The head rolled away and said: "If you had struck a little harder, you would have struck my little heart."
183846: A man from Oelegem who went to visit his brother in Ranst had to pass a farm where a strange woman lived. That woman could only walk if someone held the ribbon of her apron. If no one did, she could not go and milk the cow. When the man walked past that farm, he kicked at a cat. A little later as many as fifty mewing cats appeared. As soon as the man was past the barrier that marked the boundary of the land belonging to the farm, the cats had vanished.
183863: A man saw a black cat jump in through the window and climb onto his bed. The man had to fight until the sweat rolled down his face to chase the cat away. In the end the animal jumped under the bed and then down to the fire. There the man managed to beat the cat to death. The man believed it was a bewitched cat.
183888: Someone came to a farm peddling rat poison. The farmer said to the peddler: "Oh, you and your rat poison. I'll catch the rats myself." The peddler replied: "Farmer, you have many rats now, but you'll get many more, for it's all the same to me where I put them." Some time later the straw in the barn was teeming with rats and mice.
183895: In Beerzel the miller and his hands were plagued every night by a pack of cats while they were dressing the millstones. One night one of the hands cut off a cat's paw with his sabre. The next morning the miller's wife lay in bed with only one hand.
183932: At ten in the evening, near the Klaveren Boer, a man met two barefoot witheren (white canons, Norbertine monks) who grabbed him by the legs and threw him into the wet meadow. The man raised his hand and waved at the clergymen. The witheren waved back.
183950: At the Borcht in Vorst bears always appeared at night, lying with their paws in the air.
183984: A man coming back from café De Roos felt a cat climb onto his shoulder. He believed the cat was a witch.
183996:
A shopkeeper had put her child to sleep in the cradle. At a certain moment she heard one of her older children calling: "Mum! Mum! There's a witch with our baby!" The shopkeeper hurried to the kitchen and saw a woman shaking her child about. The shopkeeper grew angry and sent the visitor away. Then she called the doctor because her child had a strange expression on its face. The doctor said nothing, so the worried mother went to the priest. The priest came with her to the shop and said there: "Children in the room and the people outside." Then the priest began to pray until he was drenched in sweat. After the priest's visit the child recovered.
The witch suffered greatly afterwards because the priest had prayed away her magic power.
183997: When Jan M. from Kwaadmechelen was taking his girlfriend home in the evening, he saw a cat sitting in the churchyard and said: "Puss, you're still out and about so late", to which the cat replied: "If you had not spoken so nicely, I would have broken your neck!"
184064: In Wilmarsdonk the witches danced around the churchyard. When the witches' leader said: "Today it is through hedgerow and hedge", the witches had to fly through the hedgerows and hedges. They then had scratches everywhere when they arrived at their destination.
184081: A woman who was home alone one afternoon received a visitor she had never seen before. The visitor said: "You should check the child's bed, because there is something in it." The woman was startled and went to look in the child's bed. When she pulled back the blanket, she saw a large beast sitting in the bed. The frightened woman ran downstairs, where she found that the visitor had vanished.
184111: In Dendermonde there was a little child that would not grow. The child was always visited by a neighbour woman. A priest advised the child's parents to once seat that neighbour by the hearth on a chair with a holy relic beneath it. When they did so and let the fire grow hotter and hotter, the neighbour was forced to free the child. She took a pincushion from her pocket and pulled pins out of it. As the witch did this, they saw the child relax.
184120: A mother's child died one day after birth. The child had been strangled, but the finger marks on its neck were too small to be human. A year later the woman became pregnant again. That child too died a day after birth. Then the woman went to the doctor, who accompanied her to the friars on the Kluizeplein. During the delivery a friar came to the house and sealed the dwelling up thoroughly everywhere. Only the water drain was left open. As the friar sat praying, having put a kettle of water on the stove, he saw a toad come out of the drain at the stroke of midnight. The clergyman poured the boiling water over the toad. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood lay in front of her door with burns. A little later that woman's child came to ask whether the newborn was a boy or a girl. When the child was asked why it wanted to know, it answered: "Mother is all burnt and she asked". The friar then went to that woman to read prayers over her.
184131: A man went to the abbey of Tongerlo for a bewitched child. "Sit down and follow the Mass very carefully," the friar told the man. After that the child quickly got better.
184138: Some children always had to pass the churchyard in the morning. Thick chains hung on the graves there, rattling in the wind. One day the children were followed by a grey cat all the way into their house, where the cat crept under the bed. People did not manage to chase the cat out from under the bed. When the bed was moved the next day, the cat had vanished without a trace. It must have been a witch.
184158: In Bouwel lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. People coming from Herenthout and walking past that woman's house often saw fifteen or twenty cats there.
184167: A boy who was going to the fair through the woods with his girlfriend gave the girl a red handkerchief when he had to go to the toilet. The girl saw a big black dog coming and threw the handkerchief at the beast. When her boyfriend came back a little later, she saw that he had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
184170: In Merksplas there used to be a large oak called the 'cat tree' or the 'witches' tree'. The tree stood just outside the village, about a hundred metres along the road to Weelde, at the bend towards Hoogstraten. Two men coming home one evening saw a meowing cat sitting in that tree, which said: "X said to me, little pussycat, warm yourself". Then the men ran away as fast as they could. It was the cat of the farmer they had been visiting before. The men had not known that the cat that had been lying by the peat fire was a witch.
184176: Between eleven and half past eleven a man went from Oostmalle to a road mender in Sint-Lenaarts. It was always said that the road mender's wife was a witch. On the way the man saw a tall woman dressed in white walking, whose dress kept flapping back and forth. The man ran away in fear.
184202: A woman who was ridden by the mare was in a state between sleeping and waking. She saw her husband walking back and forth. One was not supposed to put one's shoes straight in front of the bed at night, because then one could fall victim to the mare.
184214: A man went with a wheelbarrow to fetch his mother, who had been to town. In the Spookbos the man saw a beautiful rabbit. He wanted to grab the rabbit, but always missed it. Strangely, the mother could not see the rabbit.
184221: A man who went catching birds with tar had to fetch a stick in the woods by moonlight. Suddenly, to his great fright, the man saw a kitten there, and he dropped his knife. The man ran away but bumped into a small tree. Further on he had to cross a ditch, but landed in the water, so that he came home soaking wet and scared to death.
184242: A farmer from Niel could no longer churn butter. What is more, ten of his twelve cows died. A pig and a horse died too. The parish priest came to read prayers over the farm, but that did not help. They then went to the friars of Dendermonde, who advised them to drive the next day in a closed coach with two horses to Niel station. There they were to pick up one of the friars.
