Once the friar was in the coach, he began to pray. The horses sweated terribly. The friar arrived at the farm and wanted to enter by the back door, but only succeeded on the third attempt. Then the clergyman said to the farmer: "Tonight at twelve o'clock you must sit by the water drain and strike at everything you see". At midnight the farmer saw a toad come in and cut off one of its legs. The next day it was found that a neighbour had lost an arm. Nine days later the neighbour died of her injuries. When the neighbour lay on her deathbed, a black cat was let into the room. Afterwards that cat was killed. The friar came to the witch's house to burn her papers. That was quite a job, because the fire kept going out.
184262: In Larum there was a place called 'Heksenbos' (Witches' Wood). The witches from the area came there in the evenings to dance and feast. A man passing the wood heard music and saw a good hundred witches dancing in a clearing. The witches wore fine clothes and gold rings. When the man made the sign of the cross, the clearing was suddenly empty.
184269: A woman staying in England during the war had been invited somewhere for tea. When she left in the afternoon, she met a gypsy who said: "It will take you a long time to reach your destination." The woman had set off at four o'clock with her two children and was still wandering about at midnight. She saw a policeman and asked him the way home. Then the woman realised she was standing right in front of her house.
184272: Three men sat in the café boasting that they were afraid of nothing. As part of a bet, one of the men had to fetch a skull from the charnel house at night. When the man picked up a skull, a voice rang out: "Stop, that is my mother's head!" The man then took another skull and heard: "Stop, that is my father's head!" The man took a skull for the third time, and the voice said: "Stop, that is my brother's head!" The man answered: "Yes, they are all yours, but this one is coming with me anyway!" and left with the skull in his hands. On the way to his friends in Veerle, the man saw an ugly beast with eyes like fire sitting in the middle of the road. Terrified, the man dropped the skull and ran to Veerle, where he dropped dead in front of his friends.
184333: A boy was coming back from the rehearsal of the brass band. By the churchyard the boy caught a little white rabbit. He took the animal to the café to show it to his friends. In the café, however, the boy found that he was holding not a rabbit but a handful of little bones. The friends said to the boy: "Take that back to the churchyard quickly and make sure you don't drop a single bone, or you'll be in trouble." At the churchyard the rabbit jumped out of the boy's hands again.
184344: At a baptism the child's godfather said to the midwife: "There you go, now you're taking a sorcerer home!" Everyone laughed, but when the boy grew up he really could work magic. When he took sand in his hands, mice crawled out of it. The mother went to the parish priest and told him. The clergyman replied: "Go home and ask the boy how he makes those mice." The mother asked, but the boy could no longer do it. The priest had cured him in the meantime.
184349: A maid working for a farmer's wife saw how, during milking, the farmer's wife conjured a whole lot of little white rabbits onto the bucket. The maid wanted to quit, but the farmer's wife said: "They won't do anything." A little later the rabbits drank the bucket empty.
184356: A man living on a large farm on the Sijshei had stacked bundles of wood in tens. One evening he saw the bundles being thrown from one side to the other. Strangely enough, the next day the bundles were simply back in their place.
184365: A girl was often visited by her uncle, who was a priest. One day the girl went with her uncle to her parents, who ran a café. Her father was sickly and always sat on a chair in a corner. The priest saw at once that the evil hand was involved and sent his niece to the parish priest. At first he did not want to help, but when they kept insisting, he went along to say prayers over the sick man. When the girl went to feed the animals in a shed, the parish priest heard a devilish din there. He said they must no longer accept potato peelings for the animals from a strange woman. When they followed this advice, the man recovered.
184415: A mother was annoyed that her little son always climbed onto the roof, because she was afraid he would fall one day. One day a wizard said to the mother: "I'll break him of it. He won't get down until it's nearly night, and then he'll have had enough". And so it happened. When the wizard was dying, he kept rubbing himself with holy water to protect himself against the devil.
184423: A man going from Brecht to Zoersel to visit his son suddenly saw fire on the heath in the Hulsebossen. Some men asked him: "How do you like it here? Aren't you afraid?" The man said he was not afraid, but he wandered about until dawn.
184454: In the kleine heide (small heath) lived a witch who always went eavesdropping at the doors of houses in the evening. If she heard someone coming, she turned herself into a black cat.
184490: On a farm in Wommelgem many animals died. A man who had learned from a priest how to say prayers against bewitchment advised the farmer to dig up the stable. When they did, they found bones everywhere in the ground. The man said prayers over the place, after which there was no misfortune for a long time. The culprit was a woman from the village.
184511: A man had kicked at a black cat. The next moment the man fell backwards and could no longer find his bearings.
184515: A farmer who owned seven cows had bought a goat from a neighbour woman. Shortly afterwards the farmer had misfortune in his stable. Now a cow died, then a pig. The cows also gave hardly any milk any more.
184529: On a farm the maids were mowing buckwheat. There was a festive occasion somewhere, so the maids would rather have stopped working. The mistress said: "Go on, that's fine," and she placed a mown bundle at each corner of the field. Then she clapped her hands, after which all the buckwheat stood up and the work was done.
184534: When a child drowned in a small puddle, people believed a witch had done it. Otherwise the child could not have drowned in so little water.
184538: In a house where three children were ill, a supposed witch said: "One more will come and it will be ill too." And so it happened. Once the people had put a relic under the door, the witch could no longer get in.
184573: A woman baking bread was visited by a witch, who said "good day" and then left again. A little later a neighbour came by and said: "Your bread will fail now, because I saw the witch coming out of here and that's no good." The woman laughed, but the neighbour was right. The bread would not bake or burned completely.
184581: A man who worked in the cement factory in Niel had the habit of resting for a while at midday. At a certain spot against the wall the man always found it hard to breathe. He would then jump up dazed and leap about without seeing anything. Everyone who took a nap at that spot was ridden by the mare.
184595: A farmer's wife had two maids. Whenever the maids had to go and cut grass for the animals, a frog was always hopping about. When the maids came home, the farmer's wife knew everything they had said while working. One day one of the maids cut off one of the frog's legs with a sickle. When the maids came home, they found that the farmer's wife had lost a leg.
184597: On a farm a woman came into the stable, began to stroke the goat and said: "You do have a lovely goat!" The next day, however, the animal was ill. The farmer went to the priest, who came to say prayers over the place and said: "If it fails now, things look bad!" While he was praying, drops of sweat appeared on his face. But it worked, for the goat recovered.
184617: A farm gave lodging to a French soldier. The soldier often went to the café and never came home before midnight. He then made so much noise that he woke everyone up. Moreover, the people had to leave their door open until the soldier was home. The farmer had had enough and told the soldier he would lock the door and the soldier would have to find his own way in. The farmer did so and was astonished to find the soldier in his bed the next morning. This happened for several nights. When someone kept watch, that person saw at two in the morning how the soldier threw his cap against the locked door. The next moment the door swung open, although two bolts had been drawn across it and a heavy table stood against it. When the soldier learned that he had been seen working magic, he became angry and said it would end badly if they did that again.
184646: A woman had promised to go on pilgrimage for her sick mother. When the mother had died, the daughter thought there was no longer any point in going on pilgrimage. Whenever she was working somewhere alone, she always felt something sitting on her apron, although nothing could be seen. At confession the priest advised the woman to go on pilgrimage after all. Since then the woman has felt nothing strange any more.
184656: A mother was walking through the fields with her daughter when the girl suddenly said: "What lovely wheat." The next day the field was completely black.
184659: A skipper always saw little lights when he was sailing at sea. Those lights were the souls of unbaptised children. As soon as the lights were baptised, they flew up.
184666: A poacher from Sint-Theunis had often tried to shoot a rabbit but could not hit the animal. When the man loaded blessed seed into his gun, he did hit it. The next day an old woman from the neighbourhood had a wound on her hand.
184725: A miller could not keep any hand in his service, for they always died. When another candidate turned up, the miller warned the young man. He nevertheless wanted to work for the miller. When he had been in service for about two months and was grinding one night, he saw a cat jump onto the sacks. The hand took a sabre and cut off one of the cat's paws. The next morning the miller's wife lay in bed with only one arm.
184770: A man who had converted to a 'new faith' came back to haunt after his death in the shape of a black dog. The dog appeared in a garden under a 'knoeselbos' (?).
184788: In a café in Branst sat a man who wanted to go home. The landlady looked him deep in the eyes before he left. The man had walked only fifty metres when he saw a hedge standing across the road. The man could not get through and went back to the café in fear. When his friends then went with him and came to the same spot, the hedge had strangely disappeared.
184815: A four-year-old boy became disabled because he was always given pears by a witch. The friars of Tongerlo advised the boy's parents not to let the witch in any more. Later the little boy had one short leg and one long leg.
184822: People who lost their way were bewitched. Witches were always women.
184825: A man always went to play cards in a café on Sundays. But the man could never win anything, until the landlady, who was a witch, came to sit beside him. After that the man always had good cards. So one evening he managed to win more than two hundred francs.
184851: Sorceresses could turn themselves into black cats. In that shape they crept into bed with children. They would then lick the child, which made it ill.
184869: A man claimed that he had had to carry a werewolf in the evening, which left him drenched in sweat.
184870: If you saw a suspicious woman, you had to cross her footprints. If the woman looked back, you knew she was a witch.
184936: From the Wouw on Poelhei a coach drawn by four wild stallions sometimes came. When that coach had driven over the fields, many chickens and cows were dead. One night a farmer was standing in the stable just as the coach came in. Nothing was ever heard of that farmer again.
184958: A mother had a little child that never laughed. When the mother went for a walk with her child, she was warned: "Make sure you don't run into X!" On the way the mother met the witch on the bridge. The witch played with the child, which made it laugh. But after that the child fell ill. The mother took her child to the friars, who said: "Your child is in a very bad way. In five days it will be all or nothing." The following Sunday the child was dead.
184968: A man slaughtered cats when people were tired of the animals. One day the man came to a farm where the farmer said: "Just take that ginger cat along". The farmer's wife objected, however, so the cat stayed there. A few days later the man saw the ginger cat sitting in the street and struck the animal to the ground. But the man had nothing in his hands; the cat was gone. Later he heard that the farmer's mother had a bandage around her head. That is how the man found out that the mother was a witch.
184975: When people walked past Weeuwboske, they often lost their way and had to wander about all night. If in such a case one took off one's coat and put it back on inside out, one got home without any trouble, while the person who had caused the harm had to wander about all night instead. A man who lived on the Ruggeveld is said to have done this once.
184977: A woman who had had a baby was visited daily by a neighbour who brought beautiful baby clothes, although the people did not need them. The young mother became so ill that she had to receive the last rites. When the priest came to her, he advised her not to let that neighbour in any more. The next day the neighbour was sent away. She was very angry, but they stood firm. After that the mother's health gradually improved. The mother's chickens often wandered onto the witch's yard. When they came back, they had lost all their feathers. Someone claimed that this neighbour was always reading books.
184986: A boy from Meer who worked for a farmer had bought new velvet clothes to go to church. One morning the boy found that his new clothes had been cut to shreds. The boy got new clothes from his master. The next night he saw a cat walking around his room. In the morning the boy's trousers had been cut to pieces. The boy got new trousers from his master. The next day the witch smashed everything in the house to bits. It was the master's wife who did it.
184993: A church is said to have sunk in Boshoven. Bells could sometimes still be heard ringing there.
185024: Someone was selling twenty-five or thirty Canadian poplars, some of which Selm wanted to buy at a bargain price. However, a man bought all the trees. Then Selm said: "I'll make sure you still won't have those trees home within four weeks". Indeed, the horses could not pull the man's trees. Selm said to the man: "If you give me a few trees, you'll get your trees home". And so it happened.
185027: A farmer working in the field with his horse saw a woman pass by who was said to be a witch. After that the horse was bewitched. The farmer went to the fathers of Tongerlo. When the farmer had been gone an hour and a half and must have been about at his destination, the horse sprang up. The farmer's wife said: "Look, now he has been there."
185037: On a farm in Koekhoven where a child was about to be born, the people were troubled by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). At birth the child wore a cap on its head. The midwife was a witch.
185045: A boy who was going home in the evening was told by people: "You will meet a witch on the way". But the boy was not afraid and set off. On the way the boy met the witch, who was holding a club and asked: "Where shall I leave it?" The boy answered: "Where you left it".
185046: On a farm there were some pigs that gained a kilo every day. One day an old woman passed by, stroked the pigs on the back and said: "What beautiful pigs!" From that moment the pigs did not gain another gram, although they still ate a lot. The farmer went to a clergyman at the Ossemarkt, who came to read prayers over the pigs and advised the man to put holy water in the animals' feed. After that the pigs grew fatter again.
185060: On a farm two heifers were due to calve during high mass. When one of the heifers bled to death, the people believed that a sorceress from the neighbourhood had brought this misfortune on them. The priest thought the same and asked whether the people had anything from that sorceress in the house. The farmer's wife suddenly remembered that their cat had come from that sorceress. The cat was then killed. The second heifer survived.
185066: The little path to the forest chapel in Olmen was called 'the Witches' Path'. One day D.'s brother heard a horse walking on that path, although there was nothing to be seen.
185081: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children that came out of the marshes.
185083: A man out poaching saw dark figures floating in the air. A little later he saw that they were horses, dancing and leaping in the air.
185096: When two men were working in the Zeept, a calf suddenly came and stood beside them and began stamping its feet. People called that calf 'de vuile meutte'. One man ran away in fear, but the other said to the animal: "What is it?", whereupon the calf answered: "Money is hidden here. If you find it, I will be released." When the man had found the money, he said to the calf: "Get it out yourself." When the calf had brought the money up, it said: "Now pick it up. I am released." After the man had taken the pile of gold crowns, the calf was never seen again.
185122: A man had hanged himself in an old house. Somewhere in the house a pot of money still lay hidden. Since then the house was haunted.
185145: Two girls coming back from the fair met a woman who said: "Put your shawl on better or you'll catch cold." The woman helped one of the girls with her shawl. A few days later the girl fell ill. She died of her illness.
185174: A man from Willebroek had sold his soul to the devil. He had signed the contract with blood from his finger. At the man's funeral people found it strange that the coffin was so heavy. Moreover, rumbling could be heard in the coffin the whole time. When the coffin was opened, they saw that there were only stones in it. The body had probably been taken away by the devils.
185175: If at the farm in the Boshoek they forgot to bring the butter churn inside, in the middle of the night it began rolling over the cobbles in front of the door. When people went to look, the churn was standing in its place as usual.
185182: A man suddenly felt a blow and could no longer get up. He felt as if someone was sitting on him. That man had been ridden by the mare.
185242: A witch lived in a remote house near a wood. On a certain farm they no longer let that witch in, because they believed she had made the pigs die.
185265: Some people sitting by the stove in the evening heard a cat miaowing at the water drain hole. A little later the cat had disappeared. The next day the same thing happened again. A day later the people heard an old woman calling, just like the cat. That woman was a witch who had taken on the shape of a cat.
185277: At Brug I the gloeiende paap (glowing priest) used to appear every year. That was the spirit of a dead man who had moved the boundary post of his field during his life.
185286: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) appeared in places where someone had secretly buried a child.
185288: On a farm in Lichtaart a cow had suddenly fallen ill. A neighbour blamed the misfortune on the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). A witch doctor came and said that a woman who often visited there had caused the misfortune. They had to keep that woman out from then on. The people did so and their cow recovered.
185335: Someone had died in a family in Doregem. One evening, when the people were sitting together by the Leuven stove, a ghost appeared, burned its hand into the kitchen door and said: "Live well, then you will be better off than I". Immediately afterwards the ghost had vanished again.
185341: In Oevel there was a large farm plagued by rats. A soldier said: "I'll drive the rats away," and he set out four sheaves. Then he made all the rats crawl under the sheaves. Next he set fire to the four corners of the sheaves, so that all the rats died.
185351: Two men working in the hay on the Berg saw a suspicious woman pass by and walked in her footprints. The witch turned around and the men knew enough.
185368: A man who was afraid of nothing walked one evening along a back path past the churchyard. There the man saw a white figure floating above the crosses.
185403: A woman had received money from someone, which she then paid as rent to her landlady. The landlady said to her: "I don't want money that comes from those people. They have been completely ruined." The landlady died.
185421: A man from Wechelderzande who was ridden by the mare saw all the devils from hell. The man tried to call out, but no sound came. At that moment the man was wide awake. He saw the devils sitting on the cupboards and at the foot of his bed. Satan was not among them, for he looked different from the devils the man saw. Satan had a flat head with two protruding horns.
185428: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. A farmer driving home with his cart saw a will-o'-the-wisp coming towards him. When the farmer said, "I baptise you in the name…", a hundred lights came flying up. The farmer hurried home. After he had slammed the door shut, the farmer heard a loud bang.
185449: One evening a man saw a black cat on the wall around the presbytery. The man took a stick and gave the cat a hard blow. The next day he met a woman who was limping. The witch could not harm the man because he always carried a holy relic.
185457: A woman who lived with a witch always saw a large black cat appear when she was milking the cows. The witch always laid three small silver coins on the lid where the cat went to sit. Once, when the witch had lain ill in bed for eight days, she got up with the words: "Now I know myself, now I am cured".
185500: To recognise a witch, you had to walk in the suspect's footprints. A witch would then look back.
185513: A drunkard who cursed all the time was walking over a bridge in Boom and said: "I will sell my soul." Then he met a gentleman, who asked: "Are you going to sell your soul?" The drunkard answered: "Tomorrow." The next day the drunkard met the gentleman on a narrow lane. The gentleman had a purse with him and said: "Here I am now." But the drunkard changed his mind and went home. He was followed by the devil, who struck the foot of the bed with his purse.
185536: One day a woman was visited by a peddler who sat down close to her. The woman, who was sewing, found after the peddler left that her sewing was full of fleas. Even after the sewing had been washed, the fleas were still in it. Only when a friar had read prayers over the sewing did the fleas disappear.
185552: Some French soldiers were staying at the Mostaardpothoeve. One day the soldiers who had to guard the money chest fell asleep drunk, so they did not notice that the farmer had dumped a cartload of manure over the chest. Because the five soldiers could not find the money, they were shot. Later the ghosts of the dead soldiers walked on the farm roof every night to punish the farmer for what he had done.
185556: The devil was to build a new barn for a farmer in exchange for the man's soul. The barn had to be finished by the time the cock began to crow. At night the farmer could not sleep and told everything to his wife. The woman ran to the henhouse and clapped her hands, which made the cock begin to crow. At that moment there was still a hole in the barn. The devil was gone, but that hole could never be closed.
185572: A farm suffered much misfortune. The farmer lay in bed for more than three months and no doctor could help him. The cows lowed every evening and pulled at their chains. When the farmer's wife went to look one evening, she saw a tomcat sitting in the stable that was a good two ells long and as broad as a heavy dog. The tomcat seemed furious when the farmer's wife came in. It jumped from one cow onto another and escaped as soon as it got the chance. The animals were freed from their misery and the farmer was cured.
185605: Sometimes a witch would come into the stable, stroke the animals on the back and say: "Oh, you have fine beasts." Afterwards the animals got back pain and began to kick.
185613: Three men going hare hunting in the snow had pulled up a savoy cabbage from an old couple's garden to use as bait. When the three saw the hare take the cabbage in its forepaws and walk off on its hind legs, they quickly made themselves scarce. One of the men who had witnessed the scene died a short time later. That hare must have been a witch in animal shape. After that incident the men never again pulled cabbages from anyone's garden.
185676: By the sunken road on the border with Lichtaart, a witte madam (white lady) was often seen in the evening, floating about half a metre above the ground. The apparition was visible for about five minutes and then disappeared.
185709: One evening a gentleman dressed in black with a bowler hat sat on the doorstep of a farm where a doctor had once lived. When the farmer came in from the field, the gentleman said: "Have a hundred masses said and all danger will be gone". Then the gentleman vanished. People claimed the apparition was the doctor who used to live there.
185761: A man came to visit a friend and said to him: "Even if you lock that door with seven locks, I can still throw it open with my cap."
185774: At Brug I a gloeiende paap (glowing priest) appeared every hundred years. That was the spirit of a man who had tried to move the boundary post of his field. However, the man had not succeeded.
185783: At a brewery where a black cat always came, the hand once poured hot water over the animal. The next day a woman lay in her bed with burns.
185784: Every evening a black cat came into a house through the water drain. One day some boys gave the cat a good thrashing. The next day the people were visited by the husband of a woman suspected of being a witch. The man said: "I don't think it's nice at all that you gave my wife a beating. Now she's lying ill in bed".
185789: In the churchyard of Geel there was a spot where the deans were buried. If you walked around that spot three times, the devil appeared and dragged that person's soul off to hell.
185800: In a house where a child had died, people found that the child's nappy was full of pins. The midwife was a witch.
185818: One was not supposed to leave one's clogs by the bed, or else one would be ridden by the mare at night. The mare was a standstill in the blood. Victims of the mare shouted loudly, but could not be heard by anyone.
185823: Four men out together saw a suspicious woman approaching. The men crossed her footprints and the witch looked back.
185832: A man who sowed a lot of flax drove with some farmers to Mechelen to sell the flax. On the way the man met a woman who greeted him, although he did not know her. The woman went on: "When your wife was lying in childbed, you were cooking beer with chunks of rye bread. A cat came in through the water drain hole. The cat grabbed a chunk from the pot and you kicked the animal, which then ran back out through the drain hole. That cat was me. But you needn't be afraid, because I can't do that any more".
185838: A woman who wore a hooded cloak and a cap always went out in the evenings. Sometimes she sat at the edge of the woods to frighten people. The night watchman of the dynamite factory once met her when she was wearing a white apron over her head. A man who once went to work for the witch found afterwards that he was full of fleas. He took off his clothes and his wife threw everything into a tub of water with the dung fork. A layer of fleas floated on the surface of the water.
185886: A man and a woman who lived near Gierle had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). Because of this their animals died and they could not churn butter. In the end the people moved house, and so they were freed from the kwade hand.
185924: On 't Galveld in Retie the ghosts of the men who had been hanged there came haunting.
185931: A man had fallen ill after being attacked by a calf. When the man was later working in his loft, he fell down and was dead. People claimed that calf had been a witch.
185957: Some people going to the fair were accompanied by a large white dog. Because they were afraid, they chased the dog away.
185963: In a house where the children had stopped growing, the people went to the priest. The clergyman advised them to pray and not to let a certain witch from the village in any more.
185975: A man who saw a witch walk past crossed that witch's footprints. At that the witch stopped. If you then said "In God's name", you were safe from the witch's magic.
185985: A man was in a relationship with a girl who was said to be a witch. When the man met the girl on the road, he walked in her footprints. The girl then looked back, so the man knew for sure that his girlfriend was a witch.
186018: A woman cycling to the shop met a witch, who took a match from her basket and said: "What have you got here? Matches?" When the woman went home again and struck a match, all the matches turned into glowing nails.
186021: A young man saw lots of moving lights above the Dijle. The young man's mother claimed she also often saw such lights in the beech tree. One day, when the young man's father was going to his work at the slaughterhouse, he was frightened to see lights above the meadows. Some people claimed that those lights were ghosts.
186061: A man walking home one evening saw a black cat jump in front of his feet. The man tried to kick the animal but could not hit it. He believed it was a witch, but still shouted: "If I meet you again, I'll break you in two!" When the man saw the cat again the next day, he struck it on the back with a stick. A day later a neighbour lay in bed with a broken back.
186078: In Ossendrecht lived a pregnant woman who was soon to give birth. One morning, while the woman and her husband were still asleep, they were visited by a little old lady who cried: "They're all lazybones here, staying in bed so long." On the following nights the pregnant woman was always thrown out of bed by a strange force. When the husband lay down in the woman's place, he too was thrown out of bed. One day the chaplain came to visit and read from his book until he was drenched in sweat.
186081: A mother heard a woman call at her window: "You think nobody can do anything to you any more, eh, but it won't be long now!" The next Sunday a son of that mother drowned. His friends stood around the water, but they could not move to go and get help until the boy no longer came up.
186102: At night a man came across a big black dog beside the cart track. That dog had only just gone when a second dog appeared, somewhat smaller. A little further on the man met an even smaller dog. People believed that dog was the devil.
186125: When people heard a cat miaowing in a tree, they did not dare chase the animal away. A man who once did so anyway found the next day that his house was full of black cats.
186132: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if a hundred kilos were pressing on his body. The man could not move and almost suffocated. After that incident the man placed his clogs upside down next to his bed.
186141: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
186156: A man coming back from the fair saw a headless dog on the way. The man stamped at the animal three or four times, but it would not go away.
186157: By the Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekapel on the Sint-Jansberg in Rijmenam, every night there stood a white calf with large burning eyes that jumped onto the backs of passers-by. One night, when the calf, heavy as lead, let itself be carried by a man, it pointed out the place where a treasure was buried. Like all the others who had had to carry the calf, this man too caught the 'vliegende tering' (galloping consumption), and he died three days later. Because of that the man could no longer tell where the treasure lay. According to people, the calf always disappeared at the Bruggenhoeve.
186163: The mare lay on people at night, so that those people could not speak and could not even breathe.
186174: A woman had got a stiff shoulder after a wicked woman patted her on the shoulder. Afterwards the woman had the mark of the sorceress's claw on her shoulder. The woman was given the address of someone from Jette who worked with Saint Anthony. The healer read prayers over the woman and transferred the illness to animals, probably chickens. The woman also had to do a strict penance. When the novena was over, the woman no longer had pain in her shoulder.
186176: A man from Kessel who could do magic sent all his rats to the neighbours. At that moment a peddler was walking by Hoeve De Vier Uitersten. When the peddler saw the rats running at his feet, he said: "I'll send them back to where they came from." Then the rats went back, and they could no longer be driven away.
186195: A man who was in the habit of having his beard shaved on Saturdays saw a ghost on the way back. It was a returned dead man who appeared in his shirt.
186198: In Weelde lived an old farmer who was married to a descendant of one of Napoleon's soldiers. When the farmer came back from the fair one day, his house was full of cats dancing around a tin pot. The farmer was forced to join the dance. When at a certain moment he said: "In God's name", all the witches disappeared into the pot. Later that pot was sold in Turnhout.
186224: In de Boshoek people were struggling with a plague of rats. When someone came who read a prayer, the rats came out by the thousands and all ran away at once.
186231: A man was always tormented by the mare around eleven o'clock. He then felt as if a weight of a hundred kilos was pressing on him. A priest advised him to give currant bread to the poor. Later the man was freed from the mare.
186240: A farmhand often drove his horse and cart past the house of an innkeeper woman who was suspected of being a witch. At that point the horse always stopped. The woman would then come outside with a large rosary around her neck. The witch called the man into the inn. After the farmhand had drunk a glass of beer and the horse had been given a tub of water, the animal was willing to go on again.
186248: On a farm one evening people saw a beast resembling a hedgehog crawl out of the henhouse. The animal jumped onto a post, then sat on the threshing machine and looked at a visitor who was just about to leave. The visitor said: "Look, what a pretty little beast", but the hostess said nothing and went inside. When the man cycled home, he could not keep the animal off him. The man kicked and struck at the animal, but nothing helped. After a long while he finally managed to hit it on the snout, so that it flew into the ditch. The man rode on as far as the railway and saw a black woman standing there. Further on he saw a snow-white calf lying on the cycle path. The next day the man went back to that place, but he saw no white calf anywhere. At the spot where he had knocked the little beast into the ditch, the grass was trampled. A few days later a procession was held in Heist-op-den-Berg. The man went there with a friend and saw that same black woman. He wanted to walk around the woman to see whether she had a scar on her face, but she kept turning so that her face could not be seen fully.
186258: While working in the field, a farmhand told a colleague that he was always ridden by the mare at night. The colleague laughed and said: "I'd like that a hundred thousand times in one night, but they have no power over me." The next morning that colleague was deathly pale. He had been ridden by the mare the whole night.
186264: On a farm where they could no longer churn butter because of the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse), nothing but filth was found in the butter churn.
186285: After his death, the father of a notary in Tongerlo appeared four times in the room where he had died. The ghost would then say: "Here is X".
186288: When cows calved prematurely or could not calve, it was blamed on the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). The people then had to fetch holy pills from the fathers.
186301: A man saw a black cat walking along a low wall. Assuming the cat was a witch, the man kicked the animal off the wall. The next day a woman was walking around the village with a large cloth wrapped around her head.
186309: A woman often woke at midnight to the sound of rattling in the cupboard. She went downstairs with her husband and saw that the cupboard was still shaking. The woman knew which witch was responsible for this strange event and threatened her: "If you do it again, I'll smash your head in."
186324: A man warned his children about a black cat because he believed that cat was a witch.
186337: Black cats represented evil. They got under people's feet and could not be chased away. One then had to lay a holy object on the ground or under the mat, so that the cat, which was really a 'zwarte madam' (black lady), could go no further.
186347: If one was ridden by the mare, one had to cross one's legs. Then one was released.
186368: On the estate of Prince de Merode there was a witch who made the cows die and untied the horses at midnight. When the witch and her husband had died, another farmer came to live on the farm. That farmer had to call in the priests several times to drive out the evil.
186378: A witch once lived in the Collegestraat. One day a soldier passed by and the witch said: "How are you, my lad?" The young man answered in surprise: "Fine, of course!" Then the witch began to laugh. The next day the soldier lay seriously ill in bed.
186422: A man was sitting in an inn in the Koningsven between Loenhout and Brecht. A woman who was also there said to the man: "Well, Janneke, you're not home yet, you know!" The man wandered about in the fen all night. On one side stood Pietje de Dood (Death) and on the other side a coffin. In the end the man found his way again.
186425: A boy of sixteen or seventeen claimed that he was bewitched at night. He felt the witch sitting on his body and squeezing his throat. The next Sunday the boy drank a lot and shouted on his way home: "Come and bewitch me now! I'm not lying in bed now!" But the witch did not come.
186439: A house where a sick child lay in the cradle was visited by a woman pedlar. The mother told the pedlar that she had a child who was ill. The pedlar came to look and saw that the wool in the child's pillow looked like a tail. The rest of the wool was growing in the child. The pedlar advised the mother to burn the wool. If a blue flame appeared, the child would recover. If the flame was white, the child would die. The flame was white and the child did not survive.
186445: Some men were fighting at the fair. The police intervened and an officer drew his bayonet. One of the brawlers fixed the policeman to the spot with his bayonet in the air. The wizard was taken to prison, but got out of it effortlessly. That wizard's book of magic had to be taken from him before he could die.
186447: The farm on the Bruinen Baard was often haunted. The doors and windows flew open, and in the morning the animals had all been untied. The tubs that were supposed to stand by the gate lay at the back.
186475: One morning a man went to call his workmate to go to work. When a cat leapt out of that house, the man broke its leg with a blow. A little later he heard that his workmate's wife lay in bed with a broken arm.
186508: A man went hare hunting with a friend. Suddenly the man saw a hare sitting right in front of his friend. The man did not understand why his friend did not shoot at the hare and wanted to fire a shot himself, but his gun did not work. Then the friend said: "Why do you have to shoot at that hare now? I was just talking to it!" When the man put down his gun, it did work.
186516: Someone who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come back to haunt as a glowing figure after his death.
186528: A girl had stolen eggs or pears from a wizard. The wizard said of the girl: "She won't get further than the brook!" And that is indeed what happened.
186534: A cattle dealer returning from the notary was frightened when a fierce wind suddenly rose in the Vondelboske. The man saw a cat sitting there and knocked the animal into the water. The cat swam to the bank and the man knocked the animal into the water again. Then the cat said: "Now hit me once more!"
186552: On a farm where the horses had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse), the animals limped at night while sweating heavily. The people were freed from the evil by going to the fathers.
186562: In Bonheiden lived a girl who could work magic. The girl had received her magic power from her mother. The mother could hardly die. If you were touched by a sorceress, you had to hit her higher up to break her power. The sorceress from Kievit read books all night. In the street she wore a veil. She married an old man from outside Bonheiden. The sorceress drove her husband to hang himself. A woman married to a brother of the sorceress lived with the sorceress. So it happened one day that the sorceress gave a plum to her sister-in-law's child. After that the child was bewitched and cried all the time. They took the child to the fathers, who advised them to go on pilgrimage the next day before sunrise to the little chapel of Harent. After that the little boy recovered.
186568: A farmer was desperate because there was not enough room in his barn to store the harvest. One day the farmer was visited by a gentleman, who said: "If you sell me your soul, there will be a new barn standing the next day." The farmer agreed to the proposal. Back home, the man told the whole story to his wife, who was very upset about it. The devil had to have the barn finished before the cock began to crow in the morning. That night the woman got up at two o'clock. She woke the chickens, which made the cock begin to crow. Because the devils were still busy bricklaying at that moment, the man did not have to give up his soul.
186575: A miller who took grain to Lier always saw a cat sitting on the horse collar at night. One day the man struck the cat to the ground. The next day his wife lay in bed with a broken arm.
186580: When the devil struck something with his foot, he left a footprint there.
186587: A man who had lost his way saw beautiful apparitions dancing. A moment later the figures had suddenly vanished.
186618: A witte madam (white lady) sometimes came out of the woods in Tielen. A child who lived nearby had a swollen head and drooled all the time. Moreover, the child did not grow.
186622: Some men were walking in the woods on the Hoven (between Pomfort and the heath) at around ten in the evening when they suddenly saw a kitten walking. The men did the kitten no harm and stroked it on the head. Then the cat said: "If you had not spoken so nicely tonight, I would have broken your neck".
186677: A witch could sometimes be seen suddenly vanishing without a trace.
186682: On the Heikant there stood an old farm with a barn that had a hole in it. That barn had been built by devils and was never finished. A man who helped people out in his spare time tried a good ten times to close the hole in the barn, but in vain. In those days all of Mariekerke talked about the devil's barn.
186701: A cat always sat on a turnpike barrier in Zandvliet. People sometimes tried to hit the animal but could not. The people decided the cat must be a witch.
186720: In the Antwerpse Straat lived a certain Jaak who did nothing but curse all the time. When Jaak died, a dog came in with a ring in its mouth. The dog jumped onto the cupboard from which people wanted to take the shroud and stayed sitting there.
186742: Witches owned a doll into which they stuck pins to torment other people.
186745: A woman going to early Mass in the dark always saw a man dressed in black walking beside her on a lane. When the woman quickened her pace, the man did the same. When the woman reached the street, there was nothing more to be seen.
186759: A man coming back from Zandvliet was jumped on the way by a person with a horse's leg. The man quickly ran into a café. As soon as he came into the light, he was freed of his burden. He had been ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit).
186765: One evening some men were working near the Nonnekensbos. Suddenly they heard a roaring there, and a wind rose that gave off an enormous heat. Then the men ran away.
186782: A man always went to play cards in a café on the Schootse Heide in Veerle. When that man dropped a card one day, people noticed he had horse's feet. After that incident the café was called 'het duvelskot' (the devil's den).
186802: The daughter of a supposed witch was in love with a boy. The girl went to the house where the boy lived and asked whether she could iron the collars of the shirts there. When the boy wore such a shirt on Sunday and rode to the fair in Westerlo or on the Blauberg, a big crow sat on the handlebars of his bicycle. When the boy was about halfway, a big black dog was suddenly sitting on the handlebars. Because the dog would not be chased away, the boy turned back. When he took off the shirt on arriving home, the dog vanished at once.
186815: A boy began to sweat every night at twelve o'clock because he was ridden by the mare.
186816: Sometimes people were ridden by the mare in their beds. They were tormented so badly that they nearly died of it. One could protect oneself against the mare by placing one's clogs crossed by the bed.
186822: A farmer had bought three cows one after another, but the animals all died after a few days. The farmer believed the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) was in the stable and so went to the fathers for advice. There the farmer received a relic to place under the stable door. After that the farmer had no more problems.
186834: Some young men going home at midnight danced around a tree in front of a witch's house. At a certain moment the boys were driven apart and lost their way.
186867: A woman going to Averbode at night saw a legless clergyman float past near an old lime tree.
186879: On a farm three cows had died within a short period because of the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). The farmer went to a monastery, where the father said: "Give nothing more to the woman who comes to fetch buttermilk. Go home. By the time you get home, a fourth cow will have died." And so it was.
186967: In Mol lived a woman who was tormented by a witch. When that woman went out in the rain, her umbrella burned. The witch called to her: "Well, what's the matter?" The woman went to the fathers to be freed from the witchcraft, but she could not get there. The father had to come and meet her.
187017: In Broechem a girl was bewitched. The girl could not hold her urine and lay in bed all the time. Later the girl moved to the Congo, where she had three children.
187029: Witches often change themselves into a toad. In Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Waver lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. When someone had struck a toad somewhere, people found the next day that the witch had lost an arm.
187032: A drunkard had to pass the house of a witch. A little later the man's face was covered in scratches. When he got home the man was bewitched; he kept walking backwards instead of forwards because he saw the witch standing in front of him, driving him back with an umbrella.
187040: A man walking home one evening met a cat by the Drieshoevebeek in Heist-op-den-Berg and said: "Pussycat dear, where are you going?" The cat replied: "Just listen, Neleke asks me: Pussycat dear, where are you going?" The man went on. Before he was home, he had seen a thousand cats. He opened the door and slipped inside quickly, so that not a single cat got in with him. The cats sat wailing outside for a long time and then went away.
187053: In Veerle lived a woman who always babysat a neighbour's children. When some people had one day shot a black cat in the paw, they expected the woman to have a gunshot wound. But she came to babysit as usual. They asked her to show her legs, and it turned out she had no wound anywhere.
187074: Some people who were cutting branches saw cats that kept screaming: "Amai, amai, amai".
187122: Sometimes a witch would stick the blankets of children in their cradle full of pins.
187136: A woman had an aunt from Antwerp visiting. The aunt had a small case of banknotes with her. When the aunt got up one morning, she found her case in the same place. Although the case was closed, the banknotes had been replaced by others of the same value. Her hostess told her so before she had discovered it. That woman was a sorceress.
187141: A young couple had come to live in Varendonk. Nearby lived a witch who often visited the young couple. The witch always stroked the children's hands and heads. After a while the children fell ill. The doctor advised the people not to let the witch in any more. After that the children recovered.
187161: In Lichtaart there is said to have once been a house where the witches held gatherings at night to dance. The occupants had several times heard a tremendous noise, but when they went to look, nothing more could be heard. One evening someone went to keep watch there. When the noise could be heard, the man began to shout and rage. The next moment some fifty cats jumped from the gutter and scattered in all directions.
187201: A boy was staying with a woman and her daughter in Berlaar. At night the boy saw mother and daughter take the syrup pot and smear their hands with syrup. Then they said: "Over hedge and hedgerow, over brushwood and Maas, to Cologne into the wine cellar" and vanished. The boy wanted to try it too, but he made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and hedgerow, through edge and Maas to Cologne into the wine cellar". When the boy arrived in Cologne, he was scratched all over and his clothes were torn.
187219: In a house near Sas 4 lived a widower who every night saw the ghost of his recently deceased wife appear in beautiful clothes. The woman's ghost beckoned the man to follow. One night the man followed the ghost to the cellar. There the ghost lifted a stone under which silver coins lay hidden. After that the ghost did not appear again.
187224: In Herentals lived a suspicious woman whom everyone avoided. When people were waiting at the butcher's and saw that woman come in, they quickly went outside. A man who got a 'negenoger' (?) on his neck was said to have been bewitched by that woman.
187228: On a farm in the Rodianostraat there was much misfortune in the stable. An old woman came to that farm every day to fetch milk. Once, when the old woman was late and all the milk had been sold, the farmer's wife said: "Oh, you're all alone anyway, I'll quickly go and milk some." The farmer's wife and the old woman went to the stable together. The next night the cow died on the stroke of twelve. In the following days other cows died too. In the end the people went to the superior of the monastery, who gave them a relic. After the relic had been placed under the stable threshold, the old woman could no longer come in.
187270: A shepherd found in his field the money a passing horseman had dropped. When the horseman came to ask the shepherd whether he had found any money, the shepherd denied it and said God might punish him forever if he was lying. The horseman then rode on. Shortly afterwards the shepherd and his dog were struck by lightning. The dead shepherd had to come back to haunt, in the shape of a glowing fire, the places where he used to roam with his sheep.
187285: Gust's husband had hanged himself. Since then the woman always heard the goat bleating loudly. Rumbling could be heard in the attic and the occupants of the house fell out of their beds every night. When Gust sought advice from the parish priest, he asked her whether she had ever promised anything. Gust replied: "Yes, I promised I would go to Scherpenheuvel, but I don't have enough money". The priest said: "Oh, my good woman, if you have promised something, you must do it. Soon we are going from Stabroek to Scherpenheuvel; you can come with us". Once the woman had been on pilgrimage, the house stayed quiet.
187300: At the baron's castle in Oostmalle a knocking was always heard. Some young people went to keep watch there once. They heard the knocking too, though nothing could be seen.
187330: A witch in the shape of a cat followed a farmer who was working at night. The farmer struck the cat, and afterwards the witch bore the marks of that blow.
187332: A man was always accompanied by a black cat on his way home at night, so that in the end he no longer dared to come to Zoerle.
187338: In a house with a baby, a witch was always seen at night walking around the child's laundry. The people went to the fathers, who showed them the witch in a mirror. The witch bewitched the laundry and so gained power over the child.
187351: A girl had fallen ill because of a rag-woman from Willebroek. While the girl lay ill in bed, a big rat came and sat on her body. Nobody dared to catch the rat. One day the rag-woman came to visit again. They put a relic under her chair, thinking she would then be unable to get up. But she could.
187377: If the women met a black cat on the way, they lifted their skirts. If they met a crow, they were afraid. If the crow flew along with them, no misfortune followed, but if the crow began to caw, it was considered a bad omen.
187384: A witch lived in Retie. A neighbour woman had once said: "You ugly dirty witch!" When that neighbour woke up in the morning, her house was full of rats. The priest had to come to the house to read prayers over it.
187402: In a large family living next to a sorceress, two children were seized by the throat. The children could just cry out: "She did this to me," before they died.
187437: In the old days the girls went spinning in the evening. It often happened that the girls dared each other to go and draw a cross on the church door. As part of the bet, one of the girls went to draw a cross on the door at midnight. When the girl turned around, she saw someone standing there wearing nothing but a shirt. Convinced that one of her friends wanted to frighten her, the girl pulled the shirt off the figure and went home. There the girl discovered that she had taken the shirt off her dead mother. The girl had made that shirt herself.
187440: A man had gone to help lift potatoes on a farm. Afterwards he played cards with the farmer for a while and then went home around midnight. The man lived close by and only had to cross a bridge. Strangely, however, the man could not get across that bridge. At four in the morning he was still not home. The man was bewitched.
187444: A cat always came into R.'s house through the drain hole. One night R. sat down next to the hole with a dung fork, so that he could wound the cat as soon as it came in. The next day Cornel lay injured in bed: she had lost an eye.
187455: One evening a man was walking home along a lane with the smith. The man had just lit a cigarette and was walking a few metres behind the smith. Suddenly he heard the smith scream. The smith stood still, terrified, pointing at bushes beside the road that were moving back and forth. There was no wind. The two men started to run. When they got home, the smith asked: "Did you see those white figures too?" The man had not seen the haunting.
187462: A poacher from the Netherlands had tried several times in vain to shoot a hare. Together with his brother, the poacher had a Dutch quarter blessed. Then they chopped the coin into pieces and put the shot in their gun. When the hare appeared again, the poacher hit the animal easily. The next day a wounded woman was walking around the village.
187468: A man who was going to the village one morning heard a hare screaming. Assuming the animal was caught in a snare, the man went to the hare. Strangely, however, he did not manage to catch the animal. It was a ghost hare.
187483: On a farm three knocks were heard in the cellar. People went to look but saw nothing. The knocking continued, however, until the people moved away.
187515: A farmer who had no barn to store his grain in saw a gentleman in the field, who offered to build him a barn in exchange for his soul. The barn would be finished before the cock had crowed three times the next morning. The farmer agreed. At night, however, he found no rest and told his wife what he had done. The woman got up, stood at the window and clapped her hands three times. At that moment the barn was only half finished, so the farmer could keep his soul.
187520: One morning a farmer found two calves in his stable with their heads in a single halter. The farmer could not undo the halter and had to send for the smith.
187540: Peter claimed that a shooting star was the soul of a child that had died unbaptised. If you pointed at such a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp), it settled on your finger and never came off again.
187542: In Beerzel lived a witch who had all kinds of books in her house. When she pointed her finger at a corner where a book lay, the book began to play wonderful music and all the chairs and tables danced around.
187557: A dead nun for whom many masses were said appeared one day with the words: "You need not have any more masses said, for I am damned anyway".
187567: When the count of the castle of 't Zwart Land had died, a young lady was to come and settle the inheritance. The heiress fell ill, however. When she set out on the journey anyway, she drowned in the Nete at Heist-op-den-Berg. The count's ghost was always seen riding around the castle on horseback. Because the castle was ill-gotten property, the dead count had made sure the lady never reached the castle. There were also said to be underground passages beneath the castle.
187594: A man was always quarrelling with his neighbour, who was a witch. One day the witch said to the man: "If you set foot on my yard again, you will die!" The man laughed, but when he came to the woman's place again, he dropped dead.
187605: A mother who skinned dead young goats had many people coming to her house. One day, while the mother was working in the stable, she had hung a cloth over the cradle of her sleeping little son to protect the child from the flies. Just then a woman came to visit, who took the child out of the cradle and sat it on her lap. The mother came inside, saw the woman sitting there and told her she must never do that again. After that the little child fell ill. Although it ate well, it grew thin and got the little face of an old man. No doctor could help, but people claimed that the parish priest could hold off the illness for six weeks. The priest was sent for; he sent everyone outside and then walked around the cradle three times, making signs of the cross and saying a prayer. After that the child gave no more trouble, but it did die at the age of nine months.
187626: In the old Hofberg a mass was held at night and bells could be heard ringing.
187641: In Bonheiden lived a man who kept books in his cellar room. He could enter houses without opening the doors or windows.
187642: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who were in limbo.
187687: A miller did not believe that his wife was a witch. One day the man struck the paw of a cat that was rooting around in the flour in the mill. Afterwards the man found that his wife had lost a hand.
187722: A man who had sold a cow had to go through the woods to deliver the animal. When the man was in Lille, he met two fellows who said: "You needn't be afraid with such a big beast behind you!" At first the man did not dare look back, but a little later he saw a black dog as big as a calf standing behind him. Sweating, the man prayed the Gospel of Saint John, and a little later he saw the dog run off through the woods.
187731: A slater was working on the church of Lommel. When the man went to Mol with his son on a rainy evening, the two decided to take shelter at the Lommel factory. There a woman came and stood between them, whereupon the men went on. On 't Hemelrijk a big black dog lay on the road. The father fell over the dog, but the animal stayed lying there. He claimed that the dog was that woman, who had changed herself into an animal.
187770: A shepherd with money in his pocket asked for lodging at 't Hoefijzer, but was refused. The shepherd went on his way and was robbed by two men from 't Hoefijzer. The shepherd threw some money on the ground and said: "That's all I have left". One of the men bent down to pick up the money, but stayed standing bent over with his hand outstretched. The shepherd had fixed him to the spot. When the shepherd went back to 't Hoefijzer, he was allowed to stay the night. But he could not go to sleep, for then his neck would be broken. The shepherd walked around a table there all night, until the next morning people went to early mass. The shepherd said to the churchgoers: "Someone is standing on the Kruisbaan. Tell him he may go on". After that the robber was released.
187787: On a farm a cat always came in through the drain hole for the water.
187795: A sick boy from Bonheiden was visited every evening by a witch who came to stand by his bed, patted him on the shoulder and asked how he was. The boy grew sicker and sicker, so that the friars had to be sent for to read prayers over him. One evening the witch was thrown out, but it was already too late, for the boy had become completely emaciated.
187804: On a farm in Schilde where many cows and horses died, a woman often came to visit. People did not trust that woman much and from then on tried to keep her out. They had prayers read over the farm, after which the situation improved.
187818: A man had to appear in court because he was suspected of practising sorcery. When the judge asked whether the man could do anything, the courtroom was at once filled with rats and mice. When they asked the man to make the rats disappear again, he said: "Then I must first go back home and read in my books." The man was given permission and made the rats disappear.
187827: On the old Hofberg south of Poederlee bells could be heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night. A procession would then go around the hill. There were also underground passages.
187843: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who came back to haunt.
187869: Near the home of Jef V.T., who lived between Tessenderlo and Engsbergen, a coach with four horses drove along the road every night at twelve o'clock.
187886: In a house where a cat always sat by the door, someone once slammed the door shut with the animal's tail caught in it. Two days later a woman was seen walking in the village wearing a bandage around her hand because she had a broken little finger.
187978: At 't Hoefijzer a Dutch shepherd was staying with his flock of sheep. In the past many shepherds came from the Netherlands to Flanders for three or four months. In winter they went to market with their sheep. When this shepherd came home one evening, he was attacked by a robber with a knife. The shepherd made the robber stand still until three o'clock the next afternoon. Then the police came to arrest the robber.
187987: A man walking through the Heksenstraatje met a cat, which scratched him. The man kicked at the animal, after which as many as seven cats appeared. He thought they were witches.
187996: A sorceress always threw a handful of bewitched grass in the doorway of the person she wanted to harm. People would then throw the grass onto the dung heap with a long stick. If you did not want to be bewitched, you must not touch the grass with your hands.
188017: Nobody dared to go near the Silsburg churchyard at night, because a woman dressed in black wandered about there in the evenings. People believed that woman was a witch who came to haunt the place and bewitched every passer-by.
188039: A man walking home one evening heard a rattling of chains. He went towards the place the sound came from, assuming it was cows that had broken loose. A moment later, however, he heard the sound behind him, and he began to run. However fast he went, the rattling went on and could be heard close by. When the man got nearer to home, he suddenly no longer heard the sound.
188056: A poacher tried every night to shoot a hare, but could not hit the animal. When one night the man used a blessed bullet, he did manage to shoot the hare. The next day a woman in the village lay dead.
188070: Knocking was always heard in an old wardrobe. On Christmas Eve the woman of that house sat knitting. Around eleven o'clock she wanted to go to bed, because on Christmas Eve one was supposed to be in bed before midnight. When the woman looked up from her knitting, she saw a swallow with glowing eyes sitting on a beam, even though it was the middle of winter. The next day the woman told her family what she had seen, but they did not believe her. When the people were sitting together by the fire one evening, the swallow appeared again and flew away up the chimney. The knocking in the wardrobe continued. The wardrobe had once been completely emptied, but nothing had been found. One day the man said at the wardrobe: "Little knocker, you must knock harder or else stop." After that the knocking was no longer heard.
188096: In a stable in Boechout, every morning two calves stood with their heads in a single halter. People untied the calves, but the next day the same thing happened again.
188098: A farmer from Wemmel wanted a bigger barn and made a deal with a stranger. The farmer had to sign with his blood and would have a new barn by the next morning before the first cockcrow. At night the farmer lay moaning in his bed and told his wife what he had done. The farmer's wife immediately went outside and clapped her hands, so that the cock began to crow too early. The barn was almost finished; there was still one hole in it. Later people tried several times to close the hole, but the next morning it was always open again. The clergy advised the people to brick a cross into the hole. When they did that, the hole stayed closed. Whole trees, with the roots still attached, had been built into the barn.
188120: A man went to play skittles at the house of a woman who was said to be a real witch. The plates and pots on the mantelpiece there danced up and down.
188136: In Vorselaar a dead man came back to haunt the cellar in the shape of a spider's web. On seeing the spider's web, the woman said: "Even if you are our father, I'll squash you dead anyway!" Then the woman killed the spider.
188172: A farmer did not have a barn big enough to store his whole harvest in. The farmer was willing to give his best pledge in exchange for a new barn. The barn had to be finished before the cock crowed at two o'clock. At night the farmer's wife heard her husband moaning and asked what was wrong. Having heard the story, the farmer's wife went to the henhouse and clapped her hands, which made the cocks begin to crow too early. The devils, who were hard at work, immediately stopped their labour. There was still a hole in the barn that had to be closed. Later people tried several times to close that hole, but the stones always fell out again. When they wanted to bring the hay in with the horse, the animal broke its leg. One day some workmen decided, as a joke, to hang someone there from a blade of straw. Lots were drawn to decide who would be the victim. While that person was hanging there with the straw around his neck, the men saw a black hare and chased after it with their flails. The hare would not be caught and disappeared into the straw. In the meantime the man with the straw around his neck had died. The straw had turned into an iron wire. Later that farm was demolished.
188173: A man coming back from the market with a cow suddenly could not get the animal to take another step. Across the street stood a small house. Suddenly the door of that house opened and an old woman came out. The woman laughed and said: "Come on, cow, go on now!" Then the cow went on.
188177: A man went at night with his wheelbarrow to fetch beets in Lier. One day, near the fort on the Kloosterheide, the man saw a woman dressed in black holding a candle and searching for something. When the man spoke to the woman, she vanished.
188197: A mother went with her child to the parish priest of Sint-Jan because the child had 'the old man'. Because the priest could not help, the mother went with a friend and her skin-and-bone child to the friars of den Oever. The friar who had the power to heal the sick was not there at the time, so the women had to wait. When the friar was back, he read prayers over the child and told the mother to do nine days of penance and also to have the child prayed over by the Poor Clares. There too the two women had to wait. A sister read prayers over the child and said the evil had been caused by someone who often came to Deurne-Zuid. The mother did indeed remember that someone had been to her house carrying a large loaf and a kilo of butter. Her child was cured.
188210: A wizard who was locked in prison said to a guard: "Go and have a drink in the Keyzer and I'll come and pay." When the guards arrived at the café, the wizard was already standing there.
188251: At a farmer's in the Netherlands all the farmhands were murdered by a ghost. One day the farmer was visited by a man who dared to face the ghost. At night the ghost appeared with the words: "All who sleep, awake!" Then the ghost lifted four paving stones out of the ground and brought up four treasures: one for the church, one for the farmer and one for the honest finder.
188258: A man claimed that a witch lived near him. At midnight the cows there made a terrible racket in the stable.
188301: In Heist lived a widow with her daughter. The daughter lay in bed with her clothes on while her mother took the goat and the cow out to graze. Some time later the daughter died. The mother also had a granddaughter by another daughter. After the death, that granddaughter went to lie in the bed. The child lay there day and night for four years until she had to make her First Communion. After the communion she went back to lie in the bed. Four years later the grandmother died and the child was cured. It was the grandmother who had bewitched her family.
188302: A few men always sat together in an attic in the evening. A cat always appeared in the attic to fetch rags. One of the men gave the cat a blow, not knowing that the animal was a witch. The next day a woman from the village was seen walking around with a black eye.
188307: A man who was going to the farmers in Averbode kicked at a cat in the evening. However, the animal jumped between his legs every time.
188316: A witch lived on the road to Herentals. If you came near her house, you could not take another step.
188323: In a family that a witch had just visited, the little daughter suddenly could no longer see. When the witch walked past the house again, the girl's mother said: "You see that knife lying here, don't you? Well, if you don't make that child see again, I'll cut your throat with that knife!" The witch answered: "Oh, we'll pray for it together." The girl could see again.
188335: A man who was ridden by the mare felt a beast approaching when he lay in his bed. Then it seemed as if something seized him by the throat.
188358: At 't Sluis lived a family whose youngest son was always being pulled out of his cradle. The boy got a hunchback from it. A neighbour woman wanted to do the child harm.
188376: People who could not make butter and who had a sick child went to the convent, where they were given a holy relic. When the people were visited again by a suspicious woman, they stoked the fire hot. When the visitor said: "You're stoking it so hard," the man of the house answered: "Yes, you may not leave until you have cured my child." A little later the child was cured.
188381: A child had beaten a sorceress's rooster to death with a bean pole. That rooster was no ordinary rooster. It attacked the people of the neighbourhood everywhere and even got over a hedge a good two metres high. The rooster would suddenly be sitting on someone's head, although that person had seen the animal a hundred metres away just before. The rooster sometimes also ran off with cutlery, crockery or toys. Two days after the boy had killed the rooster, he saw a large bird sitting at his bedroom window. The bird beat its wings against the glass six times and then disappeared. The boy leapt out of bed and began shouting and crying, drenched in sweat. The boy had to stay in bed for six months. The bird had also beaten its wings against the glass six times. That was all the work of the sorceress.
188390: A man coming home one evening after chatting with friends saw a cat in a meadow and said: "Pussycat dear, where are you going?" The cat had then replied: "Listen, Drieske asks me: Pussycat dear, where are you going?"
188424: People went on pilgrimage to Bornem for a bewitched child. The parish priest of Bornem freed the child from the witch.
188442: A man who saw a cat sitting on the dovecote beat the animal to death. A pit was dug to bury the cat. That had barely been done when the cat was sitting alive in the 'kevie' (?) again. When the man came to his usual café on Sunday, he noticed that the landlady wore a bandage around her arm, and she said: "Fons, you mustn't do that again, because it really hurt me!"
188469: A maid who worked in Westerlo had to go and fetch fodder for the animals. Because it had started raining hard on the way, the maid took shelter under a bush. At a certain moment a woman came by who said: "Ah, standing here under the bush, are you?", to which the maid answered: "Yes, I wanted to shelter for a moment, because I still have to fetch fodder." The woman replied: "If you read this note, you'll have a whole wheelbarrow of fodder in a moment." The girl did what the woman had advised and indeed had fodder at once. After that, however, the girl always had to do evil. One day she had to cook rice pudding for a wedding. When she went to serve the ten dishes, the maid found that the rice pudding had been completely churned up and that she could not serve it like that. In the end she was taken to Tongerlo. She had to leave the farm to escape the disgrace.
188476: In Borgerhout lived an old woman who was suspected of being a witch. A shopkeeper had that witch come into her shop every day at twelve noon. Strangely enough, her youngest little son always started crying at twelve midnight. The shopkeeper had prayers read over her child by the parish priest. Afterwards she also put blessed ash under the threshold. After that incident the witch never came into the shop again. But the little child died a year later.
188486: A man who did not believe that his wife had magic powers went to hide in a cornfield one night. It had only just turned midnight when the sorceress walked straight to the corn and pulled her husband out, without anyone having told her anything about it.
188501: In a family in Meerhout a girl was ill. Strangely, the sound of pebbles being thrown could always be heard up in the attic. One day the people discovered a cat in the attic. As soon as a match was struck, the cat ran away. A woman from Merksplas advised the bewitched girl's family to light a candle and snuff it out with their fingers when it had almost burned down. The stump of wax had to be left standing until it burst open by itself. On the day the bewitched girl died, someone else in the village suddenly suffered from the same ailment.
188504: A boy who was a werewolf said to his girlfriend one evening: "If you meet anything on your way home later, throw your handkerchief at it". The girl met a big dog and did as she had been advised. The next day she found that her boyfriend had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
188551: A farmer had a maid who always said: "Over hedge and hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar" and then disappeared. One day the maid asked the farmer whether he would like to ride along. "Yes", said the farmer, but he made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and through hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar". After that the farmer was dragged through everything.
188576: An old farmer was convinced that one of his neighbour women dealt in the kwade hand (the evil hand, harmful magic), although he was friends with that neighbour. The farmer had much misfortune in his stable. Sometimes four animals died at once. Another time in the morning he saw his cows rolling, sweating, over a wooden rail in the stable. When the farmer bought a new cow, he found a cow's head in the corn. That farmer walked to the friars of Lier several times to be blessed.
188581: In a farmhouse on the Berg in Retie, someone was heard walking in the attic every evening. The occupants went to the parish priest, who told them the noise was caused by the ghost of their aunt Julie, who had been buried a few weeks earlier. The aunt was unhappy because her relatives had promised to have a number of masses said but had failed to keep that promise. After the people had the masses said, they heard nothing strange any more.
188604: Whenever Fil went to the fair in Averbode, he always met priests without feet who were reading from a book. In the monastery the priests had said: "The night is for us and the day is for you." The ghosts had pointed out a spot in the monastery where a lot of money was later found.
188642: On 't Spookblok a ghost always appeared, calling: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I leave it?" It was the spirit of a man who had moved a boundary post during his life. When one day a drunkard answered: "Put it back where you got it", the ghost was released.
188680: On a farm the animals stood with their front legs in the air at midnight for ten days in a row. That was the work of a sorceress.
188705: A man had a quarrel with a neighbour woman who was suspected of being a witch. The witch smashed a milking stool to pieces on the cows.
188716: A brabasson (rough, unruly fellow) who cursed a lot had fallen ill. He was being eaten away by maggots and the devil appeared in his cellar room. A dog also came and tossed him upward, so that his entrails stuck to the ceiling.
188753: A woman was visiting a family who had a one-year-old child. They wanted to go to the Collectienen in Lier for that child, but the woman said: "If you are going out, then I will cure that child." The next day the people went to Lier anyway. They met the witch, and she said: "I know where you have been. But curing a child with the two of us, that we cannot do."
188766: A man who went to catch eel in the evening suddenly saw as many as five hundred meowing cats sitting behind his back. When the man pulled a club out of a haystack, not a single cat was to be seen.
188768: A toad came into a house where a child was playing by the stove. When the toad sat down by the child, the mother threw the creature outside with a shovel. The next day a wounded woman was walking around the village.
