188797: A man from Bornem was going to high mass in Oppuurs. When the man saw a hare running on the way, he took out his gun and fired. But he could not hit the hare. When the man had been chasing the hare for quite a while, the animal jumped up and cried: "Missed mass". Then the hare was gone.
188811: A man from Puurs traded in Brabant horses. At four o'clock in the morning the horse dealer set off for Meise. When the dealer was in Oppot one day to buy a horse from a farmer, the farmer said: "You've surely come to see the devil's barn too? You're sitting on a tree that once served as a beam for the barn." The horse dealer was sitting on a tree at least two metres in diameter, which normally no human could move. The farmer said that the devils had flown through the air with that tree and took the dealer to the devil's barn. Because the barn was already some two or three hundred years old, only a third of it was still standing. On a summer's day a farmer from Oppot was walking through his field, realising that he did not have enough room in his barn to store all his corn. While the farmer was at his wits' end, he was approached by a gentleman dressed in black, who promised him a new barn by the next morning on condition that the farmer would give him his best pledge. The farmer signed the contract. If the barn was not finished before the cock first crowed in the morning, the farmer could keep his soul. The following night, however, he grew uneasy, for he sensed that he was dealing with the devil. The farmer's wife was woken by her husband's sighing and heard the whole story. Then the farmer's wife went outside and struck her clogs together, so that a cock began to crow. The farmer was saved, but the barn was not yet finished. At the top of the roof there was still an opening. The devils had fetched the biggest trees in the region and flown through the air with them. Those trees were then used as beams. The farmer had someone come to close the hole in the barn, but it could not be done. When a small statue of Mary had been placed in the hole, they managed to brick a rim around that statue. But they could never close the hole completely. Every time the statue of Mary was taken away to close the hole completely, the rest of the masonry fell in as well. So they just left it like that.
188817: One night a baker's boy went along to pick apples at a witch's place. He picked all the apples except one. The next morning, when it was barely light, the witch was already standing in the bakery and said: "I don't need anything, but your boy has picked my apples." The baker answered: "That's impossible, because we were baking all night." The boy of course also denied all blame. But the witch was so sure she was right that she called the police.
188841: A will-o'-the-wisp was a shining star. In the past, when people saw a will-o'-the-wisp, they believed the world would come to an end.
188862: A woman who was not allowed to go to the fair said: "I am going dancing anyway, even if it is with the devil." The devil danced with her and stamped through the wooden floor everywhere. The devil flew away with the woman through the window.
188865: A few men went to a farm one evening to chat. The farm's maid was sticking pins into a cushion, whereupon one of the visitors said: "You are a witch and you are tormenting someone." The maid replied: "Then you are a sorcerer." The visitor answered: "That doesn't matter, because if I bewitch three frogs, I do no one any harm." A farmhand who worked on that farm had stomach problems, which were caused by the maid.
188904: In the Minksbossen in Heist-op-den-Berg a monastery had sunk into the ground. The monastery was called Minkshoeve, a name meaning 'monks' farm'. At the place where the monastery had stood, at midnight one could hear a voice calling: "Sold dear and weighed short, sold dear and weighed short!"
188910: A three-year-old child who could not walk always sweated terribly when a certain woman came to visit. The parents went with the child to the friars of Tongerlo, who gave them something to put under the doormat. After that the suspected visitor could no longer come in. A few days later the little boy could walk.
188953: A boy could not stay in his bed at night because he was ridden by the mare.
188957: On a farm one evening roaring was heard in the stable. When people went to look, they saw the animals lying exhausted on the ground. Within seven days seven of the best cows died. The kwade hand (the evil hand, harmful magic) had come over the farm, and the farmer did not go to the friars until it was already too late.
188985: A man who was working with the flail struck at a cat. Afterwards a woman from the neighbourhood wore a bandage around her arm. That woman was suspected of being a witch.
189015: One morning a woman found that plates and glasses had fallen off the mantelpiece. Remarkably, the crockery was not broken. The incident was attributed to a witch.
189018: In Poederlee three children died through witchcraft. The people went to the parish priest, who gave them a holy relic so that the witch could no longer come in.
189034: A woman wanted to take eggs from the land of a wizard on the border of Bonheiden and Rijmenam. But she could not, because the man had fixed the eggs by magic. When some time later the wizard had to come and see a horse of that woman's because the animal had colic, he said: "You didn't get far with my eggs, eh!"
189052: A man riding from Kalmthout to Antwerp had only just set off when a cat sat down on his horse's saddle. After the man had struck at the cat three times with his whip, the animal said: "Now knock me off once more!"
189071: A man who was hunting in the woods saw two sheep appear and sent his dog after them. The man shot, but his gun did not work. When the sheep had disappeared, the man's gun worked again. That place was haunted.
189073: An ugly old woman used to come to a café on the Battelse steenweg. The landlady urged her little daughter not to accept anything from that woman. One evening the girl did accept a sweet from the witch and ate it. A little later the sour sweet began to taste very bitter. After that the girl became very ill. Her mother fetched a friar to read prayers over the child. After the girl was cured, the mother was given a medal to put under the threshold of the house. When the old woman came back a week later, she could not get over the threshold. So people knew for certain that the woman was a witch. She never came back after that.
189076: One morning a beekeeper found his bees lying dead in the hive. That was the work of the neighbour woman, who actually admitted it by saying: "I can still do that."
189083: On a farm where turnips were being pulled, people struck at a cat that was walking around there. People found it strange that the two maids who had come to work on the farm always knew exactly what they had said to each other. When the workers came home, they found that the farmer's wife had a broken arm.
189096: Some musicians coming home through the woods met two or three sorceresses on the way, who asked whether they could play some music. When the musicians said: "God bless you, Kroes", the sorceresses suddenly vanished.
189103: Some men always went to play cards on Sundays at a farmstead in Vremdermeulen. One day a strange gentleman came to join the card game. When one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that instead of feet the gentleman had hoofed legs. The hoofprint could be seen on the door of the farmstead. The devil had knocked there before he came in.
189133: It used to be the custom to put a cow in the meadow with a rope around her leg tied to a stake. A farmer who went to fetch his cow saw a black cat sitting on the stake. The farmer had to walk for a very long time before he got home again.
189139: In the past women were advised not to lend salt or oil to the neighbours. There were people with special powers who could make someone's children cry all night. Those women tortured the children by sticking pins into a cushion.
189162: On a farm they could no longer churn butter because of a witch.
189169: A man was often ridden by the mare. He would crawl into bed and during his sleep hear something approach and crawl onto his chest. The man could no longer move. After a while he woke with a start and was released.
189179: People tried to take a statue of Mary out of the Wijngaardbos in Veerle with a farm cart. It did not work, however, because the horse could not pull the load. In the end they fetched a donkey to take the cart to the church of Veerle, so the statue could be placed there. That went without any trouble.
189180: A man who was hunting hares always saw a hare running at his feet. He could not hit the hare.
189184: A woman who worked as a maid for a farmer saw the ghost of the dead farmer's wife walking about everywhere in the shape of a cat.
189192: On a farm where a woman came to fetch water every day, there was haunting. At night noise was heard in the attic and in the stable. The people went to the friars, who gave them a holy relic to put under the door. After that the woman no longer came to fetch water and she was never seen again.
189204: A farmer whose pigsty was bewitched always saw a black cat walking about. The farmer put a blessed half franc in his gun and shot at the animal. The next day a woman in the village lay wounded in her bed.
189224: A man visited his girlfriend every Sunday. On that man's farm a cow gave birth to a dead calf on eleven Sundays in a row. The old grandmother was responsible for it.
189246: A farm was often visited by an older woman. One night a cow died on that farm and the farmer was woken by a hellish noise. The farmer saw a black cat with glowing eyes standing in the stable. He threw a club at the cat and hit the animal above the eyes. Then the cat disappeared with a loud din. When the woman came to fetch milk again the next day, she did not go into the stable. The farmer and his wife saw that the woman was wounded on the forehead. After that incident there were no more problems in the stable on that farm.
189269: A woman from Vorst went to spin in the evenings at the home of people on the Schootse Hei in Gerhagen. When witches were being talked about, the hostess suddenly said: "I'll show you that I can do something too!" The hostess made the chain of the butter churn dance through the house.
189271: A woman who was ironing saw a witch on the wall. She cried: "There she is again!" and threw the iron against the wall, leaving a black scorch mark there. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood lay in bed with burns on her face.
189289: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his field came back to haunt with the words: "A post, a post! Where shall I carry it to?" When a drunkard answered: "Carry it to the place where you got it", the ghost was released.
189293: A woman was said to have bewitched a child from her own family. She had taken the child out of the cradle and stroked it, saying: "What a sweet, sweet little child!" At the same time she bewitched the child, which became seriously ill as a result.
189342: A man coming back one evening from visiting a farmer bumped into a woman and said: "M., we could run each other to death like this." But the man would have done better not to say that, for one was not supposed to talk to witches. A bit further on the man walked straight into a pit, although he knew the road well and knew the pit was there. The man did not drown and got back onto dry land. A little further on the man stumbled into a pit again. This time too he managed to free himself. In the distance he saw a light at a farm. At that farm a cow was just calving. The man went there and was given dry clothes. After that he got home.
189345: A girl of eleven or twelve suffered from a heart disease and flew up against her bed every night at twelve o'clock. The girl made her Solemn Communion on her deathbed. After the girl's death, the mattress from her bed was put in a barn. A cat that had lain on the mattress died. One day the people heard a little mouse squeaking, although there was nothing to be seen. The child's toys and other belongings were buried. The people were always visited by someone who came to fetch milk. After the girl's death that woman no longer came.
189358: On a farm, noise was sometimes heard in the barn. People would then find that the 'treizel' (?) was working by itself and that the grain was being shaken into it of its own accord.
189377: A man walking over a bridge in the evening saw a cat sitting on the railing and called out: "What are you doing here? Get away!" The man threw his stick and hit the cat, which then ran off yowling. Two years later he came to a farm where he saw his stick hanging on the wall. The man said to the farmer's wife: "That is my stick!", to which she replied: "That may well be, for I lost my eye because of it two years ago!"
189389: A witch lived in Sint-Job. Someone who was not afraid of her saw the witch playing with dolls at midnight.
189397: A woman suspected of being a sorceress was said to have caused the death of three children in a house. Those children always heard an alarm clock going off.
189403: In a café near the Dutch border the accordion was being played while someone was being given the last rites. Suddenly a big black dog came in and crawled under a small low chair. The priest had to chase the dog out, because it was the devil. The fourteen people who were in the café at that moment had to go to confession twice.
189435: A man coming back from Borgerhout one evening saw a black cat jump in front of his feet. The man wanted to jump on his bicycle but could not get on. He started walking, but the cat ran in front of him, so that he fell over the animal.
189444: The will-o'-the-wisps that flew through the air were the souls of unbaptised children. When it was dark, the lights could be seen clearly.
189454: People who were ridden by the mare could not call out or move. Their arms and legs felt as heavy as lead, as if their blood had stopped.
189459: The mare came and lay on people at night. Those people could then not utter a word. When they woke up in the morning, they were dead tired.
189491: In Zemst a rag-and-bone woman always came to visit a farmer. When she came again, the farmer had put a small calf in his pigsty. The rag woman stroked the animal's head and praised it. But even before she left, the calf fell ill. Because nothing could be done, the farmer had to have it slaughtered. Then the farmer sent for a friar, who said: "She won't come in any more. She will look the other way when she walks past here. But you have the prayer of Emperor Charles in the house here. You must get rid of that first, because I can't work like this."
189496: A family lived in a house with a brewer's well, because there had previously been a brewery there. One day a little daughter of those people got large sores. The doctor did not dare to lance the sores. The mother went to a healer in Boom, who said: "It's high time you came! Your little child is called X, isn't she?" The healer gave the mother little holy relics and advised her to do a novena of thirty-six because the evil had already progressed too far. The man also said: "You will see who the guilty one is." All the neighbours came to fetch water from that family. When an old woman wanted to come for water one day, she turned back because she could not get in. That woman never came back after that, although she had often come for water before. Shortly afterwards the girl was cured. The child had fallen ill after the old woman had stroked her and said: "How are you, my sweetheart?"
189536: A man coming back from the village lost his way and ended up at the same broom thicket as many as six or seven times. He had fallen victim to the mare.
189537: A farmer whose stable was full of rats could drive the rats away and make them run to a tree stump.
189558: On a farm in Berlaar there were problems, and the people consulted a man who had special powers. The man said: "Go to the perch where the chickens sleep, take the black hen and chop its head off." The farmer replied: "But we have no black hen." When the farmer went to look, he did see a black hen and did as he had been advised. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had a large cut in her neck. After that the farmer had no more problems.
189599: A woman went to tell the parish priest that a witch lived near her. The priest came along and read prayers over the witch's house, so that it was blessed. When people then knocked on the door, the witch did not come out, but the house suddenly caught fire.
189613: Farmer T. from Brasel always saw a ghost wandering around his farm. It was the spirit of his late wife. When the farmer one day asked what the ghost had come for, it answered: "I have come to say that you need not have masses said for me, for I am in heaven".
189627: A woman from a wealthy non-Catholic family had died. Some time later a distant relative had a mass said for the dead woman. The dead woman had appeared to that person to let them know she had not reached her place. After the mass was said, the ghost never appeared again.
189633: A miller who worked at his mill at night always heard knocking. The miller saw that it was a cat that came knocking. When the cat once stuck its paw inside, the miller chopped off the animal's paw. When he got home, however, he found that his wife was in bed because she had lost a hand.
189663: A witch lived in Merksplas. If you crossed that witch's footprints, she would stop. When that witch was in church, nobody dared to make the sign of the cross with water from the holy water font anymore.
189675: One day a white figure was seen in the churchyard of Vremde. People were afraid at that spot in the evening.
189724: In a house where a cat always came in through the drain hole, some men had hatched a plan. As soon as the cat came in, the men killed the animal with an axe. The next day Bet V.N. was dead. Her body showed a large cut.
189765: In the Mazelakkeren many people used to see a witte madam (white lady). She often bothered people and sometimes stood in front of their beds in the evening.
189787: People who had lost a relative had promised to have thirty masses said. Because the promise had not yet been kept, the spirit of the dead person appeared every night around twelve o'clock until the promised masses had been said.
189857: In the evenings a woman always said: "I needn't lock the door, it's no use anyway. When my husband comes home, he throws it open with his cap."
189858: In Meer there was terrible haunting. A carter who had to bring the last sacraments to a sick person was tormented on the way by cats jumping onto his cart. A black man was also sitting by the sick person's bed. The carter struck at the cat and hit the animal in the hind legs. The next day a woman from the village had broken her leg.
189879: In a house a black cat always scratched with its paw under the door. One day someone struck that cat on the paw. The next day people saw a woman suspected of being a witch walking around with a bandage around her arm.
189885: A heretic returning from Turnhout through the Gierlebos suddenly saw the devil sitting in a tree. The man ran home as fast as he could while a violent thunderstorm broke out. The man converted immediately afterwards.
189886: On the heath near 't Schrijverke lived a farmer whose animals all died. The parish priest said to the farmer: "A woman will come by who will ask you for three things. Make sure you give her everything she asks for." When the witch came by, she asked for a handful of flour, a clog and a worn-out shoe sole. After the farmer had given the witch everything, he had no more misfortune.
189894: On a farm a woman often came round asking for old bread, because she only had fresh bread herself. The people gave old bread and got fresh bread in return. The little daughter who ate the fresh bread became bewitched. The witch also stuck pins into a cushion. The deeper she stuck them, the more pain her victim suffered. If the witch could push the pins all the way into the cushion, the child would die.
189903: To recognise a witch, you had to place your seventh step crosswise on her footprint. Then she would look back.
189909: In Geel 'de gloeiige' (the glowing one) was often seen floating about on the heath. That was the spirit of a shepherd who had to come back to atone because he had moved the boundary post of his field. The ghost walked around with a post on its neck, calling: "Oh, oh, where shall I leave it". One evening someone answered: "Put it back where you got it". Since then 'de gloeiige' has not been seen again.
189915: Some people went to Lier with a cart to buy liquid manure. When they left at one or two o'clock at night, some neighbours said: "Nobody has ever made it home with that woman." It was said that the woman was a witch. Although the people had lanterns of their own, the witch came walking up and said: "Shall I come and give you light?" On the way the people had a lot of bad luck. The scoop came off its handle and the donkey ran into a wall, so that all the manure ran into the cellars of a house. On the way home they had to cross a bridge over the Nete. There the donkey lay down over the railing of the bridge and began to snort. Only when they had hung a cloth over the donkey's head did the animal go on again.
189917: When people had to deal with sickness in the stable or in the house, it was usually caused by the evil hand. Beggar women or old women brought the evil hand into the house. In Oud-Turnhout such a beggar woman always came by. Whenever a child had been born somewhere, people made sure the beggar woman could not touch it. A boy coming home from school had pulled the cap off the beggar woman's head as a joke. That evening the beggar woman called on the boy's parents. When she had been given something and had thanked the people for it, she ran her hand through the boy's curly hair. Later that evening the boy wanted to go to bed and found that he was covered in lice and fleas.
189932: A wizard who drank a lot said one day: "Give me a 'dikkop' (a large glass) of jenever and I can make that farmer stand still". A dikkop cost six cents at the time. The wizard made the farmer stand still and a little later let him carry on sowing.
189983: If you suspected a woman of being a witch, you made a sign of the cross as she walked past. If the woman was a witch, she would look back.
189995: A farmer coming home at night saw a big black dog standing in front of him. With the heavy medlar-wood stick he had with him, the farmer struck his own neck, so that he fainted. When the farmer regained consciousness, the dog was gone. It had been the devil. Because the devil would not let himself be struck, the farmer had to strike himself.
190008: A shepherd who wandered about a great deal had learned all sorts of things on his travels. One day a little boy came to sit with him in the meadow, and he taught him how to make mice. The boy went home and filled the house with mice in five minutes. His parents grew worried and took the boy to the parish priest. There the clergyman took the boy's magic power away. But he had to pass the magic power on to someone else. That other person was allowed to live far away.
190022: The soldiers staying at the slekhoeve had lost a money chest because some of them had fallen asleep on watch. The farmer who found the chest had hidden it under a heap of dung. Because the soldiers could not find the money chest, they died of hunger. From then on the farmer always had bad luck. At night the spirits of the dead soldiers rode over the roof in a glowing wagon. The cardinal or bishop of Mechelen had to come to drive away the haunting.
190037: A man from Olen who had sold his soul to the devil was given a barn that had to be finished when the cock crowed at twelve o'clock. The man told his wife what he had agreed with the devil. Then the woman ran to the henhouse and clapped her hands. A little later the cock began to crow. The barn, however, was not finished, for there was still a hole in it.
190041: A sorceress from Puurs could change herself into a little black cat. People who had seen that black cat around the sorceress's house in the evening were plagued by some illness or other the next morning. This went on until the cat was killed with a dung fork.
190065: A witch from Zoerle-Parwijs knew everything. Sometimes she would suddenly stand still and seem to be looking for something.
190076: Some people bought a cow that had been touched by a witch. The people had no luck with the animal. The witch had not been able to buy that cow herself.
190077: A witch always came to sit on the windowsill of a house where a woman lay sick in bed.
190101: On Christmas night a man went hunting hares in the snow. As he stood waiting behind a tree, he saw ten or twelve hares leaping about among each other. The man fired twice but his gun did not work. Only after he had put a silver coin in the gun did it work. Still, he had not been able to hit a single hare.
190138: On a farm where a new butter churn had been bought, no butter could be made. People came to look at the machine, but nothing seemed to be wrong with it. A witch doctor came by and asked whether someone had perhaps been standing by the churn during the churning. The people immediately thought of a neighbour woman who had knelt by the butter churn and said: "Isn't it working yet? Such good milk!" The witch doctor advised the people to keep that woman out from then on. The people followed the advice and had no more problems.
190144: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children wandering about in the marshes. If you dared to baptise a stallicht, you would die.
190163: Some men who were saying mass as a joke were frightened when a big dog suddenly came in. That dog was the devil.
190200: Two friends who often went fishing together had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what the afterlife was like. After a while one of the friends died. When some other boys were fishing one evening, at midnight they heard a splash in the water, and then a voice said: "The hour is here, but the man is not". The boys did not understand what had been said. The friend, who learned shortly afterwards what had happened, knew at once what was going on.
190208: If you placed your feet in a witch's footprints, she looked back.
190220: Three men had gone for a walk on the heath one evening. Suddenly one of the men began to tremble with fear and said: "Don't you see that over there?" The second man saw nothing, but the third also became afraid, for he saw a group of white figures floating over the heath. The men started running and arrived home deathly pale.
190221: Some people walking near a witch's house were constantly bothered by a cat that walked around their legs. The people kicked at the cat, after which the animal meowed. The next day the witch was walking around with a bandage around her head and bruises on her legs.
190243: An old farm in Boechout was haunted. A man from Vremde driving a cart of potatoes to the city went to the Spokenhof to ask for help because his cart had got stuck. When the man got back to his cart, all the potatoes had vanished. The ghosts had done it.
190272: In Poppel there lived a woman who bewitched mostly children, but sometimes adults too.
190276: A brave young man was scared to death when he had seen a ghost.
190282: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. The lights tried to lure people to the water because they wanted to be baptised.
190294: People who were ridden by the mare seemed to be dreaming, but were awake. It was said that such a thing was a standstill in the blood. Those people saw and heard all sorts of things, but could not move. They were terribly frightened. When they managed to call out, it suddenly ended.
190296: A man coming back at night from visiting his girlfriend met a child half a metre tall. The child walked towards him with its little arms spread. The man asked: "Have you run away?", to which the child answered "Yes!"
190305: In Kontich an old woman lived alone in a little house. That woman was suspected of being a witch. Opposite the witch lived a master bricklayer, against whose house a lime shed had been built. When the man was slaking lime one day, a cat ran out of his neighbour's house across the street. The man threw a stone at the cat and injured the animal's paw. The cat hurried inside. When the witch came outside a little later, she was limping.
190323: At 't Moleneind a little cat always came and sat on a carter's wagon. The carter cursed and then put the cat in a tree. The next day people had to go and fetch the witch out of that tree.
190327: One morning a man found that his daughter was covered in vermin. On the girl, but also on the bed, on the cupboard and on the floor, there were all kinds of big creatures like pig lice, in different colours and with different tails. The evening before, a sorcerer had come to play cards with the father. The man said to himself: "If this is not over by tomorrow, I will drag him out of his house and cut his throat." The next moment the lice had disappeared.
190341: A boatman who wanted to go on board one evening could not get there because he saw dancing white women floating in the air in front of him.
190354: A man always saw a ghost dragging a post around and saying: "Where do I go with my post, where do I go with my post…" When one day the man had answered: "Take it back to the place where you got it", the ghost no longer appeared.
190358: A three-year-old child suddenly fell ill. The child kept crying and called out: "Mummy, don't you see that black man on the cupboard?" The others, however, did not see him. The people became afraid and afterwards always saw a strange black cat in their house. They could not keep the cat out. Even when the people put a full bucket of water in front of the door, the cat knocked the bucket over. Finally the woman went to the fathers of Tongerlo. It took her two hours to get there. Her legs were heavy as lead and the woman got lost twice. The father told her who the witch was, but the woman was not allowed to speak to the witch if she met her. The woman was given a relic to put under her door. She also had to spend the first night praying. At midnight the door suddenly opened and the cat came in. But the animal got no further than the relic. It walked around it several times, meowing, and then suddenly vanished. The next day the child was cured.
190399: If a woman was suspected of being a witch, people walked behind her and crossed her footprints. Then the witch could go no further.
190431: A woman who was ridden by the mare was completely stiff and could not get up. She tried to call out, but no sound came.
190434: On a farm the farmer's wife went to fetch her husband, saying: "Come and see how much butter there is in the butter churn!" When the farmer and his wife reached the churn, all the butter had strangely disappeared.
190437: A mother whose husband suffered from a mental illness had to care for seven children on her own. When the mother could no longer pay her rent, her two cows, her horse and the contents of her house were sold. The family then moved to the Watering, where the father died. The twelve-year-old daughter went to work on the plantation in the woods for half a franc a week. When the girl came home in the evening, her way was blocked by cats running around her legs. One evening the girl saw a big calf lying on the little bridge over the Zwarte Loop. When the girl got home, she fainted with fear. Her mother went to look at the bridge, but no longer saw the calf there. The girl was the victim of a witch who tormented her.
190443: When people had been to the friars of Bornem, they could not get home. The witches made sure they did not get home.
190492: A man met a cat in a lane and kicked at the animal. The next day a man with a black eye was walking around the village. That man was a wizard.
190493: In the old days many people were troubled by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) in their cowsheds.
190498: Jan S. went for a walk with a girl. When a disagreement arose, the girl suddenly vanished. Jan saw a cat walking in front of him.
190528: A witch who often went out at night and did harm had made a farmer's daughter ill. One evening knocking was heard on the window shutters at that farm. The people came outside and saw a black cat sitting in front of the door. The farmer took off his clog and threw it at the cat, which then ran off yowling. The next day the witch stood at the door together with the village policeman. She came to complain because the farmer had mistreated her and she was limping as a result.
190537: A man on the heath shot at a hare, which then ran away. In the verge the hunter saw a woman sitting, straightening her cap.
190599: One morning a maid had to go and dig up a bucket of potatoes. Instead of potatoes, the maid found nothing but marbles in the ground. There was only one plant with potatoes on it. That must have been witchcraft.
190609: A mother of ten children had a child that was born with half an arm and was sick. A man said to the mother: "You must keep X out, because she has bewitched the child. You must put a holy object under the threshold, so that this woman can no longer come in. When the child is about to die, the woman will come in." The witch came by with a plate of eggs but could not get in, although the mother invited her to come inside. Just before the child died, the witch came in.
190613: A boy who was going to the fair with his girlfriend said on the way: "I need to go to the toilet" and he disappeared. A little later the boy, in the shape of a werewolf, leapt at the girl. When the two got home, the girl found that her boyfriend had the fibres of her neckerchief between his teeth.
190616: On a farm where the stable was bewitched, a black cat always came and sat in the pig trough. The pigs would then sit motionless on their hind legs. One day the farmer threw his clog at the animal and hit it. The cat was not seen again. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood lay in bed with back pain.
190626: On a farm where they had a lot of misfortune with the animals, the farmer went to a man who knew more than others and said to him: "Go home. You will meet the guilty one, but make sure she passes you on the right-hand side. That will not be easy." On his way home the farmer met that woman. She kept wanting to pass on the left. In the end the farmer had to force the woman to pass him on the right. After that the farmer had no more problems in his stable.
190635: A church is said to have sunk in the Diepdal. Bells could still be heard ringing there. Stallichten (stable lights, ghostly lights) could sometimes be seen as well.
190644: A man was visited by a witch who came to ask him whether he would go and fetch peat. The man refused. A little later he decided to go after all, but he made up his mind not to drive past the witch's house. On the way the man's cart fell apart.
190667: Witches could make horses lie on their backs in the manger.
190695: In a house in Merksplas something strange happened at the birth of a child. The newborn immediately sat up on its bottom. The midwife was a witch.
190696: On a farm strange things happened because of a neighbour woman. The cows could not calve, not a single crop grew in the field, many animals died, the horse had a paralysed right leg, and the animals in the stable grew restless whenever that woman passed by. Neither priests nor friars could help. The people made novenas, but that too was in vain. The misfortune only ended when the neighbour woman died.
190697: One evening T. was coming back from visiting his girlfriend in Gestel. On the Borcht T. saw a white friar holding a post and calling: "Post, where shall I leave you? Post, where shall I leave you?" After T. had answered: "Take it back to the place where you got it", the dead friar was released.
190707: Near D.'s house, a bolting horse was often heard at night. A moment later a splash in the water would be heard.
190710: On a farm where the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) was in the stables, the cows stood for eleven mornings in a row with stiff tails all pointing to the same spot.
190717: Dwaaslichten or stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children floating above the ground. Glow-worms were not stallichten. A man who saw a will-o'-the-wisp approaching and slammed the door found that the light came along with him.
190749: During high mass some men were playing cards in a café in Heultje. A stranger came in, ordered a glass of beer and sat down with the players. When one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had goat's legs. One of the players had said: "I am going to play cards, even if I have to play with the devil."
190755: A miller was always bothered at his mill by a cat that scratched under the door. The miller chopped off one of the cat's paws and afterwards found that his wife had only one hand left.
190806: Kobeke was of another faith. After his death he came back to haunt in the shape of a donkey or another animal.
190830: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend suddenly saw two women standing in front of him. The man had to dance with each of the women, or else, they said, he would not get home. At first the man refused, but then he indeed could not get home. Only after he had danced could he easily go home.
190845: A mother lost two children within three months. A third child became very ill. The child had been bewitched by a woman visitor who came bringing all sorts of things, and by a black kitten that lay on the children's bed. A woman from Jette advised the mother to offer a novena to Saint Anthony and to push prayer cards under the door. After that the little boy recovered and the kitten disappeared. The suspicious visitor could no longer get into the house.
190888: In the glass factory in Schelle a sorceress always went about in the shape of a black cat. One day the cat flew at two small children, who were bewitched by it. The people went to the parish priest to have the children overlezen (prayed over to lift a spell). The priest sweated terribly while doing so.
190903: A witch said: "Over hedge, over hedgerow, to Cologne into a wine cellar". A man who wanted to copy this said: "Through hedge, through hedgerow, to Cologne into a wine cellar". That man had made a mistake in speaking the magic formula.
190909: If you saw a suspicious woman, you had to cross her footprints. If the woman stood still, you knew she was a witch. A few boys coming home from school unmasked a witch this way.
190951: A man came to a woman who had put a bundle of firewood in the hearth. When lots of mice ran out of the wood, the man said: "I'll kill them," but the woman replied: "No, for those are my children."
190972: A woman shouted at a schoolchild who had been fighting in the street: "You'll pay for that!" Afterwards the child fell ill. The child's legs swelled up terribly. When the parish priest was with the child, the witch suddenly stood at the door.
190978: A man who lived behind the station of Tessenderlo saw a cat come in through the drain hole every evening. One day the man hit the cat on the head with a stick. A little later the man heard the priest passing by: he was going to give a woman the Last Sacraments.
190982: A witch could always tell exactly what time people had come home at night.
190998: A boy climbed a tree because he wanted to see whether there were eggs in the bird's nest. An old woman who was said to be a witch said to the boy: "Don't bother looking, there's nothing in the nest." That turned out to be true. When the boy went to look again the next day, there were nine hatched eggs in the nest. The witch must have conjured the eggs out of the nest.
191001: A man who was troubled by witchcraft in his stable went to the friars of Bornem. On the way the man sometimes could not take another step, and sometimes it seemed as if he was walking through water. The friars said the man had done well to keep going, because now they could still help him.
191011: When people left church on Sunday, some of them found that their clothes were torn. Every Sunday the victims were different. One Sunday the parish priest said from the pulpit: "If the person who torments people every Sunday carries on like this, I will make his or her name known." After mass a woman remained sitting in the church. She was said to be the sorceress.
191037: A man returning from the market with two cows met an old woman on the way, who said: "Farmer, you have fine cows. Won't you sell them to me?" When the farmer refused, the woman replied: "You won't have them in your stable for a year." The farmer laughed and went on. But two weeks later his animals were dead.
191041: A midwife coming home late in the evening saw a foal approaching. The closer the foal came to her, the bigger it grew. The woman could no longer cry out. She leapt against the door, after which everything flew to pieces.
191043: In 'De Lichten' in Booischot countless cats sat meowing. People did not dare to walk through those woods. They believed those cats were witches.
191085: A woman who kept seeing her dead husband appear was advised by the priest to speak to the ghost. In this way the woman learned that she had to have three masses said on Salvator. When the woman had done so, the ghost was never seen again.
191088: A poacher from Roermond (NL) was after a hare that ran around at night in a miller's sprout field. When the poacher shot at the hare, it seemed as if a hundred sacks of leaves were being shaken out. The man had missed. On the second attempt he missed again. Then he took a guilder, chopped it in four and put a piece in his gun. This time he hit it. The hare turned out to be the miller's wife. Witches could not withstand anything blessed, and in the old days all money was blessed.
191095: The stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) that flew through the air were the souls of unbaptised children. You had to baptise the lights. But you were not allowed to point at them, because then the lights would settle on your finger.
191100: Two women always walked together to the butter market. One woman would knock on the other's shutter, so that the other knew she had to get ready to leave. One morning that woman heard a knock and called out: "Yes." A little later the house began to be haunted. By calling "yes" the woman had given the witch permission to haunt. After that the shutters of the house banged open and shut every night. Rumbling was heard and the chairs in the room moved by themselves. It got so bad that men from the neighbourhood came to keep watch in the house at night. When they jumped outside, they saw only a cat running. The old parish priest of Berlaar read prayers over the house. After that the haunting was over.
191104: A woman saw cats dancing paw in paw on the old road. Very beautiful music could also be heard.
191131: At the Spokenhof the window shutters kept banging open and shut all night, even though they had been fastened.
191154: A witch lived in Arendonk. When a child was to be baptised, people did not dare pass the witch's house with the newborn, because witches had power over unbaptised children. Nor did they ever tell the witch the child's name before it was baptised.
191158: It was haunted at Jef V.Z.'s in Zittaart. One day a chapel walked around there and struck a red hand into the door.
191177: There were rabbits running all over the market. A boy picked up one of the rabbits and took it home, where he wanted to show it to his aunt. But there the boy found he was holding a handful of little bones. His aunt advised him to take the bones back to the churchyard. When he did so, the bones turned back into a rabbit, which then hopped away.
191196: On a farm on the Botermarkt, witches came into the stable at midnight. The cows would then start making a racket. The parish priest of Schoten was consulted. The clergyman claimed the trouble was due to poverty and lice. Still, he read prayers over the stable, after which the situation improved.
191201: In a house where the mother had been dead for seven years, the people were sitting at the table one evening when they heard rumbling in the attic. The mother's white cap, which lay on the cupboard, was suddenly thrown towards the oven. Coffee beans flew out of the hole where the potatoes were kept.
191222: A man was always pursued by a goat when he came back from visiting his girlfriend.
191247: A farm was always haunted. The plates standing on the mantelpiece were smashed at night, but the next morning they were back in their place. In the end the people went to the dean, who gave them a relic to put under the threshold. That put an end to the strange happenings.
191265: A man had a dog called Juul. One day the man was trudging through the Warande and lost his dog. The man lost his way and wandered about sweating for a long time. When the man met someone, his dog was suddenly back. The man put his hands in his pockets and felt nothing but acorns.
191285: On the Kruisbaan in Mol a man suddenly saw a black cat jump in front of his bicycle. The chain came off the bicycle and could not be put back on. A woman came by, who said: "Not going well?" and put the chain back on the bicycle without any trouble. A little further on the man saw the black cat again and his bicycle would not go any further. The same woman sat on the back and said: "Friend, can't you go on again?" After that the man could continue. That woman could change herself into a cat and went about tormenting people in that shape.
191332: A woman came to a man to ask for a basket that was supposed to be in his house. The man said he knew nothing about a basket and slammed the door. A week later the man was dead. The other people who had heard about the basket quickly began searching everywhere. A beautiful basket emerged from the dead man's bedding. They put the basket on a little platform, but the next day it was already gone. That woman must have spirited it away.
191404: An old woman often came to a farm and stroked the animals in the stable. Afterwards the animals fell ill and died. After a farmer had the parish priest read prayers over the stable, the old woman never came back and everything in the stable came right.
191421: A man visiting friends stroked a cat that had jumped onto his lap and said: "Oh pussycat, how nicely warm you are!" When the man went home later that evening, he met a cat that he could not get rid of and that said: "X said to me, oh pussycat, warm yourself".
191424: A boy who was coming back from Kapellen with his girlfriend said to the girl: "Go on ahead. I still have to go somewhere. If you should meet anything, throw a large white handkerchief at it." No sooner said than done. When the girl saw her boyfriend coming back, she saw that he still had the white pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
191427: A man who always came home late in the evening from work saw a beautiful young lady in a long white dress standing under the trees. Suddenly the man saw the young lady standing behind him.
191438: A woman who was ridden by the mare could hardly breathe because something was lying on her.
191439: An old woman from Mazel (Tielen) who was suspected of being a witch tried to frighten a girl with a goat.
191462: A man and a woman coming back from the fair in Wezel saw two cats running in front of their feet the whole time. The two kicked at the cats but could not hit the animals. At a certain moment the cats had disappeared. When the man and the woman got home, they saw those same cats sitting on a chest in their house.
191476: Around the Postel abbey there was a moat. Next to that moat was a large gate leading to the baroness's residence. It was always haunted there. One day some people saw a white shade with rattling chains there.
191497: A boy was riding with his father one evening from Norderwijk to Achter-Olen. On the way the two saw a little white rabbit come out of a house and follow them. The father struck at the rabbit with a stick and rode on. When the two passed the little house the rabbit had jumped out of again the next day, they saw the little woman who lived there standing outside with a bandage around her arm. The woman said: "I'll get you too someday!"
191518: A man returning from the fair at Hombeek met a stranger who asked: "Are you coming along?" The man followed the stranger and walked behind him until five o'clock. Then the man found himself at his front door. The stranger had vanished. He had no more power because the sun had risen.
191525: People who had promised to go on pilgrimage and had died before keeping that promise had to haunt after their death.
191536: In Wiekevorst the miller always ground at night. Although he locked the door, the sacks were always jumbled in the morning. One night the miller saw a cat's paw in the gap of the door. He grabbed the paw and cut into it with his knife. When the miller went home the next morning, he saw that his wife had almost lost her hand. That woman had to do harm. If she could not do it to strangers, she had to do it to her own family.
191583: If sorceresses could not torment anyone, they were tormented themselves. That is why they kept a little doll in the house into which they stuck pins.
191602: In Weelde many cats were often seen in the trees and on the road. Those cats were witches, who held gatherings at midnight. Under no circumstances should one kick at the witches, for then one was lost.
191604: In summer a goat could be seen flying in Vorst.
191646:
A mother whose three-year-old son was ill was sent by the parish priest to the friars and to the specialist, because the boy had probably been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). The mother followed the advice, after which her child's health improved.
The boy had been bewitched after a woman had visited and said to him: "What a handsome little fellow!" The woman had come to say she had just slaughtered a pig and offered the people some soup. The people had accepted the soup and so got into trouble.
From the friars they received a holy object to put under the door. After that the witch never came by again to ask how things were.
191694: In Meer lived a poor farmer who had no barn. A handsome gentleman came to visit and promised him a new barn in exchange for his best pledge. The barn would be finished before the cock had crowed the next morning. The farmer agreed and signed a contract. When the farmer and his wife heard knocking at night, the farmer told what he had done. The farmer's wife immediately understood that her husband had sold his soul. She got up and went to the stable with the lantern, which made the cock begin to crow too early. At that moment the barn was not yet finished. The hole in the barn could never be closed.
191699: A man with special powers had sold his soul to the devil. When that man's time was up, the devils came to fetch him. They threw his body against the wall of the room, so that his brains splattered all around.
191715: A woman coming back from the shop was followed by a cat. At the woman's house the cat stayed sitting in front of the threshold. For two days the woman was followed everywhere by the cat. After the people had read the Gospel of Saint John, the cat stayed away.
191725: A man who lived near the Hellevonder went hunting in 't Witven on All Saints' Day, although his wife had advised him against it. The man shot at a hare, but could not hit the animal. A little later a witte juffrouw (white lady) came out of the ditch, carrying the hare under her arm.
191728: A woman often came to visit a farm. Whenever that happened, the cows in the stable looked up and the animals would not eat any more. On that farm no butter could be churned either. When the people were once again visited by that woman, they saw the visitor change into a cat.
191741: A man from Wijnegem was coming back from visiting his girlfriend in Wommelgem. On the way the man lost his way. He thought he was standing by the church of Wommelgem, but he was in a shed where a farmer's cart stood. Before leaving, the man had also visited a friend whose mother was suspected of being a witch.
191747: A girl always saw a mouse sitting on the floor in front of her whenever her mother wanted to feed her. When people threw something at the mouse, they could not hit the animal.
191757: A folk healer could fix thieves to the spot at his fruit trees, so that they stayed pointing at the tree. When one day the maid saw such a person standing there and said: "Look, someone is standing there", the wizard said: "Oh, he's stood there long enough. Go and tell him he may leave".
191777: People who could not churn butter were afflicted by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) in their stable.
191786: In de Keten there once lived rich farmers who publicly mocked God. The devil naturally had those farmers in his power. In the evening the devil appeared in the form of a black cat and went to meow at the door of a farm. One of the farmers opened up and let the cat in. When the parish priest heard this story, he went to keep watch one evening. As soon as the cat appeared, the priest made a big sign of the cross. The cat then screamed loudly and it seemed as if it crawled into the ground. It disappeared for good.
191791:
If you put a wedding ring under the doormat, no witches could come in.
A woman who was milking a goat in the stable was startled at the sight of a cat. Later the woman gave birth to twins. One child had a cat's head and the other had Down syndrome. The child with the cat's head was made to disappear. The woman had been bewitched during her pregnancy.
191796: On the market square of Zwijndrecht there once stood a large lime tree in which big black cats always sat. Those cats probably had something to do with the devil. One day those cats are said to have bewitched someone, leaving that person paralysed for life. A man always made the sign of the cross whenever he had to pass that tree.
191798: If you put the paper knob of a 'paarskaars' (possibly Easter candle) in the house, witches could no longer cross the threshold.
191814: A woman took the bus to Niel to visit a friend. When the woman got off the bus, she recognised nothing. Although she knew Niel well, she could not find her bearings. She tried to resist, but sweated terribly and could not make any headway. In the end a small child took the woman to her friend. The woman was carrying a small holy object, which meant the witch could not follow her.
191829: When it was dark, a large light could sometimes be seen hanging in the sky above the woods. Those were the souls of unbaptised children wandering about. That was the stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp).
191836: At the Wimp in Morkhoven the spirit of a dead girl sat washing. Peer went to look, because the girl had been his sweetheart.
191875: The wife of V.O. was a witch. One night the man found a broom lying next to him in bed.
191887: On the Hoevebrug a father and his child saw a cat sitting. The little child said: "Father, shall I knock that cat off there?" The cat replied: "Little man, if you did not have holy water on your head, I would make you a head shorter".
191908: A man on his way to get his unemployment card stamped saw a cat and struck at it. When the man struck at the cat again a little later, there were dozens of cats.
191925: A man coming home in the evening with a cart kept seeing black cats jumping through the spokes of the wheels. The man struck at the cats with his whip, but afterwards many more appeared. At the pond in Achterheide the man was rid of the cats.
191928: A statue of Mary was found in the Wijngaardbos in Veerle. People wanted to take the statue to Averbode, but on the way the horses suddenly could go no further, so they were forced to bring the statue back.
191929: On a farm in Aartselaar, half the animals lay dead one morning. When they tried to keep the meat, it began to stink, so it could not be used. The people then went to the friars, who gave them a holy object. After that nothing more happened to the animals.
191969: A miller saw his dead father appear on the stairs of the mill, asking for a pilgrimage. Every day the ghost stood one step higher. When the ghost stood at the very top, it could go to the Lord.
191991: Some men coming back from the fair in Oorderen met a black priest on the way. At the Zeven Wegen on the road to Oorderen a priest was once murdered.
192026: A woman always knew everything that had happened. One day, when her husband had gone to fetch hay in the meadow, she sat in her house and said: "Right now our Jan is falling off the hay cart and he is dead." And so it was.
192066: At the spookboske (haunted wood) near the road to Bolk, a werewolf sat at the Drieboomkenskuil. Sometimes that werewolf could be heard roaring. People believed that someone would then soon die. A boy coming back drunk from the fair in Hoogstraten saw a large white headless horse appear. The next day people were cutting down trees there. When the last six branches were being cut, a branch always flew out of the billhook.
192102: In a house in Mol the eldest daughter cried every night. Her head swelled up and she heard dogs howling, although nobody else could hear the animals. At five in the morning she heard a whistle. The girl was said to have once told a suspicious woman: "You are a witch." That is why the witch did her harm.
192119: A workman met a cat in the evening that kept running between his legs. When the man said: "You won't bite me", the cat leapt up at him, so that he could not get home.
192120: Two brothers digging potatoes saw a woman in a hooded cloak coming towards them across the field. The woman bent down and began making signs of the cross over the field. The boys believed the woman was bewitching their field and ran at her with their manure forks. Although the woman was a good seventy or eighty years old, the eighteen-year-old boys could not catch her. The woman always came to get milk and eggs from the brothers' father. After that incident, however, she got nothing more. Without anyone having told her, the woman went to the neighbours to ask for what she needed.
192144: Two sorceress witches lived on a farm on the heath. One morning a horse was found there in the stable. Before that, the horse had stood in a wooden shed. Strangely enough, no door was damaged.
192147: A witch lived on a farm in Gierle. This only became known when a horse died there. Once, when the farmer and the witch were standing in the stable together, the witch stood in front of the horse and said: "Yes, little fellow, your turn has come too!" A day later the animal was dead. But the farmer had heard what the witch said and showed her the door.
192156: Antwerp cathedral is said to have been built on ox hides and to sink a few centimetres into the ground every year. During the construction the master builder had told his wife that there was only one way to build the cathedral, namely by setting the building on ox hides. Their little son had overheard this, but his father said to him: "If you tell anyone, I'll beat you to death". The boy told the secret to a friend anyway, who turned out to be the architect's son. The master builder found out and beat his son to death.
192157: A boy was in a relationship with a girl whose mother was suspected of witchcraft. When the boy was visiting his girlfriend and wanted to leave for home at midnight, the girl's mother said: "Better stay until tomorrow morning, because you'll get wet!" The boy left anyway. Not ten minutes later the boy fell into a brook.
192180: A farmer had to go to the White Fathers every year to be freed from the witchcraft a neighbour woman worked on him. Witches were compelled to do evil. On that farm the butter churn plungers struck all the way up to the ceiling.
192181: In a house where a child had fallen ill through witchcraft, the family went to the monastery. They had to bring bread and eel to the monastery. But before the people were back, their child was already dead. The witchcraft had gone too far.
192201: A woman was annoyed by a kitten that always came to sit on her lap. One day the woman poured hot sauce over the cat. The next day it was found that a woman from the village was badly burned all over.
192202: A pig butcher met a woman carrying a flowerpot. When the butcher met that woman for the third time, he said: "If I meet you once more, I'll take my axe and strike it!" After that the butcher never saw the woman again.
192245: A woman had bought a butter churn in Vosselaar and was taking it home in a wheelbarrow. Along the way a witch stood watching. As the woman passed, the witch said: "But you can't make butter with that!" And indeed, the first time she used the churn, the woman could not make butter.
192246: On a farm where butter could not be churned and the foals stopped growing, the people went to the fathers. They believed a witch had caused the misfortune.
192249: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that would be finished the next morning. In the morning, however, there was still a big hole in the barn. The barn still stands between Bollebeek and Koppegem.
192275: On a farm in Stabroek the people were always visited by a witch who came begging. The maid who worked on the farm was very superstitious and claimed that you could recognise a witch by crossing her footprints. One day, when the beggar woman left the yard, the maid set her foot crosswise on the footprint. The beggar woman turned around and asked whether they meant to mock her much longer. After that the maid was very frightened.
192284: In a house a mouse always came in through the drain hole. One day the woman living in the house struck that mouse on the paw. The next day the woman found that her sister had a wound on her hand.
192289: A mother with a seven-year-old child was always visited by a woman from Achterbos, who brought rock candy for the child. That woman would lie flat on her stomach and beat the ground with her hands, laughing. Some time later the child died. After that the visitor no longer came in, but she always walked around the house screaming. On her husband's advice the mother went to the fathers, who advised her to burn all the child's toys. When the mother took the tram home, she saw strange figures through the window. After the tram ride she continued on foot. Suddenly she saw something leap in front of her and her knee gave way. There was a hole in her woollen skirt. The mother sewed a patch over the hole, but the fabric always frayed. It was a new skirt, but the mother had to throw it away. The visitor still often came around, but she no longer came inside.
192298: Some card players sat cursing. One man was dealt clubs and dropped the card. After all, they were crosses, and he could not hold them. Another man bent down to pick up the dropped card and saw that the fellow had horse's feet. It must have been the devil.
192336: A woman with a bad reputation had two daughters who did good, cheap sewing. A mother had her sewing done there, and one day she accompanied her daughter to have a dress fitted by the seamstresses. The girl had barely come in when the supposed witch offered her a pear. The girl said she had diarrhoea and so could not eat a pear. So the girl went to the toilet. On her way there she saw, through the open cellar door at the bottom of the stairs, about a hundred burning candles in a heap of white sand. The girl lured her mother to that spot so she could see the candles too. After the fitting, mother and daughter left at once. As they left, the witch offered the girl a pear once more. After that incident the mother never had sewing done there again.
192364: In Achtel-Rijkevorsel lived a woman who had learned from a calf herder how to conjure up mice without tails. The parish priest came and said a prayer to give the mice tails. That did not work, however, and the woman lost her magic power.
192366: A woman was bewitched by an old witch who lived diagonally across from her. The fathers read prayers over the woman and gave her a medal to nail above the door. Because of it, the witch could only enter if the woman gave her permission. When the witch came by, the woman did not let her in. But her grandmother, sitting by the conservatory in the garden, called out that the visitor could come in. So the woman was bewitched again. This time nothing could be done, and the woman died of the witchcraft.
192370: Two women from Sint-Job always wore hooded cloaks and walked around arm in arm, whispering. They were witches. These witches sometimes came into the stable on a farm. At midnight all the cows there lay on their sides. When the people tried to churn, they could not make butter. The people went to the fathers of the Ossemarkt, who advised them to do penance. After that the situation improved.
192380: Two men were keeping watch over a dead body. While the men were stoking up the koeketel (?), they suddenly heard a knock on the door. When there was a second knock, the men went upstairs. There they found that the dead man's feet were already warm. The men had barely come back down when the dead man came and sat by the fire with them, saying: "Men, it's cold, isn't it!" Terrified, the men ran away.
192418: In the old days there were witches who could do people great harm. A man who was visited by a woman said the following: "When the turnips were bacon, I had to hold my tongue, but now that the cat is hare, I'll give the cuckoo of my master." After that the farmhand who had worked in that house for nine years left. For the next nine years the people could not take on another farmhand.
192455: In de Hoek a little girl had received the last rites. While the neighbours stood outside talking about the poor girl, a skipper from a shipyard came by and asked what was the matter. On hearing the story the skipper said: "Now you must go and call the father's mother." They did so twice, but the grandmother said she had no time. When a cart of pitch wood was being unloaded in the street, the skipper set the wood on fire and said: "Now she'll come." They went to call the woman a third time, and this time she did come. The skipper forced her to undo the harm she had done. At first the woman claimed she had done nothing, but the skipper threatened to throw her into the burning wood, and then she confessed. The woman took a flower from under the sick girl's pillow. The petals were still closed. If they had been open, the girl would have died.
192509: A man was sitting with the old sexton in the village. When the man wanted to go home, the sexton said: "No, that's not true, you're not going home." The sexton gave the man one franc if he stayed a while longer. After a while the man said again: "I'm going home." The sexton again said: "That's not true," but the man left anyway. Then the man wandered about the whole night. In the morning he found himself by the Eierenbossen on the other side of Berlaar. He was soaking wet because he had walked through ditches. At sunrise the man immediately found his way again. He felt in his pocket and found he had been given only five cents instead of one franc. Yet when he received the coin, he had clearly seen that it was one franc.
192542: A woman suspected of being a witch always sat at the window. The children coming home from school had to pass by there. One day a girl came by crying because her apron was torn. The witch spoke to the girl: "Come, I'll mend it." It was said that the witch had bewitched the girl.
192559: A kalverkruier (calf carter) from Arendonk could work magic. When he had to go to prison, he said to his friends: "Go to the café and order a glass of beer for me." Without anyone seeing bolts drawn or doors opened, the wizard escaped from prison. When the wizard repented, he had to go to confession in Turnhout. He then had to do penance and the bells were rung for eight days.
192573: In 't Bergbos a spirit came haunting, carrying a boundary post and calling all the time: "Where do I leave it, where do I leave it?" One day a drunkard came by, who answered: "Put it where you got it!" After that the spirit was not seen again.
192606: A witch brought a sack of young goats to a farmer and said: "Go ahead, take them out." When the farmer opened the sack, there were potatoes in it. The farmer did not dare give those potatoes to the animals and threw them into the dog kennel.
192632: In Vorst lived a witch who had a son. The witch very much wanted the neighbour girl to marry her son, but the girl did not want to. Some time later the girl got sores all over and fell ill. When the girl had died, her skin, strangely enough, became healthy again.
192657: In a family in Turnhout a little child had fallen ill after receiving a small necklace from a woman. When prayers were read over the sick child, the woman who had given the necklace came pounding hard on the door.
192676: Some young men always went to play billiards in the café on the corner of the Spekkestraat. The two old people who lived there had special powers, which caused one of the young men to lose his way one evening. That witch had done it to him.
192679: In Kasterlee there used to be a house that was badly haunted. Music or cats wailing could always be heard in the chimney, but when people went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
192683: When you walked through the churchyard in the evening, you always saw many stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) flickering. They were dancing ghosts.
192684: Some people who kept pigeons had caught a cat in a sack in the hayloft. Nearby lived a woman who had cats. The people beat the captured cat against the concrete floor at least twenty times, and still the animal was not dead. Only after a neighbour struck the cat a second time with a flail was it dead. The woman who lived nearby said: "Now they have caught my cat."
192728: On a farm troubled by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft), the cows began leaping backwards at midnight. A father was brought from Gent, who removed the evil hand and sweated heavily while doing so.
192744: A man felt himself attacked from all sides in broad daylight. He wanted to call out, but no sound came. His wife saw that something was wrong, ran to his bed and cried: "But Stan, what's the matter with you!" The moment the woman spoke her husband's name, the mare had gone.
192749: An ugly old woman was suspected of being a witch. A boy was very afraid of that witch, but one day he found himself forced to knock at her door because he was hungry. The witch gave the boy a slice of bread with sugar. When he had left her house, the neighbours advised him to throw that bread away. The neighbours said: "Throw that away quickly, or tomorrow you'll be lying dead in your bed. She is a witch, who gave you sugar to bewitch you."
192764: A man who worked in the glass factory saw a cat come in through the water drain hole while he was lying in bed. The man sat up on his bed. One day, when the man was riding to work, the cat was sitting in front of him. The man decided not to go around it but, on the contrary, to ride over the cat. "Now you've got me", the cat then said.
192805: In Ruisbroek lived a sorceress who harmed small children. In houses with a child, the witch stuck pins into a cushion, which caused the child great pain. As long as the pins were not out of the cushion, nothing could be done for the child.
192819: On a farm that had much misfortune, a cat crept in through the drain hole at night. One day the farmer managed to chop off the cat's front paw. The next day he found that his mother was in bed because she had lost a hand.
192832: A man walking through the woods one evening heard a cat wailing. The man picked up the animal and took it with him. As the man went on, however, the cat grew heavier and heavier until he finally had to drop it. The man stumbled, looked down and saw an old, shrivelled little woman at his feet rubbing her leg.
192834: A newborn child always had maggots under its navel bandage. The child was bewitched by a woman who was always visiting. The family had prayers read over the child by a man from Deuren, who advised them to keep the witch out from then on. After that the child had no more trouble with maggots.
192891: When the first stone of the cathedral was to be laid, a large crowd had gathered on the Handschoenmarkt. Workmen walked back and forth, while representatives of the clerical and secular authorities stared gloomily into the hole. Three times the dug pits had filled with water. A simple mason named Mathias knew a solution. However, he would only reveal it in exchange for a lot of gold. Mathias wanted to lay ox hides on the foundations because water could not seep through them. But Mathias had been overheard by his youngest son, who ran to the master builder and gave away the secret. When Mathias learned that his plan had leaked out, he beat his son to death with a wooden bench. His wife drowned herself in the Steenhouwersvest out of despair.
192901: A man who had been out at night catching rabbits and hares was accompanied on his way home by a kitten. The man took the kitten with him, put it in a basket at home and tied an apron over it. The next day the kitten had vanished, although the basket was still closed.
192913: On Bonheiden Steenweg there once lived a woman who did people harm. She had made four little dolls and given them away. A boy who had received such a doll became very ill and the doctor could not help him. Then the fathers were sent for. One of the fathers kept praying by the boy the whole time, until he was drenched in sweat. The boy survived, but he was never fully cured. The other children who had received a doll died. The people were advised to bury a bottle of urine under the sand. If the bottle burst, the witch would have to die. On a Monday the bottle burst and the witch was found dead.
192928: A farmer's wife was churning butter when an old woman came into the stable, leaned over the churn and said: "Look how much butter you're getting!" Then the woman was gone. The farmer's wife could not churn another gram of butter, and what she had churned before had vanished. The farmer's wife was helped by a small relic from the fathers. The first churnful she made after that was overflowing.
192942: A farmer who often went to buy calves in Zittaart could not keep a single animal alive. The farmer went to Tongerlo, where he was given a relic to put under the door. Because of it the witch could no longer come in.
192961: Two men who were often drunk came home stone-cold sober one day. At a certain place the men saw a white puddle. They had barely passed that place when they were chased by a little dog. They kicked the animal, but could not hit it. Only when the men had each taken a different road did the little dog disappear.
192991: Some men who went to fetch rinsing agent at M.'s factory (for the liqueur distillery) saw will-o'-the-wisps on the way. Sometimes the lights settled on the horse's harness. Such lights were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
193023: A black cat was a ghost animal or a witch. You were not allowed to strike such an animal, or else more black cats would appear.
193036: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of aborted children who came back.
193064: In Ekeren lived a woman who could work witchcraft. Whenever that woman had touched a pig, the animal was dead two days later. One day that woman sat near a farm in the shape of a cat. Five days later all the animals on that farm were dead. Another farmer had to move because of the misfortune the witch had caused.
193083: In Nijlen lived a suspicious woman who could make children ill. Such women often went visiting. They would sit there the whole morning, observing the comings and goings of the household. Afterwards a child would get 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness).
193084: A farmer was always visited by a witch whenever he had bought a cow. The witch would stroke the animal over its back and udder. Two days later the farmer had to go to the vet and had to get rid of his cow.
193086: On his way home a man saw a rabbit sitting on the road. The man picked up the animal, put it in a sack and took it with him. When the man got home and opened the sack, he saw that there was a cobblestone inside.
193100:
A man married to a woman suspected of being a witch went picking hazelnuts around mid-August in a marshy area. When the man heard a chattering magpie fly by, he called: "Yes, wife, I'm coming!" The witch had turned herself into a magpie and come to fetch her husband.
In a thorn bush in Bergom there was said to be a glass hen. That was a bewitched hen.
193108: On a farm the milk was always sour in the morning. That was because of a woman who wanted to do those people harm.
193116: A nosy woman who had bought a book could work magic. The woman bewitched a peddler woman so she was stuck to the ground for eight days, so that the victim could not sell anything.
193121: At around nine or ten in the evening, a man saw a will-o'-the-wisp that kept moving back whenever he tried to get closer. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
193125: If after twelve noon you were visited by a woman who brought a radish, you could be sure that woman was a witch. In a house where that had happened, a cow that was due to calve died the following night.
193129: A man with a stomach ache was visited by the curate, who asked him: "Could you be bewitched?" The man answered: "That doesn't exist," but the clergyman replied: "It does exist, but you mustn't believe in it."
193148: Some people were cutting the grain with a scythe by moonlight. A cat was always walking around there, hindering the people at their work. A man lashed out at the cat and then fell on his scythe. That must have been witchcraft.
193171: Little lights were seen in the meadows by the marsh. Those were the souls of unbaptised children who had to wander about until they were released.
193185: On a farm a sudden noise was heard. When the people went to look in the stable, they saw a black witch leap away. The cows were standing on their hind legs at the back of the stable.
193200: A woman suspected of being a witch could change herself into a cat. When a cow was about to calve somewhere, people had already seen the witch walk around the house three times. From this they concluded that things would go badly with the cow. When the calf was to be born, a black cat walked among the people who had come to help. The calf was dead. The cat was seen going in under the door of the witch's house.
193237: A man had to take his cows to Sas 6, where a farmhand of another farmer was going to graze his cows. In de Brijkes there was a plain with a ditch. At a certain moment the farmhand said: "Shall I turn myself into a cat?" The farmhand stood behind a tree and a moment later a cat ran out from behind that tree. The cat sat on the farmer's shoulders. When the farmer and the farmhand went home, the latter said: "Pull out some rushes there and tie them together". The farmhand let the cows walk over the rushes.
