The farmhand forbade the farmer to tell anyone what he had seen. The farmer, however, could not keep quiet and told his mother about the sorcery while he was tending the cows in the stable. At that moment a black cat was sitting in the stable. The next day the farmhand knew that the farmer had not been able to hold his tongue. The wizard had been sitting in the stable in the shape of a cat.
193246: In a house where a man had died, people were counting the money. There was a little cat in that house. The next day the little cat was gone and a woman from the neighbourhood knew exactly how much money those people had.
193257: One day a little white rabbit sat on a small square. When people struck at the rabbit, they could not hit it and the animal immediately stood behind the person who had struck. Finally the rabbit jumped through the half-door into the stable. After that the animal was never seen again.
193264: In the Sint-Andrieskwartier in the Vlierstraat there was a haunting. One night the people there woke up in fright because they heard noise in their attic. The people were convinced that the noise was caused by the devil, who had come to punish the occupant because he had come home drunk. Two brave men went to have a look in the house, while the frightened onlookers stayed outside. The men said that a big black cat had been sitting there, which disappeared at once when they opened the door. The men thought the cat had vanished through the wall. After that everyone was convinced that the devil had been in that house in the shape of a cat.
193278: Old women living alone were often suspected of being witches. A sick man from Retie sometimes did not recognise his own children and often had hallucinations. At night, for example, he thought he could see his neighbour's cows eating his cabbages. At other times he saw a witch come in through the door. In the end the man was sent to the Norbertines in Bornem. It took the man three days to reach the fathers. His way was blocked now by a pond, then by a large forest. On his return the man reported that nothing could be done about his ailment. When the man had died at the age of forty-eight and his body was laid out, two cows and a horse died in the night. The man's wife always went in the evening with her buttermilk to drink. At that stall people's legs were covered with black cats. When people knelt and began to pray, the cats ran away. The woman had been given the following advice by a father: "The guilty one will come to the door tonight. She will knock three times and ask you to open, but you must say nothing." The woman followed the advice and found out that her sister-in-law was the guilty one. The witch even had the nerve to come to the funeral and took two of the woman's children by the hand. At that the woman went up to the witch and said: "You've tormented me enough now. Leave my children alone!" After that the woman was never troubled by the witch again. The man had probably suffered from diabetes, but in those days all misfortune was blamed on the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
193288: A boy had to go and fetch butter from an old woman. The woman gave the boy a sugar lump. In the night the boy woke up and found that his clothes were no longer where he normally put them. He got up, felt around and found that a sheet lay over his clothes. The boy tried to call out, but no sound came. After a while he could call out after all, and he saw the witch move along the walls and go out through the window.
193293: At Christmas a farmhand heard the horses talking. One horse asked: "What do you have to do tomorrow?", to which the other replied: "Tomorrow I am going to take my farmer to the churchyard." The next day the farmer was indeed dead.
193298: A man from the Kerkstraat saw a light near the Marlybrug. When the man came closer, he saw that it was all small lights. Those were unborn children. When the man was inside, there were two red hands on the door.
193300: At Sas 9 some men were playing cards. One of them cursed like a heathen. A little later a gentleman came in and asked if he could join in. When the curser wanted to pick up a dropped card, however, he saw that the strange gentleman had goat's legs. The curser screamed and made the sign of the cross. The next moment the gentleman had vanished. They had played cards with the devil.
193321: Many witches used to live in Hoogstraten. If you crossed a witch's footprints, the witch would look back. That was how witches could be recognised.
193347: There used to be a mill on the Boomsesteenweg. The ghost of a rich man came to haunt that mill on a white horse. The rich man's heir had promised to give a quarter of the grain to the poor from then on, but he had not done so. The priest came to exorcise the mill. Afterwards, however, the ghost on the white horse was still seen riding in the dunes.
193368: A mother who was a witch caused her seven children to die. The mother scrubbed the cellar and went around singing, for she did not care at all.
193387: A man struck with his whip at the lights that settled on his wagon. Such lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
193421: Near Kasterlee there once lived an old witch. The witch came from Dessel and had bewitched a little child. Because of this the child always began to cry in the evening, and it seemed as if the child's pillow was full of pins. Only when the witch had moved to Lichtaart did the child stop whimpering.
193423: At the corner of the Korte Dreef a dead man who had buried his money there came to haunt.
193446:
If your nose itched, it meant the witches were letting you know you could expect money.
Whoever heard their ears ringing knew that someone was talking about them.
Whoever spun a chair around on one leg in the house was spinning a witch inside.
Whoever walked under a ladder was challenging the witches and would soon die.
If you spilled salt on the table or put a loaf upside down on the table, you could expect a quarrel.
If you broke a mirror or sat thirteen at table, someone would die within a year.
To win at cards, you had to take off your left clog.
193448: A farmer whose barn was too small to store his harvest in was visited by a tall gentleman dressed in black. The gentleman promised the farmer a new barn, which would be finished the next morning when the cock had crowed three times. At night the farmer's wife heard noise and her husband told her what he had done. Then the farmer's wife got up, ran to the henhouse and clapped her hands, which made the cock begin to crow. The devil flew away and left a hole in the barn. That was the devil's barn or the 'blue barn'.
193467: In Burcht lived an ugly old woman who always carried a big stick. With that stick the witch bewitched children, who then fell to the ground and became ill or broke their arms or legs.
193500: A man was willing to spend the night in a haunted house on condition that he could bake cakes there. At night a ghost appeared and said: "Open it", to which the man replied: "Do it yourself, in God's name!" Then the skeleton brought up a pot of money. Since then the house has no longer been haunted.
193554: Two men who went to work in Turnhout were followed every evening by a big dog. Sometimes the dog jumped onto the back of one of the men and let itself be carried. One of those men died of it.
193586: A farmer who lived in the Manebruggestraat struck with a knife at a black cat that was getting on his nerves. When the man did so, fire came out of the cat's mouth.
193589: The witches flew to Cologne on a broomstick after saying: "Over hedge and hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar". A witch who had said by mistake: "Through hedge and through hedgerow" arrived at her destination covered in blood.
193632: On a farm in Heist a horse and a cow died. Then the farmer's wife died, and after that the farmer's son and daughter. The farmer went to the dean, who said: "Why didn't you come sooner?" and came to the farm to pray there for several days.
193635: A man coming back from the Lazernij fair saw a white cat walking in front of him in Walem. When the man got home, he heard a knocking on his window. The man jumped out of bed, opened the window and saw the same white cat in a glow of light. The man now knew for certain that the cat was a witch. For witches always appeared in a glow of light in the shape of a white cat. If one walked through Walem and spoke about witchcraft at a certain spot, one would have to deal with the witch that evening.
193640: Two boys walking behind an old woman crossed her footprints and were startled when the woman looked back. She was a witch.
193693: A little doll full of pins was found in a pillow.
193697: People who had seen something negative during the day could fall victim at night to the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) of the witches. They would try to call out, but no sound came. A man thus fell victim to a witch he knew well. The man then jumped out of his bed and chased the witch outside.
193711: When drunkards died, they were condemned to wander about as ghosts for another ten years. Only then could they rest in peace.
193741: A man had found a book and had started reading in it. Then all the devils came out of hell. One day the devils were stealing all the beans when the people came back from high mass. The man held the people back until all the beans had been picked. The people could not move a muscle.
193753: A man had heard that the witches went dancing in a certain meadow every night. Curious, he went to that meadow one evening. There the dancing witches asked him to play music. After he had done so, he was allowed to collect money. When the man had filled his pockets with money, he said something about Our Lord. The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the man was sitting on a bush with his pockets full of oak leaves.
193800: The grandfather of Beer V. lived in the Hooghuis in Berlaar. During the French period a cart with soldiers drove past the Hooghuis. The grandfather had seen a chest fall off the cart and he covered it with dung. Soldiers who lost something, however, were severely punished and sometimes even executed. From then on rattling and banging were always heard in the Hooghuis. The grandfather would then say: "Keep quiet about what you know, keep what you have, and I will suffer what I can". After a while no more strange noises were heard in the house.
193806: A man asked a cat that always came in through the water drain hole: "Pussycat, where do you come from?", to which the cat replied: "From the drain hole".
193821: Two proud unmarried witches lived together on a farmstead. A boy was going out with one of them. People had warned the boy about the witch several times, so one day he decided to put it to the test. When he was sitting with his girlfriend one evening, he pretended to have fallen asleep. So he heard the witches say at half past eleven: "Now he's still sitting here and we can't go flying. But he'll surely sleep until we're back". At twelve o'clock the witches went to a cupboard and began powdering their faces to make themselves invisible. Then they flew away on their brooms. The boy had heard everything. He got up, powdered himself too, took a broom and said: "Through hedgerow and hedge, the wine in the cellar". The boy flew through all the hedgerows and hedges and was badly injured. He reached the two witches, who were surprised at his presence and at his being injured. The boy told them what had happened, and the witches answered: "Of course you should have said 'over' instead of 'through'". The boy now knew how to do it and became a witch himself.
193860: On a farm where several animals had died, the event was blamed on the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
193863: A farmer from Kievit had two farmhands. One Sunday one of the farmhands had lost all his money at cards. Because the month was far from over, the farmhand said: "If only I had money. I don't dare borrow, because I can't pay back a loan. If I had money, I would sell my soul to the devil." That same night the farmhand saw a black gentleman appear by his bed. "Which of you two was it who wanted to sell his soul to the devil?" the gentleman asked. The farmhand answered: "I only said that as a joke" and made the sign of the cross, after which the gentleman vanished without a trace. The farmhand, who before had done nothing but drink and curse, became deeply religious afterwards.
193881: In the evening a light always appeared by a tall tree near the church. An unbaptised child lay buried in that spot. After the child had been dug up and baptised, no light was ever seen there again.
193884: A man had hanged himself. Some time later some people claimed they had seen the dead man's spirit at the market. When they wanted to ask the spirit something, it vanished for good.
193888: A woman said to the miller of Emblem: "Well, shouldn't you be grinding?" When the miller answered: "That won't work, there's no wind," the woman said: "Just go home. The mill will turn." Although it was still windless a little later, the mill did indeed turn.
193909: Four young men were walking past a field where a farmer was sowing grain. One of the men said: "Shall I make that farmer stand still?" The next moment the farmer stood stock-still in the field. A while later the man released the farmer, so that he could carry on working.
193923: In Sint-Amands lived an old woman who had once been in the convent. She had run away from there without her outer clothing and had then become a witch, for she had studied a great deal. People going to church had to pass that witch's house. It happened several times that those people lost their outer clothing or that their clothes were torn to shreds from bottom to top. Then those people had to go on to church like that.
193940: A man who worked for the mayor met a woman with a sheet over her head every day on his way home at about the same time. That witch went nowhere without her son. When the witch's daughter had married, the witch made life very hard for her son-in-law. After the witch died, someone else took over her magic power. That 'new' witch had a son of fourteen or fifteen, who also died of the witchcraft.
193953: A witch had stuck a scythe into a corn stack. After that one cat after another jumped into the stack. The corn stack could hardly be touched, for it felt as if you got an electric shock.
194031: On the road from Londerzeel to Breendonk one passed a witch. That is why most people went by way of Londerzeel-Heide. A farmer who laughed at people's fear and walked past the witch's cottage anyway had the evil hand in his stables for weeks afterwards. All the animals fell ill and died.
194040: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if they were lifted up in their bed and thrown into an abyss. One woman never went to sleep before she had placed her clogs upside down in front of her bed to protect herself against the mare.
194061: The yard of a farm in Poppel was haunted because a German soldier had been buried there after the war. People were so frightened that they did not dare go near the farm. They even saw ghosts in the churchyard. From one day to the next the haunting at the farm stopped.
194067: If one could wound a witch in animal form, she soon took on her human form again.
194069: The farmer of the Ijzeren Veld had moved the boundary post of his field, which made the poor farmer who owned the neighbouring plot even poorer. After his death the boundary violator had to come back to haunt to put the post back in its original place. A farmhand who had often seen the ghost resolved several times to help it, but in the end he always ran away in fear. After some men had put the boundary post back, the ghost no longer appeared.
194070: At the Kruisstraat a dead person came back in the shape of a headless horse.
194079: An old man out walking with his walking stick saw a cat run in front of his feet and struck at it with his stick. After that as many as twenty-five cats were running around the man. The animals could not be chased away.
194088: A man coming back from Mariekerke lost his way in a small wood. Later it was said that the man had been ridden by the mare. In reality the man was probably a little drunk. A woman who had never been anywhere before had to go to Bornem. Although her destination was only three hundred metres from her house, the woman lost her way.
194103: Through witchcraft, the cows on a farm jumped into the trough.
194121: In Hoogstraten the duke of Salm-Salm is said to have once locked a servant in an ice cellar. He supposedly forgot the servant, and the boy died there. Later a voice was heard there calling: "Aernout is in there and is coming out". The next moment the servant appeared and sat down in the saddle of a horse.
194124: The father of Zie M. saw white gentlemen in the woods, holding a candle in their hands and reading from a book.
194132: A church is said to have sunk in the Diepdal at Boshoven. At night bells could be heard ringing there. Roman objects are also said to have been dug up there.
194207: In the Goudbloemstraat in Herentals lived a man who had seen the devil at night.
194218: A woman was ridden by the mare. After the friars of Leuven had read prayers over her, she was cured. Mares were people who had sold their soul to the devil and thus had great power. Everything they touched was bad. If they came to a farm, a cow would afterwards lie dead. If they came into a house, the occupants met with misfortune. If the mare laid something on your doorstep, you were not to bring it inside, or else your whole house would be cursed. If a mare offered you something, you had either to refuse it or accept it while holding your hand higher.
194230: On a farm in Retie the horses sank to their knees before they were outside in the morning. The animals had been struck by the evil hand.
194241: On a farm a glowing wagon always flew through the stable. A glowing calf also often lay under the attic stairs.
194243: A girl who went out to cut grass in the evening saw a black cat behind her. The girl told her aunt what had happened, and the aunt decided to accompany the girl the next time. After that the cat did not show itself again. It was the devil, after all, and he was no match for two people.
194248: In Ranst lived a witch who could change herself into a cat. Such a cat was very hard to hit if you kicked at it. A boy returning with his girlfriend from the fair in Vremde nevertheless managed to hit the cat. The next day the witch had a black eye.
194254: During thunderstorms a witch always went to the cows in the meadow opposite her house. She would stroke the animals on the head and say: "Good, my little beasts." A man lying in bed one night after coming back from the fair was annoyed by a black cat that had jumped onto his bed two or three times. The man grabbed the cat and threw it down from the attic. As a result the animal had a paralysed paw. The next morning a suspect woman from the village wore her arm in a sling.
194275: Some people kicked at a cat one evening. The next day a supposed witch from the village was covered in bruises.
194310: A man who accused a woman of being a witch fell flat on his back the next moment.
194332: One had to be afraid of a black cat because it could be a witch.
194338: A man working in the cornfield was bothered by a cat that would not leave him alone. The man beat the cat until it bled. The next day the man found that his wife had a wound.
194346: A man who was cleaning beans saw a woman pass by, who said: "What lovely beans." The man did not respond. He came home with his beans and went to churn butter. While he was doing so, he saw bean plant leaves all over the lid of the butter churn.
194349: Some people were always visited by a neighbour woman who had a bad reputation. One day, when the woman came back from church, the neighbour let herself fall flat on the ground at her feet. Afterwards the woman fell ill.
194376: An old miller always saw a cat come into his mill. The man told his farmhand, who once struck at the cat with an axe, so that the animal lost a paw. The next day the miller said to his farmhand: "Boy, do you know what you've done? You've chopped off my wife's arm!"
194389: A boy who was taking his girlfriend home one evening said in the Kapellekenslaan: "I just have to go and pee. If you see anything strange in the meantime, wave this handkerchief." A little later the girl saw a large beast approaching. As soon as the girl began to wave the handkerchief, the beast ran off. When the boy came back, the girl saw that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
194400: The flickering will-o'-the-wisps seen above the churchyards were the souls of returning dead.
194445: The filter cloth had to be brought in before sunset, otherwise the witches had power over the house the people lived in. In a family that had forgotten to bring in the cloth, noise was heard at night. The cats were in the house, the animals in the stable had been untied and the doors flew open and shut. The priest had to come and read prayers over the place to drive away the witchcraft.
194454:
A market gardener had lost a little child. When another child in the same family became very ill, his neighbour advised the gardener to go to the friars of Dendermonde to have the evil hand driven out. The sick child would sometimes lie screaming, and a few moments later become very calm. 
The gardener went to the friars of Dendermonde twice, and they declared they could not help because it was all superstition. On his third visit the gardener said: "Now I will stay here until you have helped me." The friars then gave the man a relic and advised him to make a novena and say a particular prayer every day. After that the child recovered.
194455:
During the Peasants' War in 1798 many priests left the monastery. Father V. secretly said mass in a cellar on Sunday evenings. After his death the priest had to haunt. A boy who had arranged to meet his girlfriend at midnight by moonlight saw a witheer (white-clad priest) walking along, reading a book.
A man who went to fetch wood in Diest at night with a donkey and cart met the haunting priest in the Veldstraat. Terrified, the man ran home.
A farmer who wanted to bury the waste of a slaughtered pig in his garden found the treasure of Father V. in the ground. The treasure probably belonged to the church. After all, at a certain point the priest owned a house and all sorts of other things.
194487: Some farmers let their animals graze on the dyke. Every Friday a witch came along that dyke on her way to the market in Temse. Every Friday the farmers got no milk from their cows that had been on the dyke.
194501: On a farm a witch made sure that no butter could be made.
194521: The sorcerer Fons V.S. could conjure up mice wearing little bows.
194541: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the spirits of returning dead, which disappeared if one read the Gospel of St John.
194548: If you saw a witch walking, you had to cross her footprints, after which she would look back.
194587: A man always saw a hand beckoning to him in the churchyard. A nobleman was buried in the churchyard, wearing a gold ring with a precious diamond on his finger. After the funeral some robbers had dug up the coffin and cut off the dead man's hand. From then on a beckoning hand was always seen in the churchyard. Because the robbers felt remorse, one night they put the severed hand back in the coffin. After that nothing strange was seen in the churchyard any more.
194628:
If you had been touched by a witch, you had to strike her higher up. 
A man went to visit the dilapidated cottage of a supposed witch. While he stood in the cottage, a dog suddenly ran in. The animal had not seen the man and seemed like a ghost dog. When the man went to bed that evening, he saw something flutter out of his bedroom. He found bird droppings on the wardrobe. He found this very strange. It seemed as if the witch had caused these events. 
Strange things also happened when that witch died. Her grave was full of mice. Her death notice was printed upside down in the parish magazine and the sexton could not manage to toll the death bells.
194646: A shopkeeper was visited every two weeks by a farmer's wife who came to buy paraffin. The shopkeeper's child was always ill. So the shopkeeper decided to go to the friars of de Kluis, from whom he received a relic to put under the threshold. After that, the farmer's wife no longer came into the shop. The child recovered.
194648: A boy who took his cow out to graze saw the animal eating from branches someone had put somewhere. At that moment a woman came by, struck at the animal and said: "Tomorrow she won't eat from them any more." That was indeed the case, for the next day the cow was ill. The vet examined the animal but could find nothing.
194660: On a farm, rumbling was heard every night in a corner of the kitchen, although nothing could be seen. One day a big fat toad came out of the drain hole. The farmer struck the creature. The next day he found that one of the neighbour women had lost a leg.
194670: A boy said to his girlfriend: "If you should meet a werewolf, you must throw a handkerchief at it." When the girl once threw a handkerchief at a werewolf, she saw the handkerchief being torn to shreds. A short time later she met her boyfriend and saw that he had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
194710: Some men who had gone fishing in the Kil saw something rolling in the sand. In less than three minutes the apparition had grown as big as a dog. Two minutes later the dog turned into a big calf. A little further on stood an inn whose landlady was suspected of being a witch. The men went to the inn and asked the man where his wife was. The man said: "She'll be out again, because she isn't here." The men replied: "Yes, she's lying over there rolling in the sand." Five minutes later the woman came in with a handkerchief over her shoulder.
194748: On a farm the cows died and the children fell ill. The misfortune was caused by a woman from the neighbourhood.
194761: Pikkerdië used to be a remote area with woods and a few marshes. Along the sandy road from Schilde to Wezel stood a small house where weary travellers could get a glass of beer for five cents. One evening a man stood there talking with the landlady when suddenly a little gentleman dressed in a black suit and with a goatee came in. Later the landlady said she thought she had seen that the gentleman had goat's legs, but she wasn't sure. The gentleman sat down, ordered a glass of beer and began talking with the man. The two got into a quarrel and went outside. There the gentleman blew twice on a whistle, after which a big black billy goat came flying through the air. The goat flew between the man's legs and lifted him up into the air. Holding the goat's horns, the man flew through the woods and thorns. When the man was scratched all over and his clothes were torn, the gentleman blew his whistle again, after which the goat flew down and threw its passenger to the ground at its master's feet. A cloud of dust stinking of pitch and sulphur appeared as the gentleman and the goat vanished. Only the next day did the injured man get home. When he told people what had happened to him, they said he had probably met a bokkenrijder (goat rider). The bokkenrijders consorted with the devil. When they wanted to fight in the evening, they whistled for the devil, who came to their aid in the form of a goat. That is why it is always dangerous to fight an unknown man in the evening.
194773: The stone bridge was always haunted at night. Between midnight and one o'clock a figure walked back and forth on the bridge.
194778: A carter who was very afraid of witches was visited by a woman who always walked around with a cow in her hand while keeping her other hand in her pocket. The woman came to ask the carter whether he could take some potatoes along. The carter said: "Yes, but don't bring the potatoes by the back door, bring them by the front door." The witch did bring the potatoes by the front door. The next night the carter found that one of his horses had fallen ill. The animal was drenched in sweat.
194781: The mother of Vic R., who lived on 't Genendijksveld, was a wicked woman. At Vic's brother's house the devil came in in the shape of a dog that pushed the door open with its paws.
194799: If one met a black cat in the evening or at night, there was a good chance it was a witch. The best way to get rid of that cat was to make the sign of the cross.
194826: At 't Schoepeke a kitten always came in through the water drain hole. When people asked the animal: "What are you doing here?", the kitten began to speak. The cat was the soul of the parents who had lived in that house. Because the parents had failed to keep a vow, they had to come back to haunt. In the end the parish priest C. managed to drive the cat away.
194829: A witch often made her neighbours' alarm clocks go off from midnight until one or four o'clock. Then she had to stop keeping the people awake, because at sunrise her magic power waned.
194832: If a woman was suspected of being a witch, you had to cross her footprints. If the woman could then go no further, that was proof she was a witch.
194840: One evening a woman saw a child approaching and said: "In the name of God, whose child are you?" The next moment the child vanished into the ground. A son of that woman had also seen the child. When he grabbed at it, the child likewise vanished into the ground.
194870: A man crossed the new bridge at the Vloeikes on his way to Wezel. On the way there the man saw a cat sitting on the railing of the bridge. Because the cat was still sitting there when the man went back, he pushed the animal into the water. But it was a woman he had pushed into the canal.
194901: A man who was ridden by the mare cried out at night: "There's a fellow in the bed holding me by the hand who wants to do something to me." Victims of the mare could not move.
194915: A little lard pot always came back to Jan B.'s house.
194948: Two men in a café were watching some card players. They noticed there was cheating, but when they said something about it, the café owner said to them: "Don't interfere or you'll have me to deal with." When a little later the men made another remark, the café owner threw them out, saying: "Clear off! And you're not home yet!" On the way the men ended up in barbed wire and in a meadow they could not get out of, although they had walked that road many times. After that incident they never went to that café again.
194973: In Lichtaart lived a witch who was especially after small children. Whenever a child was born somewhere, the witch always lingered near that house for the first days. The occupants, however, made sure the witch could not touch the child.
194977: Some soldiers were transporting parts of a cannon on a wagon. On the way the soldiers had not noticed that their money chest had slid off the wagon. The farmer of the farm of Sintes saw the money chest and covered it with dung. Because they had lost the money, many soldiers were killed. From then on the farm of Sintes was haunted. The hellewagen (hell's wagon) drove around there every night, and in the morning two cows often had their heads stuck in the same halter. To be freed from the haunting, the farmer had to give away as many gold pieces as there were grains in a meuke (?) of wheat. Since of course they could not count them, the farmer's wife said: "Better one soul damned than seven souls poor". A priest came and banished the ghosts to the sea. Every hundred years, however, the haunting started again.
194980: People who were ridden by the mare in reality had a standstill of the blood. Sometimes victims of the mare could not find their way home. A boy sleeping alone for the first time in an unfamiliar room had a dream, but was strangely aware that he was dreaming. The boy saw a fellow come in who was as fat as seven men put together. The fat apparition, which had a moustache like the horns of a bull, lay down on the boy and crushed him. The boy called his father, but no sound came from his throat. A little later the fat apparition left the boy alone. Suddenly the boy made so much noise that everyone in the house was awake.
195027: Two brothers went to the market in Aarschot with a chicken under their arm. The brothers had left at midnight and took a back road through the woods. When they were nearly at an inn, they saw a black woman who said: "Ha, little men, are you going to the market?" The brothers said yes, and the woman asked: "And do you have many chickens at home?" The brothers again said "yes" and the woman replied: "So does my daughter, and she just can't get those chickens to grow. I wring all their necks." That woman was a real witch.
195073: A farm by the road to Geel in Achter-Olen was badly haunted. The soldiers who came to spend the night there ran away in fear. The witchcraft there was banished for ninety-nine years.
195094: Will-o'-the-wisps were children who had not been baptised.
195096: On a farm one evening a black cat sat in the stable. Because the pigs there were all dying, the parish priest came to overlezen (pray over to lift a spell) the stable. He sweated terribly while doing so. After the priest's intervention the black cat never came into the house again.
195109:
On a farm, during a violent thunderstorm, the window shutters flew open, even though a fifty-kilo weight stood on the windowsill.
On a farm a farmer had stolen the gold of soldiers. After that those soldiers came to haunt. At a certain time a hellewagen (hell's wagon) always appeared at the farm. Part of the treasure was said to still be buried under the farm. The person who later lived on the farm found the pit. Behind the farm there was also a pit whose purpose no one knew. The farm belonged to a count.
195120: It was said that if you put a scapular under the doormat, no witches could come in. At one point the witch forbade her son-in-law to sleep with her daughter any more, because no more children would be born to them anyway. The closer one lived to the witch, the less afraid of her one was.
195181: A man walking home from work one evening saw a cart stop beside him, in which sat a lady dressed in white, who said: "If you like, you can ride along a little way". When the man wanted to get in, suddenly there was no lady or cart to be seen.
195196: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) always appeared in roughly the same place. The lights were about the size of a pear and moved back and forth all the time. People said that stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children. Sometimes a stallicht would not be seen for eight days and then suddenly turn up again.
195216: In the house of the Sinjoor near the church of Kalfort a woman had died who had promised during her life to go to Scherpenheuvel on foot. Later people came to live in that house who went to mass every morning. When the people opened the door one morning, a white ghost stood before them and said: "When I was still alive, I promised to go to Scherpenheuvel. I kept putting it off until it was too late. Will you make that pilgrimage for me? Otherwise I will never be happy". After the people had promised to make the pilgrimage, the ghost disappeared.
195224: Every evening a man saw a big black cat sitting in the hallway. He threw something at the animal but could not hit it. The man believed the cat was a witch. One day he struck at it with a hook and hit it. When the man went visiting somewhere a while later, he saw the woman of the house sitting there with a black eye.
195238:
A man who was often ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit) felt the mare appear in his clogs and then creep up to his chest. Because of this the man could no longer move. One evening, when he was returning from visiting his friends, he saw a little light floating before his feet. A moment later he received a box on the ear that knocked him to the ground. Further on he met an old woman who jumped over the ditch. It was she who caused the man so much trouble. 
The man once went to confession with a friar in Tongerlo. The friar himself brought up the woman and asked: "Shall I show her to you in a mirror?" The man answered: "No, for I know her," and he said her name, to which the friar answered "yes." Then the friar said: "She could have broken your neck. You must not stand still in front of her, for then you give her power. You can only hit her with a birchwood stick. But if you miss, you will die yourself. Before you go to sleep, you must move your clogs three times, or else set them crosswise." The friar also read prayers over the man, and afterwards he was no longer troubled by the witch. He was no longer ridden by the mare. That witch caused her own grandchildren to waste away.
195285: At the Kalmthoutse hoek and at the Kruisstraat little chapels were built because those places were haunted. A buttermilk calf always appeared there at midnight. People went up to the animal, but it did not run away. After little chapels had been built there, the calf no longer appeared. Later it was discovered that the calf was a witch.
195306: A bewitched woman went to Tongerlo to have prayers read over her. The priest made the sign of the cross the whole time and gave the woman water and salt, which cured her.
195312: A farmer shot with his gun at a black cat that came onto his farm. He did not trust such animals at all.
195317: One evening a family in Kasterlee sat around the stove. Suddenly the people saw a big black dog standing there. No one had seen where the dog had come from, and the doors were all shut. A moment later there was a knock. As it happened, it was the parish priest coming to visit. The dog leapt into the air and vanished while a tremendous clap of thunder rang out. The priest knew that the dog had been the devil.
195324: A mayor who also worked as a farmer lived near a witch. The man's cow did not give a drop of milk, and every morning a cat lay underneath it. People tried to hit the cat, but nobody managed to strike it.
195342: In Mol a strange light was always seen. A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come back to haunt after his death with a post on his shoulder. So the ghost had to walk back and forth along the field.
195358: A dying man from Poederlee said: "That ugly black dog is always standing on my bed here." That black dog was the devil.
195402: In Sint-Katelijne-Waver there stood a castle called 'Lombardstein'. In the dark a witte madam (white lady) came out of one of the castle towers and floated from the tower to the back of the grounds.
195430: A man had sown grass next to the old hospice in Lier. In the afternoon he went with his child to look at the grass. Afterwards he went into an inn to drink a glass of beer and chat a bit. When the child fell asleep, the innkeeper's wife said: "Come, I'll put him in the bed for a while". Some time later the man went home with his child. But he could not get home. Only the next morning at sunrise did he reach his house. The child was so heavy, he said.
195433: There were always stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) hanging in the Torputten. Those were the souls of unbaptised children.
195460: A man crossed the footprints of a woman suspected of being a witch. If the woman was a witch, she would look back. But she did not.
195462: A few girls walking behind a woman in the snow made a cross with their right foot. After that the woman walking ahead of them could go no further. Only when a priest had said prayers over her could she move on again.
195475: A man who was bewitched did not know that he was not wearing a shirt. Another time that man could not move forward on the road and began to sweat heavily.
195503: A miller whose hands had all died was forced to do the grinding himself at night. As he sat there, he heard a cat scratching at the door with its paw to get in. The miller chopped off one of the cat's paws. When he went home in the morning and called his wife, she would not get up. She had lost a hand.
195535: One summer, some young men set off with the horse cart around half past eleven at night. When the group had almost reached Kerkhoven, one of the men became terrified. He had seen a dog as big as a calf that seemed to have two candles in its head. The others, however, could not see the dog.
195540: A boy who was ridden by the mare lay stiff in his bed at night. The boy was scared to death and had a pale complexion. He always claimed that someone was standing in front of his bed.
195543: People who were ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit) while lying in bed suddenly got a strange feeling in their legs. The feeling moved up to the heart. The people felt as if they would suffocate and could not make a sound.
195546: Will-o'-the-wisps were lost souls or souls of unbaptised children that came flying when something had happened somewhere. Will-o'-the-wisps were also often seen in the woods of Tongerlo.
195566: A man returning from the market in Diest saw a pack of cats sitting on the road one evening. The man said: "Kitties, let's go and warm ourselves by the stove!" When the man got home and lit the stove, the cats were there. The man was terribly frightened when the cats began to dance and sing: "If Bootje had not spoken so nicely, we would have broken his neck!"
195582: A man who lived in Donk suddenly fell backwards while sitting at the table. It seemed as if a storm had blown up behind him. The man flew behind the door and looked into the face of the devil. His mother went out by the front door, praying. That is how the devil went away.
195596: Some people wanted to go to Charleroi with their child. But every time they wanted to leave, they saw a large black dog that blocked their way.
195612: A miller's wife's daughter was tormented at night by the mare (a nightmare spirit). It then seemed as if her blood stood still. She saw all sorts of things at the foot of her bed. The girl was freed from the mare by the parish priest.
195668: On a farm with fifteen hundred chickens, all but seven died within a week. That was the work of a witch who could not bear that the newly married farmer and his wife were earning well.
195702: One day on a farm a butter churn was lent to a woman. When the people wanted to churn butter themselves that evening, it did not work and there was only froth in the churn.
195716: During the Schuppenzotten festival in Itegem on the tenth of June, a farmer's wife was visited by a woman who came for eggs to hatch. The farmer's wife was proud of her farm and gave the visitor a tour of the cowshed. She explained which cow was the best and how much milk each animal gave. Some time later the best cow began to bleed. The bleeding could not be stopped and the animal died. The vet claimed the animal had had a disorder of the spleen. The three other cows died too, in the order in which the farmer's wife had listed and described them. A deep pit had to be dug to bury the cows. The mayor came to see whether the pit was deep enough. The farmer went to the friars of Dendermonde, who said: "What is dead is dead, but what lives will go on living. The misfortune was caused by a woman from Sint-Rumoldus who visited you." The people had to do penance before sunrise and after sunset and go to confession and communion with the whole family.
195720: Two men came to a farm and asked if they could put their goat in the stable for a while. The goat had barely been put in when it grew bigger and bigger until it was as big as a cow. When people went to look again half an hour later, the animal had vanished.
195732: The son of a witch from Nijlen was in a relationship with a girl. When the lovers were coming back from Lier, where they had gone to buy wedding rings, three women suddenly jumped in front of the young man's feet. The women danced and made music. A little further on they flew into the air. When the girl stood under an elder tree, a whole lot of cats jumped onto her back.
195741: A soldier stationed in Brussels came home on leave. The man's neighbours had a sick little child. The soldier went to visit those people. When they were sitting up with the child in the evening, there was a knock at the door. They opened it with the words: "Come in, you are among good people here". Then a big grey dog came in. The animal silently walked twice around the cradle and then went outside again. The people were speechless and believed the dog had been a witch. If they had been able to wound the animal, they would have known who the witch was. When the soldier went home, he ended up in a pool of water on the way. The pool was so deep that the soldier did not dare to move for fear of drowning. At a certain moment the water had suddenly disappeared. The soldier's parents believed the dog had been an old woman who lived nearby in order to be able to practise witchcraft.
195782: A man who was being followed by a cat threw a knife at the animal, which lost an eye as a result. The next morning the man met a woman who had only one eye left.
195791: In Lille a dead rich farmer came to haunt every night.
195792: On a farm in Achterbos no butter could be churned. They went to the priest of Millegem, who came to look and said: "I have found it, the witch is in the butter churn. I will come back tomorrow. Make sure you have a kettle of boiling water ready." The next day the priest sprinkled the whole room with holy water. He poured the water into the butter churn, which then began to turn. "I will burn the witch," he said. After that those people could make good butter again.
195803: Two friends were sometimes thrown into the bushes for no reason in the evening when they had been out together. The mother of one of the boys was a witch.
195810: A corporal from Herentals could open the door of the cowshed by throwing his cap against it.
195815: A man who went eel fishing at night got a fright when someone stood behind him and asked: "Well, friend, are they biting?" The man looked back and saw a figure in a friar's habit floating half a metre above the ground. The man pretended not to have heard, but was terrified and was already reaching for a knife to defend himself if necessary. A little later the ghost had vanished. Friars also came haunting on the Troon.
195819: A woman who went to fetch water hurried back inside when she saw two little lights above the ditch. When the woman looked through the window a little later, the lights had gone. Such lights were the souls of children who needed to be baptised.
195828: On a farm a knocking on the door was always heard, though nothing could be seen. One day the farmer, with his gun at the ready, shouted: "If you come knocking one more time, I'll shoot through the door," but he heard nothing more.
195850: In Nijlen there was a farm that was haunted. The cow there stood with her front legs against the stakes.
195852: In a house where a child had been born, every stranger was kept away from the cradle for the first days. An old woman who lived on the heath, however, had managed to stroke the child. The next day the child was dead.
195871: A girl had been given apples by a witch who lived nearby. The girl's mother forbade her daughter to eat the apples. When the apples were seen lying there a long time later, strangely enough they were still not rotten.
195882: In the café 't Zwart Hemd the devil walked up the stairs. Everywhere he put his hands there were black stains.
195904: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his land came back to haunt after his death with the post on his shoulder. The ghost called out all the time: "Where do I leave my post? Where do I leave my post?" One day a drunkard answered: "Your post? Take it back to the place where you got it!" With that the ghost was released.
195912: On a wizard's land a woman found a nest of hen's eggs. The woman picked up the eggs and wanted to cross the ditch with them. Although it was a very narrow ditch that would be no problem for a three-year-old child, the woman could not get across. The woman put the eggs back and then found she could cross the ditch. Then she went to fetch the eggs again, but this time she again could not go on. In the end the woman had to leave the wizard's eggs behind.
195921: Three children died after being bewitched by a witch from Charleroi. Many people who were bewitched went to the friars of Tongerlo.
195946: On a farm in Wijnegem there was a cow that always pushed against the stable with her horns. The vet was called, who attributed the problem to the evil hand and said he could do nothing about it. When a healthy child was born on the farm, a woman kept coming to visit. Eight days later that child was dead. After the cow had died, the visitor advised another farmer to sell a cow to the afflicted farmer. So it happened. The new cow had barely been put in the stable before she too fell ill. The farmer went to the priest. At first the clergyman did not want to go with him, but in the end he came and read prayers over the stable. The newborn child cried all the time. For the child they went to the Trappists, where they received a relic to put under the door. After that the witch could no longer get in.
195957: In a wood there were witches in the shape of cats.
195992: A man returning one evening from the annual fair in Willebroek was pestered by a black dog that would not leave him alone. The man struck at the dog, but could not hit the animal. The dog accompanied the man all the way to his house. After that he did not see the animal again.
196007: A man who went to fetch a friend to go visiting somewhere saw a cat sitting in front of the friend's door. The man kicked at the cat, but the animal came back. The friend no longer dared to come outside.
196050: After someone had chopped off a cat's paw, it was found the next day that a neighbour woman had lost her hand.
196057: A man from Rinkven drove a cart full of brushwood bundles to town. When the man drove past the house of a certain woman, the horses began to rear. However much the man cursed or lashed them with his whip, the horses would not go on until the sun rose.
196068: A woman who saw a polecat stamped her foot on the ground, but the beast did not move. When the woman then threw her shoe at the polecat, as many as ten animals came and sat there. A little later other people joined the woman, which gave her the courage to take her shoe back.
196069: A bewitched girl from Waver always saw someone sitting on her feet in the evening when she lay in bed. She kept crying out: "Someone is sitting on my feet. She's sitting with her back to me!" The girl's mother cried so much that she eventually went blind.
196088: Some people used to play cards on Sunday afternoons during benediction. Because a black dog always came and lay under the table, they once went to the priest, who said: "If you stop playing cards on Sunday, that dog will not come any more." And so it was. That dog must have been the devil.
196098: People believed that the little lights floating about in the evening were the souls of unbaptised children.
196119: Some people who kept seeing a cat jump in front of their feet strangely enough could not hit the animal.
196135: A man walking through 't Blok (1) got lost. When he heard the church bells strike twelve, he still could not find his bearings. At one o'clock he suddenly knew where he was. For at that time the witches were gone.
196151: A young family had moved from the countryside to Deurne. They were still often visited by their stepmother, who still lived in the countryside and brought butter, eggs and milk. The young woman had a child that suffered from 'the old man' and died a few days after birth. The same happened with the second and third child. Then the people decided not to let the stepmother in any more. The fourth child, born after that, survived and grew up healthy.
196163: A man who had gone to deliver a calf in Dendermonde saw an old woman sitting by the side of the ditch on his way back. The woman was rummaging in her hair with both hands, so the man called out: "Are you catching them, old woman?" The woman answered: "Yes, yes, just hurry home. Catch your own, because your house is full of them." When the man got home, he found that his house was full of big, fat lice.
196180: The Rithaag was haunted. A farmer whose meadow lay close to the hedge struck a pot while ploughing. The farmer dug up the pot and found that it contained a lot of money. After the pot was found, the Rithaag was no longer haunted.
196198: Two men who were chopping wood saw a mewing cat walk by. One of the men struck at the cat with his hatchet, and the animal lost an eye. Afterwards the man could no longer find his hatchet. When the two men went to buy a cow some time later, they found that the dealer's wife had only one eye. The woman said to them: "At Poederlee on that oak I lost my one eye!" The men saw their hatchet hanging there on a rack.
196215: If someone was suspected of being a witch, you had to follow her and make the sign of the cross on the ground with your foot. The witch would then look back.
196222: A mother hung a relic around the neck of each of her children. When one child's relic was lost during washing, that child began to cry incessantly. The child only stopped crying when its mother hung a rosary around its neck to ward off the evil hand.
196238: At Gustje M.'s all the cows died because of the evil hand. Witches could even neutralise the power of holy water.
196260: A pregnant woman went to her sister who lived on the Grasheide. On her way back the woman had to go through a lane, where she saw three dogs sitting behind a bush. The dogs walked along with her for a while but did her no harm. When she came back some time later, she saw the dogs again. The third time the woman had her husband come along. She saw the dogs, but strangely enough he could not see the animals. The woman then went to the priest, who read prayers over her. After that the woman no longer saw the dogs there.
196376: On a farm all the cows died because of the evil hand. The people went to the friars of Tongerlo, where the evil was bound for ninety-nine years.
196414: In the old days, when people saw a light, they called it a dwaaslicht (will-o'-the-wisp). Those lights were the souls of unbaptised children who had 'gone astray'. People who had seen such a light heard a knock on their door a little later. If they dared to go outside at that moment, the child would come in.
196429: A midwife was accompanied at night by her boyfriend when she had to go to a woman in childbed. The devils have power from eleven to one o'clock. On the way the boyfriend said to the girl: "I just have to go to the toilet. If you should meet anything in that time, defend yourself with your scissors." When a dog came running up a little further on, the midwife threw her scissors at the beast. Then the dog ran off and she could go on. She did not see her boyfriend again that evening. When the midwife was picked up by her boyfriend the next day, she saw that the pieces of the scissors (?!) were still stuck between his teeth. The boy had to go haunting when his time had come.
196446: In the army a man was arrested because he had been playing cards with three dead men. When the man was thrown into prison, he was already outside before the superior had been able to shut the door. The wizard was then chased away.
196459: A nineteen-year-old boy who went to the town hall to draw lots for conscription felt a witch grab him by the throat and collapsed. Two days later the boy was dead.
196482: A man could not get the bucket into his well. A witch from the neighbourhood had caused this.
196500: A man who cared nothing for God or His commandments was walking home one evening, cursing. Suddenly the man heard a loud clap of thunder and saw a great flame. The man stood as if nailed to the ground, for he had seen the devil.
196510: A miller could not keep a single farmhand, because they all fell ill and then quit. One day a brave farmhand came to work for the miller and asked for a sabre. When this farmhand was grinding at night, he heard a mewing cat walking on the roof of the mill. When the cat came to sit on a sack of grain, the farmhand chopped off its right paw. The next morning the miller found that his wife had lost her right arm, and the farmhand was dismissed.
196526: A shopkeeper whose first four children had died at the age of nine months was visited in her grocery shop by a woman suspected of being a witch. The children the shopkeeper had after the supposed witch moved away survived.
196557: A man was about to throw a stone at a cat when the animal suddenly said: "Throw it now if you dare!" The man got away as fast as he could.
196569: A small chapel used to stand at the Fonteinputje. One day two Jewish men were working in the woods there. They took shelter from a thunderstorm in the chapel. Because it rained inside the chapel, the men began to curse. The chapel then sank along with the men. If you walked around that spot three times without breathing and then put your ear to the ground, you could still hear ringing in the chapel.
196578: A nine-year-old girl was not growing well. A few houses away lived a woman suspected of being a real witch. One day the witch said to the girl: "I'm going to Beerzel and I'll bring you back some nuts." The girl ate the nuts. Exactly one year later the child died.
196597: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come back to haunt in the evenings after his death with the words: "Post here, post there, where shall I leave you?" One night someone answered: "Put it where you got it". After that the ghost was not heard again.
196604: A sick woman kept jumping out of her bed only to jump back in a moment later. They took the woman to a quack in Berlaar, who cured her and said: "On the way you will meet people, but you must not talk to them." On the way home they did indeed meet some people from the village. The woman gradually recovered.
196605: A woman who had bought a cow at the market in Nijlen was going home with the animal. When the woman was not far from her house, a witch came up to her and wanted to look at the cow. A short while later the cow died.
196632: On a farm the cows began to low in the evening and it sounded as if chains were being dragged across the ground. One cow stood with her head twisted twice around a post. Two other cows had their heads stuck in a single opening between two beams. A young calf lay dead. Within five days three other healthy calves died. The people had to go to Bornem several times before they were freed from the evil hand.
196666: One evening a priest knocked at a farmhouse and asked if he could stay the night. They had to wake him at five in the morning, because he had to go and release three men who had been fixed to the spot in a deserted place for a day and a night after attacking the priest.
196722: If you placed your feet the wrong way round in a witch's footprints, the witch would look back.
196746: A woman went about with her twins in a pram. Whenever a certain woman had been near the children, the twins invariably began to cry at three o'clock at night. Then there was no end to the crying. Every week a priest dressed in white came from a monastery to Mariekerke to say mass in the village. One day the mother had that priest come to her house to overlezen (pray over) the twins. After that the mother never again went near the witch with her pram, and the twins cried no more.
196768: In Millegem two men knocked at the house of a witch and then ran away. The men had to wander about all night and ended up knee-deep in water. Only at dawn did they reach their homes.
196793: One evening a family was visited by a sorceress who lived nearby. The sorceress gave a three-year-old girl a sugar ball. The next morning the girl was ill. The child was ill for a whole year. Then she died of 'the great old man', as the doctor called the illness.
196829: A man who drove a cart to Mechelen always saw a cat jumping between the spokes of the wheels. The man kicked at the cat and struck his own wife.
196879: A man coming back from the station at Lint took the road along the woods to go home. The man did not reach his house until six in the morning, because he had wandered around all night. People said that the man had been ridden by the moon.
196882: A man who had seen that many hares came near his savoy cabbages wanted to shoot a hare one night. When the man saw a hare and tried to fire, he found that his gun did not work. A second attempt failed too. The man took a silver coin from his pocket and put it into the barrel of his gun. Then he was able to shoot, and the hare had vanished. The man went to look and saw blood in the snow. When he went inside, he saw his wife lying in bed with a bandage around her eye.
196897: On a farm the people went to gather eggs. When they came home with the eggs, they were as hard as stones, so that they could not break them in any way. When they threw the bewitched eggs away outside, they broke at once. Those people's stable was bewitched.
196940: A farmer coming back from the field with his cart saw a will-o'-the-wisp and said: "Come to me, I will baptise you!" The next moment so many will-o'-the-wisps came flying up that the cart was completely overflowing.
196954: A man from Zammel had moved the boundary post of his field to have more land. After his death the man came haunting on the bridge of Zammel-Veerle with the post on his neck. The ghost called out all the time: "Post, post, where shall I leave you!" One day the drunkard B. answered: "Put it back where you got it, then you won't have to drag it along!" After that the spirit was not seen or heard again.
196957: A man and a woman moved to the Blauwhoek. When they had only just moved there, a goat of theirs died. A pig began to grunt so badly that it had to be put down. A three-year-old child stamped and behaved strangely, although there was nothing to be seen. A neighbour woman was responsible for this misfortune. The farmer's wife went to the Poor Clares, where she was given a holy object. From that moment on she was no longer allowed to talk to the witch. Exactly one year after the farmer's wife's child had died, a child of the witch died too. The witch then moved away.
196959: Two women went to church together. At the church stood a suspected witch who was handing out grapes. One of the women accepted the grapes. Afterwards, however, her little child fell ill. Eight days later the child died.
196966: A hunter had often seen a hare near the abbey of Tongerlo, but had never managed to shoot it. One day a father said to the hunter: "I'll give you something to put on your gun. But you must make sure you shoot the hare in its backside." This time the hunter hit the hare, but the animal ran off. A few days later the hunter saw a little woman who had a wound on her backside.
197000: One evening the father of Jef V.D.P. went with the wheelbarrow to the shop in Veerle to buy twenty kilos of flour. On the way the man saw two women whispering. Because of those women the man got lost. At four in the morning he was an hour away from Veerle.
197019: A sick farmer kept crying out in the evening: "She is under my bed, can't you see her, the witch!" People went to the friars for the farmer, but they said it was already too late. A week later the farmer was dead.
197040: On a farm, noise was heard at night. In the morning people found that all the cows had been milked, although the doors had been firmly bolted. The farmer had to get rid of the cows because they no longer gave any milk.
197061: A farmer from the Paddepoelen could no longer churn butter and went to the parish priest, who advised him to pour a bucket of manure into the butter churn. The man followed the advice and had butter again. The next day he found a muzzle in his yard. He hung it on the perch where the chickens slept. The next day all the chickens were dead. The man found a swede, cut it into pieces and gave it all to the cows. Afterwards the animals had diarrhoea. The man then sent his sister-in-law to the priest. The priest said: "Shake hands with each other", but the two were never able to reconcile and the woman kept tormenting her brother-in-law.
197114: A witch could turn herself into a cat. If such a cat was wounded, the witch had a wound in the same place the next day.
197143: A mother had a child that lay crying in the cradle all the time. On a nearby farm the goats and pigs were bewitched.
197157: Jef S. had murdered and buried his child. When people later saw a will-o'-the-wisp, they said: "That is Jef S.!" The dog would then stand there frightened with its tail between its legs. Later the light was banished for ninety-nine years.
197169: A woman claimed she had seen two lights in the churchyard playing with each other. They were the spirits of two brothers who had come out of the grave.
197174: A farmer who wanted to build a barn but did not have the means sold his soul to the devil, who would put up a barn for him in one night. At night the farmer regretted what he had done and told everything to his wife. The farmer's wife said: "We'll build the barn ourselves. I'll help." When the cock crowed before the barn was finished, all the devils had to leave. There has always remained a hole in the barn.
197189: In Hombeek there were children who were so badly bewitched that they were pulled underneath their chairs.
197196: On a woman's farm the cows had foot-and-mouth disease. The woman went to fetch milk or something else at a neighbour's farm. The next day the neighbour's cows were also ill and his pigs lay dead. That woman was a witch.
197202: A farmer had much misfortune with the cows in his stable. An old woman from Nijlen who lived five hundred metres away once appeared in the shape of a cat. The farmer shot at the cat with his gun but could not hit it.
197213: A woman who always went to pray at a small chapel in the evening suddenly saw the devil standing beside her, blowing his nose. Terrified, the woman ran away.
197215: A man returning from the Kluis saw a meowing cat sitting on a piece of wood. The man went on and was followed by the cat. Every time the man looked back, he saw that the cat had grown bigger, until in the end the animal was as big as a horse. The man fled into a house, took a gun and said: "If I ever see that cat again, I'll shoot it dead". When the man saw the cat again some time later, the animal said: "You want to shoot me dead, but you won't have any luck".
197246: A man from Postel went to take the midwife home one evening. When the man came back, he saw a little black creature running in front of him. When the man came a little closer to the witches' hill, he saw the creature again. On the hill a cat stood against a tree. The man quickly ran away. He broke out in a cold sweat. He believed that cat had been the midwife.
197256: A woman came to visit a farm where chickens had been stolen and said: "They stole from you last night." When the people asked: "How do you know that?", the woman answered: "I know much more. It was a man from the heath who did it. You know him as well as I do." The woman was indeed right.
197288: A farm in Ruisbroek had to deal with the evil hand. One morning all the animals in the stable were pulled up and down until they dropped dead.
197294: A farmer walking through the village in the evening was pursued by a cat. When the farmer looked back, a second cat came. A little later still more cats followed, until the whole road was full of cats. The farmer got scared and went into a house, where all the doors were bolted. Countless cats leapt up as high as the fanlight above the door.
197319: Boys who had to draw lots for the army all went to a witch in Herenthout. That witch sewed something into their sleeve, so that they were sure they would not have to go into the army.
197326: One night a woman saw a tall ghost in a long white gown with black buttons come out of the bed. The next night exactly the same happened. The woman's brother had seen it too. The woman's husband was told and kept watch the next night. He too saw the ghost at twelve o'clock.
197349:
A witch from Zoerle-Parwijs who was always out at night could turn herself into an animal. A man on his way to Tongerlo was followed the whole time by a black cat. The man was annoyed by the cat and kicked it. The next day the witch wore a bandage around her head.
The witch foretold a marriage between a man and a certain woman, although the two did not yet know each other at the time. The prediction came true.
197353: A pregnant woman from Lint was going to Antwerp and on the way asked an old man for directions. The man showed her the way, but afterwards she got lost and wandered about for a long time. When the woman's child was born, it looked exactly like that old man. The child lived only two weeks.
197379: A man who was chopping down a tree saw a light with hairs like a porcupine's appear. A moment later the light dropped down with a thud.
197391: On a farm where the cows were untied at night, the misfortune was attributed to witchcraft. Sometimes the cows were tied by their tails to the haystack.
197428: At midnight a headless horse roamed on the Binneberg.
197429:
A man whose sister had died a few months earlier heard someone knock on the door. A moment later his dead sister came in. She was dressed in purple and looked very beautiful, as she had at thirty.
"What are you doing here, you're dead, aren't you?" asked the frightened man, to which his dead sister replied: "I am needed here once more", and she walked to a trunk saying: "I'll tell you what you must do. You must listen and come with me". Then the sister pointed out three places where her money was hidden. She blessed each of those places with three Our Fathers and nine signs of the cross. "There, now that it is blessed it will do you no harm", said the sister. "But why have you come back? We never quarrelled", said the man, to which the sister replied: "Yes we did, but it was my fault. We quarrelled a lot and God made me come back because I still had something to make right". Then the sister took a medal with the image of God from her handbag and gave it to her brother. After that the dead sister disappeared into the woods.
197430: In Westmeerbeek lived a witch who changed herself into a cat. After the cat had scratched at a stable, people there suffered from the evil hand. There were toads in the stable. One day they burned the foot of one of the toads. The next day a woman was seen walking about with a burnt hand. That woman was the witch.
197434: On a farm where a witch had come to visit, the piglets began to squeal loudly. A friar said he could do nothing about it because the witchcraft had gone too deep.
197449: Between Gierle and Tielen some men saw a cat sitting on a tree trunk. One of the men kicked at the animal, which then ran off howling. When the men looked back, the cat kept growing bigger. The men got scared and went home.
197484: Beer V. had found a money chest that passers-by had lost. After Beer had hidden the chest, a hellewagen (hell's wagon) flew through the cowshed every night. When that happened, the cows lay with their legs in the air. Beer's children also had bad luck. Only Beer's daughter, who married a young man who cared nothing for material wealth, had no bad luck.
197525: Some people who went catching quails always found their bird nets empty. The nets were bewitched.
197572: At a toll barrier where people had to pay, there worked a woman who was suspected of being a witch. That woman went to the farmers to overlezen (pray over) cows. She did nothing bad.
197586: When Charel O. was threshing, he saw a cat lying in the hay. Annoyed, the man struck at the animal. The next day Charel found that his own mother was lying in bed with a broken arm.
197588:
In the undergrowth along the fields, lights could sometimes be seen. Those will-o'-the-wisps were little souls from purgatory who could find no rest. People then said prayers for those souls.
Later it was discovered that the lights were in reality glow-worms.
197602: In Lichtaart a girl one evening saw the spirit of her dead mother appear. The spirit held a cobblestone in its hand and said: "I am in purgatory and I must do penance until this stone wears away in my hand". Badly frightened, the daughter went to the priest, who advised her to have many masses said so that her mother would soon be released.
197664: Two men who had been trying to outdo each other in cursing saw, on their way home in the evening, a floating coffin with four burning candles behind them. When they wanted to get into bed, a big black dog was lying in front of their bed. That was the devil, whom they had called up. The men sent for the priest, who ordered them to go to Hanswijk for a whole year to do penance.
197701: A man went to drink a glass of beer at his aunt's inn. His aunt stroked his head and said: "You are a good fellow, after all." The next day the man could not get out of bed. He was ill for a year and could not work. When the parish priest came to bring him the last sacraments, his tongue went stiff, so that he could not receive communion. The man then went to have himself overlezen (prayed over) by two former priests from Antwerp. After that the man was cured.
197706: People went to the fathers about a boy who was always playing with a crow. The fathers advised the people to kill that crow.
197717: At the B. family's house the devil came and lay under the stove in the shape of a big black dog. The fathers of Averbode came to drive the devil away.
197740: A girl from the Plein in Noeveren who was to make her communion had to go to church in the Hellegat every day. When the girl set off in the dark one morning with a friend, they saw a child in a little white shirt and bare feet standing by a drying place for bricks. The girls went on in fear. A little further on stood a house with a hedge in front and a gutter beside it. That same child lay there in the gutter. The girls were so frightened that they no longer dared to go to church.
197755: Kleudde with his chain was a big dog that let itself be carried. The werewolf was Kludde. Some people had to carry Kludde until they got home.
197796: A man returning from the fair was accompanied by a wizard who, at the Steenweg van Arendonk, said: "I'm off. Make sure you get home safely." After that the man had to wander about the whole night and wade through water. He began to pray. When he heard the bell ringing, he found his way again.
197817: A cat always came into a haunted house. When a man wanted to shoot at the cat, some people cried: "Now you are shooting at a witch".
197863: In Hoevenen a witte madam (white lady) lay on the road to Wilmarsdonk. It was a remote road that ran straight through the polder. A farmer's son who had walked his girlfriend home often came across the witte madam. When it was the fair in Wilmarsdonk, people made a detour via Ekeren because they did not dare to use that remote road at night.
197866: A woman could make herself as big as a mill. Whenever that woman had walked behind a cow, the animal gave no more milk the next day.
197876: In Schilde a girl had promised her friend to go to the chapel of Emblem for her. But because the girl fell ill, she could not go. So the friend had said: "I will go in your place", but she did not. Shortly afterwards the sick girl died. Every time the friend was tending the animals in the stable, she saw the ghost of the dead girl floating there. The friend went to confession with the curate, who said: "I will go to the chapel with you". With great difficulty the friend reached the chapel. On her arrival she saw the ghost of the dead girl rise to heaven.
197917: A man who met a cat asked: "Pussycat dear, where are you going?" The animal replied: "If you had not spoken so nicely, I would have broken your neck".
197925: In Mechelen there once lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. In the evening she always put a burning candle in the window. The wax from that candle dripped down. If the drops took the shape of a hanging hand, a child in the neighbourhood would die.
197935: In a house knocking on the wall was always heard in the evening. When the parish priest was called, he asked whether the people had perhaps ever failed to keep a promise. The people remembered that they had promised to have a mass said for a dead person. The ghost of the dead person had come back to remind the people of that promise.
197964: At the Allemanshof there were countless stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) by the water. If someone called out to such a light and then went inside, the light struck a white hand on the door. A stallicht was once seen in the Brodstraat too. People believed that such lights were the souls of unbaptised children. If you wanted to baptise such a light, you had to be very careful, or else a great many lights would come flying up.
198030: A man from Rijmenam who came with a 'wan' (?) came back after his death to make a racket.
198038: At the mill in Bornem a little kitten was seen in the evening. The animal mewed so loudly that the miller's wife wanted to take it inside. When she bent down to pick up the kitten, she heard an ugly scream. She was holding two feet in clogs in her hands.
198049: A farmer whose stable was bewitched could no longer churn butter. Horses, cows and chickens died as well. The farmer went to Tongerlo in honour of Saint Siardus.
198052: A woman went to do the washing and ironing for a sick witch. When the witch was recovering, the woman decided to do only the washing, because the witch's granddaughter could also iron. The witch held this against the woman and no longer visited her. But she often went walking with the woman's three-year-old daughter. A short time later that girl fell ill. The mother took the child to the doctor, who said it was a microbe going around. Then the mother went with her daughter to the witch, who had already charmed away fever for many people. The witch stayed alone with the child for a while and urged the mother not to go to the friars. The next day the mother's sisters advised her to go to the friars after all. In the end one of the girls did so. When the witch heard this, she began to cry and said: "I said you were not to go to the friars! Now I'll show who is the strongest. Two dogs on one bone." The little child was thrown from left to right.
198078: A woman who had gone to live in Antwerp after her marriage had a child. She went with the child to her parents, after which it fell ill. The mother no longer dared to stay alone with the child because she thought it was bewitched. Once when they were eating, the people saw a big frog fall next to their sandwich. They threw the frog away and a little later a witch stood at their door.
198087: One evening on his way home a man met a friend who was coming back from Zammel, where he had gone to see his girlfriend. When the two continued on their way together, they saw some twenty meowing cats jump out of the bushes. The men were followed by the cats. One of the men grew tired of it and shouted at the cats: "Can't you do anything but meow! Bark for a change!" Then the men were even more frightened, for the cats began to bark like dogs. The men ran away but were still followed by the cats. Only when they came to a crossroads did the cats disappear. So the cats had been witches, for they could not get past a crossroads.
