198097: When on Saint Hubert's day one gives blessed bread to the animals, one must not throw it into the manger, the tub or the pot, for then the witches make off with it and disease comes into the stable. Witches could change themselves into horses' heads or into cats. They also eavesdropped on people and sometimes crept in through the chimney or the peephole of the stable.
198118: A man who worked in Beerse had to set off at night. One night the man saw something white coming towards him. When the figure had come closer, the man said: "Good evening". A little later the figure had vanished.
198122: People who were ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit) in their beds lost consciousness and felt as if they were going to die. Victims of the mare had to make noise when they came to.
198139: A mother whose six-year-old son had died blamed a witch. When the child had been dead for three days, it still did not feel cold, so people did not dare to bury it. They laid the child in the coffin and left the lid open. When an aunt asked to see the child once more, the body did feel cold.
198165: Near the peat pits in Mol, lights were always seen in the old days. Those lights were the souls of dead people from the area. You were not allowed to beckon to the lights. Otherwise they would come and hang on the door handle until before sunrise.
198190: One Sunday a boy went to visit his girlfriend for the third time. The girl's mother gave him stewed potatoes with milk to eat. When the plates were on the table, one of the plates began to turn. Moreover, a 'topje' (a small top?) appeared on the table, which also spun. "That's nothing," said the girl, and she filled the plates. When the boy wanted to eat, the top went to his plate and kept trembling. The boy could not eat anything. Although he loved the girl, he had to leave her.
198250: A man who had read evil books went with some friends to the Goorstraat. At a certain moment the man said: "You mustn't be afraid," and he struck with a stick against the post from which the cow kettle hung. A little later a hundred thousand mice appeared. The friends were so frightened that they no longer dared to go home.
198268: Because a ghost hovered over the peat ground near Reesberg, people no longer dared to go there to fetch peat.
198286: On a farm a woman often came into the pigsty. When the people were working in the field, the woman secretly crept into the sty. In the end the pigs were running up the walls in fright. The people sent for a heksenbaas (witch master), after which the strange events stopped. One day the farmer's daughter got a sweet from the witch. Afterwards she had stomach cramps. The witch master came again and said: "The witch will walk around the house and make light at the drain hole for the water." For months the girl was wheeled around in a wheelbarrow by her brother. After she had been overlezen (prayed over) by the witch master, her condition did improve.
198297: Stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children.
198300: Two poachers suddenly found themselves at night in a chapel with an altar. The men began reciting the gospel, after which the chapel disappeared. When the poachers had seen a hare, they could not hit the animal. It kept running around them.
198395: An eight-month-old girl had been struck by the evil hand. Because of this the child was no bigger than a newborn. People went to the friars of Dendermonde for the child, who said: "She will stand in the doorway and speak, but you must not answer." And so it happened.
198397: One evening an unbelieving man was playing cards with some friends at the Kluis. Suddenly the card players saw a hare come in through the drain hole for the water. The card players were frightened. One of them wanted to catch the hare, but did not succeed. The hare stayed sitting in the same place the whole time. Suddenly the animal jumped up and disappeared the way it had come.
198417: A suspicious woman always came to fetch milk at a farm. She came in by the back door, went straight to the stable and always stroked the same cow. That cow fell ill and the vet did not know what to do. In the end the cow died. When the same thing happened again, a medal was laid under the door, so that the visitor could no longer get into the stable.
198457: At night a man saw a cat jump onto his bed. The man was convinced that the cat was his mother-in-law, appearing in the shape of an animal.
198461: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were unbaptised children who came back.
198472: Into a house where there was much cursing and shouting, a big black dog crept in one day and dragged someone away. That person was never seen again. People said the devil had made off with him.
198512: A man who was out walking with his girlfriend said at a certain moment: "I just have to relieve myself. If anything should come at you in the meantime, throw this handkerchief at the apparition." When the man came back a little later, he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. That is how the girl discovered that the man was a werewolf.
198569: A witch from Mol sometimes sat in a certain place without anyone being able to see her. Sometimes she was seen suddenly vanishing.
198616: In a house where there were rats at night, the loaves and the mastellen (round bread rolls) were always eaten. One day they managed to catch the rat in a trap. They lit the stove and tried to throw the rat into the fire with a red-hot poker. The sorceress, who lay moaning with pain, had to be taken to hospital to have her burns treated. The sorceress eventually died of her injuries.
198618: When people on their way to church believed a witch was walking ahead of them, they crossed that person's footprints. If the person was a witch, she would turn around.
198675: During the French Revolution a large unconsecrated bell had been hung in the church tower in Sint-Lenaarts. When the people had held a big feast, the devil said: "That bell is not consecrated, up, men, up to battle". First crows appeared and then devils, who took the bell out of the tower. Because they could not carry the bell, they dropped it in 't Kalkvondel. If you lay with your ear on the little bridge at night, you could sometimes still hear the bell ringing.
198679: A man possessed by the devil was playing cards in an inn in Bonheiden. "I'm done for," he suddenly said. Then his head was twisted backwards by the devil and he died.
198712: At Gerard H.'s in Vorst, a child had been given cabbage seedlings by a witch. Because the child was bewitched by them, the father had to go to the abbey of Tongerlo. The man had only just set off when the pedal of his bicycle broke off. With one pedal the man still made it to Tongerlo.
198761: Some men coming back from the fair in Itegem saw the bushes at a certain spot bending right down to the ground, although there was no wind. A white lady stood among the bushes.
198781: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) could only be seen by those born with a caul. Such lights were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. Jef H. baptised hundreds of stalkaarsen. The lights would then give him a hand and disappear. The baptiser's hand was then burnt.
198801: A farm was often visited by a midwife who was a witch. If the people on that farm had bought a cow, the witch knew it too. One day the farmer went at night to fetch a thin cow in Herenthout. Although nobody had seen him, the next day the witch knew he had a new cow. Three children died on that farm. In the end the farmer no longer let the witch in. A man from the neighbourhood who also had to deal with witchcraft went to the friars to have a little shirt blessed, but it did not help.
198831: A little girl was called into a witch's house, where she was given a waffle. When the girl then went home, she was flung from one side to the other. A farmer then took the girl home in his cart.
198841: A man coming back from the café could not get home, although he did not have far to walk. He knocked at the door of a man from the neighbourhood and asked him to accompany him. The neighbour accompanied the lost man until he was nearly at his house. The next day the man visited him and said: "You can't believe how long it still took me to get from that spot to my house". The man had been bewitched in the café.
198843: People who were bewitched had to stand still.
198848: On a haunted farm, pots were sometimes heard rattling. At other times music was played in the attic. When people went to look, suddenly nothing could be heard any more and everything in the attic was back in its place.
198878: Among the bushes next to the town hall sat a glass hen, which the girls going to the factory were very afraid of.
198912: On a farm in Schoten a seamstress sometimes came to work. Whenever that woman came, the dogs could not be held back. In the stable all the cows fell ill. The people went to the parish priest, who sent them to the friars of Bornem. The friar said: "There must be something. Is there perhaps someone you suspect?" The friar gave the people a medal that they had to put in water. They had to wash the cows' bellies with that water three times every day. When the people came to the bridge, they would see the culprit. At the bridge the people saw the seamstress standing. The friars said it was good that the people had come, because otherwise the witch would have broken their necks.
198922: On a haunted farm the straw always burned up.
198954: A man who was out on the Bergen after midnight saw a friar walking and said: "Oh, Father, you gave me a fright!" But there was no answer. The man went on, but when he looked back, he strangely could no longer see the friar. The man wanted to run away, but his blood stood still.
198982: A man who had to go and fetch barley was followed on his way home by a black cat that kept jumping back and forth. When the man came to a crossroads, he saw that the cat could not get past it. For it was a witch.
198996: A boy of about fifteen had been given a note by a gentleman. After he had read the note, he could do all sorts of things. For example, he could make as many mice as he wanted. If he took a handful of earth, he conjured a mouse out of it. The boy could also make the mill turn very fast.
199013: A man walking drunk through the village saw a black cat sitting on the railing of the bridge over the Wamp. "Shall I make you fall in there?", the man asked the cat, to which the animal replied: "Yes, if you do that, I'll make you a head shorter". After that the man was sober at once and ran home as fast as he could.
199053: A man walking home late in the evening through a dark, deserted street heard something. He looked round and saw a row of kittens. He said to the animals: "Kittens, are you warming your little bottoms?" Then the kittens came forward and surrounded him. They all raised their paws. After that the man ran away, terrified, without looking back.
199066: A girl was sitting with her father in a café where a woman was sitting who was suspected of being a witch. The girl was given pears by that woman. As soon as she had left the café, her father advised her to throw the pears away and never to accept anything from that witch again.
199094: In Broechem lived a woman who was accused by her own sons of being a witch. That woman tried to get in everywhere and then caused misfortune there. Many people went to the curate of Oelegem. If one put a holy object under one's door, the witch would not be able to come in any more. On a farm in Ranst no calf could be kept alive. Nor could butter be churned there. Those people were advised to put a wedding ring in the butter churn.
199095: On a farm two animals died in a single night. Noise was heard in the stable, and the next morning two cows were found with their necks twisted.
199131: A witch lived in Geel. A farmer going to work in his field had a bowl of rice pudding with him to eat at midday. On the way the farmer met a woman, who asked what was in the bowl. The farmer answered that it was rice pudding. When the farmer wanted to eat at midday, there was no rice pudding in his bowl, but green mud and filth.
199154: Some men playing cards kept hearing miaowing, though there was no cat to be seen. When a cat finally did appear, the men let loose two cockerels to catch it. But the cat was too quick for the cockerels and climbed into an oak tree. De Witte V.D. wanted to climb the tree or shoot the cat down. Just then a man came along who said: "No, you really mustn't do that." He was the husband of the witch who had turned herself into a cat.
199156: In Bergom lived a black-haired woman who was suspected of being a witch. When people saw this witch walking somewhere, they sometimes suddenly found that she had vanished and that a black cat was walking in her place.
199183: Some men who were playing cards saw a fellow with horse's legs come in. Because they knew it was the devil, they went to fetch a priest. A card player who was cheating said: "If I'm cheating, the devil may take me." The priest arrived just in time to save the cheat from the devil's clutches.
199192: An ugly, dirty woman from Burcht was suspected of being a witch. People said that if you walked in that witch's footprints, she would look back.
199200: A bricklayer who could not work because it was too cold went for a walk. He ended up in a wood where beautiful roses grew. However he walked, he could not get out of the wood. He called a friend's name, but in vain. The man was wearing new shoes, but when he got home the shoes were worn out. The man had fallen victim to the mare (a nightmare spirit).
199218: A mother who had many children could not keep a single little boy alive. Every time a boy was born, he died. The neighbours attributed the misfortune to the woman's mother-in-law, who was a witch. If anything happened again, the mother was to have a wax child ready and dedicate it to Saint Joseph. The mother did so. The next son she had did live. The mother-in-law never showed herself again.
199239: One morning a farmer found all his cows in the manure pit. The cows were facing backwards and tied up.
199242: A devil's barn is said to have stood in Londerzeel. A farmer had bricked a gable into his barn, but in the morning that gable had always fallen out. A devil came and said: "By the time the cock has crowed three times, the gable will be in place and stay in place." The farmer did have to sell his soul. The gable stayed in place and the farmer had lost his soul.
199255: A family was often visited by a woman who went straight to the children. She gave the children a sweet, after which they fell ill.
199272: A woman who saw a large spider walking in her house threw the creature into boiling water. The next day she met a little old woman who was badly burned all over and wore a bandage around her head.
199273: In a family the mother was ill. Whenever the children were outside, a neighbour woman always called: "How is your mother?" One day the sick mother had visitors. At that moment a woman came in and said: "Ha, there are visitors." She took a good look at everyone and then left again. On the way she passed a pile of wood that still had to be tied into bundles. Although there was no wind, the pile of wood simply fell over. When the visitors left, their horse in Nijlen loosened its own harness collar and the cart tipped over backwards. It was that woman who had caused all this misfortune.
199297: A farm in Bouwel was visited by a woman who came to ask for a jug of milk. The next day the cow on that farm gave no more milk. The people went to the parish priest, who said: "Oh, witches don't exist." The people then went to the brown friars in Herentals, who gave them something to pray. After that the cow gave milk again.
199372: A fisherman sitting by the brook one night saw a barking little dog come towards him. When the man wanted to hit the little dog, it had suddenly vanished. Two metres further on sat kludde (a shape-shifting goblin) with a lump of fire in his hands. The man then walked home in fear.
199377: In the old days the farmers went to fetch manure at the Antwerp zoo at three in the morning. When they came back around seven, they saw many 'glimmaaikes' (glowing lights) in the dark. People believed these were the little souls of unbaptised children. If a farmer turned around and said: "I baptise you", the lights vanished at once.
199380: On Walpurgis Night, or on Easter and St John's nights, the witches came to the Heksendonk in Arendonk to hold their sabbath. The witches were woken by a whistling in the air that other people could not hear. The witches then quickly rubbed themselves with ointment and flew up the chimney on their broom or goat to their destination. Thousands of people gathered there. A great silence preceded the arrival of the witch master. The devil first counted all his witches. Then the witches knelt one by one before the devil and kissed him. The witch who pleased him most was his queen. The witches all told of the evil they had done since the last meeting. They mocked the mass, desecrated hosts and slandered Our Lady. Laid tables rose up out of the ground and novices had to light the guests with torches. The torches had been lit from a burning light between the horns of the chief devil. The witches ate toads, the flesh of hanged men, of corpses from the churchyard and of unbaptised children. They drank from hollowed-out cow hooves. If one of those present accidentally said the name 'Jesus' or 'God' or the word 'salt', all the devils vanished and the witches noticed they were eating spiders, mould and other filth. After the meal a musician sitting on a platform began to play a fiddle made of horse hide with a bow that was really a cat's tail. Music was also made with drums and flutes. The dancing witches made mad leaps. The great goat was burned and all the witches took some ash home to do evil with. At dawn the naked witches flew home again.
199406: Three farmers tried with all their might to pull a sick horse to its feet. When the farmers saw a black cat sitting there, they smashed its head in. After that, two people were able to get the horse onto its feet.
199426: Because two sows had died in his stable, Peer went to the parish priest for advice. "Have you any idea who might be to blame?" asked the priest, and Peer answered: "Yes." The priest then said: "You must not borrow anything more from that witch. If she comes to bring a loaf, you must bury it and not eat from it." The very next day the witch of Meerhout came to bring a loaf.
199435: A man walking past the mill in Tielen suddenly saw an old woman standing in front of him, who cried: "What are you still doing here so late?" The man said it was none of her business, but she answered: "We'll see about that". When the woman was gone, the man got lost and ended up in Herentals.
199452: During the Boerenkrijg (Peasants' War) some women in Herentals had killed each other in a fight with stropijpen (straw pipes). After their death the women flew through the air with the stropijpen.
199488: Every evening a black cat walked over a child's bed. It was a witch from the neighbourhood.
199489: People who could not churn butter went to a clergyman from Tongerlo who could solve every problem. Usually that clergyman advised people to clean their stable thoroughly and whitewash the walls.
199505: A woman went to a farmer with a brand-new can to fetch milk. She was accompanied by a sorceress. When the woman reached the farmer, she found that the bottom had fallen out of her can.
199530: In a house there was always banging in the attic at night, although nothing could be seen. In the mornings tarts were always found in the yard. The children ate the tarts, until one day their mother told them to throw the pastries into the fire. The mother had in fact already been bewitched, but she was still freed from the witchcraft. Anyone faced with such witchcraft had to go to the friars of Dendermonde.
199553: On a farm in Merksplas a farmer struck off a cat's paw. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was missing a foot.
199560: People plagued by witchcraft went to the friars of Herentals, who came to pray over them. The clergymen put a relic under the threshold, so that the witch could no longer come in.
199586: A man who was taking a hare out of a snare on the Tielenhei suddenly saw the werewolf, which put its two front paws on his shoulders. The man kicked the werewolf in the belly and ran away. He jumped on the first train he saw going across the heath and slammed the door in the werewolf's face. The werewolf was so furious that it dug a hole in the heath and crawled into it. An hour later the heath was still moving up and down (?).
199590: In a valley all the cats of Grobbendonk were gathered together. A man passing by said: "Cat's head, I'm not afraid of you." The man grabbed a kitten, but a moment later had to run away because the animals all scratched his back.
199599: A man had a child of three or four who was ill. The man went to the monastery of Tongerlo and had salt and bread blessed there. He then had to let the child eat of the salt and bread for nine days. He also had to put a relic under the door. Because of that the witch could no longer come in.
199600: People who were ridden by the moon got lost and walked around for a long time. A man who had lost his Transvaal hat in the woods of Beverlo went to look for it. The man got lost in the meadow and did not find his hat. Only towards morning could he find his bearings again. That man had been ridden by the moon.
199621: A man who was afraid of nothing saw a black cat in his path one evening. He kicked at the animal, but then as many as a thousand cats appeared, so that the man did not get home until nearly morning.
199634: A farmer from Herselt had moved the boundary post of his field. After his death the farmer came back to haunt with the words: "Post, where shall I leave you? Post, where shall I leave you?" One day a drunkard answered: "Take it back to the place where you got it!" At that the spirit thanked the drunkard for releasing him.
199654: A farm in Herenthout was haunted every night. Knocking was always heard there. The farm had once been a monastery. The noises were caused by the soul of a friar who came asking for a prayer.
199657: To find out whether a woman was a witch, you had to place your feet crossed on her footprint. A witch would then have to look back.
199665: Some people who wanted to know whether a certain woman was a witch walked behind her in rainy weather. In the wet earth they could clearly see the suspected woman's footprints. They put their left foot in the woman's right footprint and began to pray the Gospel of Saint John. Then the witch could not move forward any more. She asked what she had done to them.
199683: A man who owned evil books was invited by the parish priest of Kessel. The clergyman wanted to get the man drunk and make him talk. The priest said to his guest: "I've heard you play cards so well. I'd like you to play a game of cards with me and the two curates." The card game began and drinks were poured regularly. The priest said: "It seems there are so many ghosts. Aren't you afraid of them?", to which the man replied: "No, I'm afraid of nothing. Some believe in it, others don't. But I can fill your garden with white mice. Just put your hat in the corner and lay a sheet of paper over it." The priest did so and the hat was full of white mice. Then the clergyman said: "Now try to get the sheet off and take the mice back out." The man could not, because he had lost his power.
199684: A child always saw a hen flying above its cradle. The other people could hear the hen, but not see it.
199728: A boy whose mother was a witch went to visit his girlfriend. He got lost in a wood and only got out again at nine o'clock in the evening.
199738: A thatcher from Wiekevorst was working in Itegem. Whenever he went home through the woods in the dark, he was pestered by a cat that ran under his feet. One day the man killed the cat with his hook. The next day the landlady of a nearby pub lay dead on her bed.
199768: An exceptionally strong man who could lift a plough with one hand was possessed by the devils. When that man's time was up, he still tried to drive the devils away, but in vain. They beat him to death, and his brains flew against the wall of the cellar room.
199772: A neighbour woman kept eavesdropping at the house of a woman who was soon to give birth. It was the custom for the women and girls of the neighbourhood to come and help the woman in childbed. When the time came and the neighbour walked through those people's stable, the cow standing there, which had just had a calf, was all sweaty. The neighbour touched the cow and a little later the animal was covered in lice. Later the woman of the house went to the friars of Mechelen and said to them: "I have no evil thoughts, but you must help me." The woman had a mass said. When she came home afterwards, there was not a single louse left on the cow.
199786: When there was terrible cursing in a house in Nieuwmoer, people said: "The devil will come in here one of these days." Those words had barely been spoken when the devil stood at the door.
199801: Some men went to visit a tightrope walker who was married to a witch. The witch said: "I'll light the fire, because it isn't warm in here." She had barely left the room when at least ten meowing cats jumped onto the floor. When the witch came back in, she laughed, but the men no longer felt at ease.
199806: A man was always pursued by a large black dog. If the man stopped, the dog stopped too.
199859: A man went fishing for eel in the Pannekensput every night. On Christmas night at twelve o'clock the man heard bells ringing in that pit.
199868: A woman who lived in a café could do witchcraft. A widower sitting in the café wanted to go home. The woman then said: "Make sure you get home safely". On the way the man had to walk through the water as far as Ginderbroek. He was bewitched.
199879: A knight returning from a crusade had left the abbey of Postel, where he had spent the night, and was on his way to Westerlo to visit his friends. On the Dessel heath the knight got lost. So he lay down on the ground to rest. When he woke up, he heard bells ringing that seemed to come from a marsh. He followed the sound and at dawn stood before Sint-Dimphna in Geel.
199881: On a farm where butter could not be churned and the cow did not get in calf, the misfortune was blamed on witchcraft. The people went to the friars and had novenas said. Parish priests laughed at such things.
199890: A man who had been playing the werewolf was unmasked. When he went to eat, people saw that the fibres of his girlfriend's clothes were between his teeth.
199896: In Vosselaar there lived a witch who sat in the churchyard in the evenings with a white sheet over her head. She wore a large hoop skirt and did not move. Witches had to do such things, whether they wanted to or not.
199936: A sorceress who was often out at night causing harm had a son-in-law who did not believe in her magic powers. When the man was mocking again, the sorceress said: "Just wait, little man, tomorrow you'll be dead." The next day the son-in-law lay dead in his bed.
199944: Around All Souls' Day, stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were often seen. They were the souls of unbaptised children who came to ask for help. Most people did not dare to help the lights and ran away in fear.
199972: At Polleke H.'s in Ham there were three women who were all witches. Someone had advised Polleke to stick a blessed candle under the church door. When Polleke had done so, the witches could not get out. As soon as the candle was taken away, the three women ran outside as fast as they could.
199997: A boy who suspected a woman of witchcraft put his left foot in the print of the woman's right foot and his right foot in the print of her left foot. When the boy had done that three times, the witch turned around and asked: "Aren't you coming along?"
200019: On a farm where the evil hand was in the stable, the horse was so wild that it could not be tied up.
200022: Someone who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come back to haunt after his death until he had sufficiently atoned for his sin.
200066: A miller's hand claimed that you were ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit) at night if you put your clogs under your bed.
200067: Every evening a ghost dressed in white with a basket appeared at the Reusel chapel. The police went to take a look and they too saw the ghost around midnight. The officers shot at the ghost, but the next moment it had vanished for good.
200080: A girl became seriously ill after accepting a sweet from a neighbour. The girl always said: "What is that big black fly doing here?" Other people in the same room did not see the fly. They went to the friars of Tongerlo, but it did not help, for the girl died.
200085: A man always walked past a widening of the canal where a mewing cat sat. One day the man kicked the cat, so that it fell into the water. After that the man never saw the cat again. It must have been a witch.
200101: A man saw a black cat sitting under his hedge and said: "That is a witch." He shot at the cat, but the animal did not move.
200104: In the 'Kweek' in Oorderen a large black dog was seen crossing the road every night. One night some men decided to keep watch in the ditch. When the dog appeared at midnight, one of the men shot at it with his gun. Although it was a hit, the dog made no sound. The bullets went right through the dog's body, so the animal could not be hit.
200109: A family with a bewitched child sent for the friars. The clergymen prayed over the house and put a relic under the door. After that the witch could no longer enter the house.
200118: On a farm struck by the evil hand, there was much misfortune. When the daughter came back from a nearby farm, she lay down on the ground along the way and pulled up grass. Another day she was found with her head in a tub of water and had nearly drowned. In the stable the cows all became skin and bone, although they were fed a lot. One day a cow dropped dead after being milked. The pigs did not fatten. One day the farmer's wife was told by her sister-in-law: "Give your daughter a blessed candle. She will not accept it." And so it was, for the daughter cried: "I mustn't, I mustn't!" An unblessed candle, on the other hand, she accepted at once. A book of Saint Gerard was placed under the daughter's head, but the girl always turned her head away from it. The daughter tore the sheets to pieces and pulled the hair from her head. The farmer's wife's brother-in-law went to the friars of the Kluis. When he cycled past the house of the evildoer, his lamp suddenly stopped working. A friar was driven by car from Lier to Putte. The friar came in and saw that the girl kept staring at a corner of the ceiling and a moment later went as stiff as a board. The friar gave the girl his hand, after which she immediately behaved normally. The friar said: "I will come back tomorrow morning, for I must do this fasting." The friar then blessed everything and the people were given a medal. After that the situation slowly improved, but that friar died young. The friar had asked the girl whether anyone had touched her. After a while the girl remembered that a farmhand who lived on the farm had once patted her on the shoulder. Without the people having told him, the friar said who was responsible for the evil. The people did not pass this on. The girl recovered and married. Two years later at the fair she saw the farmhand who had done her harm. He asked: "Won't you come into the café and drink a bottle of wine?" The girl went along and was bewitched again. They went to the friars at once, but they said they would not come until the next morning. Because the girl was dying, they turned to the parish priest instead. The clergyman undid the evil and the girl was cured for good.
200130: A farm often had poor people come by looking for a place to spend the night. One morning around six o'clock the barn burned down. One of the lodgers was in fact a witch. When that witch stayed at another farm, a fire broke out there too.
200134: A woman going to the shop met a strange beast on the way. The doctor of Herselt had once said that in that street one could indeed be confronted with all kinds of evil.
200139: On a farm in Broechem the cows stopped giving milk because of a witch who lived nearby. The cows were prayed over.
200180: A girl had burns on her little arms. An old woman came to tend the wounds. The girl's mother went to the friars to have the wounds prayed over. "If you don't do it, I won't believe in anything any more, for it is in the catechism, isn't it?" said the woman. The friar prayed until the sweat rolled down his face. After that the girl's wounds were healed. The old woman had caused the harm.
200186: Near Diest stood an abandoned barn where strange things happened. A farmhand passing the barn one evening heard lovely music and was pulled inside by two pretty girls. The farmhand had great fun and was even offered money. When one of the girls sneezed, the farmhand called out: "God bless you". The next moment he found himself all alone in the dark. His trouser pockets were full of oak leaves.
200191: At night a large pig walked on the road between Lippelo and Sint-Amands near the Biste bridge. Nobody managed to catch that pig, because it always suddenly disappeared. In the daytime the pig was never seen.
200223: A woman who was always ill felt at night as if a heavy weight lay on her. Because the woman's husband suspected his own mother was causing the trouble, he went to the parish priest of Willebroek. The clergyman told the man: "Get up tonight and a black cat will come in through the cellar hole. Hit the cat with the poker, but do not kill it." No sooner said than done. When the man went to his mother's foster daughter the next day and asked for his mother, the foster daughter answered: "She isn't here, she's lying in the cellar room." The mother had a bandage around her head. Her daughter-in-law died because her husband had gone to the priest too late. The clergyman died a wretched death.
200238: A man coming back from visiting his girlfriend in Heffen saw white cats everywhere. The man assumed that the apparition had something to do with witchcraft. When he threw something at the cats, the animals disappeared. A few days later the cats were back there again. Other people could not see the animals.
200243: A man was courting the daughter of a woman who lived in Ekeren and was said to be a witch. The daughter broke her leg twice near her house. For if a witch found no other victims, she had to bewitch her own daughter.
200294: In one house three children died within a single week because of an evil hand. An old witch who lived nearby had caused it. After a while the fourth child of those people also fell ill. The father, who slept in the bakehouse, always saw a bumblebee flying about. One day someone came to visit and said: "You must take the broom out of the corner." The people did so and their sick child recovered.
200295: A witch tormented her father whenever she did not get her way. One day her father would not let her go to the fair. The next day all the man's pigs lay dead.
200310: On a farm in 't Watereind the horses had foam on their lips. They were often exhausted without anyone understanding how. In the end it turned out that it was the farmer's own wife, who could work magic. When the woman later died, she passed her power on to her daughter.
200322: A miller who was possessed by the devil had a mill that always turned, even when there was no wind. The miller also had a black dog with special powers. When a farmer somewhere had got his cart stuck, the miller went there, harnessed the black dog to the cart and solved the problem. At midnight the miller always read from a book while keeping a black cat with him. In this way the miller learned to do magic in two days. If he smeared mud on a green leaf and then pressed on it, mice appeared.
200325: Two brothers both had bad luck in the draw for military service because they had met the witch Soo B.
200350: A man going to high mass on a Saturday was patted on the shoulder by a woman walking beside him. The man was startled and quickly hit the woman on the head. For one always had to strike witches higher up to make them powerless.
200370: A pregnant woman picked grapes at a witch's place. The witch found out and became angry. When the pregnant woman gave birth, a little son was born with a bunch of grapes under his jawbone.
200375: A brewer who could not make beer told his hands to keep a close watch. When one of them saw a big toad crawling in the barn, he chopped off one of its legs. The next day the brewer's wife came downstairs. She had only one arm left.
200398: A twenty-four-year-old young man who had just come back from the army came home late in the evening. His mother had already gone to bed, but when he reached his house, he called: "Mother, open up! Open up!" The mother opened the door and heard at least a hundred cats miaowing. The cats sang: "Hand and hand, paw and paw, and Neleke must go in the ditch." A short time later the young man fell ill. Three weeks later he was dead. The mother then laid a holy object under the door, so that the witches could no longer enter the house.
200401: Someone struck at a cat. After a few attempts, the blow landed. The next day that person found that a neighbour woman's face was badly injured.
200412: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field came back to haunt the toilet after his death. One day someone went to the toilet and heard the ghost ask: "What shall I do with it? What shall I do with it?" The man then answered: "Put that post back where you got it!" After that the haunting was over.
200442: A sick woman going to the doctor in Keerbergen walked along a road where a little shrine hung on a lime tree. Suddenly the woman saw a burning wagon with two horses flying through the air. An animal kept running round the trunk of the lime tree and a moment later disappeared. The woman's husband also always saw something moving at the Sint-Janskapel, which a moment later vanished without a trace.
200458: Some people going home from the Oppuurs fair took a wrong road. Although his friends pointed it out to him, the man could not manage to take another road. He had been ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit).
200467: Every Sunday during high mass a woman went to have a drink in a café. The landlady found this strange and told the parish priest. The clergyman advised the landlady to put a medal under her threshold. If the woman had anything to do with the evil hand, she would no longer be able to come in. The landlady followed the advice. After that the woman never set foot in her café again.
200508: A witch who owned fifty to a hundred chickens did harm to herself, so that all the chickens died.
200515: A farmer whose cows no longer gave milk went to the parish priest, who advised him to keep a close eye on everyone living on the farm the following night, as there might be a witch among them. That night the farmer saw the maid go into the stable and stroke the cows, saying: "Dear little beasts, dear little beasts!" The maid was sent away and after that the cows gave milk again.
200571: In the cellar of his house a man struck at a toad with his shovel. Afterwards a woman in the village lay dead in front of her door. Witches could take on all kinds of shapes.
200572: A mother with special powers had two sons and a daughter. One day a man from the neighbourhood who helped people came by. Without looking, the mother took a stick from a stack of brushwood bundles and stood it upright on the counter with a candle on top. Strangely enough, everything stayed standing.
200605: A man who had struck at a cat heard the next day that a woman from the village had a broken leg. This is said to have happened in Schilde.
200613: A witch played with a little doll in her pocket to torment people.
200631: A woman had vowed to go to Scherpenheuvel for her little daughter. But the girl died before the mother had fulfilled the vow. After her child's death the mother always saw a cat sitting on the bed. "Mathil, is that you?" the mother would ask, but no answer came. Nor could anyone touch the ghost. The mother had to carry her daughter's ghost until she reached Scherpenheuvel.
200661: By the Nete in Walem there was a place where one could never cross the bridge at night. The bridge was guarded by a large black dog that lay down at the feet of passers-by.
200676: A man went to Dendermonde at night because he wanted rabbits. When the man came back, he could not manage to stay on the road. He kept walking into the field without wanting to. The man could not get home because he had been ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit).
200685: Somewhere a girl danced with the devil.
200697: A wizard fixed someone to his chair without touching that person. When another wizard came in there, the victim could get up and leave.
200703: A witch used to live in Aartselaar. A man coming back from Hemiksem saw a small kitten sitting at the Grunenhoek. He wanted to grab the kitten, but just then a car drove past. When the car was gone, the man saw a witch sitting against a tree stump on the other side of the street.
200716: A mother had a child suffering from 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness). The child had long hands, long feet and a long face. The mother went on pilgrimage with the child to Brustem. There a piece of cloth was dropped into the water. If the rag did not stay afloat, there was no more hope. The witch who had caused the harm lay on her deathbed for three days.
200751: A boy slept in the attic room. Whenever he lifted his blankets, he always saw something like a flash of lightning. The boy's parents claimed it was a woman who came in through the water drain and changed into a black cat.
200856: Some people waiting for the tram saw a woman approach, who said: "Do you want this loaf? I found it in the street. The baker must have lost it." A man who had found a loaf by the gate gave it to his cow. Shortly afterwards the farmer and his wife died, and then two other people.
200857: A man coming back from the fair in Boom was followed by a cat the whole way to his house on the Oude Baan. When the man was lying in bed, he suddenly heard a loud bang.
200864: A boy saw a hare and shot at it. The hare was not hit and grew bigger and bigger. The boy ran away, but came back the next day with a blessed bullet. When he fired it, the hare flew into a ditch. The boy went to look and was terribly shocked to see a badly wounded woman lying there.
200893: On Christmas night at twelve o'clock a bell could be heard ringing in the water of a pond in Mol.
200910: Witches were all ugly women who wore hooded cloaks. Because there was no soap yet, they were usually black with dirt too. People who had been bewitched by a witch from Noorderwijk went to the monastery of Tongerlo, where they put something in the offering box and had masses said.
200915: A man who no longer knew which way to take home had been bewitched by a witch.
200922: In Weelde there used to live little old women who could haunt. They were usually women of about seventy.
200934: On a farm there were two fat, healthy horses and cows in the stable. One morning it was found that the two horses lay dead in the stable and that the two cows had their heads in one halter. The other animals were dead. The people then went to the friars of Dendermonde, who gave them a relic to put under the threshold. After that they had no more trouble in their stable. The misfortune had been caused by a woman from the neighbourhood who was possessed by the evil hand.
200969: On a farm in Hingene there was an old oven in the yard. When one day a rough fellow walked past that oven, he was seized and thrown into the oven. Afterwards the same happened to a number of other people. It was the work of the devil.
200973: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) moved above the ground at the height of a person. They were the little souls of unbaptised children floating about. One day a fisherman saw a stallicht come and settle on his iron.
200977: People who had the evil hand in their stable could not churn butter. They went to Tongerlo.
200986: Witches could take the shape of an animal. If such an animal was wounded, it was later found that the witch was wounded as well.
200992: The pit in the Molenstraat used to be badly haunted. Sometimes a white goat was seen walking there, at other times a troop of dancing cats. A man who always laughed at ghost stories had to pass the pit one evening. The man was nearly frightened to death when he saw as many as twenty maidens sitting around the pit. Terrified, the man went on. When he looked back a little later, the maidens had vanished.
201045: On a farm they had to deal with the evil hand in the stable. In the evenings the animals began to stamp and pull at their straps. When people went to look, they saw a large red hand on the stable door. In the morning the hand was gone and during the day the animals were calm.
201046: In the past people were sometimes plagued at night so that they could no longer find their house. A man often got lost on the road by the Ekelenveld. He would walk past his house as many as twenty times without seeing it. At sunrise the man could go home because the witches' power was broken.
201048: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had to burn after his death and come back to haunt with the words: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I leave it?" When a drunkard answered: "Where you got it", the ghost was released.
201074: If you left your clogs in front of the bed in the evening, you were ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit). The mare sat on her victim's body and weighed so much that the victim could hardly breathe. In the morning the mare was gone.
201090: In Ginderbroek a white ghost could sometimes be seen. A man walking home through the fields saw that white ghost by the ditch. Suddenly the ghost jumped into the middle of the ditch and then vanished.
201096: A girl who had fallen ill always saw a cat come in through the window in the evening. That cat was probably a witch. The girl died.
201102: A family in which seven or eight children had already died went to the friars of Lier. A friar told them: "On the way you will meet a woman who will drop a piece of wool, but you must not pick it up." What the friar predicted happened. The culprit was a woman who came peddling with a basket every week and often came near the children.
201114: At the Poel in Ravels all the witches took the shape of cats at night.
201117: A curate went for a chat with a man suspected of having special powers. "I've heard it said that you can do something", the curate said to the wizard, who replied: "No, but unfortunately many people believe so". After much insisting the curate got the man to admit that he really had supernatural powers. The man had a book he had got from his grandfather, with which he could, among other things, fix people to the ground. The curate asked for the book and threw it into the stove. The man took the book out again undamaged. The same thing happened a second time. The third time the book did not come back.
201163: On a farm a cat always scratched at night with its paw through the drain hole for the water. The hole had once been closed up, but in the morning it was open again. A farmhand kept watch by the drain hole and chopped off the cat's paw with a knife. The next morning the farmer's wife lay in bed with one arm. She was the witch.
201179: One Sunday a man had gone to the fair in Zittaart together with Selm. When the man wanted to go home, Selm said: "You won't be home today." The man left for home in disbelief, but he did indeed get lost.
201193: Sorceresses used to come peddling apples and sugar balls. In a house where a baby lay in the cradle, the sorceress could cause the child to get 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness). The child would then die unless it was taken to the friars.
201199: A sorcerer always had to make sure he was home by twelve o'clock, wherever he came from. When people wanted to trick the sorcerer one day, they set the clock back an hour. The next morning the sorcerer lay dead with his brains beside his head. When the sorcerer went to mass, he always left the church during the consecration. A man who could cure erysipelas could have learned much more, but he did not, because it was already so dangerous when he read in his books.
201220: Kludde with his bells was a figure who walked around with rattling chains. If Kludde had walked twice around the same house, misfortune would befall the people living there. For example, there would be a death. Some people claimed that Kludde was a calf.
201222: On a farm a black cat always sat in the horse's manger. Nobody dared to feed the animal. The people went to the fathers of Bornem, who gave them a relic to put under the stable door. The people did so and the cat was not seen again.
201291: Many witches used to live in Balen. When two friends were coming back from Balen, they said: "We'll go this way". Then they heard someone call out: "If only you get home". After that the men wandered about until morning.
201307: In a brewery where the brew always went bad, a cat roamed about. One day the cat fell into a kettle of boiling brew. The next day the baker's wife lay in her bed with burns.
201308:
People who consorted with the devil took a walk every evening, dressed entirely in black. At the corner of the street they were awaited by others who also wore black clothing. Together those people then went somewhere.
There was only one way to convert such people, namely by bringing them a sack of grain and making them count all the grains. But no one ever succeeded in getting them to carry out that task.
201320: If you dared to chase a cat away, you got into trouble. A cat was a witch. A man who once kicked at a cat was never healthy again afterwards.
201327: A woman who had put a basket full of eggs in the cupboard was visited by a neighbour who came for a chat. When the woman went to the cupboard after the neighbour had left, she found that her basket was empty.
201353: An old woman always went gathering firewood. A neighbour always heard three knocks on the oven lid after she had finished baking. Yet there was nothing to be seen. One day the sheets had been pulled off the bed and thrown into the toilet, although nobody had been in the house. The witch must have done that. The animals could no longer get up in the morning. A child fell ill after the old woman had picked it up. They took the child on a pilgrimage, after which it recovered.
201363: A farmer who could no longer churn butter had to move because his cowshed was bewitched.
201375: Some people saw a large spider crawl into their house every evening. One evening the farmer struck off two of the spider's legs. The next day it was found that a woman from the village had only one leg left.
201399: A horse dealer who was often on the road regularly met a witch. Sometimes the witch appeared in the shape of a black cat, at other times she wore a red kerchief on her head. One day the man lashed out at the animal with a stick, but that did not help. Only after the man had fetched something blessed from the friars was he rid of the witch.
201418: If you saw a black cat walk in front of your feet, you were not to harm it. Such cats were witches, after all.
201420: A man who had kicked at a black cat saw twenty-five cats appear a little later. That was witchcraft. When he got home, the man saw the cats take hold of the wheelbarrow in the barn and put it in the 'scheerwerk' (?). If you had holy water in such a case, you could chase the cats away.
201438: A man walking home one evening had accidentally walked past his house and could no longer find his bearings. He knocked at a farm and asked the way. The people who lived there said: "You must have been ridden by the moon."
201458: Two brothers returning from the village of Heist-op-den-Berg kept seeing a cat running in front of their feet on the way. The men kicked at the cat but could not hit it.
201459: A woman from Balen who went to close the window shutters one evening saw the ghost of her dead mother standing against the wall. The woman sought advice from the parish priest, who advised her to hold a white cloth in her hand the next time she faced the ghost. After all, anyone touched by a ghost became paralysed. The mother came to tell her daughter that money was hidden somewhere. As soon as the money was found, the ghost appeared no more.
201483: On the Kloosterheide in Lier there used to be a convent that became confiscated church property during the French Revolution. Later a little nun came haunting on the meadow there every night at twelve o'clock.
201505: Many witches used to live in Bevel. A woman who thought she was being followed by a witch placed her feet in a cross. Because of this the witch could go no further.
201510: At night hundreds of cats gathered on the Loecht in Brecht. The animals lay there meowing, fighting and playing. In the morning they were gone. The cats were probably witches holding a meeting there.
201511: In Lichtaart a boy was going out with a girl whom his parents suspected of being a witch. The boy wanted to put it to the test and one day stayed a little longer at his girlfriend's house. Just before midnight he left the room and peeped through the keyhole from an adjoining room. So he saw his girlfriend go to a cupboard and take out a little pot. The girl rubbed some ointment under her armpits and said: "Over hedgerow and hedge to the wine cellars in Cologne!" The next moment she had vanished. The boy broke off the relationship immediately afterwards.
201531: On the Platweg between Hoevenen and Oorderen a priest or a friar always came haunting at night.
201537: In a family there was a child that had been born healthy but a short time later got all sorts of problems. At one time the child's little head was twisted round, at another it was full of lice. They went to the friars, but they said the people must not harbour evil suspicions. One day the people's cow stopped giving milk. From then on they no longer let the milkman in. After that everything was all right with the child again.
201538: On a farm where a cow was about to calve, a woman stood watching. At a certain moment the woman was sent away with the words: "You'd better leave, or else she certainly won't be able to calve." The woman had barely gone when the calf was born.
201550: A man coming back from the mill with a wheelbarrow had his little dog with him. Normally the dog was afraid of nothing and hated cats. When the man saw a white cat in a bush along the road, his dog kept quiet. That cat was a witch.
201570: A sorcerer sent his own rats to other people's houses. The animals were seen running across the street from his house to two small farms nearby.
201605: Two men were coming back from work one evening. One had a chopper with him and the other a flail. On the way the men came across a large beast. At the moment the men wanted to wound the beast, it turned around. The men were so frightened that they ran home quickly. When they went to look at the same spot the next day, they saw their own footprints, but not those of the beast.
201635:
A boy was given a drink at his neighbours' wedding party. The next day the boy suddenly felt unwell and sat down against the hay. The boy believed he was bewitched because in the evenings he always came across a cat that would not be chased away. The boy only met the cat when he was out alone. At the wedding party the boy had had a nosebleed, and a woman had struck a cloth around his neck three times. Afterwards the boy's whole head had to be put in plaster. The doctor said that only a miracle could still save the boy, but a few days later he was nevertheless doing better.
They went to the fathers, who gave them a relic. The fathers came to the boy's sickbed. They advised the people to accept nothing more from the witch, who was a seamstress. One day the seamstress came along with the words: "Could you give me the needle of your sewing machine? Mine is broken and I still have to finish something." The sick boy's mother passed the needle through the window, because the witch could no longer get over the threshold, as there was a holy object lying there. A few days later the witch brought the needle back. A few days after that the boy got much worse. He was in great pain and said: "Mother, you are destroying me with that needle!" The mother should indeed not have lent the needle. A few days later the boy began spitting blood. Nothing more could be done.
When the boy was dead, his head fell off his body, because it had completely rotted away.
201673: A farmer went to the market in Diest every week. He always left very early and knew the way well. One morning, however, he could not get away from his farm. He walked in a large circle and kept ending up in the same place. This went on until seven in the morning. The farmer then decided to go home, where he told his wife everything. She laughed at the story, for she had actually caused the trouble herself.
201711: Some people out for a walk were given a basket of fruit by a witch. However, the people did not dare eat the fruit for fear of being bewitched.
201724: A man often went to visit his neighbours. He lived about a hundred and fifty metres from the road. Whenever the man walked along that road in winter, he always met a woman there who had pulled her skirt over her head. The man always had to step aside to let the silent woman pass. He met the woman every time, no matter what time he went home. His friends laughed at him and said: "Just push her out of the way." When the man saw the woman again, he struck at her, but at that very moment the woman seemed to vanish into thin air.
201729: On a bewitched farm at 't Gilseind the cows stood sweating in the cowshed. The parish priest read prayers over the animals and sweated terribly while doing so. The farmhands and maids had already been to the fathers of Bornem, but the clergymen had said that they could do nothing about it. Only the parish priest could.
201757: Witches could make people and animals die. You must never accuse a witch; you could only say: "You can do more than I can."
201779: In a house where people had just fetched vegetables, an old woman came to visit, touched the cabbages and said: "Oh, what beautiful cabbages!" When the people later ate those cabbages, they fell ill. The old woman was a witch who had bewitched the cabbages.
201782: A miller's wife always told of a child that had fallen ill through witchcraft. Once it was known who the witch was, everything was all right again.
201793: A girl was afraid of black cats because those animals could be witches. When a disease broke out among the cattle somewhere, people often blamed a witch for the misfortune.
201818: Some men sat playing cards in a café. At a certain moment a gentleman came in who wanted to join in. Strangely enough, the gentleman won every game. When a man bent down to pick up a dropped card, he noticed that the gentleman had horse's feet. It was the devil. They fetched the parish priest, who came to read prayers over the place to drive the devil away. This incident is said to have taken place in the café 'Grote Leeuw' in Blauberg.
201830: A man who went to confession with the friars in Bornem one Saturday evening got lost. He had been ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit).
201835: A woman from Merksem was suspected of being a witch. If you walked crosswise in her footprints, she looked back and disappeared as quickly as possible.
201848: A man had a little child that cried all the time and could not be helped by the doctor. The child died. When the little body was laid out, they saw that the pillow was full of pins. The people knew that this was the work of a witch. They suspected who was to blame, but never dared to say so.
201868: A girl had learned from her mother how to conjure up mice without tails. A friend of the girl told the parish priest what she had seen. When the girl was sitting with the cows grazing on the verge, the priest came and asked her to make mice. She did, and the clergyman said: "What is that now? I didn't see it properly. Do it again." After that the girl could no longer make mice. The priest had probably freed her from the magic power by means of prayers.
201877: A maid sitting by the fire in the kitchen suddenly saw the sewing machine by the window start running without anyone having touched it. The maid could not explain what she had seen.
201889: A witch gave a sweet to a child. The next day the child was ill.
201903: In a family in Woensdrecht, some of the children had fallen ill through the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). Some neighbour women who came to keep watch in the house saw a toad come in through the drain hole for the water. One of the women took a pair of tongs and threw the toad into the fire. The next day it was said that a neighbour woman was badly burned all over.
201907: On a farm in Putte they were churning butter when a woman came by to sell something. The people bought nothing, however, whereupon the woman said: "You'll be churning for a long time yet." The people indeed got no butter and had to go to the fathers.
201921: A family had a little daughter who sometimes suddenly disappeared and then could not be found. When the girl came back, she no longer knew where she had been. A neighbour was causing these strange events.
201966: A witch from the Heembeemd had bewitched her neighbours. As a result, those people were always thrown into the air at about half past twelve when they were lying in bed. In the end the people went to the fathers, who gave them a medal that they always had to wear on their chest. That put an end to the witchcraft.
201981: A man whose child cried all the time went to the fathers of Tongerlo. Twenty minutes after leaving, the man came back sweating, saying: "I can't go, because the road keeps being cut off with a knife." When the neighbours went to Tongerlo for the child, a father gave them a little cloth to put under the threshold. Two days later the people noticed that the witch could no longer get over the threshold. The little child no longer cried.
201998: A woman who was eating saw a witch come in, who patted her on the shoulder and said: "How well you can eat!" After that the woman's head was full of lice. No remedy, however drastic, helped to get rid of the lice. When the woman had taken communion at midnight mass at Christmas, all the lice had suddenly gone.
202006: One evening a boy had been visiting his girlfriend. When the boy wanted to leave, the girl's uncle said: "Are you sure you're going home?" The boy left but could not get home. He was in a field right near his house that he could not get out of. After he had lain flat on the ground for a while, he did reach his house.
202008: A man coming back from the fair one evening saw a crowd of horses, soldiers and noblemen moving along the road. The man was hemmed in by the company and barely made it home.
202044: A boy could not sleep at night because a witch crawled over his feet. One night the boy decided to stay awake. The boy recognised the witch. When he met her after mass, he said: "Ah, X, come and teach me witchcraft!" To which the witch replied: "Your mother is just as great a witch as I am!"
202084: A girl went to a café with a boy. In the café the boy conjured up mice. The mice ran over the table and onto the bar. Because people were afraid of the mice, the boy made the animals disappear again. In another café the boy conjured five-franc coins onto a table. When people tried to pick up the money, it vanished. People claimed the boy was in league with the devil, so his girlfriend was no longer allowed to go around with him. After the priest had read prayers over the boy, he could still do magic. During catechism class the priest took away his magic power, but at the age of eighteen the boy could do magic again.
202108: A kitten crept into the house through the water drain hole and crept up to the fire. When the people said "poor kitty", the animal replied: "If you had not been so good, I would have broken your necks". That cat must have been a witch.
202164: A man had bought a farm in the Goorstraat for 24,000 francs. The farm was haunted. Twelve children were raised there. It often happened that they suddenly found that all the money in the house had disappeared. Close to the farm an old woman lived in a wooden hut. The farmer went to the parish priest, but since the priest did not take him seriously, he went to the Trappists to fetch a holy object. After the farmer had put the holy object under his door, the neighbour no longer came for milk, although she had always done so before. After the neighbour had moved away, no more money went missing at the farm.
202170: In Aartselaar lived an old woman who was a real witch. One day a mother noticed that her children would not eat and were shivering all the time. This went on for eight days. The witch had caused it.
202193: A man who went to catch eels saw a light sitting on the iron. The man caught nothing at all and headed home. On the way he met a witte madam (white lady) and said three times: "Qui vive - who goes there?", but there was no answer. Then the man said: "Speak, or I'll speak with the iron in your body!" The apparition then screamed and vanished.
202202: Stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. When you saw such lights, you had to make the sign of the cross to baptise them.
202220: A man from Schilde who had been given clothes by a witch saw rats coming in all night. In the end the man had to throw those clothes away.
202249: In the evening figures dressed in white wandered about the churchyard. When someone came into the churchyard, the ghost leapt in front of the person's feet while loudly wailing, cursing or foretelling disaster. Then the ghost ran off laughing among the graves.
202261: A man who came home alone one Sunday evening was flung from one bush to another. A sorceress stood in front of him and said that he must not tell who had done this to him. Otherwise it would cost him his life.
202278: Some people who had gone digging on Kesselhei got lost on their way home until they met someone. That broke the witch's power.
202286: A farmer's wife from Langdorp was visited by a woman from her family. The woman was shown around the farm and said: "But you have beautiful cows and a fine ox!" When the woman tried to touch the animals, the farmer's wife said: "Watch out, that cow kicks." The next day the ox lay dead. The other cows were ill, except for the one cow the witch had not dared to touch. The chickens and pigs died. The farmer's wife went to a witch doctor, who made the witch's face appear in a mirror and said to the farmer's wife: "You must raise the floor of your cowshed. You needn't be afraid, for your cows will run up against the wall." The cows became skin and bone. After that the witch never came to that farm again.
202311: A woman walking home through the woods saw a big dog that walked beside her the whole time. When the woman made the sign of the cross, the dog suddenly vanished. It must have been the devil.
202330: In the old days people often told of those who had been ridden by the moon.
202337: A family had a child who was ill and cried all the time. The doctor said: "I can do nothing about this illness. The rural policeman's children had it too, and they recovered." They had prayers read over the child by two little old men from Wilrijk. Afterwards the people had to make sure they were home again before sunset. The child was cured. The two old men had asked the mother whether she had given anything to anyone, whereupon the mother remembered that she had given someone a basket of potatoes for free. That was how the child had become bewitched. When the child was two years old, its father gave it some money to buy sweets. In the sweet shop the witch put a stockfish in the child's basket. The child had also been given a biscuit, which it had already bitten into. The mother threw the stockfish away, but the boy fell ill and afterwards always cried after sunset. Over time the crying lasted longer. In the end the little boy could no longer walk and was thrown up into the air in his bed. The mother went to tell the parish priest what was going on, but the clergyman did not take her seriously and would not help. So the mother and father went to Wilrijk. There the father, although he was a strong fellow, had the greatest difficulty lifting his child out of the cart. In Wilrijk they were told: "It has gone too far. It's already in his little belly." Then the parents went to the fathers of Bornem. After they had been taken across the Scheldt by boat, they had to ask the way three times in a café. They sweated terribly while doing so. A father said: "I will give the boy a special blessing, so that nothing more can happen to him." The mother did not dare go back the same way. On the train the child cried terribly. When the parents got home, their child was cured. A father from Bornem had offered to show the culprit in a mirror, but they did not want that, because the child's father would have become very angry with that person.
202345: Whoever was in the company of a man who could turn himself into a werewolf saw the man disappear behind the hedge and reappear a moment later in the shape of a wolf. A boy who had had to carry the werewolf died three days later.
202364: One night at twelve o'clock a woman heard bells ringing in the marsh near the Postel woods.
202392: A woman who was ironing was visited by a witch. A little later the woman got backache. The pain was so bad that she could no longer hold her iron.
202442: On a farm worked a maid who never slept in her bed. In the evenings a magpie sat in a tree making a strange noise, as if it were laughing at someone. The farmer grew tired of it and aimed his gun at the magpie. He tried to shoot, but the gun did not work. He tried twice more, in vain. Then the man dipped his gun in blessed salt. When he fired again, the magpie fell dead to the ground. The next day the maid lay dead in front of the door of the washhouse.
202443: When Feel S. was on his way to church, he saw a hare running near H. The man then hurried home to fetch his gun. On his return he heard the hare say: "Now I've got you, now you've missed Mass!"
202494: In Sint-Lenaarts the crows are said to have taken the bells out of the church. The crows wanted to carry the bells away, but because they were too heavy, the birds threw the bells into the Klokkeven.
202527: On a farm they always had bad luck. Many animals died. When the farmer wanted to go to bed, he took the stairs to his room. But he fell asleep on the stairs, because he could not get any higher. When he had bought a horse one day, he met a suspicious woman who said: "Oh, what a fine horse." After that the horse grew very thin. The farmer went to the Poor Clares in Lier, who took away the evil.
202537: A man who was ploughing suddenly saw crows settling in a nearby wood. The man went home, left his ox there and set out for the wood with his gun to shoot some crows. The man shot at a tree full of crows, but could not hit a single bird. Strangely, after that the man could no longer reload his gun.
202540: Many stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were often seen in the churchyard. People said that such lights were the little souls of unbaptised children.
202578: Some soldiers had lost their war chest at a farm. The farmer had hidden the chest under a load of dung. Because they had lost the money, the soldiers were killed. From then on a wagon with glowing horses and a driver rode through the cowshed every night. Perhaps these were the dead soldiers wanting revenge.
202581: A farmer from Gelderland coming back from the market was walking across the heath with his little money case. A little further on the farmer found that he had lost his money, and he immediately turned back. On the heath the farmer asked a shepherd whether he had seen his money. Although the shepherd denied it, the farmer said: "It can't have been anyone else, for we are the only people here on the heath". Then the shepherd swore that he would burn if he was lying. The next moment the shepherd burst into flames. Afterwards the shepherd still wandered the heath as a shade.
202599: A man was boasting to his friend about his horses. The man said his horse was so strong it could pull five hundred kilos. The friend replied that his horse could manage a thousand kilos. The man responded: "Your horse can't do that. It can't even pull five hundred kilos". The friend harnessed his horse and put a load of five hundred kilos on the cart. The horse began to sweat terribly and could not move a step forward. The man had bewitched the horse so that it could not move forward.
202629: A man who went on a pilgrimage to Strombeek for his child came to the little chapel where the pump stood. There he had to give one of his child's little shirts to the children standing there. The children laid the shirt in the water with a stick. Part of the shirt sank into the water, but the sleeves stayed afloat. The children looked at each other but said nothing. Three weeks later the sick child was dead. The child had fallen ill because of a witch who often visited those people. The fathers had given the people a holy object so that the witch could no longer come in. But one day they had invited the witch with the words: "Do come in," so that she could get in after all. They should not have done that.
202633: In a poacher's house a hare was seen coming in every day at about the same time. The poacher shot at the hare, but the animal did not move and ran away. The next day the hare was sitting there again.
202656: After a woman had been at a farm, all the cows broke loose at night and the chains flew up against the ceiling.
202677: In the old days there was a castle in the woods in Brasschaat. Later a light was always seen near that castle. That was the ghost of the maid who had died.
202680: When a child somewhere was dying, a man was visited by a woman who asked him to go with her to the priest. The man went along and stayed at the church gate while the woman went inside. As he stood there, he saw large cats lying across the street, at least four or five kilos in weight, with eyes like marbles. The moment the woman left the presbytery, the cats had vanished. When the two got back, the child was dead.
202693: Will-o'-the-wisps or stallichten were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised. When you saw a will-o'-the-wisp, you had to say: "If you are of God, 'wekt' (give way?). If you are of the devil, be gone."
202704: In a house a spider's web hung above the bed every day. It was removed, but shortly afterwards it was back. The little child there cried every night at about the same time. The people went to the fathers of Bornem, who gave them a relic so that the witch could no longer get in. Someone would come and lean against the door and say she was tired, but that woman must not be let in. The next day the child's mother saw her mother-in-law standing at the door.
202713: Roos went to visit a sick old woman who could no longer get out of bed. The woman's medicines stood on a small table. Every time Roos had been outside for a moment, she found the medicines on the floor, even though the sick woman could not get out of bed. When the old woman was dead, a big cat with glowing eyes sat on the bed. Nobody managed to hit the cat with a cudgel.
202718: Some people who had been to a café after a baby's baptism were walking home along a lane. Suddenly they saw a black cat sitting on the road. The child's godfather, who feared nothing, shouted: "Go on, get away, stupid beast!" When the cat stayed put, he went over and kicked it so that it flew across the road into the bushes. When he got home the man was ill and deathly pale. Over the following days his condition grew worse. The people thought of the black cat and sent for the priest, who spoke all kinds of exorcisms. A few days later the man was cured.
202722: Some people were telling stories in an inn when suddenly a billy goat came in dancing on its hind legs, although all the doors were shut. It was the innkeeper's billy goat. These events were the work of a witch.
202751: Some friends coming back from Rielen looked back along the way and, to their great fright, saw a white figure standing at the edge of the Rielenkot (1). When the men came closer, they saw that the figure was floating over the water. On reaching the other bank the ghost vanished.
202756: When people heard cats meowing in the evening, they did not dare go home. The witches sent the cats out.
202779: A mother believed that her neighbour was a witch. The parish priest told her that if she believed that, she should move. So this mother moved house four times with her family. The mother had five boys, who all died young. The woman's daughter was also always ill. The mother was convinced that the witch was behind it.
202792: It was said that the lights floating above marshes were the little souls of unbaptised children.
202818: In a cowshed a noise was heard every night as if a whole army of rats had broken loose. The following week they could no longer churn butter on that farm. They went to the brown fathers. After the reading of the Gospel of Saint John, the kwade hand (evil hand, a curse) was driven from the farm.
202834: At night in the churchyard Jan zonder Vrees (Jan without Fear) always saw two dead men rise from their graves to fight each other. Fearlessly Jan shot the ghosts dead, so that they lay down in their graves again.
202883: A man could make mice appear by striking a beam with a stick.
202939: At Charel's they could not make butter because a woman always came to fetch sourdough. When Charel one day put a holy object under the door, the woman could no longer get in. From then on they managed to make butter again.
202942: A man coming back late in the evening with his cart from the Diepevoort met a witte madam (white lady), who asked if she could ride along with him. The man refused, but a bit further on he was confronted with the apparition again. When the man struck at the witte madam with his whip, he heard her say: "I'll get you, little man". Then the horse took fright, and the man lost his little finger, around which he had wrapped the reins.
202976: In the old days people did not dare to go to the churchyard with a dead unbaptised child. That had to do with stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps).
202985: A woman had a sick child who wore a scapular. When the scapular was washed, it was hung behind the house to dry. The next morning the scapular had always disappeared. One day a woman came in, looked at the child and said: "Oh, that little man is getting big." A few days later the child was dead.
203025: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come back to haunt after his death. The ghost walked around with a post under its arm and called: "Where shall I go with it?" One day a drunkard answered: "Put it where you got it". When the ghost had put the post back, it appeared no more.
