203034: A girl whose mother was a witch went to mass. She left her umbrella in a man's house but forgot to collect it. Every evening that umbrella danced in the corner of the room, so that the people were frightened. In the end the girl did come to fetch her umbrella.
203068: In Breendonk lived a woman suspected of being a witch. When she had not been seen for a while, a black cat was found in the stone well. The next day the witch was back in her house.
203070: Some men who always had to pass the churchyard claimed that the spirit of a dead man who had crawled out of his coffin sat on the churchyard wall. The police commissioner went fearlessly to the churchyard and struck the spirit to the ground with his walking stick. After that the spirit was never seen again.
203082: On a farm a cow died after a witch had visited. Within one year those people lost three cows and a number of pigs. After they had called in the parish priest, the evil came to an end. If a witch found no other victims, she had to bewitch her own child.
203083: A boy fell ill after accepting a biscuit from someone. The fathers of Lier helped the boy.
203106: One evening, on the dike between the castle and the first house by the lock, the lock keeper of Heindonk had seen a large object lying. A moment later the object flew up into the air and disappeared. The lock keeper then ran away in fear.
203127: A woman who had had a baby was unwell and lay in bed for a month. When the woman's husband was working in the field with a friend, the men saw a witch walking towards the house. The friend said: "Now X is going to your wife, so she won't live much longer." A few days later the woman died, and her husband was stabbed to death at the fair.
203133: A sorceress brought a dummy for a child. After that the child began to cry. The mother put the child to bed and went to the white fathers in Dendermonde, who gave her little roses to put under the threshold and hang above the door. Once a woman walked behind the sorceress and crossed her footprints. The sorceress stepped aside and let the woman pass without saying a word. Another woman, who did not know that a sorceress was living near her, took the nappies off the washing line in the evening after sunset. After that this woman's child began to cry, and a black cat came and sat at the back of the cradle. If anyone grabbed at the cat, the animal vanished. A father came to the house and said prayers until the drops of sweat rolled off his body.
203150: Some farmers from the Watervoort saw a large magpie sitting in a tree in Poederlee. They threw a stick at it, which got stuck in a tree. The farmers continued on their way to the Netherlands, where they came to a small farm where an old woman sat tending the fire. The farmer suddenly saw the stick he had thrown at the magpie standing in a corner there. Then the old woman said: "At Poederlee in the Kalekiek they threw a stick and I lost an eye."
203188: The 'heksenjacht' (witches' hunt) were witches who flew through the air on a broomstick.
203194: A man coming home late in the evening kicked at a black cat that was walking ahead of him on the road. The next day he saw his neighbour woman with a cloth around her head.
203208: Two men who were caught up in an argument kept swearing. When the men reached the start of a lane, they saw lids of cooking pots falling from the trees. The lids swirled around the legs of one of the men. The other man quickly made himself scarce.
203241: A man was returning from the fair at Balen with a friend. When the man said: "I'm going this way," the friend said: "Then you won't be the first one home." The man got lost and only reached his house in the morning. That friend could work magic.
203256: In the past people were afraid of cats that followed them, because they believed they were witches.
203265: Some people going to the fair together saw a cat by the side of the road. A man tried to catch the little cat, but the animal arched its back and scratched him.
203292: A man coming home late one Sunday evening saw a white young lady walking back and forth on the road the whole time.
203300: A sick girl was always visited by a witch who brought her a bunch of grapes. One day they did not give the grapes to the child but threw them under the cow. The next day the cow lay dead.
203306: A woman always saw a ghost sitting there when she was milking the cows in the stable. The parish priest asked the woman whether she had ever promised anything, and the woman remembered that she had promised to go to the chapel of Emblem. The woman took the ghost on her back and carried it to the chapel. There the ghost suddenly vanished.
203316: A farmhand worked on a farm near 't Duifhuis. Strange things happened on that farm. In the morning the cows stood the wrong way round in the stable, or two cows stood with their heads in one halter. At night there was noise on the barn roof, as if a pile of bean poles were rolling off it. In the house there was rattling, as if chairs were being thrown about. Only the farmhands heard the noise. When they went to look, everything was back in its original place. Horses were always jumping back and forth over the well in which the fodder was washed. A hell wagon also often drove over the barn roof. In the end the people went to the friars. After a friar had put an iron cross on the barn roof, the strange happenings came to an end. When the cross blew away in a storm, the haunting started again. The parish priest had to come to put the cross back on the roof.
203352: In Vremde lived a woman who had six or seven sons. Strangely enough, not one of those boys had to go into the army. People believed that the witch had a means of making sure her children were lucky in the draft lottery.
203367: People did not dare to go past the 'drie Benetten' because all kinds of ghostly apparitions could be seen there. Tied-up dogs lay on the verge of the road. Sometimes there was also a white cow. People always saw something walking beside or around them.
203371: Because people wanted to recognise the witches in church, one Sunday during Mass they placed relics at the church exit. When Mass was over, there were a few women who could not go outside. They were the witches.
203385: One evening in Geel a woman saw a big black dog. Then she saw a big black cat that would not be chased away. That cat was a café landlady who was a witch.
203397: The fathers of Dendermonde could lift the kwade hand (evil hand, a curse) by reading prayers. A woman who had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, a curse) went to the fathers. They foretold that on her way she would meet an old woman on a little bridge, to whom she must not speak. The woman followed this advice and was freed from the misfortune.
203420: A woman who had spiteful little eyes and wore a cap was suspected of being a witch. A man who had bought a heifer from this witch had nothing but trouble with the animal and had the witch come to him. The witch said to the cow: "Come on, get up," and the animal got up at once.
203427: Gust E. lived with a farmer who was married to a witch. One day Gust and the farmer were threshing together when the farmer struck a cat on its front legs. At lunchtime the men found that the farmer's wife was lying in bed with a broken arm.
203435: Two girls had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what the afterlife was like. A few years later one of the girls died. Shortly afterwards the spirit of the dead girl stood silently by the other girl's bed. The next day the other girl, frightened, went to the priest, who advised her to ask the ghost next time what it wanted. When the girl did so the next evening, the spirit answered: "Strictly reckoned, little forgiven!" Then the spirit vanished for good.
203492: A man from Berendrecht was coming back from drawing school in Ekeren around half past seven one Saturday evening and had briefly visited a friend, when he got lost near the Binnenpad. In the Stoofstraat the man knocked at a door to ask the way. By the time those people had set him on the right road, it was already eleven o'clock. The man was worried because the Germans had imposed a curfew. After that incident the man never again visited his friend in the evening.
203499: A man who was coming back from the village through the woods one evening cursed the whole time. Suddenly the man felt a devil in the shape of a cat jump onto his neck. The man had to carry the cat, which grew heavier and heavier, until he got home. The next day a thatcher was working on the man's roof. When it suddenly began to rain, the thatcher came down and the whole company stood cursing in the barn. A little later an oak beam of fifty centimetres broke in two, so that the whole hay loft came down.
203511: Three women, one of whom was a witch, went to 't Stokt. Although the witch was already eighty-four, she leapt over the brook like a cat, while the two young women could not get across.
203526: The stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) that were seen in churchyards in the evening and at night were little souls coming out of their graves.
203533: In a house horses could always be heard walking around. In the attic and around the house creaking was heard. Under the mutsaard (bundle of brushwood) twenty cats could be heard singing, although only one could be seen. One day a man shot at the animals with his gun, but then nothing more was to be seen.
203539: On a rainy weekday an old woman knocked at a house. The daughter opened the door and heard the visitor say: "Haven't you got a piece of ham for me? I feel so weak." The daughter replied: "No, the men will be back from the fields soon and they will make good use of the ham." The next moment the woman had vanished without a trace. The next day the visitor appeared again, but only the women could see her. The men did not see her. The visitor was spotted in the room above the cellar, where she was making the bed. As soon as the visitor had seen the farmer's wife's face, she vanished. She always wore black clothes. When the farmer's wife went to bring the animals water on another day, the little black woman was standing there again, leaning against a post. "You filthy redhead," cried the farmer's wife, and the little woman vanished. The women on that farm went about in constant fear because they met the little black woman everywhere. One day the horse was stiff and the cows lay exhausted on the ground. The farmer could not understand it. By doing a novena those people managed to drive the little black woman away. When one day they had forgotten to pray, the little woman was back. Holy objects were also placed under the threshold to keep the little woman out.
203577: On his way home a man always saw a white ghost come out of the roadside verge. The man struck at the ghost with his walking stick, after which it stayed lying there.
203594: One morning a man had to drive his cart to the market in Antwerp. On the way the man gave someone a ride. When the man wanted to come back, he got lost. He wandered about the whole night. The next morning he saw a farm, where he went to ask the way to his house.
203636: It was haunted between Westerlo and Blauberg. A light appeared with a head like a cow's. A man who did not believe the stories about this light went to have a look at one o'clock at night. The man had barely said "There's nothing to see, that's just rubbish" when the light appeared. The man wet his trousers with fright.
203643: On a farm in Tielen four or five cats were seen in the stable in the evening when someone wanted to milk the cow. When people got up in the morning, they found the cows tied by their tails to the rack. There was much misfortune there.
203673: On a farm the farmer's wife sat alone by the radio one evening, listening to the election results. Her husband was walking about because he had a sow that was due to farrow. At a certain moment a suspicious woman came in, who also came to listen to the radio. Suddenly the two women heard piglets squealing in the sty. The visitor jumped up saying: "I must see that!" and rushed into the sty. Three days later all the piglets were dead.
203676: A man coming back from Retie in the dark met a procession of five or six men on the road, as if someone were getting married or moving house. The men in the procession said not a word. The man walking in front was much taller than the others.
203682: A man always saw a hare sitting in his clover field. One day the man tried to shoot the animal. At first he could not, but when he had put salt on his gun, the shot hit. A moment later the hare had vanished, and in the same spot stood a woman with a gunshot wound in her arm.
203686: There was haunting at the Mostaardpothoeve, at the Schaliehoeve, at the Krankehoeve, at the Turfputten, but above all at the Tongsken and at the Moermanshoeve. Every night a glowing hellewagen (hell's wagon) with glowing horses with burning manes rode noisily over the roof of the Moermanshoeve. The former occupants of the Moermanshoeve had once stolen a war chest from soldiers who were lodging with them. The thief had filled the war chest with stones, so that the soldiers starved to death. At night those dead soldiers came looking for the missing money. Because the haunting at the Moermanshoeve was so bad, the bishop had to come and exorcise the place; the priest did not have enough power for it.
203687: A headless horse roamed the Binneberg. When S. saw the horse, he ran away in fear.
203688: A farmer from Tielen was coming home in the evening by way of Opstal. When the farmer had to cross a bridge, he saw a cat sitting on the railing there. He struck at the cat, but could not hit it. A little later the cat had disappeared. When the man wanted to continue on his way, he got lost. He wandered about until the next morning. The whole time he felt as if he was wading through water. In the morning he was standing in Grobbendonk.
203713: On the Binneberg every night at midnight a man appeared with a stick on his back, who had to come back to haunt as a punishment.
203769: On his way home a man kicked at a cat. The next moment the cat had vanished and a woman was sitting in that same spot. The man had to appear before the judge, but was not punished.
203798: A man who had to go home in the dark carried a stable lantern. In the light of the lantern the man saw some dogs walking, tied to each other with a cord. When the man was home, he went outside again a little later to see where the dogs were. But the animals had vanished.
203808: A man who had died came back after his death. When the ghost was asked: "And what is it like over there?" it answered: "Everything is strictly reckoned and nothing is forgiven". Then the ghost disappeared again.
203818: Stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were little souls from purgatory who came to ask for a Mass or a prayer. The lights appeared mainly above marshes and fens. Some people believed they were glow-worms.
203821: A farmer had a field full of grain, but his barn was not big enough to store all that grain. While the farmer stood lamenting, a gentleman dressed in black appeared and said: "There will be a barn if you give your best pledge." The farmer agreed and told his wife what he had done. At night the farmer could not get to bed and so went to sit on a boundary post. At a certain moment he heard rattling and rumbling. The devils appeared and pulled the trees out of the ground with their roots. The noise went on all night. When the cock crowed, one of the devils clapped his hands, after which all the devils jumped through a hole in the floor of the barn and went back to hell. That hole in the floor could never be closed. The barn is said to stand near Leuven and to have been converted into a kind of small factory.
203826: A girl was home alone on a Sunday evening. While she was milking the cow, she suddenly saw something being written on the wall with a dung fork, giving off sparks. When a little later she also heard banging in the hayloft, she ran away in fear. These strange events went on for three nights. Then they stopped.
203849:
On a farm a cow died every week for six weeks. The farmer believed he was dealing with the evil hand and went to Bornem. Afterwards the whole stable was dug out and incense was burned there. After that the situation improved.
A woman had also died who used to come for buttermilk every week. In Bornem the farmer had seen that woman's face appear in a book. He was given a prayer and a holy object to take home and lay under the door. The fathers also advised him not to refuse that particular woman buttermilk. But she could no longer get in because of the holy object. She opened the door a little way and asked whether the buttermilk was ready yet. The farmer's wife lied and said: "No."
When the farmer came home one night, the witch was standing by the stable. The farmer struck with his stick but could not hit the witch. When the witch lay dying, her two black dogs sat with her on the bed. Her death throes were long and painful. The dogs had to be killed before the witch could die.
203851: A woman had a child that was bewitched. When the girl lay in her bed, she always cried: "Mother, please chase away that black woman by my bed."
203858: Three friends coming back from the village were followed by a meowing cat. One of the men said to the animal: "Minneke puss, minneke cat, where are you?" But the cat kept meowing the whole time and after a while said itself: "Minneke puss, minneke cat, where are you?" After accompanying the three men for an hour, the cat disappeared.
203860: In a barn in Olmen people had seen Lucifer sitting. To little Louis they would then say: "Don't you see Lucifer sitting there with his grey mug?"
203862: On a farm first the son and then the mother fell ill. The children there lay tossing and flew up in their beds. The witchcraft always began at the same time. A witch could only be hit by shooting with a gun loaded with blessed shot.
203872: A man from Lille went to visit his parents, who lived in the Arendonks Hoekske. On the way he met a gentleman and a lady, who invited him to a table laden with all kinds of delicacies. At first the man did not want to eat with them, but in the end he gave in. When he said "In God's name", the whole scene suddenly vanished.
203906: A cat could turn itself into a witch. A cat that jumped on a passer-by's neck in the evening was a witch who meant harm.
203922: In Vorselaar lived a woman who saw her dead little child appear. When the woman had washed the child, she could still smell the soap for hours.
203924: A man drove to the factory for his father to fetch swill (1). On his way back, while he was talking to a friend, he saw two old women approaching with baskets under their arms. The women cried: "Oh men, go home quickly, for the world is going to end. On the Ruggeveld we have just seen a glowing ball with a black cross!"
203938: A gamekeeper had shot a hare in the leg but could not find the animal. In the evening people in the village were saying that a certain woman had a gunshot wound in her leg.
203949: A farmer whose farm was bewitched found maggots in the hens' eggs. One evening, when the farmer had sat down on the toilet with his gun, a large dog with a very long tail suddenly stood beside him. A moment later the dog had vanished. The farmer eventually moved away.
203956: Some people on their way to the theatre saw a little clay house on the way. In front of that house was a wood. A dog came running out of the wood and walked with the people to the theatre. Afterwards it followed the people to their home. A man had tried several times to throw something at the dog, but he could not hit the animal.
203962: A small statue of Mary is said to have been found long ago in the Wijngaardbos in Veerle. People wanted to take it to Averbode on a horse cart. At a certain spot the horses suddenly refused to go on. The horses would not go right and went left. The statue of Mary was then placed in the church and dressed in costly robes.
203967: A man who drank a lot always had to pass a small dung pit on his way home in the evening. However, the man never managed to get past it and fell into the dung pit. He then had the feeling that someone was pulling his arm and dragging him into the pit. Many people said that the man was the victim of his own wife's sorcery.
203991: Two men who had gone to cut litter were walking home in the evening. Suddenly they saw something standing on the road ahead of them. The men came closer and called out: "You must let us pass", but then they heard a terrible caterwauling. The thing in front of them flew up into the air and vanished. The men were convinced it was something beyond the forces of nature.
203994: A child had fallen ill after an old woman had dropped a pin on it.
203997: A man who had two pigs was afraid of a witch. So he laid beams over the pigsty so that the witch could not get at the animals. Yet once the witch managed to touch the animals. After that the animals could not be fattened, no matter how much feed they were given.
204012: Fons V.S. went ferreting with his dog at a place close to the house of the witch Schoon Marieke. When Fons saw a ferret running, he sent his dog after it. The ferret ran off and the dog came back frightened with its tail between its legs. Two days later the same thing happened. On the way home Fons met Schoon Marieke, who stood in the middle of the street and said: "You can't catch that ferret anyway!" Fons no longer went hunting, because that ferret was the witch herself.
204053: A witch often sat spinning in the moonlight. When her husband wanted to go to church, she forbade him, but he went anyway. The witch said, however: "You won't get far." When the man wanted to enter the church, he suddenly fell down dead.
204056: The girls of the congregation always went to the little chapel in the month of May. One evening they saw a figure made of stars there and ran away in fear. Eight days later the figure stood there again. Everyone ran away except one girl who could not run and fell. Later that girl was found dead.
204078: On a farm where the stable had been bolted in the evening, people suddenly heard the bolts of the stable door opening during the night. They were so frightened that they did not dare get out of bed. When they went to look in the morning, they found that all the cows had been milked and that the door was bolted.
204122: A headless figure appeared near the big barn.
204133: From a farm where all the animals were dying, people went to the fathers of Tongerlo, who gave them holy objects. The fathers also told the farmer: "When you go home, you will meet someone you know, but you must not answer if she asks anything." On the way the farmer met a woman who asked twice: "Where have you been so early?" The farmer did not answer, and the woman said: "Is this my thanks for all I have done for you?" After that the woman never came to the farm again.
204165: Anyone walking behind a supposed witch had to step in her footprints. The witch would then look back.
204209: A man went for a drink at a witch who ran a café. On his way home the witch patted him on the shoulder and said: "Little cooper, make sure you get home safely". The man had to cross a long meadow to get home. Although he knew that meadow well, he could not get out of it. Every time he ended up in front of a big ditch. He wandered about all night and only found the way in the morning.
204234: A girl was given eighteen fine apples by a sorceress. The next day the girl fell ill. The doctor could not help her. After lying sick in bed for eighteen days, the girl died.
204261: A man walking home one evening had his smock slung over himself. When the man got home, he found he had lost his smock. He went back to look and found his smock in front of a witch's house.
204267: The soldiers were always kept company by a girl. One day the girl stopped coming, but every night a black cat came and sat with the lads. One night the soldiers struck at the cat with a sabre. The next day the girl had a wound on her face.
204298: Some people were standing in the street with a small child. When a sorceress passed by, the child began to cry. The child cried all day.
204313: On a farm in Goor (Kasterlee) a lot of noise was always heard in the cowshed. The child who drank the cows' milk became disabled. After the parish priest had come to read prayers over the place, everything returned to normal and the child was cured too.
204318: A man who had given a cat a beating one evening met a neighbour woman with a broken arm the next day.
204345: In a little house lived an ugly old woman who only came outside when there were children nearby. People said she did that to bewitch those children. The woman chased the children with a broom.
204380: In Oorderen a little kitten that was in reality a witch always came by. When the farmer wanted to hit the cat with an axe, the cat said: "Oh, that's nasty, stroke me instead" and then ran away.
204386: When it was high tide at midnight, sunken bells could be heard ringing in the Heksenboske. They were said to be bells from a monastery of friars that stood at 't Schranske.
204398: A sick woman always saw a hand coming towards her, which stroked her. The woman died. Then the son became gravely ill. The father went to the fathers at the Ossenmarkt in Antwerp. One of the fathers told him: "I will give you a holy object, but it will no longer help. Drive out of your house a woman who will make you all die. Hide the holy object and do not say 'come in'. And accept nothing more from that woman." The woman always brought sweets and other things. When the father got home, his son was already dead. The culprit was an aunt of the father. That witch never set foot in the house again. When she came once more, she said: "It is better outside than inside," and she stroked a young goat that stood there. By that afternoon the goat was dead. After that the woman was not seen again.
204406: In the old days people were afraid when they saw cats. A man coming home in the evening with his father saw a cat sitting on his shoulder. Cats were also meowing in the trees.
204415: A pigeon fancier released his pigeons for a race. A witch, however, made the pigeons come back.
204420: A farmer whose stable had been struck by the evil hand went to the fathers of Dendermonde to fetch holy objects. After that the farmer never had any problems in his stable again.
204427: A woman went to tend her goats in the meadow by the convent gate. Suddenly the woman saw an elegant lady walk through the closed gate. The lady came right up to her and then went back.
204465: In Meerhout lived a sixteen-year-old girl who had been bewitched for eight years. When the girl was eleven, the parish priest came to read prayers over her and her family did a novena for her. They would have done better to visit a man from Testelt who could make witches appear in a mirror.
204574: On a farm in Wechelderzande a witch threw bunches of grapes under the cow. Afterwards the animal died. The farmer's wife died as well.
204601: People used to tell of a sorceress who could put two cows with their heads in one 'kennef' (1).
204609: A man who had beckoned to a light heard a thud on the door a little later. The next day a small child's hand was imprinted in the door. The light had been the soul of an unbaptised child.
204625: In Zemstlaar lived a farmer whose stable a cat always came into. Afterwards a cow died in that stable. One day the farmer had had enough of it and struck the cat. Afterwards a man in the neighbourhood was walking around with a bandage around his arm.
204668: A witch lived in Westmeerbeek. If you crossed her footprints, she looked back. The witch's son and daughter always went to play cards at their mother's. One day the whole family went to Hulshout, except the daughter, who went to visit her mother that day. When the family returned, the witch was dead. People believed she had wanted to be alone with her daughter to pass her magic power on to the girl.
204679: A woman was visited by a peddler woman selling cloth for a made-to-measure suit. The peddler could get no further than the threshold because a holy object hung above the door. Then the peddler went to that woman's sister. The sister gave money and ham, although she had not wanted to pay nearly so much. She did not know how the witch had managed to make her give so much.
204692: A farmer driving home with his horse and cart met a little woman on the way who wanted a ride. After a while the woman said she saw a light approaching, whereupon the farmer said: "Let it come to me; I baptise everything." Then the farmer took water and threw it all around the cart. Because the farmer was then overwhelmed by countless will-o'-the-wisps, he had to send for the dean. He told the farmer: "You must not baptise everything; you must say 'I baptise you' and baptise only one."
204744: A four-year-old child living in Deurne-Noord was one day taken by the arm by a little old woman from the neighbourhood. Afterwards the girl got a nervous illness, followed by smallpox and a worm infection. Because the girl had grown very thin, the doctor said the child needed building up. The dean came to the house and advised the mother to do a novena. After that the child became healthy. The dean came once more and said: "Mother, it was in your house, but now it is out." After that incident the people moved away as quickly as possible.
204759: In a house, everything that had stood on the mantelpiece lay on the floor in the morning. These strange events only stopped when they managed to keep a certain woman out. That woman could not bear that everything in that house was so tidy and clean.
204766: When there was a fair in Kalfort, the priest came through the village with the last sacraments. Everyone knelt respectfully. At one point a drunkard jumped in front of the priest, making a lot of noise. The priest ordered the drunkard to kneel, but he refused. Then the priest said: "You will stay standing on this spot until I come back". When the priest came back, the drunkard was indeed still standing there. He had not been able to move a foot. The priest said: "Now go on", and the drunkard could move on. Afterwards, however, the drunk man was ill for a long time, probably from fear. The altar boy who had seen everything told everyone about the priest's power.
204773: A man said: "Just let a witch come to me; then she's done for!" When that man rode home, cats jumped all over his legs, so that he could not go on.
204775: A man was crossing a meadow to fetch the midwife for his pregnant wife. In the meadow he saw a leaf moving although there was no wind. The man was afraid and went back home. In the evening he tried again, accompanied by a friend. At the same spot the two men saw something like frogspawn. Only when they began reciting the Gospel of Saint John could they go on. At the street corner the two heard a pack of cats meowing. A little further on a girl sat in a window meowing like the cats.
204777: A man coming home in the evening felt his hat fly off. The hat fell into a hedge. When the man went looking for it, he found at least ten hats, but his own was not among them. Terrified, the man ran away.
204792: A woman from Herselt was always dressed in black and burned candles. Whenever someone was ill somewhere, people believed that this witch had made the person ill.
204795: A man was walking behind a woman suspected of being a witch. The man walked in the suspected woman's footsteps. A little later she could go no further and looked back. The man then ran away in fear.
204813: A poor woman went to a farm every day to eat the leftover food. On that farm the daughters always got strange illnesses. The parish priest went to the farm and put something under the threshold, so that the poor woman could no longer get in.
204819: In a family in Eindhout two young cows died within a week. The people went to a fortune teller in Leuven, who said: "At this moment the witch is at your home." When the people got home and asked who had visited, they knew who the witch was.
204858: A farmhand coming back from the village one evening saw a white figure approaching. He believed it was the witte madam (white lady).
204880: In Itegem, a hundred metres from 't Schranske, there was a small wood called 'Heksenbos' (Witches' Wood) or 'Nonnekensbos' (Nuns' Wood). At night, nuns dressed in white sat in the trees with lanterns, holding a meeting. If people came closer, the whole scene disappeared. When they walked on again, the nuns were back.
204886: A sorcerer was driving his cart past the house of a witch. The witch stood in the doorway and looked at the man. Then the man fell off his cart and was run over. "She was stronger than me," the man said afterwards.
204887: At night lights could sometimes be seen in the sky. It was said that those lights were ghosts.
204889: A ghost called out all the time: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I leave it?" One day someone answered: "Put it where you got it!" Since then the ghost has not been heard or seen again.
204895: A man from Poederlee lost two children on the same day through witchcraft.
204968: Two men went fishing one night. Suddenly the fishermen saw a little dog jump out of the water. The little dog choked one of the fishermen by the throat. His companion wanted to grab the dog, but he always missed it.
204972: A man who had to keep watch over a dead person with some acquaintances told of a house that was haunted. At midnight the roof tiles of the house flew up. The cows were untied and the furniture was thrown about.
204981: A man stood before the bridge in Gompel and could not get across. A black cat sat on the bridge. The man hit at the cat, but the animal always came back.
204987: Someone who had been ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit) saw ghosts in broad daylight.
205029: A woman struck at a cat sitting on her well. The next day a suspected woman lay in her bed.
205039: A man and a woman from Wolfsdonk who were waiting at night for the tram to go to the court in Turnhout were followed by a hen and a cockerel. The cockerel grew bigger and bigger and struck against the trees. The man kicked at the hen, but could not hit the animal. When the people went into an inn, the cockerel went in with them. In the end the people stayed the night there. The tram came, but they could not get on it. Because of this the two eventually had to go back home.
205041: In Walem the cradle of a bewitched child kept turning upside down. Eventually the child was taken to the fathers, who said: "It is a woman from the neighbourhood doing this to you. You must work against it, and then she will come by to bring something for the child." The people had barely got home when a neighbour woman was standing there with a net to hang over the cradle. They threw that neighbour out at once.
205045: A farmer from Wommelgem was taking his relatives home in a cart. When the farmer reached the village, he saw a shadow on the front of his farmhouse. It looked as if a cart was driving through the gate there. When the farmer himself drove in, sparks flew from the stones under the horses' hooves. The animals were also sweating terribly. All this was the work of a witch who lived nearby.
205065: A man coming home at night saw a woman float from one 'löze' (1) to another. That woman had no legs. She carried a basket of eggs.
205077: At a farm on the Locht (a hamlet of Brecht) people were playing cards. A woman had said: "I'd rather play with the devil than with you!" Then a big black dog came in and lay down under the table. They sent for the priest, who said to the dog: "You must play with me." To that the beast replied: "No, priest, I play with the mistress, but not with you!"
205092: On a farm a cow stood with its leg in a ring. Another cow stood mortally ill in the meadow. The farmer had to put down all his cows. He had become the victim of a witch.
205120: A dying man did not want the priest to give him the Last Sacraments. When the man was dead, a big black dog came running up, all ablaze.
205144: In Hoevenen a man saw a little piglet walking in the street. The piglet was put in a pen. The next day there was a stone lying in the pen.
205149: At a house in Zandvliet a cat always sat on the doorstep. People claimed that the cat was a toverheks (witch). A farmhand managed to shoot the cat in the paw. In Zandvliet lived an old woman who always wore a glove because something was wrong with her hand. People claimed that this old woman was a toverheks (witch).
205155: A woman from Poederlee claimed that the deceased J. stood naked at night with a white sheet in the furrow of the cornfield.
205161: A woman had bought beans from a woman selling them from Millegem. Afterwards the woman's pig went mad, so that it had to be got rid of. Then the woman's husband fell ill. The man felt as if his throat was being squeezed shut. One evening the woman gave the pot of beans to a visitor to take away. The next morning, before early Mass, the witch was already at that person's door. The woman went to the fathers of Tongerlo, after which her husband recovered.
205165: One night a woman saw five or six men standing before her. The woman was terrified at the sight of those ghosts beside her bed.
205179: A witch was always reading books. Whenever a visitor arrived, she stopped at once. One day a woman went to visit that witch. When she left again, the witch knocked her down two or three times without getting up from her chair. Some time later the woman was planting potatoes in her field when she again fell victim to the witch's torments. The woman's legs became so swollen that she had to go to a healer. The woman had trouble with her legs ever after.
205185: A young man going to the fair in Wilmarsdonk at about twelve o'clock saw a light flickering in the grass. After the man had made the sign of the cross, the light had disappeared. Such lights were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
205192: Some men from Balen-Wezel went to check on the bees in Postel at night. Towards morning the men heard the haunting witheren (white canons, Norbertine monks) of Postel walking in their slippers in two rows between Balen-Wezel and the Blauwe Kei, singing. One of the witheren took a man's cap off. Another witheer gave the man his cap back. That night the man's hair had turned grey with fear.
205200: On a farm, the windows and doors flew open at midnight and a lot of noise was heard in the chimney. The people did not know what caused it.
205212: In the army a man was locked in prison. A little later the prison door opened and the man came out. The man could open the locked door by blowing through the keyhole.
205236: In a house where a child had been born, the parents knew that a witch lived nearby. So they took great care that no one could come near the cradle. A few days later the witch was inside after all. She had the child in her arms and was stroking it. The next day the child was dead.
205241: A farmer who could no longer make butter went on pilgrimage to Tongerlo to pray. On the way back, the woman responsible for the misfortune had to come and stand in the doorway; she could no longer stay inside.
205300: The mare (a nightmare spirit) came and lay on sleeping people. The sleepers then went stiff and could no longer move.
205315: A girl always saw a light floating near the woods. Her grandfather claimed that dwaaslichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of aborted innocent children.
205321: People who were ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit) while awake felt as if they were going to suffocate. They could not get out from under their blankets. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to place your clogs with the opening facing the bed.
205327: A family had a crying baby lying in a cradle. Strangely, the cradle was pulled up to the ceiling.
205343: A man going home on a winter evening suddenly saw a cat jump out of the bushes and walk along with him. When the man said: "Kitty, you'd better go and warm yourself", the animal disappeared. When the man came to the farm the next day, the cat was there too. He heard the animal say to the farmer's wife: "Mistress, your husband said I should come and warm myself!" Then the cat crept behind the stove.
205378: A woman from Mol could not sleep at night. She flew up and sat at the foot of her bed with her arms in the air. When people went to look in the attic, they found there was nothing to be seen. Someone advised her to put her clogs upside down in front of the bed in the evening to protect herself against the mare (a nightmare spirit).
205396: On a farm where no butter could be churned, a black mother always sat by the door.
205407: A girl of seven or eight months cried all the time. The mother took the child to the dean of Heist-op-den-Berg. Without the mother having said anything, the dean already knew why she had come. The mother had to go with him to the sacristy, where she was given something to put under the threshold. The dean said: "If she comes in, it is not true, but if she stays outside, she is the guilty one and she will stay outside." The mother then went home. She had not yet left the church when her baby stopped crying. When she got home and laid the child in the cradle, the witch came along at once. But she turned back and never visited there again. Before that the witch had always stroked the child and given it a biscuit. The witch's husband always said in the pub: "My wife is a sorceress."
205422: On a farm where the stables were plagued by the evil hand, all the horses stood back to front at the manger one morning. Moreover, they were tied to the manger by their tails. The horses' ears were also tied together.
205430: A man had magical power from reading books. He could make rats and mice appear. When the man went to confession at Easter, the priest said to him: "Next time, dig a big pit and put food for two days in it. Then drive the rats into that pit."
205458: In Vorst lived a disabled woman whose legs had been tied together with straws. After her death the woman came back.
205469: A woman who was bewitched went to the brown friars to have prayers read over her. The clergymen advised the woman to make a novena and said: "For nine days you must accept nothing from anyone, or it will not help." After all, by accepting something from someone, one could bring the evil hand into the house.
205488: In Ezaart there stood a cross in memory of two officers. When the road was being dug up at that spot, a light was seen floating there. Those were the spirits of the two officers.
205507: A man who often went to the churchyard saw a black hen there one night at Easter. The man claimed that it had been the devil. Beside the hen a ghost in a light-coloured robe could be seen.
205532: A woman walking home along the Vliet saw a witte madam (white lady) walking on the dike.
205568: In the old days people were afraid of black cats because they could be witches in animal form. If a witch had been in the cowshed, the cows could not calve until the witch had undone the harm she had caused.
205575: A man from Kessel sank up to his neck in water three times a day, although there was no water to be seen anywhere. The man set out at half past seven and only reached his house at five in the morning. He only had to walk half an hour, yet he could not reach his destination. He had been visiting a woman who had bewitched him.
205577: On the highway from Wolfsdonk to Herselt lived a farmer who had an orphan girl working for him. Whenever the farmer's wife wanted to go to church, she could no longer find her rosary and her prayer book, even though she had laid them out ready. A big tomcat was always seen in the farm's cellar. The people went to a clergyman, who advised them to send the orphan girl away. The people did so and were rid of their troubles.
205634: A woman from Wijnegem could no longer go on because of witchcraft. She had to stay standing where she stood.
205720: A poacher in Kasterlee shot at a rabbit in bad weather. He saw the animal roll over and shortly afterwards walked over to his catch. Where the rabbit had been running sat an old woman straightening her cap. She was a witch.
205743: In Wolf (a hamlet of Liezele) a farmer heard a voice in the evening from a dark wood, calling: "Posts moved, posts moved!" The farmer fled, but was chased by the spirit, which kept on calling. It was the spirit of someone who had lost a piece of land because the farmer had once moved a boundary post of his field.
205749: On the Blauberg lived a male witch who owned a little wax doll into which he stuck pins. Each time he did so, a child somewhere in the neighbourhood was in pain.
205765: A man was courting a girl from Geel. When the man went home in the evening, he always saw a cat following him. When the cat lay down flat on the ground at his feet, the man wanted to kick it, but the cat said: "If you dare..." The man kicked anyway and lost his clog. The man told his story to his girlfriend, who said she would go and fetch another clog. The girl brought back the man's bloodied clog. The girl's mother lay in bed with severe back pain.
205769: Two women coming back from Zammel one evening were followed by a strange light. The women ran home as fast as they could. When they looked back, they saw the light strike downwards.
205770: Gypsies often used to camp by the brook at Kruisbrug. The gypsies made wicker pincushions and sold them. One day a farmer who sold flour and bran was coming back from the field when the gypsies came up to him to buy bran. A pretty gypsy girl walked over to the farmer's horse and made signs of the cross on the animal's head and right haunch. A few hours later the horse fell ill. After two days the animal died in the meadow. A dealer bought the dead horse for a hundred francs. But when the horse was cut up, the right haunch turned out to be completely rotten, so the dealer got his money back. The farmer had a lot of bad luck after that. In the mornings his pigs lay dead in the sty. Whenever a calf was born, it always came three months early. The farmer sought advice from the friars and was freed from the evil. Because he was rich, the affair did not bankrupt him.
205772: A man who had to fetch a German shepherd in Corsendonk got lost on his way home after the dog had run off. The man had to go through ponds, ditches and marshes and could not find his bearings. When it was already two in the morning, the man walked to a house where a little light was burning. An old woman sat at a table on which a small oil lamp burned. Six black cats sat on the floor. The man asked the way to Arendonk, and the woman answered: "Just keep going straight on". But the man felt uneasy, and half an hour later he knocked at a farm. He was soaked in sweat from fear. Fortunately he was allowed to sleep in a bed in the attic there.
205815: A man who lived on the Meulenberg had filled his whole mill with sacks. There had been no wind for six or seven weeks, but one night a strong wind finally rose. A cat always came to the mill and reached under the door with its paw. Once the miller took his dung fork along and wounded the cat's paw. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had lost her fingers.
205840: One night Sus V.N. got lost because of a witch. Only at four in the morning did the man find his way again. For at that hour the witches no longer had any power.
205854: A farmer who heard a lot of noise in his stable went to look and found that a fattening calf kept trying to leap up against the wall. A big black cat was sitting in front of the calf.
205857: An old man came knocking at a farmer's house in Stelen. The man was looking for a priest because he wanted to confess. The farmer, who liked playing pranks, dressed up as a priest. Because it was evening, the old man did not see through the deception and confessed his sins. When the farmhands went to have a look in the barn where the old man was sleeping a while later, they saw a big black dog next to the man. The farmhands warned the farmer, who went into the barn to chase the dog away. A little later there was nothing and no one to be seen in the barn. The dog was the devil. The devil had dragged the farmer off to hell. The old man had disappeared too.
205879: A man from Bergen-op-Zoom who was a good skater was coming back from the auction one morning. He was skating with his hands behind his back and heard someone on the bank ask: "Going well?" The man answered: "Yes, a little longer and I'll be home." The onlooker replied: "But it will be a long time before you're home." The man went on skating that day until evening. He did not get home, because the onlooker had bewitched him.
205898: French soldiers had lost their war chest at the farm 't Slaapt in 't Stro in Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Waver. The farmer who lived there had hidden the chest under a dung heap. Because the soldiers did not find the money, they were punished. Some of them were even executed. Since then the farmer always had bad luck. After a while the farmer decided to confess his crime to the priest. The clergyman then said to the farmer: "Take a meuke (?) of wheat and count the grains. As many grains as you count, that many gold pieces you must pay back into the war chest. The rest of your money you must spend on good works." Because the farmer was greedy, he did not do what the priest had advised. One day the hellewagen (hell's wagon), driven by a woman, was seen riding around in the stable and on the roof of the farm. Every hundred years the hellewagen (hell's wagon) with its four glowing horses appeared again. Other frightening things also happened at 't Slaapt in 't Stro. When there was a storm, the wind howled and all the doors flew open. In the morning two dead cows were found in the stable with their heads in the same halter. The farmer and his wife were far too greedy to give away any of their money to make the haunting stop. "Better one soul lost than so many poor children," the farmer's wife always said. One day an old man was brought to the farm, who banished the hellewagen (hell's wagon) for ninety-nine years. In 1936 those ninety-nine years were over. The farmer who later came to live at the farm, however, never saw the hellewagen (hell's wagon) again. Perhaps that had something to do with the fact that a relative of the former occupants had become a priest.
205900: In Geel lived a witch who one day went along with some people on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. In Scherpenheuvel the witch suddenly vanished. But she had bewitched the women, for their hair stood straight up on their heads.
205920: When Trees D. saw a will-o'-the-wisp on the edge of the well one evening, she decided to baptise the light. A little later, however, so many lights appeared that Trees ran home in fear. Then a loud clap of thunder sounded. A blue hand was burnt into the door.
205950: A man always got socks from his aunt, who knitted them for him. One day the man was working in his pigeon loft when his aunt came by. The man was just holding his best pigeon. The aunt stroked the bird and said: "Oh, that is a lovely pigeon." The next day the pigeon lay dead in the loft.
205987: A woman went to the brown friars to have prayers read over her little child. The child had fallen ill after being touched by a woman peddler. The friar said: "I will read prayers over the child and you must make a novena. But the child will die all the same. If the mother is ill too, she should come once as well." On the ninth day the child died. The mother also went to have prayers read over her, and she did survive.
205997: In a house banging was always heard in the attic at midnight. When the man went upstairs to look, he got stuck to the attic door. Only ten minutes later could he free himself.
206020: On a farm two cats were often seen walking in front of the stables. When someone came outside, the cats sat down somewhere, but then the livestock pulled themselves loose and ran about the stables making a great deal of noise.
206051: When V.B. was going to Meerhout, he saw a cat sitting along the way. The man stamped at the cat, after which the animal moved over and said: "Stamp at me again!"
206069: On a bewitched farm there were cats on the roof at night. At night the cows stood two in one harness. When bacon was fried there, the meat simply jumped out of the pan. The calves were born too early and many cattle died. One day the parish priest brought a relic for those people and put it under the threshold of the farm. When he said: "Our Lord visits most often the people He loves most," the farmer's wife replied: "Well, then I'd rather be a bad friend of His for once."
206073: One of the ancestors of Fluppe S. had promised that his descendants would keep paying for the oil of the sanctuary lamp. But when Fluppe no longer wanted to pay for the oil, his house began to be haunted. At night the house began to shake, so that the pots and pans fell to the floor and all the paintings hung crooked. When Fluppe paid for the oil again, the haunting stopped.
206093: Near the Wimpehoeve it was always haunted. In the evening people often saw a group of white figures floating around the farm. The ghosts all carried a book, from which they sang unintelligible songs.
206114: In an inn in Schaffen some men sat playing cards. Suddenly a gentleman came in and stood beside the players. The man the gentleman stood beside was lucky in the game. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the strange gentleman had a horse's foot. One by one the frightened players went outside. The gentleman, however, would not leave the inn. When a priest came to drive out the devil, the gentleman said: "You have stolen something. That is why you have no power over me," to which the priest replied: "Yes, but I did penance for that theft long ago." After the priest had prayed for a long time, he saw the devil fly out through the window.
206150: A woman went to borrow a plough from a neighbour who had special powers. At night the workers went to plough the field. When the work was done, they put the plough in their barn and locked it. When the farmer's wife wanted to return the plough the next morning, it was no longer in the barn. She went to the wizard's house and saw the plough already standing in his barn. That wizard could get in anywhere without opening the door. He was known everywhere for his magic powers.
206153: Two lovers were coming back from the fair one evening. On the way the boy grew restless and said to his girlfriend: "I have to go away for a moment. If anyone should bother you, throw a handkerchief." When the girl had been standing alone for five minutes, she heard growling behind her. She turned around and was terrified to see a werewolf. The werewolf came closer and began leaping around menacingly. The girl threw her handkerchief, which the werewolf tore apart. A little later the boy was back and heard what had happened. When the lovers got home, the girl suddenly saw that her boyfriend had bits of her handkerchief between his teeth. The girl ran home crying and now knew that her boyfriend was a werewolf.
206162: A woman had lost her husband in a bombing. Afterwards the widow saw a tall grey man appear in her house. That was the ghost of her dead husband. Whenever the woman saw the ghost, she crawled under the blankets and began to pray. After the woman had visited her husband's grave, the ghost no longer appeared.
206163: Witches always tried to give children something in order to bring the evil hand upon them.
206174: Pol H. went to Tongerlo because his child was ill. The friars told Pol: "When you get home, the evil hand will be standing beside your child's bed." But because the witch already had too much power, the child died anyway.
206196: Some men hunting polecats had to take shelter because it had started to rain. When they went to collect the caught polecats at night, they met a cat that stretched itself out completely and stepped across the ditch that way. Then the animal rubbed against the legs of one of the men. He wanted to kick the cat, but was advised not to, because it was probably a witch. Shortly afterwards the rain stopped. On their way home the men met the same cat again.
206240: People who were ridden by the mare (a nightmare spirit) felt a heavy weight fall on them at night. They tried to call out, but no sound came.
206257: If someone was suspected of being a witch, you had to walk behind her and cross her footprints. She would then look back.
206280: A woman who lived in a house in Herenthout believed in witches. She said the mice came in at night through the cracks in the windows and ran over the bedstead.
206309: A farmer had often struck in vain at a black cat that always came and sat at the foot of his bed. When the farmer struck at the cat, he saw nothing but fire. The cat was the ghost of a dead woman to whom the farmer had promised to have masses said. But with the money he had been given, the farmer had still not had any masses said for the woman. After the farmer had kept his promise, the cat did not appear again.
206316: A man who came to collect alms turned out to be the devil.
206349: The Zammelsebrug over the Nete was bewitched. You could not get across that bridge because you always saw a cat running in front of your feet.
206365: Two witches lived in Achter-Olen. When one of those witches went into a cowshed, all the pregnant cows suddenly lost their calves.
206367: A small child who was always ill could not sleep at night and crawled under its little bed in fear. One evening, after the child had been put to bed, it was found the next day among the wagons in the cellar of the brewery across the street. The people got a relic from the friars, after which the witch who often came to visit could no longer get in.
206377: In the countryside it was the custom to sweep on Saturdays. A farmer's wife had several times seen a toad jump in front of her broom and could not chase it away. She told the farmer, who advised her to cut off the toad's front legs with a spade the next time. The farmer's wife followed the advice. The next day she saw an old woman from the street going to church with bandages around her hands.
206406: In a house a knocking on the door was always heard. Someone advised the occupants to bolt their door at a certain time and then pray a rosary. They were not to open the door, whatever happened. After that those people no longer heard the knocking.
206421: A farmer returning from the village late in the evening saw a cat sitting by the road and asked: "My kitty, my little niece, what are you doing here?" When the cat answered: "Nothing", the farmer gave the animal a kick. The next day the farmer's sister-in-law had a broken thigh.
206446: In the Kruinbos cats came to dance in a circle. Those cats were people in the shape of an animal. One day someone chopped off one of the cats' paws. The next morning a woman had lost her arm.
206455: On a farm no butter could be churned because of the evil hand.
206468: In the Floorgat there was a deep hollow. When the bell was heard ringing at midnight at Christmas, the ringing could also be heard from that hollow.
206472: A woman known to be a witch often changed into a white goat. The goat was often seen wandering around the Molenstraat. When the witch died, the goat was not seen again either.
206488: In one family there was a five-year-old child who saw a little black dog every night. Strangely enough, the parents did not see the dog. One day the child flew over the stove in fright without being burned. When the mother wanted to wipe her child's nose, a pretty white handkerchief with a flower on it lay on the floor, though there was no such handkerchief in the house. A piece of string was seen lying on the floor. When someone pulled the string, it turned into an animal, but a moment later it was a string again. When the string was thrown into the stove, it flew upwards. In the morning the people went to the friars and saw a pencil and a pack of cards lying on the road. But they had to leave all of it where it lay.
206499: One night a man went to chop wood on the baron's estate. Suddenly the man saw a beast with a horse's head standing beside him. The man ran home sweating and cried: "I have seen the devil." The man was ill with fear for a long time.
206517: A shepherd going to the heath with his father saw something floating about a metre above the ground. Strangely, his father could not see the apparition. The shepherd shot at the ghost, which then flew into a house. The old woman who lived in that house died afterwards.
206521: When Charel H. from Ham was coming back from the Hoef, he was hindered by a cat that kept running between his legs. After Charel tripped and fell, he struck at the cat with a medlar stick. A little later the cat came back, and the man struck at the animal a second time. The cat's head was bleeding. The next moment countless cats came running up, but they left again at once as soon as they saw the blood of that one cat. After all, cats lost their magic power when they saw blood.
206529: Will-o'-the-wisps floating above a marsh were the souls of unbaptised children who lured lonely travellers into the depths of the marsh in revenge for the injustice done to them.
206540: One was not allowed to hang washing outside before sunrise or after sunset, or one would fall victim to the evil hand of the witches.
206587: Two or three sorceresses used to live in Oppuurs. One of those sorceresses is said to have brought the evil hand into the cowshed of a farm, so that for ten years in a row a calf lay dead there on the same day.
206605: A maid worked on a farm where strange things happened. Whenever the cows were being milked there, a black cat always ran over the animals. The cat jumped from one cow to another. The cowshed doors flew open and shut, even though they were bolted every evening.
206619: M. from Ham could conjure up mice. He could also make the animals disappear again a little later.
206661: On a farm where a novena had been made to be rid of the evil hand, the evil spirit left through the drain hole for the water. Before that, moaning and wailing had always been heard in that house.
206716: A mother who believed her child had died because of the evil hand went to the friars of Dendermonde. While the mother was away, the other children were looked after by their aunt. When an old woman came by and wanted to give the children a sweet, the aunt cried: "No, no, not that!" Then the old woman went away. That evening, when everyone had gone to bed, a knocking was heard at the door. The children's father went to look out of the window. Although no one could be seen, he heard a voice call: "Open up, good people." But the father was sure it was a witch. He threw a stone down, after which the witch disappeared.
206730: A boy always saw a cat appear when he went to visit his girlfriend. One day he kicked the cat against the hedge. When he then arrived at his girlfriend's, he found that the girl had a nosebleed.
206733: In an inn in Weelde a woman said she felt like dancing, even if she had to dance with the devil. A little later a gentleman dressed in black came in and asked the woman if she wanted to dance. While the woman was dancing with the gentleman, the farmers suddenly saw that the stranger had horse's feet.
206739: Nobody wanted to live in a farmhouse in Itegem. Many people used to live there, but the young women all died. When the farmhands came home late one evening, there was a calf lying in the room. It also often happened that the butter churn started turning by itself without any dogs in it. The people all fled from there. Nobody dares to walk past that farmhouse in the evening.
206749: In Kontich an old woman lived alone in a little house. The woman was suspected of being a sorceress. She always went to fetch milk in the evening. Across from the sorceress lived a master bricklayer. One day, while slaking lime, the man saw a cat come out of the sorceress's house and threw a stone at it, injuring its paw. When the sorceress came outside afterwards, she was limping.
206764: A man coming back from town was accompanied by a witch who claimed to be clairvoyant and able to predict the man's future. When the two came to the old castle at 't Ekselaar, the witch fell into the water around the castle. At that the man said: "If you had known that in advance, you wouldn't have walked so close to the water," and he made off.
206773: A farmer's wife struck a black cat. The next day she met a woman with a black eye.
206789: Sometimes cats could be seen dancing in the moonlight. Cats with green eyes were witches.
206805: Some people were felling trees between Sint-Amands and Oppuurs when a linen seller drove past with his cart. An old woman was sitting on the cart. One of the trees fell on the little cart. Since that incident, everyone who passed that spot was knocked to the ground. A loud crash was heard as if a tree were falling. That was the old woman using her power.
209153: An encounter with the devil, who bursts apart like a fireball after being asked who he is.
209154: An encounter with a silent woman dressed in black, who bursts apart like a fireball.
209155: A dead person returns after a promise to have masses said was not kept; an indelible burned-in hand appears.
209179: Bewitchment of cattle and house; protection by using Easter nails.
